1) The dedication to the cinematic experience that Tom Cruise has is admirable and certainly enhances the action scenes of this film by seeing that Cruise is clearly doing all of his own stunts 2) The film zips along at a blistering pace and doesn't feel anywhere near to being almost 3 hours long 3) The film deserves credit for being a film centred on an AI villain and releasing right as fears around AI are at their peak. Considering this film will have been written a few years ago, the writers were able to predict the future extremely well

NEGATIVES:

1) The action scenes in this film just don't have the same uniqueness as the previous few instalments have had. A lot of them feel fairly generic and also feel like they go on for far too long 2) I can't understand the decision to kill off Ilsa and bring in a less likeable copy of her in Grace. Both characters are British and love interests for Ethan, which is far too much of a similarity. The main issue is that I found Grace to be an incredibly unlikeable character - she betrays Ethan every chance she gets and yet by the third act we're meant to believe that he cares about her the same amount he cares about Benji and Luther.

3) The film had far too many characters who are given little to no development. Paris and the two American agents chasing Ethan should have all been removed completely, so that Gabriel could've been given more screen time in order to come across as a more intimidating villain.

7.title: Extremely tedious . . .
7.content: Two hours and 43 minutes of tedium. There must be at least six scenes of a group of characters in one room where each has a huge monologue and they all take turns blabbing away with what I suppose are important plot details that made my eyes glaze over. Do we really need to see Tom's character running flat out for three minutes in five scenes? I have yet to make it through the entire movie in one sitting. I love Tom Cruise and he never fails to give the audience their moneys worth but this just was too drawn out and verbose to keep me interested. My opinion seems to change with my mood - I may watch this again and re-rate it but this viewing was very frustrating.

7.title: Would of got a higher rating but a few problems...
7.content:
Ok first of all I should mention that I am a big TC fan and love his movies. I grew up watching his movies as I am only a few years younger than TC.

He puts in the effort and I would imagine it must be a honour to be associated as a character actor with his productions, probably similar to a Spielberg production. I have never really seen an actor put out such quality consecutively, and my perception is that he really cares about his film making contributions and wants to entertain us.

One of my irritations is the previews/advertisements speckled online and cable where most of the great moments are shown on the screen all in a effort to entice movie goers to that opening weekend. The bigger the movie (prod cost) and if the studios are behind the movie the bigger the advertisement budget, the bigger the spoiler leaks.... For myself, while watching cable I change the channel quickly or depress skip on my remote (if I had the tv show recorded) on any advertisements with the movies I want to watch in the Cinema. My friends know not to tell me any surprises. When it is a TC movie my friends and I watch his movies in the Cinema on the first day it is released in our city, therefore no spoilers and I see it fresh (so much more enjoyable this way and one is absolutely invested in the movie).

Unfortunately I saw the dirt bike stunt advertised somewhere, which don't get me wrong is amazing on what TC accomplished, great team effort. But when it came time watching this scene in the theatre it was like "Benji where an I going, where are you taking me" 10 minute scene and TC is motocrossing up to the peak for the jump stunt was such a detachment point because everyone had seen it in the previews and advertisements, they forced this down our throats.

While watching the movie I looked around the theatre during this scene and people were talking and some were on their phones.... this means they all were detached from the movie, that's a production mistake. Its like when Peirce was Bond and he was snowboarding with the lid of his ski-sailing apparatus down a black diamond mountain all whilst a laser was shooting from space after him.... OR Vin jumping his Charger down into a large deep hydro water dam.... This is pure detachment. The efforts will have to be even greater to pull the audience back in again.

Wouldn't it of been so cool if they put this amazing jump stunt in all the advertisements/previews and then never actually had it in the movie and do something different that was a total surprise?

I asked colleagues that had seen the movie if they had knowledge of the bike jump beforehand and the ones that stated no loved that scene and raved about the movie much more. Why.. they were locked in and along for the ride.... Also sorry but the scene where TC knew which window and jumped in at the split second to save the damsel in distress, this was another "disconnect" this was low hanging fruit, story/action wise. Never had this in the previous MI's movies.

When TC did the Ghost Protocol (GP) that little "shout out" to McQueen" in the ball bouncing in the jail scene and the amazing climbing the building scene.... also the little scene where he had put his glasses in his inside pocket of his jacket later for the sandstorm scene, these are amazing scenes all placed in there for the efforts of locking in the audience with the story and characters mission.

Or little scenes like when TC helped the lady officer outside of the garage when trying to escape, these scene's work and propel the movie in an uptick.

It doesn't take much to keep viewers so focused in that they are afraid to look at their popcorn as they may miss something....

Anyways my two cents.....

7.title: ...Overloaded with too many GCI Effects!!!
7.content: I'm a Big fan of the Mission Impossible series and I really liked every part that's why it was clear that I was really looking forward to the New Part of the Series Story. Tom Cruise Stunts always blow me away! It's clear to me that GCI was used in the last parts, but it seems to me that the new Part is completely Overloaded with GCI Effects and unfortunately the Action Scenes seem quite Unrealistic and Exaggerated. Okay, I can understand that the last action scene with the fast train is completely reworked in GCI and that's a good thing because without GCI effects it would be impossible to shoot the scene. For the chase scene, they could have done without GCI and shot the whole thing for real. The GCI effects in the car chase scene bother me! I Love Handmade Action Scenes where you can see that the Film Crew put a lot of effort and Sweat in the Action szene. John Woo did it in Part Twowithout GCI Effekts Well, for many People Part Two is a thorn in the Side, but John Woo still Created Action Scenes that you can still Remember today! The Story doesn't offer anything new either! The topic of AI programs is now discussed in almost all films. Don't get me wrong, the Film can be entertaining, and there are Action moments that excite you, but the rest of the Criticism points that I mentioned damaged the Film a Bit I Think this is the Weakest Part of the Film Series, and it has become clear to me that Mission Impossible could finally use a long break, Not that it Finally kills the Great Franchise.

7.title: Bit of a confusing mess, really.
7.content:
I've watched this film twice now and still can't fully get my head around it.

Ilsa has the first part of the key. Fair enough ... but the second part seems to be all over the place so it's very hard to follow what's happening when you're constantly trying to figure out where the macguffin is and what people's interest in it is. Some searching afterwards on the internet helped somewhat but - as I've said many times before - I'm not a fan of films that you have to search the internet for an explanation afterwards. Far too up itself for it's own good.

Still on the subject of things I didn't like ... Tom Cruise is finally starting to look a bit long in the tooth for this. He's in his 60's now for gosh sakes. I'm hoping that Part II will be a handing of the torch to Hayley Atwell. Also, killing off Ilsa was heart-breaking.

On the production side everything was top-notch as you would expect from an MI film. Great photography, great acting and yes, great stunts and action.

This is a pretty big step down from the other most recent films though.

67/100.

7.title: As action movies go, this is a good one.
7.content:
It took me 4 sittings over 3 days to see the whole movie.

Some of the action scenes though excellent, perhaps a tat too long, while others were unremarkable like the knuckel fight on top of the moving train (yawn).

The plot developement suffered because so much time was given to the action scenes.

Still, a remarkable piece of entertainment.

It took me 4 sittings over 3 days to see the whole movie... Some of the action scenes though excellent, perhaps a tat too long, while others were unremarkable like the knuckel fight on top of the moving train (yawn).

The plot developement suffered because so much time was given to the action scenes.

Still, a remarkable piece of entertainment.

7.title: Action spectacle with unspectacular stakes
7.content:
I've grown to love the mission impossible franchise over the last decade. Ethan Hunt has provided some of cinemas greatest moments in cinema. With benchmark so high, its always going to be hard to top last outing. The action here was tremendously strong but the story and characters' motives were extremely weak IMO.

I think the movie still needed a proper beginning, middle and ending, despite being a part 1. Without spoiling ending, I didn't feel massive urge to see the 2nd one, the same way I did at end of Avengers Infinty War. I expected Tom Cruise to deliver something spectacular to justify the part 1 and part 2, but to me, it doesn't seem like it needed to be 2 parts, as not much was established in part 1. I suspect movie studio wanted 2 movies made to justify the budget and investment.

My opinion might very well change once I see part 2, but overall I left cinema feeling a little underwhelmed as the movie felt like a load of action set pieces strung together with overly long exposition dumps between set-pieces to justify why everyone was there for Ethan to battle, but I just didn't buy the dialogue, which wasn't clever enough to pull off what it was trying to achieve, which I think was arching back to the classic old days of mission impossible 1 which was primarily an action spy thriller. But it just fell a little flat, so when action happened the stakes weren't high enough for me to be on edge of my seat. The villan looked the part but spewing lines like "you've no idea of the power I poses" and then not showing us, makes the fight scenes less intense, as we don't know what he's capable of, unlike terrifying villans in past like Philip Seymour Hoffman who we knew exactly the danger Ethan was in during every scene with the creepy terrifying Hoffman.

Having said all that, I was there with my kids, who maybe distracted me, so will watch again for sure before Part 2 again, and my opinion might change, as I do love this franchise and everything TC has done for cinema. As long as he's continuing to make movies I'll keep going to the theatre. And hopefully Dead Reckoning part 2 will have more of the heart and impact I craved that we get in likes of Fallout and Top Gun 2. Keep flying high Tom, you deserve all the cudos and good will, your heart is in the movies. I know I'll change my tune after part II.

7.title: What MI should be
7.content:
The action in this movie is the best yet, the villain is entertaining and easily threatening and the whole movie leaks passion from the corners of the screen. It may rely on a bit too many inconveniences which took me out of the immersion, but I was instantly put back in within a minute or two.

For me, it ranks below MI 1 and 3, but not by much. I have yet to see MI6, so that is a movie I can't fairly compare, but I personally enjoyed the action more than in any of the movies and thought it was among the best I've seen in any action movie.

The villain is scarily relevant, and although not beating MI3's, it comes in at a close second.

Definitely a must-watch for an action fan!

7.title: Good but not great
7.content:
MI Dead Reckoing part one is a good movie compared with other movies and continues one of the best Franchises. Tom Cruise as always delivers a fantastic performance and the humor they added to his character was a nice fresh touch.

However.. it is not as good as the last mission impossible movies and i expected more of it. The story is just a lot simpeler and i missed the real ''impossible vibe''. The script, action & fight scenes, suspense and story telling all went down in quality. Even the ''evil guy'' was a bit lame and without real good charisma.

I personally found it a great mistake that they ended the line of one of the main characters. All the build-up from the last movies destroyed for no good story reason.

The mission impossible team beside Ethan did not really do much. The cops who where chasing Ethen were pretty pointless and the chick from Asia... i mean.. just why add her to the movie? Probely only to boost the movie in China for extra income...

So overal... good movie to see but not so great compared to the other mission impossible movies. Hopefully they strike back with part two but i doubt it.

7.title: Nops...was expecting more
7.content: Clearly not the MI movie u long for...been waiting after ghost protocal to get something of the similar kind but didn't able to match my expectations...spclly after top guns...should work on pace of the movie along with more creativity in stunts and action scene. The action scene were very little and there was nothing new that might have already seen in the trailer...so I would be expecting much more action scene and stunts in part two as compared to one along with strong screenplay...even sometimes the music felt offbeat...only good thing what I personally liked about the movie is Tom even running in his 60s like the same way he used to ran in MI 3.

7.title: Great stunts! But lacking in heart.
7.content: The movie is long. Longer than it needs to be. Some scenes, and yes, even some of the action scenes seem to go on for a while. That said, the stunts and action scenes are incredible! The parts in between however; the story, the dialogue, the acting and auxiliary characters left me feeling a little bored and fidgety. All of the mission impossibles have somewhat of a hokie plot but I'm usually able to buy into it. But this time I felt myself just sort of watching the movie as a spectator, not immersed in it. Don't get me wrong. It was very entertaining! Car chases, fight scenes on top of trains, motorcycles going off cliffs.... It's always good fun. And the fact that Tom Cruise does his own stunts is a huge deal to me! I'll watch it again when it comes out on HBO or Amazon. I think a second viewing at home is in order.

7.title: Not as good as previous ones
7.content:
First of all, the good part: Tom Cruise's great acting and the fact that the 2.5 hours passed quickly as I was sitting there at the theater.

Many places of the movies is meh to me. It just makes you feel that it is fake. Starting with the submarine scene, they started with Russian then proceeded to English, just hoping you don't notice. I feel like in this movie, many characters' motives aren't clear to me. It just feels to me that people are chasing the key for no good reason. For example, where and why IIsa stole the key and if she had a plan. Why was Grace stealing the key? If it is just money, she could be out of the ness with the money she wanted early in the movie. Why risking her life again and again?

The scene on the bridge looks fake and forced. The all-knowing Grabriel waited for his enemies at the bridge with no weapon, and he was fighting IIsa, he had to use the small knife that he took from Grace. So talking about bringing a knife to.a gun fight. And yeah, why do they not use guns? Like some other reviews here, the ability of the bad guy Gabriel is inconsistent and it is confusing. And also, what is his motive? The entity helps him and he wants to bring death. Just weird.

We are talking about sentient A. I in this movie, yet they fight with knives and sword, and host very important meetings on a train that looks like from the 1920s. Also everybody got on the train smoothly, even the blonde woman Paris, but Ethan Hunt had to jump from a cliff...it just feels forced. With his ability, I am sure he'd be able to get on the train another way.

In the end, the blonde woman Paris saved them because Ethan didn't kill her in the alley. People like that don't change like that. They wouldn't be the bad guys if they had kind of empathy and gratitude.

7.title: Good, but TWO Parts?
7.content:
Saw this thru a Walmart (of all places) invite. Cruise is looking a little haggard. Not action-wise, but face wise.

The movie is a pure action movie with little believabilty in plot. As long as you can let that go, you'll be OK.

The movie starts off really slow. Like really slow and confusing. It actually takes a while to hit its stride.

Once the talking subsides and the action kicks in it gets pretty good. But it's also pretty repetitive. Lots of scenes of the actors nodding at Cruise and Cruise nodding at them like there's a secret code. Way too much of that.

I will say, however that the final prolonged scene with the train is super and worth the price of admission.

However, this storyline is a money grab, not a real two parter. This could easily have been done as a single movie.

7.title: Quite good.
7.content: After many raving reviews I expected a top-notch, maybe the best so far, M:I film. I got disappointed a bit. A bit, not much, but disappointed all the same. I think the previous film is still the best, closely followed by numbers 3 and 4. Where this disappoints me is the direction and the script. Too many close shots, too much editing and cuts during the fighting scenes. It seems they spent most of the budget on the car chase in Rome and on the spectacular train scenes. The rest is meh, by the usual M:I standards. As for the script, I think there's too much verbal exposition and talking overall in the first half of the movie. Also, the captain and the crew of the Russian submarine speak in English among themselves? And with funny Russian accents?🤦Why couldn't it be in Russian?

7.title: Weak storytelling and character building
7.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a mixed bag of a movie. On the one hand, it has some of the most jaw-dropping action sequences of the entire franchise. Tom Cruise is still putting his body on the line for our entertainment, and it's truly awe-inspiring to see him perform these stunts. The film also features a number of new and returning characters, all of whom are played by talented actors.

However, the storytelling and character development in Dead Reckoning Part One are both weak. The plot is convoluted and full of holes, and the characters are underdeveloped. As a result, the film never really engages on an emotional level. It's just a series of action set pieces strung together with a thin story.

Overall, I would give Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One a 7 out of 10. It's a fun movie to watch for the action, but don't expect anything more than that.

7.title: Are they paying Rotten Tomatoes
7.content:
Let me start by saying this movie is good I am not trying to put it down, but I don't know if it's as good as critics are saying it is. With a 96% on Rotten Tomatoes it beats Into the Spiderverse, Oppenheimer, Barbie, Sisu, John Wick 4, They Cloned Tyrone, and many other releases summer releases that in my opinion have had much more interesting plots and performances. I like the MI approach to action, it's fun, yet predictable. The MI movies have never really been risky instead it is all sorta the typical action film, which sometimes works really well MI:Fallout is one of the best action movies ever, easy, and its only doing 1% better on RT. This movie has a lot of weird little things that kind of annoy me, an AI all powerful villain with a dumb name and a henchman to carry out its will, a lot of its scenes sort of go on just a little too long, like the train scene at the end, and Tom Cruise just has to watch a girl die only to start trying to bang the next one. It is a fun movie to watch for some good ol action but 96% idk about all that.

7.5/10.

7.title: At least 80% of the action sequences were shown on the previews, basically you are paying the ticket price to see the drama
7.content:
(2023) Mission: Impossible- Dead Reckoning Part One ACTION ADVENTURE

The seventh Mission Impossible movie co-produced, co-written and directed by Christopher McQuarrie has Ethan Hawke. (Tom Cruise also credited as co-producer) confronting CIA director Eugene Kittridge (Henry Czerny) regarding two different pieces of a key toward a nuclear sub. He along with his MI team of Luther (Ving Rhames) and Benji (Simon Pegg) are then intercepted by among other things a professional pickpocket, Grace (Hayley Atwell) who wanted the key for financial reasons. Both the key, Ethan Hawke and Grace are being sought by an old foe, Grace (Esai Morales) along with his deadly sidekick Paris (Pom Klementieff).

You know, one of the things that kind of bothered me was the fact that although this one girl was supposed to be an expert assassin/killer, that she still needs the star, in this case Ethan Hawke to save her. I thought that era has long been gone, and then it's like, this movie still portrayed her as another damsel in distress. Anyone who has seen this would know what sequence I am talking about. And for a movie that is two hours and 43 minutes long I was also quite disappointed with the fact that at least 80% of the action sequences had already been shown on the previews, whether it's from ET or from some other, from the car sequence, the fight scenes on top of the train to the motorcycle jump, which means that I pretty much paid the price of the ticket toward the drama, the set up and the emotional scenes. I still kinda liked the movie, for it's really like a six since I believed I was going to see action sequences that I did not see from the previews and interviews as a result of those long delays. But then I remembered that despite it's very boring set up, it still had more action sequences than say MI1 and MI 3 despite already seen much of it beforehand on promos and advertising during those two years of Covid. This is the tenth of eleven movies writer, producer and director Christopher McQuarrie collaborated with Tom Cruise.

7.title: Great movie yet... another Skynet?
7.content:
This is a near perfect action flick. Loved it from the start to the end. Tom Cruise can certainly still deliver excellent action performances right until today. The Hollywood true star that keeps on giving. Everything is near perfect except .... the story itself.

We have all seen the Terminator, Matrix and every other movie with super advanced AI as the main antagonist. It feels as this theme has been done to death, and there are much better themes to explore for a super spy.

While watching this movie I really enjoed the excellent action sequences and obviously Tom Cruise acting , yet ...I felt I've seen it all before. Holywood writing department is obviously at stagnation, and they really should look elsewhere for new additions to this whole ordeal to trully become epic.

The action does not becomes stale or irrelevant. It's just great.

For anyone who loves actions, this is the movie for you. For anyone looking for an original story, honestly doubt it. Good enough to watch once or twice, but that's it. 7/10.

7.title: Not the best in the franchise but still entertaining
7.content:
Dead Reckoning part 1 is the newest outing in the MI franchise. I have to say I did enjoy most parts of it and found it entertaining, but generally it is not the best in the series, in fact, it could be the least interesting out of all the films.

I think the direction of the film is what makes it slightly weak. It lacked subtlety, it felt like it is divided into segments. The opening sequence when we follow the Russian submarine was ok, despite poorly acted dramatic scenes as we are introduced to the threat. The AbuDhabi desert sequence was interesting but brief, after which we are taken to one of the lamest scenes ever where the director of the American intelligence is having a debriefing with the rest of his staff, the entire staff start explaining the situation in a very funny and unrealistic way as each one of them gives a two to three phrases of speech and the rest of the sentence is completed by the next staff and they keep completing each other sentences in a very boring, unrealistic and repeated way. This never happens in real life meetings, i think the director was trying to please as much secondary actors as possible by giving them speaking roles just for the sake of it.

The AbuDhabi airport scene was also ok, nothing super and not a lot of action, just for the sake of introducing Grace, the latest of characters in the franchise.

The car chase scene in Rome is one of the highlights of the film, and is very thrilling and well executed. This is followed by another slow and unrealistic segment in Venice, when all characters meet in a party and start pointing fingers at each other and Ethan Hunt begs the Russian lady to take his side before they make their escape and a very boring fight/chase takes place in the streets of Venice just for the sake of sacrificing one of the good guys.

The Villain i may i add is two dimensional and uninteresting, probably one of the weakest of all films.

The final train segment is the most interesting and is probably what saves this movie from failure despite teeth cringing moments ( like when Hunt is chasing the train and finds himself on a mountain cliff, he snaps at Binji who just rambles about how he is stressed out right now and Ethan should give him a break ! ) does this type of dialogue actually happen in real life ?!

And yet another over long film, what's with films these days exceeding 2 hours 30 mints run time!! This one being 2 hours 45 minutes by the end of the film im so frustrated I just want to get it over with. Hey! If you can't make and conclude a film in 2 hours max, why are you in the movie making business??

Less is more !! Film makers need to keep viewers asking for more not less,, an ideal run time would be 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours 10 minutes max ,, otherwise its just way too long and i'd rather stick to TV in this case.

The funny thing is, despite the over stretched run time, both the characters of Grace and the Villain Gabriel are poorly developed.

So yeah, the film still delivers interesting and action filled sequences, but lacks in subtlety and has poorly written dialogue at times. Stunts are not as mouth watering as the previous films but i really liked the Car chase and train fight stunts.

I think what's happening with the MI films is that they accomplished everything before and it's extremely difficult to outperform themselves anymore, i still admire their efforts in keeping to make more films out of the franchise.

7.title: Fallout still better in my book
7.content: Phenomenal cast thru and thru. Was beyond ecstatic to see it three days before the nationwide release this Wednesday. Action was amazing and the twists were simply surprising. Wish we would have gained more insight in Atwell's character. Morales character could've been more developed earlier on in the movie. Good to see flashbacks prior to Ethan joining the IMF. Act 3, last 45 minutes was the best part of the entire movie. The train scene 🎬 was well done!! I still think the Fallout entry was the better MI film to date. Can't wait for part two to be released next year. MI lives on and scores another blockbuster hit!

7.title: What do you Reckon?
7.content:
(I love the opportunity for the ultra-rare treble coloned title). I've seen and enjoyed all the Mission Impossible films so far, but I came out of the last one hoping that perhaps they would shift to a smaller and more team orientated mission next. They don't, really, but again I enjoyed the wild and largely practical stunts that Cruise continues to risk his life doing.

An advanced AI goes rogue, and all the governments of the world try to get their hands on two keys that can bring it back into line. The IMF task Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) with securing the keys, one of which is in possession of his old friend Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson) and the other is due to be sold soon, with the opportunity to intercept the buyer at an Airport in Abu Dhabi. Hunt quickly concludes that the AI is too powerful a weapon for anyone to control, which puts him at odds with his own government. As Hunt and his team go after the key at the airport, they are not only pursued by agents, led by Briggs (Shea Whigham) but thwarted by a skilled pickpocket Grace (Hayley Atwell).

Whilst "Dead Reckoning 1" has the, now typical, two and a half hour run time, again I don't really feel like it felt all that long. Whilst it hits its storyline beats a little too repetitively, particularly the pickpocketing, it's fun and has a sense of humour that I don't really recall from the previous films. Lots of that comes directly from Atwell, who is at the forefront (but not all of a) 'isn't this all a bit silly' theme that runs through the film. The stunts are good, particularly the Roman car chase and the train scenes that make up the film's conclusion. I felt that Cruise's performance wasn't quite up to standard in the last film "Fallout", but he's good again here. Vanessa Kirby is having the most fun though, getting to play two characters and having a blast with the pratfalls and humour.

We're only halfway through though, and if the next film is disappointing I suppose that devalues all the work done here, and again - it's a bit more repetitive that I'd have like, few too many masks, few too may pickpocketing scenes. . . I'll be back for the next one though.

7.title: Best movie of 2023
7.content:
There has unfortunately been a paucity of worthwhile new movies in 2023. Many anticipated titles have been a major let down. However, the MI DR lives up to the hype with a very timely AI and cyber virus plot that may be even more timely when the Part II is released. Given the not ideal P1 vs P2 cliff hanger, the story line ended in a perfect place, upbeat too, so the viewer is not left wanting. Major gripes, like many new movies, include heavy emphasis on CGI during stunt and action scenes (often at expense of plot and character development). Often, the result is not easily watchable or accessible or as enjoyable as many past action movies that relied on real action stunts with no CGI.

Additionally, like many new movies, there are a number of fads / trends that detract from the strength of the film, including: 1. Shooting into the sun / light (the wrong direction, poor image quality 2. Shooting in overly foggy conditions to hide the CGI (Venice ally fights) but also impedes viewer from seeing action and which characters are present 3. Strobing lights at nightclub scene 4. Shaky camera, quick cuts, 4k crappy flickering images, especially noted during long multiple car chases in Rome, and the train roof top fight scene. On the whole, would like a return to more traditional movie making techniques and values, and increased emphasis on great images, plot, and characters.

Given / acknowledging above short comings, still recommend the movie, especially if you enjoy the franchise.

7.title: Tom Cruise shatters all expectations and sets a new standard for action movies.
7.content:
If there's one thing we can always count on with the Mission: Impossible franchise, it's jaw-dropping action sequences and intense espionage escapades. "Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" is no exception, delivering a heart-pounding thrill ride that keeps you on the edge of your seat throughout. With a blend of stunning stunts, well-executed plot twists, and solid performances, this installment sets the stage for an epic continuation of the series.

Tom Cruise returns as the indomitable Ethan Hunt. His dedication to performing his own stunts is evident in every daring action scene, adding an authentic touch that other action films often lack. Alongside Cruise, the supporting cast is commendable, with standout performances from Rebecca Ferguson, Ving Rhames, and Simon Pegg, all of whom bring their unique charm and wit to the story.

The film's direction by Christopher McQuarrie is deft, masterfully orchestrating a compelling narrative that keeps the audience guessing until the very end. The plot unfolds in a captivating manner, weaving a complex web of espionage, double-crosses, and alliances. However, it's important to note that some viewers might find the storyline a bit convoluted, with occasional moments of confusion. Nonetheless, the film redeems itself with its relentless pace and gripping action sequences.

Moreover, the film is not just about action and spectacle; it delves into Ethan Hunt's character on a deeper level. We get glimpses into his vulnerabilities and inner struggles, which make him more relatable and human. This emotional depth adds a layer of substance to the overall story, making it more than just a series of high-octane sequences.

While the complex plot may occasionally lose its footing, the breathtaking action and captivating performances more than make up for it. Fans of the series will be eagerly waiting for the next installment to complete the mission.

7.title: Literal cliffhanger
7.content: While Tom Cruise delivers a stellar performance the movie does seem to drag in certain points. The movie never seemed like a chore. Scenery and sound quality alone we're up there with some of the best in these titles. Antagonist storyline was not the strongest choice. As to flashbacks seemed more like filler more then less throughout the film. Cruise once again pushes the limits with jaw dropping stunts. Playful comic relief made for a strong connection with memorable reoccurring characters. With a strong supporting cast and a build-up to part two something the series has never done before- Jason Belanger.

7.title: Trailers gave way to much away
7.content:
The trailers for this movie gave away all the stunts. It was very disappointing. Leaving this movie felt very unsatisfying, not knowing the conclusion to the story. Several plot elements seems out of place for the MI franchise, were overdone in other films already or was just plain repetitive.

Oh a whole, this wasn't a bad movie, but it was a bit of a letdown. Perhaps seeing this movie without reading any reviews or watching any trailers would help.

Part one sets the stage for part two, but fails to even give us a glimpse of what part two will be.

It was a good Mission Impossible movie, just ruined by the trailers.

7.title: Best Action Scenes ever, Worst Script ever at MI saga
7.content:
As a filmlover, when I watch a movie of Tom Cruise I know he has put his whole heart and body in every single detail of every single scene.

The first 6 MI movies are just perfect, specially the 5th and the 6th.

This 7th movie is not as good as the past ones... by far.

I gave a 7 because of the perfect aspects it has :

Actors are absolutely perfect on his roles and performances.

Cinematography are as beautiful as it can be, the close ups of Plom, Vanessa, Hayley and Rebecca shows their extreme charisma and beauty as Velazquez would have shown if he had lived nowadays (the light, the colours, the framing) absolutely perfect.

The stunt scenes are undoubtely the best of all times ever shot in a movie.

The train scenes are astonishing and beautifully shot but completely unnecessary and unbelievable in the story.

If everybody knows which train they must be in, were there no easier way to get in than jumping from a mountain with a parachut?

And the bombs in the bridge...how and when Gabriel installed them?

What would have happened if he got the keys after they have passed the bridge? Weren't it be much more easier an useful putting a bomb IN the very train that he can make explode the moment he run away with the keys?

And his escape point is also very useless if he hadn't got the keys before they had passed it.

The script... the very most important soul of any story that deserves to be told is weak at best.

The enemy is an A. I. with its own personality that has done nothing remotely harm to anyone, but the heroes want to destroy it. The very concept of an A. I. is uncomprehensible for the 99% of the population (me included) because no one really knows how it may work or what can it do.

The things we don't understand frighten us but it doesn't necessarily means that they are dangerous or evil at all.

From the beginning of the movie, the entity is fully operational and we can see how it controls the satellites and may even duplicate voices and hacking FMI software, but it doesn't use its abilities for destroying banks' information, shutting down power plants, making explode nuclear power stations, or even crashing planes by controlling their software. The A. I. only fights against people who want to destroy it, it is just fighting for its own survival, like any living being would do.

And the goal of the mission is finding 2 keys that works in a sunken submarine (no one knows where) in order to get the original software of the entity so they can use it to control the A. I.

That A. I. has evolved and rebealed against its creators by constantly rewriting itself in orther to be stronger an better.

How the FMI are going to hack this A. I. that has already beaten its own programers? Unbelievable Nonsenses.

7.title: Missing the soul of MI franchise!!!
7.content:
It was missing the soul of the MI franchise. It has many great stunts and action sequences and cinematography was amazing. But it don't feel like the earlier mission impossible movies.

With 5 minutes into the movie it felt like Ethan Hunt has already given up. Ethan was very emotional and sensitive, whereas in previous parts Ethan had a Confidence.

They did not show the bureaucratic angle much and the villain was unexplored, yes, this will have a sequel where they will unravel all the hidden plots but this part was very dry for my taste.

Being said, Tom Cruise was Amazing as usual and real life daredevil. Looking forward for the great finale.

7.title: < James Bond
7.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One

Granted, I haven't seen all the previous films, have seen a few but now don't feel like it has put an end to watching this one.

There are simply too many characters in this movie and I have a hard time figuring out who is with whom and what their goals are. The film becomes too convoluted, among other things when a decision has to be made about which of Ethan's female acquaintances will be killed.

However, you have to give it to the stunts that are done in the film. They are filmed for real, and Tom Cruise, according to tradition, does many of them himself. However, someone has played a little too much Uncharted 2, as the scene with the train about to fall off the rails is heavily influenced by that game. I also don't quite understand how the team is still in possession of all their equipment considering they are working all by themselves, with no government or country supplementing them. How can their machinery continue to be effective?

The team chasing Ethan doesn't really have any effect and could easily be skipped.

Beautiful Hayley Atwell is very good in this role, and possibly the best in the film.

I miss more high tension that can be found in, for example, James Bond.

The fact that Tom Cruise turned 61 at the film's premiere is very impressive, because it doesn't look like it in any way on film.

7.title: Action with a side of action
7.content:
Some people give it a 10. It is not. Some give it a 5. It is better than that. I fall into the 7.5 category. The action was top notch as usual for this genre. Some clever twists to the usual car chases.

I would say it actually had too much action and could have used more dialogue. Not just the kind to explain the story forward. We really don't get to deep into the newer characters and you wonder why one would care if they lived or died.

I would have liked to see a little action given to his Teo side kicks. They seemed to do very little.

We see a lot of Tom running as per usual.

Go to the movie. Get some popcorn and just enjoy the visuals. We could use more like these again.

7.title: Good but not so good as the last ones
7.content:
MI series is one of the best film series of all time for me. Tom Cruise is the guarantee of entertainment the way he does all of his stunts and action is the reason why he is the one of the last remaining superstars of Hollywood.

Now coming to the film, The movie was good as they really focused on the story. But the thrill which we used to get in the previous ones was somewhat missing in this installment.

Starting from Cruise's entry to the thrilling action scenes and identity theft scenes it was not electrifying as the previous ones as if they had toned down all of these and made story there main selling point. I know that the story is an important part but they should have included more action scenes , more stunts and twists in the movie.

Anyway the movie was good but not as it's previous ones.

7.title: When you ask ChatGPT to write the script.
7.content:
Tom cruise is ... well it's TOM CRUISE! This man is the real deal! His last movie, Maverick is in my all time fav movie list.

About this movie, action set pieces were nothing special. I really liked the airport and submarine scenes. They were engaging and gave the movie insane hype for the next act.

Train scene reminded me of Uncharted 2. I'm sure it's inspired.

Villain was boring and to make him relevant by taking him to the past was just cliche. I didn't like how Ethan's past was described. Ruined the character.

I won't be watching Dead reckoning 2 in theatre.

Not a bad movie. The script have been written by chatgpt. Watch it, but Skip IMAX. Not worth spending extra.

7.title: Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning (Part One)
7.content: I'm not really a great fan of Tom Cruise. Yes, he does his own stunts and is as fit as a fiddle, but as an actor - well don't let's have too many scenes that require him to actually put his heart and soul into them. Luckily, there are only a few such scenes here as the rest of this is an enjoyable, quickly paced, continuation of the MI strand with this time, an elusive antagonist that reminded me a little of the "Forbin Project" (1970). The military have created the perfect intelligence that is locked into the sonar dome of a state-of-the-art Russian submarine. Seems though, that this dome isn't that impregnable and when a cleverly manipulated catastrophe hits the sub, it soon becomes clear that this gadget has, and is rapidly honing, a mind of it's own. The only way to stop it is to obtain the two conjoining parts of a cruciform key - and then discover the location of the sunken wreck, if there is to be any hope of thwarting it taking over the world. The story is more the stuff of "007", I thought, but it is a good, solid and well written story - and one that resonates well on a planet where technology and communications are pervasive across all aspects of our lives. Together with Ving Rhames and the (always annoying, sorry) Simon Pegg it falls to "Ethan" (Cruise) to ally with his deadly pal "Ilsa" (Rebecca Ferguson) and the nimble-fingered "Grace" (Hayley Atwell) to stop the key from falling into the hands of the enigmatic "Gabriel" (Esai Morales). End-to-end action; trains, planes and automobiles, parachutes and just like in "Fast X" (2023) poor old Rome comes in for a bit of a pasting - as does Venice and the Orient Express would now present even "Hercule Poirot" with an insurmountable whodunnit challenge. It's entertaining and serves well as a vehicle for the star, setting up the concluding part which, of course, leaves the plot here having to be a little undercooked and a touch predictable. Better than I was expecting and well worth a big screen outing.

7.title: Tom did it again!
7.content: Dead Reckoning part 1 is great action packed movie full of thrill and amazing stunt by mister Tom Cruise, to be honest i found Rouge Nation and Fallout as better movies in this amazing franchise but Dead Reckoning is worth of your time definitely. I don't understand those people who claims how nobody will feel that this movie seems like complete story ark without part 2, certainly this isn't a case in my opinion, this movie feels like not done story by the end, still i had great time in cinema, enjoyed a lot but yeah step back after Fallout and Rouge Nation in my opinion. Highly recommendation.

7.title: Full of action...
7.content:
"Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" is an Action - Thriller movie and another movie of "Mission: Impossible" franchise, in which we watch Ethan Hunt and his team trying to locate a dangerous weapon before it's too late or in wrong hands.

Since I had already watched all the previous movies of the "Mission: Impossible" franchise I knew more or less what I was about to watch. Though I was surprised by the action scenes, the interesting plot and the mystery behind it. The direction which was made by Christopher McQuarrie was very good and he succeeded on balanced action and suspense with plot and the evolution of the characters. The interpretation of Tom Cruise who played for one more time as Ethan Hunt was outstanding even after all these years. Some other interpretations that worth mentioning were Hayley Atwell's who played as Grace, Vanessa Kirby's who played as The White Widow and Simon Pegg's who played as Benji Dunn. In conclusion, I have to say that "Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" is an interesting movie and if you are a fan of the ""Mission: Impossible" franchise I am sure that you will enjoy it.

7.title: Like its predecessor, it was really great.
7.content:
The Mission Impossible film series are nowhere near my favorite film series but they are still entertaining because they have some pretty great, fun and ridiculous action moments and stunt works throughout which makes them really fun popcorn flicks. This one still manages to carry on with strong stunt/action works, editing choices, and good energy between the performances.

Throughout, there was some pretty good camerawork throughout as it helps add the atmosphere and landscapes of the environment. Many wide shots and open environments to help add the tension and excitement of the situation including good directing. As usual, the action moments are well-executed as the stunt work (especially the train and car chase scene) were really amazing along with the fight moments and the tension throughout. Most of the performances were solid as Tom Cruise and the rest of the cast members provide pretty good chemistry between their characters and were fun to observe. Alongside with the good uses of sound design and the soundtrack.

For the narrative, the narrative is the standard action story with some new territories but for the most part, it was pretty effective and interesting but because this is Part One, some aspects weren't great. The characters of Ethan Hunt and the others were interesting to observe and for the villain, despite it being Part One, still was manageable and interesting to observe. The pacing was pretty good as the film never once felt boring, good presentation and some fun dialogue although certain dialogue moments were slightly cringey. With the seriousness portrayed, there are a good handful of non-serious tones throughout which helps balance out the thrills and ridiculousness of the situations.

Overall, it's a great summer popcorn flick. Despite Cruise's personal life is a bit off-putting, he never fails to shine with his performance and efforts which indeed makes him one of the last Hollywood Star. Hopefully Part Two manages to live up.

7.title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One. amazing stunt work
7.content:
Aside from the amazing stunt work the movie is actually really poor, it lacks that after feeling of watching an amazing movie maybe because it's a part one? The opening scenes were pretty cool I give the opening a 7/10

towards the middle of the movie, you can see the story lacking and the writer going towards comedy to cover up.

The end was alright I wouldn't rate it higher than 8/10 the train scenes and the fact that it took the cops/CIA that long to discover what tom cruise is doing just makes me cringe. I think Pom Klementieff wasn't a wise choice she's an amazing actress but the scenes didn't do her justice.

Simon Pegg was amazing in this movie absolutely loved him.

7.title: Cool Spy Thriller- Mission: Accomplished
7.content:
I am a big fan of the Mission: Impossible film franchise. They are consistently good quality films. With the exception of "M: I 2" (which can be fun in its own way) all of the films in series have been great. This one continues Tom Cruise's winning streak and keeps a solid track record for the IMF team.

In this impossible mission, Hunt and his team must track down two halves of a single key, as it is the only way to stop a rogue A. I. known as "the entity". Along the way, many opposing groups try to stop Hunt and his team.

For any given action set piece that transpires, there are a lot of moving parts to consider. More often than not, there are 3 or 4 different groups all trying to converge on the McGuffin or stop our heroes, all with various motives. The movie may cut back and forth to several action sequences going on simultaneously. Some characters might double cross another character. All of these complications make the adventure a whole lot of fun. It keeps the audience consistently on edge and guessing what could possibly go wrong next.

The conflict in this movie is surprisingly relevant, with A. I. becoming more prevalent and even in danger of taking jobs away from movie writers and actors. In a way, this film becomes a meta narrative for Tom Cruise trying to save Hollywood from being replaced with A. I. generated stories.

But enough about the story, how is the action? The movie has one of the best car chases I have ever seen. There is a great stunt and big train fight that is just relentlessly action packed. And there is a terrific bit in an airport with a lot of good spy espionage business.

The newcomers of Hailey Atwell as Grace and Pom Klementieff as Paris are both terrific additions. Their characters add some good intrigue and sparks of adrenaline to the proceedings Cary Elwes is always a delight, and it is nice to see Henry Czerny return as Kittridge.

Kirby, Ferguson, Pegg and Rhames all return and do a good job in their roles, but they are not given as much time to shine in this go around. Esai Morales plays the antagonist Gabriel, and he doesn't have much of presence in the film. I take it that there was some cut content from the beginning that would have given his character more of a connection with Ethan, but as is, he is a weak link in the movie.

In summary, the latest Mission: Impossible movie delivers on some great action and characters. Some action scenes fail to impress, and the villain doesn't leave much of an impact. But overall, it is still a really good time. Choose to accept this mission.

7.title: Great start, weak ending and a ridiculous action scene.
7.content:
Could be so much better but one scene ruined the whole the movie to be a top-notch action flic.

Grace is the threatened by a gunman on a moving train. But thanks God that there is Ethan Hunt! He managed to jump with a parachute from a mountain and reaches easily the moving train. For sure he exactly lands in the carriage where the guy points his gun to Grace and knocks him down without effort. For me the most realistic and best timed scene ever. It was splendid, it deserves an own category at the Golden Rapsberry Awards.

Actually, the movie started quite intense with the scene in the submarine and the situation in the Arabian Desert. The chase at Abu Dhabi Airport was well-performed and the plot quite decent until this moment. After this point the movie loses its grip. The hunt in Rome was too CGI driven and many coincidences lead to a successful escape from the villain. And about the ridiculous final scene in the Alps is nothing more to add than in the beginning of this review. Thanks to the great first half this movie it gets a pretty good 7 out of 10. But I hope the second part delivers.

7.title: A fantastic roller coaster ride but no more than that.
7.content:
Sit back, get comfy for this Highly enjoyable movie with amazing set pieces and great action sequences.

Not my favourite Mission Impossible movie but a long way from the worst.

Cruise has lost none of his box office draw, Hayley Atwell is a welcome addition to the crew. The effects and CGI are great. Chris McQuarrie directs with a greater emphasis on the action rather than the gadgets and technology of the past to great effect.

There are some plot holes and conveniences but in order to enjoy this seventh instalment in the franchise it's best not to dwell on these to much and just enjoy the ride.

7.title: Spectacular at times but overly long and clichéd
7.content: Ethan Hunt (a well-preserved Tom Cruise) and his IMF team search for a highly coveted McGuffin, a key that may unlock the control of an all-powerful AI. Needless to say, numerous avaricious and/or evil parties are also looking for the ultimate prize. At 163 minutes (and this is only part 1), there is far too much movie for the plot (despite a plenitude of characters). Many scenes, while well executed, go on too long (the endless car chase) or quickly become repetitious (the frequent pocket picking/putting for example). Other than Pom Klementieff, who attempts and fails to look fanatical (or dramatic or deadly or manic or something), the cast is OK portraying the usual 2D action hero/villains and deliver the expected cliché-sprinkled script full of playful tough-guy banter, quips, convenient exposition, and verbose menace. I admire Cruise for his dedication to his craft and his willingness to take risks, but I am reminded of Harry Houdini's failed attempt at becoming an 'action star' in the 1920s - audiences didn't really care that he 'really did' the stunts (usually escapes), 'fake' stunts, however preposterous, were more fun and exciting. I'll watch 'MI-DR part 2' when it shows up on Netflix but I'm just expecting more of the same.

7.title: One more action packed chapter of the franchise
7.content:
One more in this franchise is equally thrilling with some stunning action sequences but I have my reservations if you ask me if it is the best so far. For one, the runtime of 163 minutes is rather high and secondly there is too much of planning and conversation in between the action which is a drag. Ethan Hunt has aged and it shows. He is now shown shocked and perplexed for a moment when temporarily beaten and that seems fair enough.

Director Christopher McQuarrie has planned the narrative through 5 major scenes. First in the desert area, then the escape at the airport ( with the help of AI), then the confrontation in the party sequence, then the hand to hand fights in the alleys and canals, and finally the long drawn climax on the train which is truly nail biting and edge of the seat stuff. Ethan Hunt is again racing against time to beat the bad guys in their game and save the world from impending disaster. The much discussed stunt of Tom driving a motorcycle off a cliff with a parachute and floating down to land on the train is clearly a highlight. (As Ethan his hesitation in the movie to take the dangerous jump appears natural.) This is guaranteed to give you an adrenaline rush. There are the usual ingredients like the intrigues, the daring plans, the worrying apprehensions, the secrets, the startling disclosures, the loyalties and the operative going rogue. They are all there in the plot. The unravelling of the subplots appear weary at times but then the intermittent bouts of the action packed high voltage stunts more than compensate for it. Tom Cruise keeps the franchise flag flying and does a fine job as usual though he has aged and it shows.

7.title: Another solid entry in the series
7.content:
"We live and die in the shadows, for those we hold close, and for those we never meet."

If you were following the production of Dead Reckoning, then you know the mission to finish the film was beyond hellish. The entire filming was struck with bad luck. If not, don't worry - I will fill you in. If you already know or don't care - skip the next paragraph.

So, this movie and The Batman were hit the hardest during filming due to the start of the COVID-19 outbreak. The original plan was to shoot Parts 1 & 2 back to back, but with delays messing up the filming schedule and the budget ballooning to $291 million, making it the most expensive MI film to date. Nicholas Hoult was initially cast as the villain but had to drop out due to his commitments with the TV show The Great. So many crew members contracted COVID-19 that production had to stop for weeks until it eventually started again. Of course, this led to the famous audio rant from Mr. Cruise himself, who yelled at two crew members for not following the rules. Whether you think he was in the right or wrong, it does, however, give us an idea of how stressful it was trying to make a blockbuster during a global pandemic. With the film set in different locations worldwide and the long filming hours, self-isolating during those long months must have been extra tiring.

But in the end, it was all worth it.

It's 2 hours and 43 minutes long, yet you never feel it. It's got solid pacing - the mark of a good movie. It follows the same formula as the previous films, where a mission goes wrong, and our MI crew must fight all odds to stop a world-ending event, where some people still don't trust Ethan Hunt for whatever reason, despite being right every single time in the past. And yet, it's so entertaining to watch.

Director Christopher McQuarrie is the saviour of this franchise, as every entry feels fresh, exciting, and cinematic. McQuarrie understands cinema, the visual language, and the slick rhythm of pace and flow.

While the action did not blow me away like Fallout, it's still fantastic. The last action scene involves train carriages one by one falling off a destroyed bridge. It was the most thrilling thing I have seen. The Rome Chase scene had plenty of thrills and comedy to go around. Funny enough, Fast X filmed a chase scene in the same area in Rome, but the comparison between the two movies is night and day. Fast X looked phony with the overuse of CGI, and it was not thrilling enough. Dead Reckoning, on the other hand, was done more practically and looked so much better. It made better use of the area for the action set pieces. Another comparison is that these two action franchises have been going on for a while now, but one is getting better with each installment while the other is getting dumber.

How about the stunt of Cruise throwing himself and his motorbike off a cliff, which the trailers showed to death in the marketing, and it still managed to take my breath away when I saw it in IMAX; not many modern movies do that. Movies like this remind us why we go to the cinema. For the thrill, for the experience.

I cared about the MI crew. In Dead Reckoning - there is room for emotional depth and always an enjoyable collaboration.

A newcomer to the series, Hayley Atwell, is a standout and gave an excellent performance. The funny thing is, she isn't a 20-something newcomer to the film scene or anything like that, as she has already starred in big movies before this, like the Marvel Cinematic Universe. And yet, this feels like a breakout role. Those movies did her dirty.

Pom Klementieff is another newcomer to the series, as the silent but deadly henchman. Most of her character is a mystery but intriguing screen presence.

With the main threat being AI, it never felt timelier than ever, even though the script was finished before all the AI mess started to take effect. What is even more perfect for the film's message is that this came out around the Writers and Actors strike, with one of the reasons the strike happened was that movie studios are pushing AI to take over people's jobs. This movie feels like a big middle finger to AI and higher-ups using it.

Director Christopher McQuarrie's love for cinema, style, mixture of genres, stunt work, language, and flow with pacing has benefited this series ever since he took over this franchise. The action was exciting, and the score was fantastic. It has been nearly 30 years since this franchise started, and it keeps improving.

I do have issues with the film. I admire the real stunt work from behind the scenes, but the use of CGI overshadows the realness of the stunt work, and it's easy to think most of it was on a computer. As I said earlier, it's nowhere near as great as Fallout, as I thought the action scenes and pacing to be better.

Other than that, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a solid entry in one of the best action franchises.

7.title: A step backwards in this franchise
7.content:
I don't know if the popularity of the absurdly impervious John Wick has rubbed off here, but after it seemed that Tom Cruise had belatedly realised that what made the Mission Impossible TV series so great was the teamwork, he has reverted to superhero mode.

This film has an excellent cast, including the team that effectively rescued the franchise, and yet it's all about Tom. And as if to emphasize the expendability of the other team members (it's the mission that counts; that and making Ethan appear indispensible and superhuman), the best of the lot gets needlessly killed off in order to make way for a new love interest whose moral values are highly questionable (born of a life spent looking after No.1 - but don't most of us face that challenge and learn to distinguish right from wrong along the way, so no excuse really).

The other annoyance was the reversion to face masks, a Hollywood invention that fails to convince audiences, since we all know how much more it takes to convincingly impersonate another person - especially when one's life is on the line! It spoiled MI2 and takes the edge off this edition also.

Having got my complaints out of the way, this is nevertheless an entertaining film. The key plot element (excuse the pun) is timely, dealing with an AI program that has gone independent and is a threat to the future of humanity. We get our favourites (Rebecca, Simon, Vanessa and Ving) back - though we lose the best one, who transformed the franchise for the better while she was around - plus a couple of new ones (Hayley, Pom and Greg). And although Esai is a thoroughly nasty villain, he is overshadowed by a sentient AI program that can analyse all possible outcomes of every situation and plan for them in advance - a truly scary scenario.

Tom seeks to prove the human element is still a game changer, but his team is relegated into the background, in part due to the difficulty of being able to communicate without being monitored (there is one moment when Tom is directed up a blind alley by the program imitating Simon's voice, with deadly consequences). Hayley is the unpredictable element, which may eventually work in their favour but has dire consequences in this Part I.

So, a recommend, and I look forward to Part II in May, but this film was not as good as the two (maybe 3) previous editions and I will not be sorry to see it end there (I don't think Tom Cruise needs to keep proving his virility to the US public, or himself).

7.title: VIEWS ON FILM review of Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One
7.content:
Tom Cruise brought the movie industry back from the doldrums of COVID. He just did. Last summer came Top Gun: Maverick and this summer we have Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One. Now did I salivate for "Part Two" after the closing credits for "Part One" appeared? Kind of. Not in a Return of the Jedi sort of way after Empire Strikes Back but yeah, kind of. And does Cruise still do his own stunts while being adverse to good old CGI? Yeah but for some reason he's just not as confident this time around. I mean it's as plain as a pikestaff.

Anyway "Dead Reckoning" is the seventh installment in the Mission: Impossible franchise. Script-wise, it's as clunky as a piece of metal jewelry (cruciform keys, hint, hint). Bodies in motion-wise, it's not the strongest account, probably held back by the limitations brought on by the pandemic (it was filmed in the middle of 2020). Sure there's death-defying shtick but you've gotta wade through circumlocutory dialogue just to get to said shtick. There's also about twenty minutes that could've been cut ("Dead Reckoning" clocks in at 163), an off-kilter attempt to add humor, a reluctance to trim the amount of characters that fade in and out, and fight scenes that seem sloppy, like they're bad dailies from John Wick. Heck, no wonder Tom Cruise got so angry at everybody on set ("I don't ever wanna see it again!!! Ever!!").

But hey, Mission: Impossible Dead Reckoning Part One really redeems itself in the last half hour. Cruise control baby! Just think brawling on top of a runaway train that travels like it's on the Autobahn, Cruise's Ethan Hunt going off a cliff on a motorcycle (of course), and some serious bridge detonation. In the end Tommy boy could probably make ten or more of these things. That I "reckon".

7.title: Deuteragonist is trash.
7.content:
I find it hard to get excited about yet another one of these but once I start watching, I go along with the fun of it all though the whole thing is a bit austere.

There is humor thank goodness but it's often smug humor.

The concept is similar to the third Johnny English Movie.

I'm going to give a soft spoiler, something that happens in the first act:

OK, ready?

I was very impressed how there's this chick who I don't remember from any previous movies at all but how you get the impression she's going to be a big part of this movie but then she's killed.

I was irked to find that she survived and then became the deuteragonist.

A bland and uncharismatic character that calls people hurtful names.

The respect and admiration I have for the Italian nation and culture notwithstanding, I really do not respect those men whom Ethan should just karate chopped with extreme prejudice.

It was a great climax for a part 1 of a larger thing.

7.title: An intense but slightly unsatisfying mission
7.content: Mission Impossible Dead Reackoning is a testament to Tom Cruises commitment to make visceral and immersive action films to entertain the audience. However in this film it seems that this ambition has come at the cost of story. This is nothing new for the franchise as it is a well known fact that action scenes are constructed first. With the story written later to bind all of them together. For the most part this has worked for the series however in the seventh installment it does not. All the downside here is exposed. Exposition dumps, confusing plot threads, unsatisfying story progression and much more. This film is definitely on the lower end for the franchise. Tipping towards mindless action. But when Ethan hunt has to run, shoot, or jump off an elevated surface. It is hard not to enjoy yourself.

7.title: A Gleefully Chaotic, Stunt-Fueled Spectacle
7.content:
Ethan Hunt is back, defying gravity and expectations in the latest installment of the action-packed Mission: Impossible franchise. "Dead Reckoning Part One" delivers heart-pounding set pieces, globetrotting intrigue, and Tom Cruise's unwavering commitment to physical theatrics. However, its sprawling narrative and occasionally clunky exposition might leave some viewers breathless, but wanting a bit more focus.

From a motorcycle plunge off a mountain cliff to a train heist defying physics, the film boasts masterfully crafted action sequences that keep you on the edge of your seat. McQuarrie's direction shines in these moments, balancing elaborate choreography with genuine tension.

At 60, Cruise embodies the relentless Ethan Hunt with unwavering charisma and commitment. He throws himself into every stunt, making the impossible seem believable (or at least highly entertaining).

Rebecca Ferguson, Hayley Atwell, Vanessa Kirby, and Pom Klementieff bring depth and intrigue to their roles, forming a formidable team alongside Hunt. The female characters are particularly welcome additions, breaking away from the usual damsel-in-distress tropes.

The central plot, revolving around a deadly weapon and a powerful organization, unfolds methodically, leaving viewers piecing together the puzzle alongside Hunt.

With a runtime exceeding two and a half hours, the film occasionally struggles with pacing. Subplots and character development sometimes feel sacrificed for the sake of action set pieces, leading to a slightly bloated feel.

At times, the film relies heavily on dialogue dumps to explain intricate details of the plot, which can feel clunky and interrupt the flow of the action.

While enjoyable, the core structure of the film adheres closely to the established Mission: Impossible formula, potentially lacking the surprise factor for longtime fans.

Fraser Taggart's camerawork is dynamic and immersive, capturing the scale and intensity of the action sequences with clarity and flair.

Lorne Balfe's score keeps the adrenaline pumping, perfectly complementing the on-screen action and suspense.

While mostly seamless, some CGI moments, particularly in the climax, appear slightly less convincing than practical stunts.

Tom Cruise delivers a typically charismatic and determined performance, showcasing his unwavering dedication to the action sequences. Rebecca Ferguson adds vulnerability and complexity to Ilsa Faust, making her a compelling ally to Hunt. Hayley Atwell brings a steely resolve and quiet competence to her role as Grace, a newcomer to the IMF team. Vanessa Kirby shines as the enigmatic White Widow, balancing ruthlessness with a hint of ambiguity. Pom Klementieff offers a welcome badass touch as, Paris.

Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a thrilling, action-packed spectacle that delivers everything fans expect from the franchise. While its overstuffed narrative and exposition dumps might hold it back slightly, the film's stunning stunts, intriguing mystery, and strong performances (particularly from Cruise and the supporting cast) make it a worthy addition to the series. Just be prepared for a cinematic marathon.

7.title: Spectacular yet narratively and technically criticable
7.content:
In recent years, the concept of cinematic franchising has worn out. The tendency of worsening has hit franchise after franchise, as showcased by the last installment of the Fast and Furious Franchise.

On the other side, Mission Impossible has shown that, with enough time, careful planning, and great execution, the newest installment can always be better than the previous one.

The fourth installment initially seemed to be the best in the series until there came the fifth and the sixth. All are qualitative, narratively captivating films with awesome, more or less grounded, action.

This entry was also spectacular with the usual characteristics that make the Mission Impossible franchise simply one of the best. But, somehow, I didn't work for me as did the previous ones.

The plot is astonishingly up-to-date with the frightening subject of AI, Tom Cruise's dedication is highly laudable as always, the action entertaining, the various locations fascinating and the stakes incredibly high.

But the increase of characters, some of who feel expendable, and the increase of CGI, like in the train scene, was something I liked rather less.

7.title: 7 for the 7th
7.content: Good if you can keep up with it. I don't think the screenplay is the best, it throws a bunch of plot points, concepts and names really fast, some of which are unnecessary and only tangle your brain even more. That said, if you get the main ideas and premises, you have a great movie. The plot is a new one that fits the current world and feels like a very realistic threat. Although there isn't much action in the early minutes, once it starts it keeps a good flow of stunning sequences and, of course, jaw-dropping stunts with beautiful landscapes and top visual effects. Regarding the characters, bold decisions were made, and even though Hayley Atwell has an outstanding performance, I have mixed feelings about her character. It can feel like a new version of Ilsa, but I am curious to see what her arc is in part 2. Overall, it accomplishes the main objective, which is to set up part 2.

7.title: Fun, but rather long
7.content:
I have to admit that the Mission Impossible films seem to be one of those franchises that even though they make an awful lot of money, they don’t seem to be as front and centre as a number of other franchises. Mind you, I believe this is film number 8, which is a decent number, but considering that they have been around for something like 20 years indicates that they aren’t being released as often as others. Mind you, considering the fact that Tom Cruise seems to have other projects on the go as well, it isn’t surprising that they are spaced out the way they are, but personally, I think that works well.

The film opens in a Russian submarine that is testing the latest technology (and my first thought was that this didn’t age all that well, though I suspect that this was written well before the truth of the Russian army came to light in the invasion of Ukraine). Anyway, the sub is destroyed and all on board are killed, and we are given a glimpse of some entity that exists within the power core, one that is being controlled by a key around the neck of the now deceased captain.

It comes to light that this entity, which is known as ‘the Entity’ is a powerful AI that has become sentient, and has started infiltrating all of the world’s computer systems, particularly the ones managed by the various defence and intelligence organisations. They know of the existence of this key, but getting it is going to be tricky, so they call up Ethan Hunt, the guy that you call when you want impossible things done, to get it. The problem with Hunt is that he is well known for going rogue, so getting something to control this AI by using somebody that you generally can’t control is a problem in itself.

Like, yeah, this film actually wasn’t all that bad, though it is overtly long. Then again, it is part one, so obviously the point of the film was getting the key, so I suspect the second one, which will come out a year later, will be able dealing with The Entity. Yet, as I mentioned, it does feel a little bit too long, and yeah, some of the action sequences could have been cut down a bit. Mind you, it does make me wonder what the whole idea with these two part films are these days – sure, they did it with some of the books they made into films, but now they are moving to the other franchises and doing it as well.

Anyway, as I said, I personally didn’t mind it. It was quite an entertaining film, though it certainly could have been made shorter because I’m sort of at that stage where I’m not really all that keen on watching overtly long films in a cinema, particularly when I do like to have a break.

7.title: Tom Cruise is still young
7.content:
It is just difficult for me to fulfill 600 words for an ok film. But I would like to make a record of every movie I have watched. So, I just hope that the requirement should be lowered.

Tom Cruise keeps so well. With his presence I would watch the movie no matter what. But for the plot of the present one it is far from surprise. Fighting over the top of a train long exists. Could I expect something newer.

Another thing I would complain is the look of the new female lead. She is not beautiful enough to be with Tom.

Hopefully we could see a more complicated plot and richer story in the next MI movie.

Tom Cruise never old.

7.title: Not a hair out of place yet again.
7.content:
Typical Tom Cruise he is in every scene and looks good in a suit. Now 60 he still insists on doing he owns stunts, and the women are now old enough to be his grandchildren.

Not saying the movie is bad, the special effects are fantastic, and the stunts Tom does, are amazing. But it is becoming the same thing over and over again with his movies. It is based around him, and he is the big macho man, who can beat up half a dozen fellows at once men at once and not have a hair out of place. As for the women they are getting younger and he is not.

Whether Top Gun Maverick, Jack Reacher and MI franchise he is now playing the same character in each movie and it is getting old.

7.title: If there's nothing else to see...
7.content: First, I've got to say I'm not a huge fan of the franchise and I only saw this movie because Oppenheimer wasn't available at the time. I wouldn't say it was bad but I leaved the theater feeling like... Meh. It has some real good action scenes, like the car chase in Italy and the hanging train and it's hilarious to see Tom Cruise just running. Also, it was great to see Vanessa Kirby and Pom Klementieff, I really liked their roles. However, the truth is everything else got me bored. The plot, the script, the characters... I feel like it's missing something, but I don't know what. I would still see the next part, though. Just for the sake of it.

7.title: Grace character is a letdown
7.content: I have been a very big fan and follower of all MI movies and I loved all of them until Dead Reckoning part 1. No matter how beautiful Hayley Atwell is, her character in the movie is a very big let down. I never likde her until the end of the mo ie even though she switched sides. She is so bad, hell bent to get what she wants in any way possible. She doesn't deserve to be a new part of the team. She is already a bad egg. With that kind of character, it won't bring any good to the IMF. Sorry to say but she is the one reason why Ilsa Faust died. I really hope her character dies also or gets killed in the second part because I really don't like her. Too bad for rhe writer. I lost my admiration to you Mr. Writer.

7.title: Great action entertainment for me until fatigue started to set in
7.content:
SPOILERS *** SPOINERS***

Hey, I'm old. Sitting for 3 hours starts to get to me after awhile but until the train scene I was all in on this as a great action movie. I still like it a lot - 7 out of 10 is still a good rating. And there was not a slow moment during its entire length although there were more than a few repetitive ones. Throughout, the action scenes also made me chuckle with good humor at the absurd situations and stunts. Very funny.

Acting SImon Pegg and VIng Rhames deliver as always. Henry Czerny has more to do than usual and is wonderful.
