All four women are fabulous - tough to say adieu to Ilsa (Rebecca Ferguson) but Hayley Atwell as Grace plays her part to the hilt and her background, also quite funny, fits well into the team. The two blond quasi-villainous women, Black Widow and Paris were amazing, the latter in personifying her character and in her action scenes. Cary Elwes was a hoot in his brief role as a dufus "Head of Intelligence." I saw some critics were a bit negative on Esai Morales as Gabriel. I thought he hit just the right notes and his knife-fight ballet duel to the death was superbly choreographed and realized. The simultaneous fight between Paris and the Tom Cruise stunt double was a bit of an unwanted distraction but certainly didn't spoil that great finale for Ilsa. What followed, however, was Tom Cruise at 50% of his best acting wise in my opinion. His mourning seemed superficial and while Grace was plenty alluring, she seemed to captivate him more "professionally" than anything more than that - and I think a bit more was warranted.

After Grace became a team member, what follows on the Orient Express is terrific but the stunts/action became more over-the-top and time-consuming and as obligatory as navigating an obstacle course. In particular, the motorcycle stunt was ridiculous and took forever. The car-after-car train escapes, one after another were very funny but that was when butt really started hurting me and I finally thought enough was enough already. From there, the conclusion and epitaph seemed by-the-numbers.

In short, entertaining and worthy of your time. A bit disappointed by Cruise's performance (80% overall) but everyone else was so great, it more than makes up for it. Perhaps Cruise was trying to convey Ethan's emotional and physical fatigue because that came across loud and clear.

Overall not as good for me as the previous two - both 9/10s - but certainly worth seeing and a lot better than the Marvel stuff.

But, if you're old like me, pick a modern theater with very comfortable seats or bring a cushion.

7.title: Slight of hand - the movie
7.content: Take a shot every time someone secretly steal or plant "the key" 😛 no but seriously the AI villain and it's henchmen is a creative addition to the genre. Good set pieces. The new woman is annoying as hell, she acts like a 5 year old. The "haunted past" thing is getting old. It could be more lighthearted considering how over the top it is. The close-combat fighting is not as exciting as it could be (think something like kingsman, the raid or bourne or mad max). Ended on an exciting note. Again I liked the incorporation of things that are real potential AI risk that's actually rooted in reality. Very nice.

7.title: Not the target audience but.......
7.content: This was the first Mission Implausible film I've seen and as a 52 year old man who tends to go for social realist dramas and not multiplex fodder (pretentious, moi?), I didn't go into this film expecting to love it. And I didn't love it by any means. But, despite the 2.75 hours running time - not including the 35 mins 'trailers' (ie mostly adverts) - I was never bored. I even kind of understood what was going on even though I'd never seen an MI film before. The action scenes were very impressive. Did they blow my head off? No, because it was all implausible nonsense. But to be fair it's one of the best action films I've seen. The best Tom Cruise film since the equally implausible Top Gun Maverick. And kudos to Cruise - he might be as mad as a box of frogs but Crikey he immerses himself in his projects. 7 out of ten.

7.title: If a 40s Noir Was Made Today with Tom Cruise, This is What it Would Look Like
7.content:
If you choose to accept this mission, you will be entertained. This is a great action movie that brought something new to this storied franchise with an enemy that is even scarier than others seen before due to the way it operates. It's a fairly timely movie as the topic of the villain (not spoiling on purpose) is something people talk about constantly in this technological age. I liked the way they handled the villain, even though I think at times the script struggles to address the topic by overusing the words "The Entity".

Tom Cruise is back and for a man above 60, I don't think you can ask much more from him from an action standpoint. I think he will go down as one of the best action stars of all time, and this film will definitely help bolster that argument. He really is amazing when he does some of the stunt work and you get to see it with your own eyes. Shout out to the Fiat 500 for an iconic action scene that got the whole theater to cackle. I also have to give a shout-out to Haley Atwell who absolutely killed it in the new role. I actually felt tense during some scenes because she was acting genuinely terrified and I believed it since Cruise probably did some of the stunts right in front of her eyes.

I do have to say there are a couple action set pieces, but overall, I wasn't feeling as many goosebumps or thrills as I did with previous installments. Also just a warning, there is a lot of people talking in rooms in this, which does slow down the pacing. I would not rank this close to "Fallout", "Rogue Nation", or even "Ghost Protocol" due to the fact the action just wasn't as exciting. However, this movie does deliver in that it remains entertaining to see Tom Cruise jump off buildings and run from place to place. Go see this on the biggest screen possible and I assure you that you won't be disappointed. Just don't go with expectations like this is the best Mission Impossible movie and you will thank yourself after.

7.title: Whatever You Wanted But Not Ethan Hunt Needed
7.content: When it came to this film it delivered whatever you expected from an MI franchise. Whether it's breathtaking stunts, awe-inspiring tools, or down to the last minute win or die situations it lacked in two elements overall. The effect and the story. In the end we feel like the movie is at the intermission. The team could fit both the Dead Reckoning parts in the same. The plot is not that compact or complicated. It could be done and would've helped. There is no reason to half-cook this movie. Yes, there are some serious turns in this movie but in the end, it was all about action stuff. The sequence takes place but we miss the the foundation or the description of its existanse. Tom Cruise still has that James Bond charisma as well as the rest of the cast. Hayley Atwel filled her screen time as a fresh start and she nailed it. Her presense was a plus point. Overall it is a fine movie. Tell me otherwise if one could find a decent action movie in 2023.

7.title: Franchise losing steam?
7.content:
I've seen all the movies in the franchise and always felt they improved with each one. DR (Dead Reckoning) has lost something along the way. Way too many chase scenes with either cars or people running that don't add anything new. Too many characters that don't need to be there. Begins to seem like 'filler' just to plug up some plot holes. One thing missing from this film is the tongue-in-cheek humor that really set the last few installments apart. Jeremy Renner was missing and I felt Luther didn't add much in the way of character. Plus, Simon Pegg's character was underused and he just wasn't funny this time around. Overall, the storyline has a disjointed, messy feel to it.

The movie took itself too seriously this time. A notable figure was killed off (no spoiler) which added weight. The stunts were great, as usual. One thing that tended to take the steam out of the base jump off the motorcycle scene (for me) was having so much of it revealed (how they made it) before the movie even opened. There was no element of surprise left there.

I didn't go see the movie at the theater, and just today bought and watched it online (Oct 11) I'm glad I didn't drive 2 hours into my hometown theater as I would have felt letdown. I did drive in to see Top Gun: Maverick; it was one of the best movies I've seen in a very long time. Just about as perfect as it could get.

So the stunts saved DR from being totally flat but I think it was a good storyline that was mishandled. I probably won't watch it again, that's how much I didn't care for the movie. Tom Cruise has held up well but I didn't sense much of a "team" in this movie. I hope part 2 does a better job.

7.title: MI breathing Last
7.content:
It's as good as mixing all the older MI movies. All are growing old but the movie is made to appeal younger generation.

AI and machine learning is new thing in the world and a scifi twist is definitely makes this movie in new league.

Actions are slow and too much talking makes the movie a bit of odd. Some chase can be better planned and spicy.

Train squense is from some older movie with escape from falling bogie is straight from Jurrasic park 2. Overall MI spice with some AI and some comedy but serious killing makes it kids love.

Watch with family to mKe it fun evening and there is no story as it's simple plot with actions.

7.title: It's Ethan Hunt against the whole world!!!
7.content:
MI franchise is back with the first instalment of it's seventh part Dead Reckoning. Hunt with his whole team as always won't dispoint you. Though this part is long but the drama & action will not let you feel that a bit. Let it be the car chasing scene in the streets of Rome or the mountain biking in the Alps, Tom cruise at 61 still gets us glued to the seat throughout the whole movie.

Hayley Atwell is a new addition to this franchise (no Jeremy Renner this time though), taking the baton from Rebecca Ferguson. Vanessa Kirby too finds a good amount of screen time in the later half. Benji aka Simon Pegg adds the humour part as always.

And the best part is that we'll have another one like this next year.

7.title: The 3rd best Mission Impossible movie
7.content:
I always liked the Mission Impossible movies, but it wasn't until my recent marathon of the series this year when I finally started to love them. Starting with Ghost Protocol, each Mission Impossible movie got better and better. I knew Dead Reckoning Part One would be good, but it still had a lot to live up to. While Fallout and Rogue Nation are still my favorite Mission Impossible movies, I'd say Dead Reckoning Part One is my third favorite installment.

Just as the previous installments, this movie has great action. Something I liked about the Rome sequence is that it wasn't just a standard car chase. Tom Cruise and Haley Atwell's characters being handcuffed to each other was an interesting obstacle, which made the Rome sequence feel more unique compared to other car chases. My favorite action scene in the movie is when Ethan Hunt and Grace are trying to escape the falling train cars. That entire sequence was nerve-racking.

For this movie's new additions to the series, I enjoyed Haley Atwell's character, Grace. I thought she had great chemistry with Tom Cruise and I'm looking forward to seeing her in Part Two. As much as I liked Grace, this leads me to my biggest issue with the movie: the way Ilsa Faust was handled.

Since Mission Impossible 7 focuses on Grace, Ilsa was sidelined for most of the movie. I was disappointed by her limited screen time because Ilsa Faust was my favorite female character in the Mission Impossible movies. I enjoyed her character in Rogue Nation and I was glad that Fallout carried her over. When I saw Ilsa and Ethan having a happy moment together in the trailer, I had a feeling that this movie would kill her off, which ended up happening. Because Ilsa was sidelined, her "death" wasn't as impactful. I put quotes around death because I feel like her character is coming back and no one's ever really gone nowadays.

Speaking of dead characters, I thought it was strange that Ethan's first lover, Marie, wasn't fleshed out in this movie, since Gabriel killing her was the reason why Ethan joined IMF. I'm hoping Part Two will have more flashbacks to develop Ethan's past with Marie.

When it comes to villains, this movie has three: Gabriel, Paris, and the Entity. Gabriel wasn't as memorable as Jon Voight, Phillip Symour Hoffman, or Henry Cavill's characters. To me, he was in the same category as Solomon Lane and the villain from Ghost Protocol, who are bland and forgettable antagonists. With Paris, I thought she was a cool secondary villain and it was neat seeing Pom Klementieff doing a villainous role. For the Entity, I thought it was a unique threat since the previous movies never dealt with artificial intelligence before. I'm actually more interested to see how Part Two will handle the Entity than Gabriel.

Overall, Dead Reckoning Part One is another good installment in the Mission Impossible franchise. Even though Part One wasn't as good as Fallout and Rogue Nation, I still have faith in Part Two and will be watching that movie opening weekend. I give Dead Reckoning Part One a 7/10.

7.title: Wasted a good opportunity to make something great!
7.content:
It is still a good movie. But it could have been great. The action is top notch. The acting is top notch. So are the supporting cast.

( The Phoeniase Freak, The net Ranger, the only man alive who hacked NATO Ghost Comm. Worthy inclusion of the past glory). Movie started well. Giving a glimpse of something great that might have followed. But by introducing a thief and spending so much time just behind that character, the plot lines get very confusing and cocktails. They should have followed a traditional way of making the "Mission Impossible" movies. By introducing the thief character, they forcefully killed one of the great character in Mission Impossible franchise. One can still enjoy MI DR for its great action, acting, screenplay, choreography.

7.title: A fun watch
7.content:
So far this is the best experience I have had in the cinema this year, but a few of the contenders that I assume it would be up against isn't showing in the region I am currently in.

The movie is a good addition to this genre, it had it suspenseful moments, thrilling car chases and other really amazing stunts that is worked in between the movie.

I mostly felt engaged with all the newer characters and it was good to see the recurring cast again.

Somethings in the plot just felt a little too convenient, but for most part it was easy enough for me to overlook this.

This is a part one, but it does feel like a complete movie - we just basically have an idea of what the mission for the next one will be by the end of this movie.

7.title: Dead Reckoning, meet Dead Horse
7.content:
Mid to low 7/10

I know MacGuffins are not new to the MI franchise, but I think they may have outdone themselves on that bit in MI Dead Reckoning (MI:DR). The physical dual keys to a physical lock on a sunken submarine housing the hard drive for a rogue AI are uninteresting, transparently trite, and prompt more questions than they're worth. They do look nice though, so credit to the prop design team. Also props to whoever Pom Klementieff's hair stylist is. Her hair was far and away the star of the show.

The dual keys are reflective of a larger issue with MI:DR, we're starting to noticeably replay the same beats with the same characters and very similar dialogue. The sort of quasi-suave dialogue that sounds fresh and cool only to someone who's never watched a spy flick before. "You mean to tell me" exposition, goobidy gock hacking jargon, other ham-fisted exposition, the all-knowing omniscient arrogant predicting-your-every move stuff right before your MacGuffin unexpectedly gets pickpocketed from your jacket, again. I mean there were good lines too. The bit where Hunt is bewildered by his team not telling him about the potential nuke was pretty funny. But in all, the script this time around just feels more tired than before. Adding on to that woe, this did not need to be a 3 hour affair. The fact that the plot needs to continue in a second installment fills me more with dread than it does excitement. For such an action-forward franchise, the pacing of this movie sure does feel slow.

At the end of the day, I'm not watching an MI movie this far in the saga for the nuanced characters or compelling storytelling. I suspect that like most, I'm in it largely to see Tom Cruise's latest brain-damaged stunts and his efforts to have Paramount finance his inevitable on-tape death from a stunt gone wrong. So my review more heavily weighs the action than it does the plot. And the stunts in this movie are: just ok? Idk, after scaling the Burj Khalifa, hanging onto the side of a plane taking off, the big hyped up parachute off a motorbike was just OK. I mean it was cool, but with all the sludge I had to sit through for 3 hours, it wasn't as sweet a reward as I would have hoped for. The other action in this movie is fine. Nothing special, but still relatively clean action choreography.

In all, MI:DR could stand to cut a lot of fat from its runtime. The action central to the franchise is fine, but not spectacular and the writing leaves a lot to be desired. Almost everyone on the cast is hot though, so there's a plus.

7.title: Spectacular action thriller
7.content:
These kind of action scenes in this Mission Impossible were crazy done. In fact nothing seems to be impossible to create these spectacular shots.

I liked a lot the filming locations in Venice and Rome with the car chase. It was a great experience to hear the Oscar worthy special sound effects. The running time is perhaps stretched out by some unnecessary dialogues for at least 15 minutes but didn't disturb at all the entertaining value. I think this movie is even better than the last Fallout.

Go watch it in the theatre cause it's more exciting than on stream or dvd.

All the actors did a good job and congratulations to Tom Cruise for his stunts and performance.

7/10.

7.title: Are You Ok
7.content:
For some reason, I just haven't gotten to writing this review for a month. I think it was just because I felt unsure about how I felt about the film. I had high expectations about the film because it was the only one that I had not seen before. I think it was an ok installment given the MI fatigue.

First, the overall premise was interesting. It's timely with all the AI-related topics we see in our daily lives. In MI series, I think the importance of having a formidable villian is very important. The Entity on paper is scary, but its intangibleness is certainly a minus. It's unique but I'm not sure if it serves its role well. There are other "antagonists" like Gabriel but he himself hasn't revealed too much of his strengths. The plot was a little confusing but it's all good. The movie showcased great environment, atmosphere and felt like it relied less on stunts but on more well-choreographed action scenes, such as the alleyway scene.

I found some of the writing a little silly. Why does Ethan care about choosing between Grace and Ilsa? I just thought Ilsa was the obvious choice as Grace is essentially a stranger. Character of Paris was pretty silly and added nothing to the movie. Ilsa's death was not memorable and feel like it added nothing to the overall movie as well.

However, the stunts and the overall train sequence (Act 3) was just built different. I think in that sense, the movie has served its purpose as an action movie well enough. I respect Tom for his continued dedication (watch the bts of the stunts) to the series and I will certainly watch #8.

7.title: Fantastic action, a few plot holes
7.content: One thing that's great about the ongoing series is that each movie has its own feel and tone - even with the same director as in the case of CM. The latest installment seems to harken back to the original movie with some longer scenes of small groups and dialogue. Yet that does not mean this movie did not deliver on insane action that keeps you very entertained. Obviously CM loves vertical dangling scenes - with the helicopter in Fallout and the train here. A few nits though: why does the visual list of Ethan's loves not include Julia? How is Gabrielle able to defeat so many dressed as a Banana Republic mannequin? Why were the Russians not frantically searching for the sub knowing what is on it? That aside you will definitely leave the theater thrilled that you came.

7.title: Mission pretty good: But not the best
7.content:
The good: The movie lives up to its hype and is an entertaining thrill ride with great set pieces, globe-trotting action and twists and turns galore. You know what this film is here to provide, so does Tom Cruise, and on that it delivers.

The bad: Specific sections let this film down, after an intriguing start, we get this hammy dialogue scene full of suits and characters that could be important but are never seen again. The film hasn't got the best pacing and is a tad too long. Also, whilst I applaud the film for trying to tackle the action in different ways (i.e. How many fight scenes can you see before it gets stale) thematic equivalents in other films (such as the bathroom fight scene in fallout) do it better. Finally, some of the characters are outright cartoony and others are given undeserved treatment. I'll say no more on this other than expressing disappointment in what could have been much more poignant delivery of a certain character's arc.

Should you watch it: It's a mission impossible movie. Tom Cruise once again puts his life on the line for our entertainment. And for that, it is absolutely worth the price of admission, should you choose to accept it.

7.title: All over the place...
7.content:
The bar was already set too high by the previous installment, but I really wasn't expecting so many MAJOR flaws...

Excessive use of deus-ex machina (even for a franchise like MI), very weird decision of character replacement (I guess because of some unknown behind the scenes issues, otherwise it doesn't make any sense to me) , weak/lazy hand to hand combat (worst than tv show combat at times), no new cool/memorable gadgets/tech, WAY too much importance and screen time for a new/underserving character.

I had a great time seeing this film in theater because of the sound effects, soundtrack and a couple of memorable action set pieces.

Hopefully the team making the next one / final one will learn from these mistakes (or maybe they just held their punches on this one to save something really amazing for later) and conclude the saga with the biggest bang yet.

7.title: Good Thrills
7.content:
This is the first Mission Impossible movie I've seen. Without too much SPOILERage, I'll give 3 things I liked, and 3 things I disliked.

***LIKED*** (1) It was a bit campy, which was good b/c some of the scenarios stretched believability. Like, the way Luther was hacking satellites on the fly to patch up communication gaps, etc.

(2) Obviously, the stunts were amazing. The motorcycle jump off a cliff; the train dangling off a bridge, etc. That latter scene lasted quite a while, too, it wasn't just a single close call.

(3) The acting of Pom Klementieff. I had no idea who she was before this movie, but now I will watch anything she's in.

***BAD*** (1) As with any pick-pocket/double cross movie, you never know for sure who's got the Mcguffin. That gets frustrating.

(2) The pacing is so "all-out" from start to finish, it's kind of exhausting. The only calm moment I can think of was when Tom Cruise and one of his accomplices are on the patio overlooking Venice and both mention how they have never been to the city before. Then your jammed right back into the action.

(3) It's just part 1.

7.title: Good Action packed Mission
7.content: Tom Cruise almost 3hrs on screen did a outstanding performance .The screenplay went as per script. The background score is an highlight for the movie .As this is part-1 the audience needs to wait for the upcoming Parts .The action scenes were awesome really the car scenes ,bike parachute stunt is an highlight of the entire movie . The cinematography was good and the direction there was a bit lag in some scenes. Dont expect this part to complete like other MI versions still to be continued....... This part the audience will enjoy but not much like other MI versions and this is the first time Tom Cruise has initiated the Mission in 2 parts .My rating 2.99/5 .The audience will definitely enjoy the movie.

7.title: Aims For Slapstick
7.content:
I think we're at a point now when he is asked the impossible, we just sort of know the mission isn't just impossible, it's improbable anyone would even be asked. And here is the silliness of it all.

Ethan is tasked, this time, to find a key, split two ways, that opens "something" The Bond like opening sequence "For Your Eyes Only") tells us what it is. It holds the security to a massive bomb that could kill everything in the world...um...stealthily. Also, it contains A. I. Which left to its own, is going to be VERY horrible with the things thinks Ethan is out to get it ( a la "L. A. Dead Reckonin' II: The Yee Haw Code"). In his way is someone from Ethan's past, Gabriel (Esai Morales). A man who had murdered someone he was close to, which set the path for Ethan to "choose the missions" By the way, can I vent here? I said in the last one about the mission choosing thing, and the people here who vote on responses dogged me over it. Guess what, ya jerks, it's the center of this movie and the next. It's all about choice (or focusing on whether or not we "choose to accept the mission"). Venting done.

So the key is pickpocketed and juggled around by a thief named Grace (Hayley Atwell) who was funded by a mysterious entity (hell, this is marked for spoiler, it's Vanessa Kirby). They are planning to see the key to this "Entity" to the highest bidder. This is where it gets REALLY confusing. You see everyone involved here has some stake in the key BUT also they have either some information or a piece of the key. It gets really confusing. Especially when you start to do callbacks from previous characters. I digress...

MIDRP1 is kinda fun. It just seems to meander until there is a something of an ending, then tells us it's the end of Part One. If you ever want to make a movie feel less of a movie, have it end with a narration similar to the Christopher Nolan Batman's. "There will be more...and they will be coming, and you better be ready" This is aggravating to listen to. And, frankly, is there really a part 2? The key is in Ethan's hands. The world is safe. So what?

There are a lot of moments made for humor in this. Driving through Rome had me smiling. As does some of the banter between Grace and Ethan. Sadly, I think this was to just give breathing room for them to get Elsa (Rebecca Ferguson) out of the picture. Though we spent a LOT of time with her, you can tell the distance they wanted to put between us and her. I didn't think it was that noble. At any rate, it does feel like a breezy 2 hours and 43 minutes. There's enough action to keep things moving. It feels really like the first M. I. movie. Very lowkey and low tech. In fact, it is the reason to go "analog" A pleasant afternoon waster with no heavy lifting.

7.title: A Fun Popcorn Movie
7.content: Dead Reckoning feels like the ultimate MI film, for both good and bad. The good are the franchise hallmarks of thrilling set-piece practical effects and stunt work; a strong and capable main character (in contrast to the likes of Thor, Luke Skywalker, Han Solo and Indiana Jones, Ethan Hunt isn't constantly getting belittled and upstaged); charismatic supporting characters; and straightforward morality (these movies often present the morally-correct choice as the most difficult, but there's rarely nihilistic moral relativism.) The bad is predictable plotting; occasionally hammy dialogue; and repetition of the same scenario (Dead Reckoning acknowledges as much in a line from Shea Whigham.) Overall this exactly what one wants and expects from a summer action blockbuster in general and this franchise in particular. It doesn't transcend conventions, it's just a fun and enjoyable popcorn movie.

7.title: capturing movie
7.content: Ultimately this series has never been as overly successful in setting a consistent narrative arc. The about whether Tom Cruise is a very good actor or simply a movie star can be solved with the first solution by showing his dedication to an ever-increasing range of extreme stunts. He's surely one of the talents giving how he's building his characters. At its core, the Mission Impossible franchise is an office drama about a guy trying to balance the weight of his life and the ones of the strangers having to do with him. Overall it works and the other charachters as well deliver good performances.

7.title: Tom Cruise runs successfully through the part one of the seventh film in the franchise.
7.content:
This time again, it is personal and the rival, not just from the past but the one he has teamed up with is simply too powerful. Ethan Hunt's new mission is gonna cost him someone dearly and he obviously chose to accept the mission. With an all knowing entity up for a grab, many wants to control it to own the power it gives while only one wants to kill it. How Ethan and his team try to beat the unbeatable is what the first part of Dead Reckoning is about. This time there is a gorgeous thief for Ethan to run with.

The main negative is that the screenplay is slower and I wished for it to pick up the speed to match Tom Cruise's running speed a few times. Barring that, the drama does work as intended as the film resorts to a grim tone right from the beginning. It's not all non-stop action as this Ethan Hunt knows the price he has to pay. Considering this part is to build up for the next film, the runtime feels a bit longer strictly owing to the pace.

But the drama is well complimented by the stunts. Though the bike stunt was the most hyped, it was the train scene in the end that worked for me. The humor in the chase scene is thankfully not dragged for long and it ends up being adequate. It is the characters that leave a mark otherwise an AI going rogue isn't really a catchy subject. The mystery behind the AI and it's first attack is kept intact to be unraveled in the next part. All in all, Dead Reckoning Part One does deliver.

7.title: Good enough.
7.content:
Just back from the theater with mixed feelings.

It's pretty to look at and, because of some stunts and a few clever lines, a decent summer escape. But the plot and a number of the action scenes are things you've encountered a million times before....endless motorcycle chase through a big city anyone?...and they have often been done better by Bond, Wick and even Dominick Torreto.

There really is little chemistry between Tom and his leading ladies and, frankly, it's all (with a couple of exceptions) a little derivative and long in the tooth.

My friendly advice is to lower your expectations, buy the big popcorn (2:43 run time!), and find a big screen to watch it on. You've seen worse.

7.title: A solid action flick, but weirdly less sure-footed and impressive than some predecessors
7.content:
In recent years I've rather tired of the action blockbuster, and this is a series that I've missed much of in the first place, ever since the first sequel. Given the chance to watch all of Tom Cruise's 'Mission: Impossible' films, though, my curiosity got the best of me, and I'm happy to say it was rewarded much more than not: all of them have been pretty enjoyable, in one measure or another. There's inconsistency from one title to the next, and there are reasonable criticisms to level with even the best of them, but for anyone receptive to what the genre portends, there's not really any going wrong here. All the same, it's fair to wonder how Cruise and returning filmmaker Christopher McQuarrie could follow up 2018's 'Fallout,' which while still not my personal favorite (that would be 2006's MI3) was surely the most polished, focused, and balanced up to this point. Not least recognizing that the big stunts and action sequences only grew from one sequel to the next, how does 'Dead reckoning' stack up compared to its forebears? To be honest, I find myself surprised. I do like this seventh feature, and it more or less fits in with its kin, but in my opinion it's an awkward step backward from its immediate predecessor.

For as much as 'Fallout' was ever so carefully crafted in every capacity, its writing not least, I don't think the same supreme judiciousness was fully applied in this case. Don't get me wrong, in terms of production values this reflects the very best of modern cinema, and every single person in front of the camera and behind the scenes turned in impeccable work. From a fundamental standpoint of the visual experience the picture is so vibrant that it's genuinely pleasing, and much the same goes for the sound design. I love Lorne Balfe's dynamic score even as - contrary to a few years before - it borrows more from Lalo Schifrin's original theme, and the other music selectively used throughout is a blast. The stunts, practical effects, fight scenes, and otherwise action sequences, the keystones of these films since the beginning and only ever more so over time, are utterly outstanding. The computer generated imagery that's used to round out particular sequences looks as good as it could (though as ever, the more we see of it, the worse it looks). All this is swell. It's McQuarrie and Erik Jendresen's screenplay that leaves me a bit unimpressed, raising a quizzical eyebrow, and some other facets are impacted in turn.

From the outset the premise, involving super-smart artificial intelligence, brings to mind numerous abject sci-fi flicks of the past, from 'The terminator' and 'Demon seed' to B-movies of the 50s. After 'Fallout' so thoroughly cleansed itself of such trappings aside from a few props, it seems strange for 'Dead reckoning' to fully embrace them. Granted, it's not as if Ethan Hunt is facing off against cyborgs, and there are certainly human elements opposing our protagonist, but it's a sharp turn for the series. And it's definitely not just about the hi-tech gadgetry. I do have to ask: is it just me? Is watching the series back to back to back putting the whole at a disadvantage as they all start to blend together after a time? There are many points at which the writing is decidedly heavy-handed, practically brow-beating us with the dialogue and scene writing. As a prime example, look to one of the earliest scenes, where McQuarrie and Jendresen unflinchingly speak to the calamitous precipice over which our world hangs in real life, speak to the foolhardy arrogance and ignorance with which techbros toy with the digital landscape, describe Ethan Hunt as if he were a comic book superhero, and lay out exposition with all the elegance of a hippopotamus in heels. There are the flashbacks, not fully fleshed out, and the attempts to less convincingly address thoughtful questions as MI6 had. Then there are the instances that exceed the substantial playfulness of other past installments to embrace outright comedy - watch for the action sequence just after the one-hour mark, or a late shot of an actor having their "William Shatner screaming 'Khan!'" moment - or that are very nearly so; parts of the last big action sequence are a heartbeat away from being a bit for Keaton or Chaplin. Elsewhere the writing is weirdly self-parodying, as if 'Dead reckoning' were a deadpan send-up a la John Carpenter's 'Ghosts of Mars.' With this latter quality in mind, some odds and ends don't come off so well: some overzealous cinematography or editing, a cartoonish look a character wears for one sequence, some otherwise artistic shot composition, how the female characters are written, and more. McQuarrie very clearly made his best effort as a writer for the 2018 antecedent to be its best self; what happened here?

Please understand, I do enjoy this movie. So much about it looks and sounds superb. The cast is splendid, and I believe in this case the women, all given only supporting parts, rather outshine their male co-stars. I look forward to seeing more from Hayley Atwell, who easily holds her own as the most important second fiddle; Rebecca Ferguson needs no introduction, nor Vanessa Kirby, and Kirby in particular is allowed to demonstrate more of her skills this time around. Pom Klementieff, to my delight, might be one of the top highlights here, as she is obviously living her best life in portraying cold, vicious Paris. While the writing, and in turn McQuarrie's direction and oversight of the whole, lends to some tidbits that I find questionable, the contributions in and of themselves are unassailable. Why, though the details are less sure-footed and open to dissection, the foundations in the story and screenplay are solid. I'll even go so far as to say that I - someone who scoffs judgmentally at how so many blockbusters of recent years feel the need to be nearly, exactly, or more than three hours long - think that at its core the narrative is penned so well that these 163 minutes pass quite quickly and smoothly, and meaningfully necessitate another full-length feature to finish the plot. I might even hope that once the eighth 'Mission: Impossible' is released, it will complement the seventh so well that the criticisms I have now may be somewhat tempered.

It's just that for a series that seemed to find its true voice five years prior, 'Dead reckoning' - for all its splendor as a production - feels like a throwback to a time when each subsequent installment was trying something a little different, some with more success than others. The overall vibe I have with this comes closest to matching those I have with the 1996 progenitor and 2011's 'Ghost Protocol': solidly made, and overall enjoyable, but imperfect, not as outwardly grabbing, troubled by issues with the writing, and less certain to demand viewership once, or to inspire a second viewing. I'm glad for those who get more out of this picture than I do; we all have our personal preferences. For my money, excellent as it may be in many ways, in some critical ones the latest 'Mission: Impossible' comes up short and a smidgen unimpressive. Check it out, by all means; if it's an action flick you want, it's an action flick you'll get. 'Dead reckoning' just doesn't have its feet planted as firmly as some of its brethren, and to me, therein lies the problem.

7.title: Hunt: "Your life will always matter more to me than my own." Grace: (pause) "You don't even know me." Hunt: "What difference does that make?"
7.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One (2023) is the 7th instalment in the Mission: Impossible franchise and the first of a two-part story where Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his IMF team get involved in a chaotic race around the globe to get their hands on two halves of a key which gives full access to an incredibly powerful, sentient AI known as 'The Entity' which, if in the wrong hands, could spell disaster for the planet as we know it...

I'm not gonna lie, Act 1 and Act 2 felt pretty basic, in the sense that I feel like I've seen plenty of action movies with scenes like that. The small twists and whatnot, whilst they are definitely exciting, are all too common in these kind of movies. The first two hours of the film really did not stand out as a result. Which I really dont want to be saying considering the MI franchise is one of my favourites, plus Tom Cruise is literally my favourite actor, so I was very pumped up going into this, so that might be why I'm a bit disappointed. Additionally, when comparing this to the previous 3 Mission Impossibles (which I probably shouldn't be doing but still), they were all better than this one. What I loved about those movies was that I genuinely felt an impending sense of doom that had me on the edge of my seat every time. But not with this one, and I think that's mainly because of the fairly dull plot. I understand the modern approach of using AI as the enemy, but let's be real, nobody cares about AI at all. The threats in all the other MIs were tangible, or at least palpable. But here I didn't feel the sense of imminent danger which I so desperately wanted from this picture. Maybe it's just more of a me problem though.

But I don't like talking about negatives, let's look at the good bits shall we? Whilst Act 1 and 2 were somewhat underwhelming for me, Act 3 was pretty special. I was so stoked to see the cliff jump having seen it in the trailers, but seeing it in the theater, and seeing it all play out exceeded my expectations. It is simply yet another reminder of just how cool and bold Mr Cruise truly is. And he actually had lines to speak whilst he was diving down?? Incredible. And the train sequence, wow. Some of the twists here were actually unique, and it was this whole act that made this feature that little more... spectacular. Everything from Grace's act as The White Widow (Vanessa Kirby) to the fighting scene on top of the train was brilliant.

Also, I absolutely adore the two scenes where Ethan shows his true, immense care for Grace (Hayley Atwell) above himself, and the way she manifests her genuine surprise at this through her emotion (as you can see her tear up a bit as she realises that someone out there sincerely does care about her, even though that someone barely knows her) almost made me tear up myself.

The cast were great, as per usual with this franchise, but oh my word, Ilsa's death took me completely by shock. Fair play McQuarrie, you actually didn't stick to the "main characters always stay alive no matter what happens to them" cliché. This also elevated this film from a 6 to a 7 for me.

And by the way the Dutch angles in this were used unbelievably well, I just had to mention.

So overall, I will be truthful and say that not a whole lot about this movie really stood out for me. Not just compared to the previous Mission: Impossible movies, but to action movies in general. But whilst it isn't as astounding as some of the other MI movies, it certainly isn't the worst. Here's to hoping that Dead Reckoning Part Two blows Part One out of the water, as the last thing I would want is for this franchise to gradually wane and die out, especially after some of the absolute gems we've been gifted over the past years.

7.title: Nothing new here....
7.content:
It was exactly what you'd expect from the MI franchise, loads of action, great dialogue, fast paced, lots of fighting but unfortunately nothing new which was a complete disappointment. The movie was just too predictable and there were so many unexplainable moments but you just play along because it's Tom Cruise.

My favorite character was Ving Rhames. I just loved how he spoke with that calmness and that wise big brother vibe. It was really nice seeing him get a lot more role and dialogue. Am not sure if he had as much screen time in previous MI movies. But it was cool watching him. I also kinda enjoyed watching Pom play other role aside playing Mantis in Guardian of the Galaxy.

It wasn't a bad movie but if you've seen previous MI movies, you've seen it all. The only change here is the storyline, the scenes are just borrowed from previous movies.

7.title: Visually stunning, exhilarating on most parts but still not as thrilling as most of the previous MI films
7.content:
The previous film Fallout is near perfect for me and I guess it would be really hard to top that one. Dead Reckoning Part One, overall, is not as thrilling as I hoped it would be and some scenes don't feel well-written or something. There's also too much talking, most of the time I had no idea what they were talking about but I still got the gist. Also I don't like what they did to Ilsa too.

On positive notes, Tom Cruise delivers, as always. New cast members are great as well, especially Pom Klementieff who played Paris. This film is visually breathtaking with still plenty of exhilarating scenes, but not just as thrilling as the action scenes in the previous films. The train scenes, particularly, are my favorites, as well as the motor jump on the cliff...WOW. Some of the talking scenes can be a bit confusing as well and how they explain that AI thingy is a bit too complicated, but you'll get the gist anyway so it doesn't really matter much.

I am excited for part two.

7.title: Not as bad as Mission Impossible 2 but almost
7.content: Since we know there is a second part, what I say is not a spoiler. Namely, I hope the second part is better than this...but I am not counting on it. This has a similar "flavor" as the second one. The action is comparable in concept though the quality is better. (After 20+ years, I would expect that.) And the antagonist of this pushes credulity, in my opinion. Even the dilemmas of the good guys seem artificially inserted. The character development is like a stage of characters sitting in a couple of scenes. And I have to say the acting from Cruise is not really well acted. At one time I turned off the sound to turn off the dramatic mood music. I did have on the captions, in case there actually *would* be dialogue. I won't add more since it would include minor spoilers. My summary is, watch it to get through it and hope the sequel is better.

7.title: Can't believe I'm gonna say this.
7.content: Mission Impossible 7 was a particular movie of interest to movie as I'm a huge fan of the franchise, still am. And I liked this movie. But not so much as the recent few ones. As another 4-star reviewer mentioned, the most interesting and engaging scene came out after 2 and a half hours which is the meticulously planned out train surviving. It was solid, unique and one of the best action scenes I've seen recently. Tom Cruise's stunt (the biggest stunt in cinema) was awesome. (Not sure about one comment where it said "it was so short", well what do you expect? A guy to keep falling in real-time without CGI for 2-straight minutes or something from the top of a mountain that ain't even that enormously high? Parts I hate the most was Ilsa's character assassination and I'm not talking literally. Her character was painfully minimized. Hayley, I love her but also, Ethan quickly caring about her was so out-of-place like it hasn't even been half a day since they met but he cares about her as he does the other team members? What? I think Christopher MaQuarrie fell a step down on the writing part but I love his works and he's a good filmaker. Ethan's and Grace's plot armour was ridiculous but I don't care. I like em. 7.title: Longer, sillier, and still worth an IMAX trip
7.content: This movie was over-long and over-silly (even for a blockbuster franchise known for both), but it was still worth the price of admission. The story took a while to get cooking, but the action set pieces were fantastic, as always, and the callbacks to earlier movies offered a sense of finality to this last chapter. I could have done with less talking and wasn't sure we needed new faces at this point in the franchise, even if the charm and hijinks that resulted were delightful...but the last 45 minutes cooked just like last time around. This wasn't as good as Mission Impossible Fallout, but that is a high bar for any action movie.

7.title: Good Movie
7.content:
"Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1" delivers another action-packed adventure featuring the indomitable Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his team of skilled operatives. Directed by Christopher McQuarrie, this installment retains the franchise's hallmark high-octane stunts and intricate espionage plots.

As expected from a Mission: Impossible film, the action scenes are spectacular. Tom Cruise once again performs his own stunts, providing thrilling moments that keep audiences on the edge of their seats. From high-speed chases to daring jumps, the action is relentless and expertly choreographed.

The ensemble cast, including familiar faces like Simon Pegg, Ving Rhames, and Rebecca Ferguson, delivers solid performances. Their chemistry and camaraderie add depth to the characters and provide some lighter, humorous moments amidst the tension.

The storyline is complex, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers guessing. The plot weaves together elements of global conspiracy and personal stakes for the characters, creating a sense of urgency and high stakes.

At times, the film struggles with pacing, particularly in the middle section where the narrative can feel bogged down by exposition and setup for the next installment. This occasionally disrupts the momentum built by the action scenes.

While the intricate plot is engaging, it can also be confusing, with multiple threads and characters to keep track of. Some viewers might find it challenging to follow all the nuances and connections without getting lost.

Despite the film's many strengths, it doesn't stray far from the established Mission: Impossible formula. While fans of the series will appreciate the consistency, others might crave more innovation and freshness in the storytelling.

"Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1" is a solid addition to the franchise, offering breathtaking action and strong performances from its cast. While it suffers from some pacing issues and a plot that can be hard to follow, it remains an entertaining watch for fans of the series. It sets up an intriguing foundation for Part 2, promising even more thrills to come.

7.title: Meh.
7.content:
Oh, to be an unwillingly contrarian fish, reluctantly swimming against the tide of general critical acclaim & mass popularity amongst cinema-going audiences who (for the most part) bewilderingly seem to be in unison with their cumulative love for this film... But (ever the one to keep things tediously original - apologies in advance) I didn't like "Dead Reckoning: Part 1", if I'm honest. Feels somewhat sacrilegious to admit publicly (& even whilst typing these words, I have an overwhelming urge to apologise sincerely to the devout film fans who'll immediately be stripping me of my metaphorical badge & membership card to this esteemed club, armed with fiery torches & bloodied pitchforks - in punishment for this unforgivably heinous blasphemy), yet I'd be kidding myself (& others) if I argued anything other... Because it felt so painfully dissatisfying for me to sit through.

Why?

As far as I can tell, Christopher McQuarrie clearly had a thoroughly engaging tale to tell for the "Mission Impossible" franchise (one I seriously enjoyed from beginning to end) & manifestly, it began with "Rogue Nation" (his debut), then ended with "Fallout" (arguably one of the greatest action blockbusters in the history of Hollywood - masterfully building upon the themes of its predecessor whilst evolving the visual language of the feature to elevate the storytelling to new heights which were both groundbreaking & previously unparalleled - in a direct sequel, expanding the complexity of the ensemble & granting the characters closure, feeling necessary as an organic continuation, offering completion to a narrative we never knew was incomplete until we'd seen it; a gift, in summary).

This, however (compared to that), feels like an attempt to add more on for the sheer sake of adding more on, not because it's truly required but because the production studio cynically wished to capitalize off of Tom Cruise's increasingly profitable brand (he's one of the last remaining mega stars, capable of drawing in viewers to theatres, hot off the billion+ dollar hit "Top Gun: Maverick" - thus, who can blame them? It's not surprising to assume Paramount would want another piece of that lucrative pie) & therefore, the differentiation in motivation - for the cultivation of "Part 1" - shows in the final product we see before us.

Financial intent, basically, devoid of the sincere artistry I appreciated in the past.

Plus, since the latest installment in this spy-genre is tasked with establishing the basis on which a subsequent movie shall bravely endeavour to build upon (in the future, depending on present strikes etc.), it lacks the same momentum as its forebear ("Fallout" wasn't held back by world building & provided a satisfying resolution to the earlier problem presented - spanning multiple projects - & wisely, the writer's keen to not diminish the emotional stakes of prior outings. Ergo, rather than fleshing out what came before any further, he seeks to start again - from scratch); a wise creative decision I comprehend (why ruin pre-existing content - when it's perfect as it is - for brazen capitalism? If one's to make a forced expansion, theoretically, separating events very distinctly ensures no damage done reverberates back down the timeline - akin to removing an infected ligament before the rot can fester up a limb - retaining the quality of healthy elements), but in doing so, bogs 2023's action epic down in endless exposition & obligatory introductions (obviously, a timely process at any start), conflicting with the snappy pace the creators are attempting to preserve (when such essentials weren't as indispensable as they are here). Resultantly, there's a jarring disconnect between what the story wants to be (in theory) & what it actually is (in practice).

That's one reason I'd give as to why I'd say it doesn't work.

Another? The narrative doesn't progress naturally & a lot of it plays out like a derivative rehash of previous plot beats we've witnessed on numerous occasions. Consequently, the repetitious nature the script possesses comes across as if the producers are unadventurously playing a rendition of the lead actor's greatest hits (just bigger, on a far larger scale) - with no ambition to make any worthwhile, beneficial amendments, nor saying something we haven't already heard before.

For instance, Ilsa Faust? How the mighty have fallen; a fascinatingly complex supporting figure & justifiable fan favourite returns (she's included in trailers - that's not a spoiler), although those at the helm clearly had absolutely no idea what to do with her this time. In spite of that, Rebecca Ferguson made it explicitly clear in interviews (before principal photography began) she personally wished to come back (an actor seeking employment - groundbreaking) & viewers also supported her calls, wanting her to be included... So she was (once more) - not with any discernible purpose (predictably doing what she normally does throughout sequences), but for the sake of it. Hence, her two dimensional characterisation is a shallow caricature of her younger self & I became frustrated, realising how she'd been unimaginatively utilised because she deserves better.

An eye-wateringly high budget take on Sherlock S4's divisive finale "The Final Problem" (crossed with Gore Verbinski's "The Lone Ranger") is the most apt description I can concisely hope to offer (a TV series ironically renowned for outstaying its welcome in the closing chapter) flinging ingredients we've been known to like the taste of in one giant, corporate soup (mashing people together - with no consideration as to whether they truly fit cohesively - as if they're a child's toy figurines); hubristic, self indulgent & barely legible, it's so convoluted, subverting developments for the sake of shock value - an irritatingly cheap trick for something so expensive - 3 long, consecutive hours of endless, predictable, monotonously foreseeable twists for the literal sake of having TWISTS & impressive set pieces (thrust in to our faces) designed to compensate for the deprivation of substance. All style.

7.title: No more intricate plot, the amazing high-tech gadgets but with magic tricks
7.content: The movie delivers some thrilling action scenes, but it falls short of the MI series standards. It lacks the intricate plot, the amazing high-tech gadgets, and the clever twists that the fans expect. The only thing that remains is the spectacle of the stunts. Let me explain why I was disappointed by this movie. First, the action scenes were not as impressive as they could have been. I admire the cliff jumping and the locomotive crash to be real shots. But they were ruined by some poor editing choices. For example, the cliff jump scene had a faded silence followed by a loud sound effect, which startled me instead of awing me. This is not a horror movie. The train crash scene had some fake-looking water splashes that contrasted with the realism of the shot. Second, there is no more impressed high-techs that made the previous movies so fun. The "Entity" is the only advanced technology, but it feels like a copy of Skynet or Genisys from Terminator. Plus, the mask maker fails again, but with no reason (The Entity took control of it?). Third, too many fighting actions and magic tricks. I listed this in the third place because this is more of my personal interest, maybe you like it. I prefer more spy action and less martial arts in a MI movie. I feel like there is too much fighting scenes, and are always using cold weapons, sword, knives, or even tubes. And way more magics. Hunt and Grace are all playing magics. We never know if they took the keys. Magic can be entertaining in real life, but not in a movie. It only creates mild surprise and confusion. As for the story, the opening scene was impressive, but the rest was average and full of holes. I have only watched it once, so I might have missed some clues. A lot of the scene transitions are a bit stiff and don't seem to give a reason why things are happening there.
