7.title: A great film, But with no real depth!
7.content:
I stand by what I said, this is still a great film. And ofcourse the beloved Tom Cruise knows how to make an action movie. The different settings throughout the film were really interesting, and developed the story. The film was a 2hr and 43 Minute Movie, and some scenes did drag along, but overall this film was a great watch.

These negatives are really only minor,

The first point I'd like to make more though, but if you don't care for that then just scroll down by (3), I've seen bits of the 3rd film, so I can't judge how the movie works within the context of the siries, or for the characters, so I do apologise for any inconvenience. However, the movie did seem to just give us great spectacle. And the Characters didn't get much development, and the newly introduced Hayley Atwells Character gets the spotlight. Which will annoy hard-core fans of the siries who just want to see there main characters get the spotlight and be more interwined within the story, others like me who's only a recent viewer can be seeing these characters for the first time, and at first glance. And won't really mind. But the Development is lackluster to say the least, and specially the train sequence dragged on. Some of the same scenes happened again and again! In the train sequence. And I got the point the second time, the fifth time it just got annoying. Which leads me to my next point. The Action-Sequences.

Action,

Extremely good music for the tense and atmospheric action-Sequences. My personal favourite is the car chase scene. Brilliantly well-crafted, and had me on the edge of my seat. The scene also adds some humour to the mix, which is great too, whilst the action is going along, faster then you can say STOP! It was really fast. The first set-piece Is great too, as it's well integrated within the story and the plot. With this Key, this scene is incredibly atmospheric. And in one way strange and bizarre, because we as an audience can see the crewmembers getting scared. And for a good reason, there about to crash into another moving object, bur when they do hit it, it fades away. So as an audience we are shocked, atleast for me I was. And then the scene happens again. And third time lucky, oh no wait they actually do crash into it this time. Which it holds one piece of this Key. Which is important to the story, but not important right now. Then the second action-Sequence is at the airport. Where men are chasing Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) character, and we here that there's a bomb. He doesn't here till late actually, but no don't worry because we are. And we're also introduced to Hayley Atwell (Grace) into the story. Who seemingly has the second part of the Key. She gets used, not literally. To hide Ethan out of sight, otherwise the gang members will find him. There's also many people inside this movie, who get severly beaten up and die. With incredibly quick reflexes from Ethan, he can think of an ideal way to get out of a difficult situations. When his loved one dies, I Don't feel the impact. As he's only showing his despair for a moment or two, and then it cuts to the next scene. Where he has no real emotion, and this character never gets brought up in the story again, feel like it's a bit of a disservice to Furgusons character. Maybe the second part will give us a bit more, but I Was hoping for a bit more in this one. The action-Sequences are unique, and very intense.

The Story/Plot,

It's about the key, thanks for stopping by and reading this part.

The Villains,

For the most part hammy and cheesy looks on both there faces, does have a threatening presence. His voice is silent, but deadly. And his presence is certainly known. He's the only one that knows where the Key is, the second part. And Knows what it will do, and ultimately that means it can do the things that he knows. But Ethan and his team, and Grace have to stop this from happening. Although he figures out a clever way to get of the train, the team are stuck. Grace and Ethan, have to solve the issues occurring.

The performances are incredible throughout the story. Simon Pegg is brilliantly and effortlessly charismatic in literally everything he's in. Tom Cruise is the stuntman expert, and is incredible at knowing how to make action movies. And Hayley Atwell has great chemistry with Tom Cruise. And got great chemistry with Chris Evans. She just knows how to interact with people.

And the end scene shocked me. A great film, and I certainly would recommend it, to any viewers.

Verdict,

I Enjoyed it, just slightly holds back with a few minor nit picks. Best Action-Sequences inside any movie I've seen though.

7.title: This is why we go to the movies. 😎
7.content:
Tom Cruise did it again! The last action movie star that just keeps getting better and better at what he does. His performance is golden as he makes sure that everything that appears on the big screen follows exactly like he wanted to. He provides constant thrills to the audience, serving us with death-defying acts that no other actor is as par as him, not even Hemsworth for Extraction or Keanu Reeves for John Wick. He is the man, the legend. ✨

Were all the practical stunts top-notched? Yes. Holistically, could the stunts top the previous installments? No. We believe that MI4: Ghost Protocol & MI6: Fallout are the benchmarks and these two still have the best amongst the best stunts we've seen in the age of filmmaking. Now, don't get us wrong, Dead Reckoning Part 1 still has those breathtaking, edge-of-your-seat stunts, putting it at number 3 of the MI list, with our favourite being the train-wrecking scene. These stunts are still gorgeously made and meticulously planned that will keep your heart beating fast.

The film does its job for having the narrative as realistic and grounded as possible including the practical stunts. But the rawness and grittiness are watered down by the overuse of music every single time action scenes pop up for us to experience. If we could recall, there wasn't ANY action scene without the background music. We were looking forward to this. Imagine a fighting scene, hearing only the banging, crashing, creaking, breaking, thudding and thumping, it could have been wicked. That's what made Fallout so good; an instance, the bathroom scene with Tom Cruise and Henry Cavill, ❌ music, just man-to-man fighting in all its rawness.

Bringing AI as the focal point, the storyline here is something that the franchise has never done before. It might have been for other movies, but the story here is well told as elements of past, present and future are the essentials for it to progress forward. Not only that but the higher stakes and the ubiquitous villain will get you to think, 'how can they defeat this?', making it unpredictable.

With 2 hours 40 minutes, Dead Reckoning Part 1 feels overly long as the FIRST HOUR is pretty much a slow-burner for a commercially made film. It takes its time to hit the engine running. While it's important for them to set up the world-threatening stakes and establish a grounded plot which they did, we feel that the way it could have been told can be more engaging and attracting every target audience like what Ghost Protocol and Fallout did. It's a slow burn, with minimal jaw-dropping stunts and incessant expository dialogues. Those expecting they're gonna get the same with 4 & 6, they're gonna be disappointed. Nevetheless, don't worry, the final 30 minutes is worth the ticket price, it's everything you're hoping for in a Tom Cruise action film.

There is one major problem that we're truly let down by. With the first act maximizing on expository dialogues, it has potential for this film to be rich with contexts and little details that can make the film much more interesting throughout. But the whole story is driven by Grace, played by Hayley Atwell. Her character, led by her actions and decisions is the steering wheel that pretty much sums up the reason why the film is soooo long. Her character feels unwelcomed and incongruous, like she doesn't belong here for the movie. She takes everything lightly and repeatedly messes things up, putting everyone and everything at risks. If only she could get herself together, the film wouldn't have been a drag.

However, we can't say that we didn't like her chemistry with Tom Cruise. There's a certain affection and admiration on the existence of their relationship that we felt we wanted more. We're fond of seeing them together, it sparks a good chemistry, establishing their character arcs and maturity, as if their get-together scenes are like the cherry on top to an already great action movie.

Normally when 'Part 1' is attached with any title of any movie, they would have an abrupt cliffhanger; this year alone, we have 5 movies, with a 'Part 1 or 2' title; Fast X, Across the Spider-Verse, The 3 Musketeers D'Artagnan, Buya Hamka and this film. But what made Dead Reckoning different from the others is its cliffhanger that is well-made and polished. It ends fittingly where it's supposed to be instead of just leaving the audience hanging while the ongoing narrative is left unfinished. This film should be the exemplar for any 'Part 1' movies, ending it at the right place, slowing down the film's momentum while also keeps the audience eager for the next one.

Verdict: A thrilling cinematic experience, Dead Reckoning Part One reminds us why we go to the cinema. It is a rip-roaring adventure filled with breathtaking action set pieces, pulled off by the last action movie star, Tom Cruise. Nevertheless, it misses the opportunity to reach the helicopter-level heights set by Ghost Protocol and Fallout due to its incessant expository dialogue, one important but incongruous character and overused background music. But should you still choose to accept this mission? YES.

7.title: It's All About the Final 45 Minutes
7.content:
'Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning, Part 1' is not the best in the series. But the film's final forty-five minutes may well be the best action / thriller set-piece ever filmed; in any film, ever.

We've got a runaway train, a parachute-descending Tom Cruise, a heroine in peril, US Government Officials in peril, villains turning heroic, hand-to hand combat a top that train, a railroad bridge about to blow ... and no, this is not the cliff-hanger that ends Part One. If I were going to tell someone who hates action-thrillers why they should make an exception and see this film, I'd say, 'The Final 45'. And after seeing it, they'd thank me.

So then, why only '7' stars? Why not '10'?

1. The film is long, and in my opinion, too long. And in order to fill the two hours and a half we've got action sequences that simply go on forever; the car chase in Rome is simply interminable, and frankly, wholly unrealistic. I ultimately felt numb to its excesses.

2. A scene that takes place at a party in Venice is totally without tension. The dialogue here is solely expository, the Cruise character seems weak (or weaker than we've seen him), and the action sequences take place in a too-dark world and, as such, are hard to follow. And the ease with which Cruise's Ethan Hunt is located on the Grand Canal is simply preposterous.

3. There's a lot of inter-gender fighting here. Now the female fighters truly do hold their own, but I couldn't help thinking that the film is pandering to prospective female members of the audience.

4. On this 'female' subject, there are four major female characters in the film. Are they each essential? Or could their qualities be compressed into ... fewer? I do believe so.

5. The story? It involves the quest for a key that can save humanity. Early on there's a lot of discussion of 'real' versus 'fake' keys. But this turned out to be a 'red herring'; if the possibility is mentioned again, I missed it. Moreover the key is located pretty much with little effort. So little effort, I found I was wondering whether the real versus fake plot-line might raise its head. But it didn't. So far.

6. The Train. It's got a steam locomotive. The film, set in the current day, is all about technology: Artificial Intelligence and Beyond. So, steam locomotive? Now possibly there is one running in Central Europe. Perhaps it's supposed to be The Orient Express (I have no idea what sort of locomotive it actually uses). But I was unprepared for the steam, the engineer stoking the fire, the ancient controls. Steam locomotive?

As for Tom Cruise. He's fine. Like always. Has he aged? Does it show? Yes, he's aged. It shows in a face slightly jowly. But frankly that sort of works to his advantage. I found myself marveling at him and his character's continued ability to do what they do.

Hayley Atwell makes a great heroine in peril; she's good looking but also smart, sassy, and - it turns out - quite the fighter. Simon Pegg as sidekick #1 spends a lot of this film shouting; at Cruise. Got to say I found it annoying. But Ving Rhaymes as sidekick #2 does a great job of helping to ground the film in something approaching reality. His lecturing Cruise's Ethan Hunt is a great piece of acting.

Finally, the film has a definite sense of conclusion to it. I felt satisfied by its ending (though it's not the end at all), and looking forward to its Part Two.

And that's a hard trick to pull off.

7.title: An honest opinion, I've watched more than 2000 movies(so I guess I am qualified for some attention).
7.content:
The female characters are overrated by some, I didn't see anything special in their performances. I didn't mean they were not good. It sure as hell was not the peak mission impossible movie. I have seen many movies with the concept of Al, in Mission Impossible it was pretty much same as others, so there was no extraordinary story or something, but the action was good and the only complaint about action was there was very less gun fight or fighting with weapons other than knife and unarmed. Some fights of the character 'Grace' was just not a good choice since she isn't a trained or professional personnel, she was just an expert thief.

There were many scenes that were just epic like the jumping from mountain, running in airport, explosion of bridge and the opening desert scene. Overall this was a very good movie.

7.title: Upping the action and stunts does not make a great movie
7.content:
Tom cruise has been knocking out mission impossible movies for 25 years. 7 so far with a final 8th installment to come. And fair play Tom Cruise he is the last real movie star. But like most modern franchises particularly the fast and furious films the bond movies John wick films each instalment concentrates on upping the stunts and action till it turns into a unbelievable video game plot.

I personally think the best action set piece in the entire mission impossible franchise was Tom dangling from wires where his sweat would set off alarms in the very first movie not only was this beleaveable it was possible and intense. Fast forward 25 years and he's jumping off a cliff on a motorbike parachuting onto a moving train crashing into it and saving the damsel about to be shot to the train crashing off a cliff, and no spoilers here it's in the trailer and the money shot. But Tom's in his late 50s when this was actually filmed this, Tom easily deserves his pay day just for this stunt. Yes he did it most of it for real and it's filmed gloriously but it sums up this movie, style over substance epic action set pieces after the other but ignoring how to make a real gritty spy thriller to something borderline realistic which the first film had. It's such a shame Tom cruise is a fantastic actor at one point in his career he was begging to be in movies that proved how well he could act in movies like born on the fourth of July to magnolia please bring back the old Tom Cruise making a movie for it's dialogue not how well a stunt looks in short not a bad film but a disappointment it's not memorable at all.

7.title: A New Direction
7.content:
Wow! Six movies in and audiences are still wanting more and more Tom Cruise risking his life for our entertainment. Now with the seventh entry, into one of the most solid franchises out there, the stakes and pressure were on to deliver yet again another fantastic addition to the series.

The film is a little bit of a new direction for the franchise. All of the previous films more or less had the story wrapped up in one film (or sort of conjoined with Rogue Nation and Fallout). However now we have a story split into two separate films, firstly with this film Dead Reckoning Part 1. Which I have to admit is an awesome title for a MI film.

A interesting concept and ballsy move to create a story so grand that it requires two films to tell. McQuarrie and Cruise are obviously cooking something special.

However although I like the idea of doing something new in the franchise and splitting a story into two films, I feel this film was being held back. Part 1 had a LOT of filler, in terms of story and character development. It feels to me as if Cruise and co are keeping a lot back for Part 2, maybe too much.

Don't get me wrong this film is still extremely entertaining and very enjoyable to watch (especially on the big screen). The action and stunt coordination is simply sublime and a gold standard for the industry. Cruise yet again delivers truly mind-blowing blockbuster cinema, a brilliant achievement. Sadly I just feel as if a lot more attention could have been payed towards the story which feels like it drags in this Part.

The performances across the board are terrific as they always are in these films. In particular would love to shoutout the newcomer to the team and that is Hayley Atwell's character "Grace". Steps up to the plate and is a brilliant counter to Cruises "Hunt".

Overall this film is still stupid crazy fun and a feast upon the eyes. However I just feel as if the story was lacking just a bit more than other entries into the franchise due to the "two part" style this is crossing into. 70% out of 100!

7.title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One(2023)
7.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is Film by Christopher McQuarrie from 2023

The dream team Christopher McQuarrie and Tom Cruise are now presenting the seventh part of the action series with "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part 1", but there is no sign of fatigue, in fact they still manage to surprise. However, it is not just the furious action scenes and a Tom Cruise who, as always, walks beautifully that make this film special. The film also breaks new ground thematically: the world certainly has to be saved once again, but the concrete threat scenario with an overpowering AI that strives for world domination makes the geopolitical situation unclear. What if the individual can ultimately only rely on friends? Or maybe even only on themselves, as the newly introduced film character Grace (Hayley Atwell) envisions? "Mission Impossible 7" explains these questions less in dialogue than with the means of motion cinema, which nevertheless leaves room for thought.

7.title: Good, but unfortunately not more
7.content:
Our dear Tom has grown old, you can clearly see that on his face, but guaranteed not yet in his fitness. It's unbelievable what stunts were shown and when you know they're all real, they look even more amazing. At least that's what I thought when I saw all the making-ofs! Because in the final film, with so many scenes that I know were shot in real life, CGI effects were scattered over it and below that the scenes simply didn't look real anymore. I wonder why, for example, you had to recreate and scrap a train in real life, if it might seem even more realistic in pure CGI.

The film lasts a proud 2 hours and 45 minutes, but would it really have taken it? In my opinion: definitely not. The story could easily have been told in "only" 2 hours. There are places in the film where you should have deep compassion for characters that have never really grown close to your heart. The slapstick moments in Rome, on the other hand, liked them very much and were really amusing and so to be seen for the first time in this film series! The music was also good as always, but this time they tried to let the main theme run at double speed. I somehow didn't understand why the music had to be "heated" by the film, if they were actually a guarantee of positive points.

But... of course I will also go to watch the next part again, but would I urgently have to recommend this film to my friends because you have to see it? Again: probably not. It's a good movie, with good action and good actors, but unfortunately (which is extremely unfortunate!) Only good. That's why I give the movie 7/10 stars.

7.title: Is the M:I franchise on the decline?
7.content:
Since Tom Cruise teamed up with director Christopher McQuarrie in 2015's Rogue Nation, the Mission: Impossible franchise has elevated itself to a new level. This summer, they have come together again to bring us the newest installment of the series with part one of Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning.

Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise - Top Gun, Jerry Maguire, Minority Report) is a rogue government agent, and he has been brought out of hiding once again when a new global threat appears. He accepts a mission that requires all of the IMF (the Impossible Mission Force) to assemble and risk their lives to save the world.

The ultimate computer has been developed, and it has the power to control every piece of technology in the world - from private cellphones to nuclear missiles. To make matters worse, this computer, which they call "the entity," is constantly learning. This means it will begin to anticipate every tactical decision Ethan and his team maken, and soon it will be one step ahead of any strategy Ethan and his team prepare.

The only hope of stopping this "entity" is to find two connecting pieces of a single key. This key has the power to control or destroy the entity, but locating the entity is not going to be that easy. The team must allow their enemies to gain possession of the key and lead them to the entity in hopes of stopping it.

The mission gets even more complicated when a pickpocket, Grace (Hayley Atwell - Captain America: The First Avenger, Christopher Robin, Blinded by the Light),steals one half of the key. Not understanding the value and the dangers this key brings, Grace gets caught by Ethan and the IMF and must grudgingly work alongside them to evade their enemies while moving forward in their overall operation.

The Mission: Impossible franchise has mastered the use of the macguffin - a plot device designed to further the story. In this case, it is the key, but some other excellent examples are Rosebud in Citizen Kane, the briefcase in Pulp Fiction, and the One Ring from Lord of the Rings - which may be the most apt comparison to Dead Reckoning's key because this key brings ultimate power to whoever possesses it. This power threatens to change the person who holds it, and it makes the key even more dangerous.

The past two Mission: Impossible films have been groundbreaking - specifically the most recent Mission: Impossible - Fallout. They have taken this already-fun franchise and established a style and tone that is strictly its own. It feels fresh, original, and separate from every other experience I currently have at the theater. However, with Dead Reckoning, I began to notice some cracks in the Mission: Impossible armor. The action sequences are certainly amazing. Specifically, there is a car chase through Rome that is as good as any I've seen, but I began to notice some strong resemblances to another popular action franchise - John Wick. There is a neon-lit fight scene in a club that feels point-for-point like a PG-13 version of the Keanu Reeves thriller. Then, when the action stops, the characters repeatedly spout out the exposition of the plot, like Inception. However, that film's plot was extremely complex, while this plot is simple. Nonetheless, their wordy explanations convolute the basic story with confusing, nebulous "spy" language. During these elongated discussions of the plot, the director chose to use closeups of the characters with fast, confusing edits that felt like forced tension usually associated with directors like Michael Bay (Transformers, Armageddon, The Rock). This franchise that was breaking the mold just a few years ago now feels like it's, at times, trying to keep up with the Jones'.

As always, Tom Cruise gives everything he has to this role which spans seven movies and thirty years. He runs like a maniac, performs ridiculously dangerous stunts, and is charming as always.

I've hardly even mentioned Hayley Atwell's standout performance as a petty criminal caught in the middle of something much bigger...... She is excellent as a half-heroine/half-foil, but my favorite characters are two new CIA agents played by Shea Wigham (Take Shelter) and Greg Tarzan Davis (Top Gun - Maverick).

Unsure of the IMF's motives, they are always just one step behind our heroes. Their self-deprecating humor points out familiar aspects of the franchise. For example, when they meet someone suspicious, they pull at their face to ensure it's not a mask - which is a tactic often used by Ethan and his team to escape certain capture. These meta jokes are a fun, new addition to the franchise traits that sometimes feel redundant.

Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1 is an impressive summer blockbuster, and many people will enjoy it, AND I enjoyed it, but still, I was somehow disappointed. I think it's because it reveals that the best of the Mission: Impossible franchise may be behind us.

7.title: A Great Part One!
7.content:
As always in this film series, the action set pieces are beyond phenomenal. Even if you are not interested in the plot, I would recommend checking this out for some enthralling action.

I did actually find the AI narrative idea to be quite interesting, despite many recent films attempting and often failing to explore this topic. It also allows for an almost overwhelming final enemy for Ethan Hunt and his team. The cinematography and editing is quite good, but possibly could have been a little more creative.

This is worth a look in my opinion, but it is only part one of story. So hopefully the upcoming next part sticks the landing!

7.title: Awesome action scenes and Tom Cruise and... not much else
7.content:
The above on its own is enough to make this a move I recommend, and though I enjoyed it, it didn't blow me away like the other MI films. Tom Cruise is great as always and some of the scenes although highly CHId at times were awesome.

But Sure it had the sequences, the tension, the great locales, Tom Cruise running, but it was just weird at times.

It felt like the supporting characters were there to narrate and explain rather than be at times. The night club scenes were ridiculous.

The amount of women who could "kick ass" was a bit ridiculous. Hayley Atwells character wasn't likeable and was more annoying, but great to look at. A lot of characters ( new ones) too in this film.

The villain(s) were not great. Looking forward to an improved Part 2.

7.title: Good but not the best MI
7.content:
A solid entry which I hope brings about an epic dead reckoning part 2. Casting in this one is excellent with the returning regulars plus the introduction of Pom klementif, esai morales. It's a solid action packed fast paced entry but I think the problem is it doesn't have an ending as such as it's the precursor for what is to come. In all likelihood it may be better to review this as one entry when part two comes out but until then this is my review.

Stunt work and effects as solid as ever. I love the fact that this series or saga doesn't mind killing off a main character here and there.

Great film, it's just not fallout.

7.title: No clever dialogue
7.content:
Definitely an action packed movie, but in the past, there have been pithy lines, funny moments between the IMF team. And this time those were lacking and I missed that so I would say, add some humor back in and add some dialogue that has a little depth. It is pretty shallow.

Definitely an action packed movie, but in the past, there have been pithy lines, funny moments between the IMF team. And this time those were lacking and I missed that so I would say, add some humor back in and add some dialogue that has a little depth. It is pretty shallow.

These reviews need to be too long to make a submission possible.

7.title: The key to a kill!!
7.content:
Mission Impossible- Dead Reckoning Part One review :

The core focus of the latest Mission Impossible movie is a key. Yea, you heard it right, a key!! I think the last time a key played such a pivotal role in a Hollywood film was Hitchcock's Dial M for Murder (1954). Of course, this ain't a key to a house where a murder is planned but a mean to unlock an AI generated software called 'The Entity', which can create a global havoc.

The Mission impossible franchise is all about Tom Cruise and the guy continues to amaze us with some amazing stunts this time as well. From the elaborate car chase in Italy to the climactic train mayhem, Cruise is first rate. Hayley Atwell impresses a ton as the grey shaded Grace, who turns effortlessly from an expert thief to an Ethan ally.

The new Mission Impossible is certainly worth your ticket price, especially if you have followed the franchise since its inception in 1996 when Tom Cruise became Ethan Hunt. Go and enjoy it pronto at your nearest cinema.

Warning : This review will self destruct in five seconds. 5...4...3...2....1...Boom!!

Regards, Sumeet Nadkarni.

7.title: There but not there
7.content:
Finally got to watch the much-awaited movie. I watched it almost as a 'MI ritual'. If the movie is taken in that sense, as a part of a series, a ritual, it's quite watchable. To be very fair, it's difficult to review this one without watching the second part since much is left to be recovered in the second. In fact, the way it starts is quite interesting despite being a little close to modern scenario in a nightmarish way. Ilsa Faust plays a small role in this one but has a great entry. That was a bummer! The chemistry of the IMF crew here is more tense than fun. Tom cruise looks old but doesn't act old and like many have pointed out 'the grin' is pretty much absent. Atwell does her part well, but her role could have been wittier. She seems more like 'that woman from HR' in a small establishment rather than the background they have crafted for her. The Cliffhanger at the end of the movie is more of a coat hanger. Sorry!

I have grown next to Mission Impossible movies, and I could associate many milestones in my life to a MI movie. In that sense, this one is as dull as life about now and I hope there is more to come. I normally get an adrenaline rush out of watching a MI movie or a 'Tom Cruise' movie, for that matter. Felt it with Top Gun Maverick. This one however left me where I started, a lot like the pandemic did. It lacked the magic that Tom Cruise once spoke of in one of his opening speeches. With that said, I'm glad they finally released it and got it out of the way. Awaiting the next one...

7.title: The search for The Entity
7.content:
This is similar in story to another action film I just saw, Heart of Stone starring Gal Gadot. In that film, something called The Heart gave whomever has it the power to rule the world. Here it's a key and the power is known as The Entity. Same deal.

Ethan (Tom Cruise) is sent after half the key. His plan is to get both halves and destroy it. He runs afoul of Grace (Hayley Atwell), a professional pickpocket/con artist - the two wind up on a joy ride handcuffed together while a ferocious blond assassin, Paris (Pom Klementieff) is after them. The car chase is amazing - the producers state in the credits that no, cars did not go down the real Spanish Steps.

Rebecca Ferguson is back as Ilsa, though she doesn't have a huge role.

Lots of action, great stunts, and let's hear it for the MI latex masks, such a huge part of the tv show.

I spend too much time trying to figure out what's wrong with Tom Cruise's face. It's not about looking older, there's just something odd. Still, these films are definitely his metier.

7.title: The action and stunts are more believable than the plot.
7.content:
The Action and the stunts in this film are 10/10, the M. I: franchise has managed to nail this to the highest degree. Combining real stunts within both real and CGI backdrops that look and feel brilliant.

Tom Cruise has shown us all his stunt collections over the years as well as extensive behind the scenes footage, i can't fault any of that and as usual some stunts are tense and others are fun and others are comical.

I have 2 issues with the film however ....... The first being that its a 2 parter, there was enough in that first part to resolve the film completely.

The second was the plot, it all got a bit silly. Chasing 2 halves of a key combined with rogue AI.

An issue more so was how for some reason the IMF seemed to forget the last 25 years of spy work. They react to the situation like its something they havnt seen over and over before ( under a different guise ). Like this is something completely new because its an AI. It turns out its just the same as usual, something you would expect Hawke and co to know full well.

At times it felt like I was watching a previous cruise film called Knight and Day. A comedic action adventure about a spy and a female civilian, i did enjoy that film though.

I enjoyed this film as well but ive now got to watch part 2. This has to continue with the weak and silly plot, the slightly comical scenarios, maybe have bigger and better stunts while no doubt chasing/protecting a brass key with LEDs on the handle.

A lot of the acting throughout is very tongue in cheek and bordering parody combined with other scenes tonally, deadly serious.

As an action film its a 9/10 with a 5-6/10 plot, especially for a Mission Impossible film that have often been reasonably clever.

Overall a 6.5 out of 10 for me a better plot and it would be an 8/10.

7.title: A higher rating only because of the fantastic action scenes.
7.content: When the MI movies first came out, I was super excited because the TV series was among my top 5 shows of all time. At first the movies did not disappoint. But this most recent one certainly has done that. I had to give a higher rating of 7 only because the action sequences are so good. However, the plot was so convoluted and the characters so confusing that I felt cheated while watching it. On top of that, I am one of those who sadly didn't realize the movie would end without any kind of resolution at all, being only Part One of a Two Part film. That's my fault, but it didn't keep me from immense frustration at the end of the film. And now I'll have to wait until 2025 to see the continuation of the story. Hope Part Two has at least more humanity in it and a tad less action then.

7.title: Action Movie With Budget
7.content: The latest entry in the Mission: Impossible franchise, Dead Reckoning Part One, is sure to excite fans with its signature blend of intense stunts and high-octane action sequences. If you've enjoyed the death-defying antics of Ethan Hunt and his team in previous films, then Dead Reckoning is likely to deliver a satisfying cinematic experience. This review is geared towards fans of action movies and the Mission: Impossible series in particular. If you crave adrenaline-pumping stunts and death-defying action sequences on the big screen, then Dead Reckoning Part One is likely to be right up your alley. Be aware that Dead Reckoning Part One boasts a lengthy runtime. So, prepare to settle in for a film that will keep you on the edge of your seat for an extended period.

7.title: too long
7.content:
I was already bored with the Mission Impossible films. I can't even remember which one it was, but I thought oh God I don't know what's going on and, well I don't really care.

This is worse.

Honestly, I was also put off by the deaths of characters I really liked. I loved the character of Paris with her deadpan expressions, but as for the rest... ho hum. Lots of characters all double crossing each other.

What was the story? Something about two halves of a key. It got a tad science fictiony with lots of unrealistic scenes and big CGI thingys. We've seen all this stuff before. A fight on the roof of a moving train? Seriously? Can't stop train, mad dash to decouple just in time and front section crashes/falls over cliff. Been there since even cowboy movies!

Just when I thought it ended... no.. on and on it went.

I'm being generous with my rating.

7.title: Reckoning Dead
7.content: Best thing about this chapter of Ethan Hunt's journey is that it's ability to keep an audience captive for a span of over 120 minutes. Though the movie series is purely based on old-school flabbergasting spy trickery the story still manages to bring a little relevance with the idea of this virtual enemy. Premise of a Russian vessel was traditionally represented the politics and downplaying that wasn't really successful. Visual effects were flawless carrying more burden. Great audio effects. Great performances by the cast loaded with stars. Dead reckoning could make a difference if the battlegrounds shift from traditional to somewhere realistic.

7.title: Still Jumping on his own
7.content:
You got to give it to Tom Cruise, He is looking for recognition and he is constantly emphasizing his love for the authenticity in an era of fake and digital measures. As part of production's efforts to market this film was a 10- or 20-minutes video of how they made the grand jump from the Norwegian cliff.

It was so impressive to see it as almost a trailer before another movie, that I came back and watched it several times more with family and friends - and I am not a huge fan of Cruise or the Mission Impossible movies. Then my father asked an important question: will I notice if it was a digital stunt? I said that probably not. And that summed the contribution of one expensive effect which sums up in less then two minutes in the movie.

In this digitalize era, that we live in, it is hard to know who or what is original. The technology is still not perfect, but Harrison Ford can act as a younger Indiana Jones in his latest movie - it is still noticeable, but in a few years, he will only need to sign a contract and not even act.

Cruise still believes the value of himself as an actor and as an artist, he also doesn't need digital effects go get younger face, he also did it himself, as the total action actor he is. He pulls his own stunts in the age of 61 but at the end of it, all his movies are pretty generic action movies, which are following the genre basic dictations.

The plot's relevancy to 2023 reality is the fact that the enemy is an AI entity, that can rule the world, which is monitored almost fully by technology. This fear exists way back, before we even though AI can actually exist.

It translates wonderfully to the screen, but the bigger questions, about movie theaters remains the same and even will increase once Cruise will not be able to perform his own stunts and other actors won't give a rats ass about authenticity anymore - then we will know AI is starting to take the upper hand.

7.title: A mediocre entry...a step down from the previous one but still good for several things.
7.content:
MI6/Fallout is one of my favorite action movies and favorite movies of all time. The music, action, directing, stakes/suspense, cast, plot, and movie-making of that one blew me away. Unfortunately I didn't feel the same way at all about this movie and I was expecting better. There was too much awkwardly placed humor in more serious action scenes like the car chase and it was a bit predictable (especially Ilsa's death). Also, how could they not tell that wasn't the White Widow on the train when her eye color is completely different?? They could've also used blue eye contacts for that and it would've been more convincing!

However, I cannot deny the quality and effort put into making these movies. The film still had quite a few good scenes and I liked quite a few of them. Hayley Atwell did very well and was a welcomed addition (and looked/acted amazing). Pom Klementieff was good as well, and as always the main 3 team members including Tom Cruise always do well too. I'm sure that part 2 will be better and it needed a part 1 to set it up. And I surprisingly followed the plot decently which can be hard to keep up with sometimes with these movies. It was also saved by a wonderful train scene at the end which was somewhat original for how it was executed.

While this movie was more grounded and has a unique spin, I still couldn't help being disappointed.

7.title: Great execution but lengthy
7.content:
The quality of Mission Impossible movies increase with every installment and this installment was a fine example of that.

The story was good, it's execution was great; the screenplay, which could have been better, was uneven and streched; the direction was good; the action/ stunt sequences were good and the performances were also good. The main problem this movie had was the lengthy screenplay, I started feeling bored at one point and at some point movie feels like never ending. Theu could have shortened the script and tightened the screenplay.

Overall, it was a good installment in the franchise and I am excited to see what will happen next.

7.title: Losing its fastball, but still worthy of taking the mound
7.content: Perhaps you've seen your favorite athlete who has become a step slower, or you favorite singer who can't hit that signature note as often and have the mixed emotion of remembering the glory days yet knowing the time is near to say goodbye. Welcome to the latest installment of this classic, and almost never failing, franchise. The pure escapism has always been the hook that keeps us coming back: the lavish scenery, the improbable but mind blowing action, the clever plot twists and turns and above all, the last real movie star, Tom Cruise. This movie checks almost all the boxes that are proven and expected but the dialogue drags in redundancy at times and those stunning action scenes which we all pay to see, actually are overdone at times as crazy as that sounds. More isn't always better and that's the issue trying to outdo the previous one- make it longer, throw in a few more mindless chase scenes ( think if Mannix had CGI capabilities) and even make those implausible but expected stunts are an after thought to the plot which is a stretch even by summer movie standards. Yes the pace slows with overtop action which makes as much sense as most of the story. . Without giving much away, there is a needless elimination of a character, a supernaturalistic character of borderline silliness adding to a convoluted storyline. . Director /writer McQuarrie has done exceptional action flicks, Jack Reacher and MI Rogue Nation with Cruise. If there had not been other Mission Impossible movies, this would be very good, but the template has been pounded too much and the wear is showing. Back to the aging athlete. Cruise remains remarkable and still brings it, but The Franchise has lost something off its fast ball but is still mound worthy for the summer scene. But the bullpen is getting sparse of ideas.

7.title: Stretching the imagination
7.content: As a big MI fan I have always been excited by the storylines and stunts carried out. This one I have to criticise regarding the chase scenes. I wish I had the Fiat 500 that tumbles down the steps and finishes up totally unscathed at the bottom, not so much as a ding or scratch! Windows so clear of fly dirt and blemishes you have to look carefully to be sure there is actual glass. Just imagine, a car that is impervious to damage. Same goes for the occupants...not a single injury. My reasoning and beliefs were challenged and usually I am accepting of certain "bending" of the truth, futuristic methods of tracking are believable but steady on.

7.title: mission: Impossible
7.content: I was disappointed when I learned that there was another part... The movie in general is great, but it is not the best in this series. The visual effects in some scenes were quite bad. While watching, I felt bored at times, and most importantly, the character Gabriel, from the beginning of the movie, tried to make me hate him, but he could not. The use of masks is still the most beautiful thing in this entire series. The sixth part is the most beautiful part in this series. I hope that the next part will be the most beautiful. The dialogues were not as expected and the comedy with Tom Cross was bad. The film was successful as a story. I am very excited for the next part because the story is not over yet.

7.title: Entertaining but a step back from its predecessor...
7.content:
I'll keep it short and simple. Fallout was one of the best action movies ever and a hard one to beat, and this movie just couldn't do it. Yes it was entertaining and didn't have me feeling bored, but it didn't have the impact of the last film. It honestly felt like it was becoming borderline "Fast and Furious" with over the top, unrealistic spectacles and physic defying stunts (yes, I know Mission Impossible is not realistic, but it's stayed reasonably believable over the past few films). And on top of that, the action sequences are drawn out too long (for example the train falling off the bridge).

In the end it just did not have the emotional impact it should have, especially in regard to Ilsa Faust. Spoiler: they kill her off. What? Why? They built up her character quite well over the past two movies, and to just take her out like that? Totally missing the emotional weight it should have had. Other reviews express the same.

Overall still intertaining and maybe part two will make it better, but I finished it feeling, well... a little sad.

7.title: This movie lacks consistency
7.content:
This movie is good. A lot of action. A lot of Cruise running. A lot of great stunts, choreography, practical effects and a very entertaining plot.

That being said, this movie lacks LOVE. Ethan Hunt lacks consistency on his actions. The plot focuses on the action and misses on developing the relationships between the characters. You could argue that someone who watches this movie already watched at the very least the last 2 or 3 movies, but that adds to the detriment of this movie cause instead of acting like very close people, the characters keep having to tell you they went trough a lot cause the filmakers didn't care to show how much they care about each other, instead they have to keep telling you "the thing I care the most are my friends". Maybe this time the focused too much on the action and missed the heart of Mission Impossible, last 2 movies didn't feel like this and I very distinctively remember they stablish this at the start of the movies by showing Ethan risking his life to save Luther eventhough he keeps telling him the mission is more important than his life and Ethan not accepting the sacrifice of his friends.

Also, that plot. God. Feels so 80s, but also feels like it's gonna be super dated by the time part 2 comes out.

7.title: High-Tech Thrills, Familiar Formula
7.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1 delivers the high-octane thrills and top-notch production values expected from the franchise. The technical elements are impressive, with sleek cinematography, stunning action sequences, and a pulsating score that enhance the film's adrenaline-pumping appeal. Tom Cruise and the supporting cast provide solid performances, bringing their characters to life with the charisma and intensity that fans have come to expect.

However, the film has its drawbacks. The plot follows a familiar "end of the world" scenario, which, while entertaining, feels predictable and lacks fresh twists. The villain's motives and identity can be confusing, making it difficult to fully engage with the antagonist's role in the story. Additionally, Dead Reckoning Part 1 assumes a certain level of familiarity with the previous films, which can leave new viewers or those not up-to-date with the series feeling a bit lost.

Overall, while Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1 excels in its technical execution and delivers plenty of action, its reliance on established tropes and continuity from earlier films may limit its impact for some audiences.

7.title: I don't know if I can choose to accept this is only part of the story
7.content: I don't know if I can choose to accept the fact that, even with a runtime of 164 minutes, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is only half of the story. I felt a little unsatisfied not getting a conclusion after all that. I'm also left wondering why, with a bloated budget of $291 million, this sequel feels less spectacular than the others in the franchise. There are a few fun action sequences along with some suspenseful moments, and I thought Hayley Atwell fit in well with the rest of the cast, but I miss the days when Mission: Impossible was about a singular assignment told in one movie.

7.title: Tom Cruise against ChatGPT
7.content:
"Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part 1" delivers an exhilarating cinematic experience filled with one amazing action set piece after another. The film impresses with its emphasis on practical effects and minimal use of visual effects, which is a refreshing change in today's cinema landscape. Tom Cruise, reprising his role as Ethan, takes us to new locations such as the Orient Express, Abu Dhabi, and Venice, where he engages in mind-blowing stunts that never fail to captivate. If you're a fan of the franchise or simply love action-packed spectacles, this movie is an absolute must-see on the big screen.

What sets "MI: Dead Reckoning Part 1" apart is its surprisingly effective infusion of humor between the intense action sequences. The comedic moments never feel forced and provide delightful breaks from the adrenaline-fueled excitement. One standout scene involves Grace (played by Hayley Atwell) struggling to drive a particular car model, leaving the entire theater in stitches. Another one where Ethas to make an impossible leap from Alps with assistance from Benji (played by Simon Pegg), resulting in heart-pounding laughter.

My personal favorite action set piece occurs in the last 20 minutes aboard the Orient Express, rivaling the intensity and creativity of Extraction's remarkable single-shot sequence.

Overall, "MI: Dead Reckoning Part 1" lives up to its promise, offering a thrilling and enjoyable movie experience packed with larger-than-life set pieces. Tom Cruise continues to raise the bar for the action genre. If you seek a fun and adrenaline-fueled adventure, this film will undoubtedly leave you entertained and craving more.

7.title: Enjoyable, but very long
7.content:
I enjoyed this movie. But to be honest, I had to watch it in two sittings--it's that long. What is it with Hollywood these days? I know the theater owners can't be happy with the length of movies because they can run as many showings.

That aside, Cruise is his usual charismatic self, as are the supporting actors.

The plot is easy to understand as it's explained via exposition. Several times in fact, as it's that convoluted. The script isn't subtle or clever enough to convey it otherwise. Hollywood apparently thinks their audience are all morons.

Of course, the action is top-notch, and there are some nice comedic moments which provide respite don't detract from the overall gravitas.

At times the drama and pathos seemed forced, but the movie never really stops long enough for it to be more than a temporary issue.

So it's not Gone with the Wind. It's certainly entertaining thanks to the cast and action, which these days is hardly a given for a Hollywood blockbuster.

7.title: Some Terrific Scenes
7.content: Full disclosure: I am an action movie buff and a lifelong fan of "Mission Impossible" all the way back to the the tv series. I am also not a Tom Cruise hater. 7.title: Some of the best action in the series, still messy in its story
7.content:
Of all the parts of the movie to sacrifice, writing and story is probably the one to do; I just wish it didn't have to be. It fumbles the bag pretty hard, making heavy concessions in its story's solidity and in its characters' handling. The story in and of itself is vague at best. The nature of the all-knowing Entity is never truly explained, but it leaves a lot of questions such as "how does it get power to actually run its something-illion computations a millisecond?" The movie also graces us with questions like "why did our characters continue using digital communication during missions when they knew damn well that the Entity could and would mess with it?" (which happened, of course, and resulted in Ilsa's death).

On the contrast, this movie has some of the most striking action sequences ever put to the big screen. It was anywhere from refreshing to gripping when it simply stopped background music, stopped the big FX, and let the second-to-second action carry the tension for minutes on end. The best example is the train sequence at the end: there's no music to give away when they're approaching the safe train car, we just have to keep guessing with the characters as they jump from car to car and hoping alongside them that the chaos is over. They also take (admittedly hit-or-miss) time during the action to use the situations to characterize the cast further. In cases of characters like Grace, it works wonders and helps the audience fully invest in the journey she's starting.

Well-made action backed by a not-as-bad-as-its-contemporaries-but-still-messy story. Worth a watch, but not worth two.

7.title: A Prelude To Something Better?
7.content:
Some action franchises seem bent on merely ratcheting up the action: Longer chase scenes, more fights, bigger explosions. That will count as success to a certain degree.

Some try to wow with more special effects, sometimes layering the effects in a scene until there is little on screen that is "organic".

But there is no substitute for good writing, good dialogue, and good character development. To make the viewer invest in the suspense, make him care about the character(s). Help the viewer understand the character and his perspective, so it feels like there is more on the line.

This "Part One" has a long list of characters, and it could do a better job of explaining which each is important to the story and what their history means to them. The story hops around the globe, giving us some wonderful settings. It also contributes to the feeling that the narrative is disconnected.

The final scenes of Part One are the best, largely due to some wonderful special effects. So this part deserves credit for that.

As for the acting, with a few exceptions there is not much emoting. These characters are supposed to be inscrutable, to face danger without fear, or to move on quickly from a setback. But there are emotional moments, and they are done well.

I will definitely watch Part Two, and hope that it builds on this film, allowing the audience to have more emotional buy-in.

7.title: Ethan Hunt is fighting a new threat
7.content:
The modern "Mission Impossible" series began its glorious journey in the middle of the now distant 1990s. But until now, the release of the next part of the immortal franchise makes fans of the team of heroes and just fans of high-quality action and good stories with special interest to contemplate the adventures of spies led by Ethan Hunt. So it was with the seventh film of the series.

The picture immediately declares itself as a high-level blockbuster. The stated budget of $ 290 million suggests that producers and creators are once again raising the bar for their offspring, and a modern plot about the confrontation of secret agents with artificial intelligence must attract an audience. Fees, however, suggest the opposite. The picture did not even pay for itself, having collected a little less than $ 570 million (to go "to zero", she had to collect twice as much worldwide as the budget was). And this is one of the "bells" that informed me, as a viewer, that the picture is not as good as it could be.

The film once again gathers a beloved team under its leadership, where the viewer will meet the heroes of Tom Cruise, Wing Reims, Samon Pegg and Rebecca Ferguson. The bright team will travel to different corners of the planet to follow the idea of the screenwriters, meeting new and well-forgotten old faces along the way. The plot is not bad at the same time, but not to say that it is very good. The declared omnipotent artificial intelligence and its machinations are supposedly deliberately twisted by the screenwriters and beautiful speeches of both the heroes and villains of the film. In fact, I have not been able to experience the true scope of the dangerous actions of this all-powerful AI. It's like he's shallow and not so dangerous. I can't help thinking that the writers cheated and couldn't come up with something really worthwhile for Hunt's team. Although a couple of moments were tense, in general, the narrative does not shine with something large-scale. And after all, almost all the previous paintings in the series were such.

Good, as before, scenes with chases, shootouts and fights. Here, the creators, as always, are on top, allowing numerous heroes to show all their skills and capabilities. I am pleased with the acting and new faces on the screen. The aforementioned heroes were joined by the well-known Marvel Cinematic Universe Haley Atwell and Pom Klementieff. The actresses turned out to be very good in their roles. I especially remember Pom, who perfectly conveys her rage and audacity on the screen. But the main antagonist-a man (yes, he is here too) seemed to me somehow ... useless or something. The character was clearly conceived as the brightest antipode to the hero of Cruz, but in the end it turned out to be even somewhat annoying and somehow unreal, unimpressive and of little interest. Esay Morales, who played the role of this villain named Gabriel, pales against the background of other less significant characters, including the memorable Frederick Schmidt. And of course, I really liked Vanessa Kirby's game. The actress's reincarnations were excellent.

The film is full of dynamics, tricks, decent humor. The film is good, but still turns out to be somewhat lagging behind the background of previous works. There is no zest in it for me personally, and the finale requires waiting for the continuation, as if breaking off at the moment. Well, there should be a much more significant climax of the third act in an action movie than the one that was shown to us. Although in the title itself you can immediately see that this is part of at least a dilogy. Well. We will have to wait to understand which way the pendulum of the narrative will swing. The same movie turned out to be a strong middling, which is definitely worth watching, and then one day to review. But he clearly does not reach the usual "Missions". Is Tom Cruise getting old after all? The question is of course rhetorical.

7 out of 10.

7.title: Ethan once again leaves a trail of destruction behind
7.content:
The new movie in the Mission: Impossible series is another wild, action-packed rollercoaster ride around the globe. Now the trademark of this series. Gone are the days of secret espionage operations. Stealing sensitive data using technical gadgets. Now the sledgehammer method is the method of choice, leaving a trail of destruction and countless deaths behind every operation - and every time without Ethan Hunt and the IMF being sought with international arrest warrants. And the fact that a US special organization basically carries out state terrorism in foreign countries never leads to diplomatic tensions or even crises.

The action scenes are once again brilliant, don't get me wrong. Nothing like the train accident has ever been seen in a film. But I now miss the subtlety, the espionage craft. The gadgets are now mainly limited to Luther hacking into all satellites and security systems worldwide, allowing Ethan and the rest of the group to move freely and infiltrate anywhere. The tension and thrill are missing.

The story itself is also a bit exaggerated. The all-powerful AI that wants to bring humanity to ruin. A metaphor for the internet and social media, for fake news and conspiracy myths that have people all over the world in their clutches. But in reality it is not a god-like artificial intelligence but rather the collective stupidity of humanity that fuels hatred and agitation and leads to the rise of autocratic and dictatorial regimes.

Otherwise, Tom Cruise does Tom Cruise things again: he runs, he rides a motorcycle without a helmet, he climbs and he jumps over cliffs. By the way, it's amazing how empty Rome and Venice are - absolute tourist magnets that are otherwise almost flooded with people. But not when Ethan Hunt is visiting: there are hardly any cars on the road around the Colosseum. The streets are deserted, not a single stroller in sight. Clear streets everywhere, just a few parked scooters standing in the way. And Venice? A ghost town! Not a soul anywhere. Closed and empty restaurants. Rome and Venice didn't even look like this at the height of the COVID pandemic!

And unfortunately, the bad film industry custom has now found its way into Mission: Impossible and the story has been cut into two parts. We already know this from other films - from Harry Potter to The Hobbit.

7.title: The film wasn't badly made, but it was too old-fashioned
7.content: Although I can't say where it is bad, I'm really tired of watching it. This one is still the same old thing, whether it is the shooting technique, the plot, or the sense of technology, there is no novelty. It can be said that there is nothing that can show that this is a movie of 2023. And there are all kinds of small bugs, such as the suitcase on the conveyor belt opens when the zipper is opened, the poisonous gas smokes down others, and the color does not change and immediately fails, which affects the sense of immersion. I still think the fourth installment of the Mission: Impossible film series is the best entry in the entire series.

7.title: LMAO
7.content: Tis is up there with some of good popcorn flicks i have seen - ridiculous stunts bond women eye candy villains, good guys, evil self righteous, the list goes on for cliche action films - but i love to laugh at the nonsense in this one the best so far - don't misread this a dislike - many a good film want there to be comedy - some blatant some subliminal often its accidental... the franchise is no mistake - it makes money, therefore it needs storyline, each succesive needs to be better than the one before and this one does not stop to try to be over the top... still i lmao as i watch .... the rest is repeating - if you have 2 hours and nothing better to do who can finish this in about 30 mins if you fast fwd past fluff and many of the action scenes.....

7.title: A little bit bored
7.content: Ethan Hunt is going to save the world again!? The seventh part of Mission Impossible and Tom Cruise is again risking his life to film a good movie for us. However, maybe the repeat of too much and we were just with too high expectations, the movie is the same to me and it's a bit long and boring in the middle. Frankly I could not remember much of the movie though I only watched it a week ago. The boss is not evil and attractive enough and the pretension was just too expectable. However, it's quite surprising that Rebecca Ferguson was killed in the movie! Wow. Would I watch the second part of it, I really dun know...

7.title: The matrix part 1
7.content:
This film doesn't have the smooth construction or feel of previous MIs. The fact that Grace looks like a dead lost love Gabriel killed, the fact the groups of characters know where Hunt is all the time and the dialogue's little premonitions etc etc makes this feel like we are in some VR mindscape of Ethan Hunt. Or is this a VR testing regime for Hunts protogé, Grace. Either way, the disjointed scenes etc spell out perhaps something more is going on. Intrigued and waiting for part 2.

Perhaps the title "Dead Reckoning" is a clue as to the narrative arc of the film. A narrative within a narrative.

7.title: Accept this Mission
7.content:
Mission: Impossible is an odd franchise. For one, it's nearly 30 years old and features the same actor in the lead. During that same time 'Batman' has been rebooted three times and is on its fourth actor. The other oddity is that it's continued to get better.

Typically long running franchises begin to fizzle out and end on a whimper. Not M:I. Most people agree that part two was the worst of the series, that part three was a decent course correction and that four was a solid step forward (for the record I don't care much for either of them ). But things really began to take off when writer/director Christopher McQuarrie came on board.

Suddenly there was some continuity and it began to feel like a "cinematic universe". Ethan Hunt, who heretofore had no real discernible personality, started to feel like an actual person and a cast of regulars began to fill in around him. But if all of that was the tinder then the match was the action. In short; no franchise going does it better than M:I, and that is certainly on display here. It's not just that it's frequent, which far too many action movies mistake for being good, it's that it's fun, creative and expertly executed.

Despite being in his 60s now, Tom Cruise is once again in fine form, embarrassing action stars half his age. The rest of his crew are solid as always, and the new actors and their characters are all good additions.

'Dead Reckoning' isn't a perfect movie. For one, it's just too long. Believe me, it's no slog, but I can't believe that there's not a better film in here with ten to fifteen minutes trimmed. The MacGuffin is also a bit generic and redundant. But these things do not diminish the fun and white-knuckle thrills of this movie and saga which should serve as a blueprint for Hollywood.

I currently rank the films in order from best to worst: 6, 7, 5, 1, 4, 3 and 2.

7.title: Thrilling Action, But Feels Incomplete
7.content:
The Mission: Impossible franchise has long been the gold standard for high-stakes action filmmaking, and Dead Reckoning - Part One continues that legacy with jaw-dropping set pieces and Tom Cruise's relentless commitment to pushing the boundaries of practical stunts. However, while the film delivers on its action-packed promise, it suffers from pacing issues and the inherent drawbacks of being just one half of a larger story.

Action That Sets the Bar High From start to finish, Dead Reckoning is packed with exhilarating chase sequences, brutal hand-to-hand combat, and gravity-defying stunts that cement the franchise's reputation. Cruise once again proves why he's the face of modern action cinema, throwing himself into the chaos with a level of dedication that few actors can match. Whether it's high-speed pursuits or death-defying leaps, the film's action remains top-tier, ensuring that the audience is always on the edge of their seats.

A Story That Struggles With Its Structure Where Dead Reckoning falters is in its pacing. Unlike previous entries that felt like self-contained thrill rides, this installment is burdened by the weight of setting up a larger narrative. The stakes are established, the players are introduced, but there's a noticeable sense of incompleteness-scenes drag longer than necessary, and the film sometimes loses momentum between its big moments.

Characters and Stakes The returning ensemble delivers strong performances, but some characters feel underutilized due to the film's sprawling nature. The main antagonist, while intriguing, doesn't quite have the same presence as past villains in the series. With so much time spent setting up the larger arc, some character moments feel like they take a backseat to exposition and plot mechanics.

Final Thoughts Dead Reckoning - Part One is an entertaining but slightly uneven entry in the Mission: Impossible saga. It delivers breathtaking action and the franchise's signature spectacle, but its pacing issues and the burden of being just one half of a story leave it feeling somewhat incomplete. While still a thrilling ride, it lacks the tightness and urgency of its predecessors, making it a solid but not flawless addition to the series.

7.title: They can go on just like this
7.content: When you are making a movie just to do business they you can do anything, people will go to theaters just to watch their favourite actor doing breath taking stunts on their own. This time they are just milking MI's good past. Yes stunts are good, the execution was pretty neat and editing was on point when it comes to action but where is the story. The main character is living the name of MI, he can get into any country, he has access to all the latest technology even when the agency it self not supporting. I mean what a movie! One time watch and forget, you will not remember this edition. The good old days are gone. But yes they can keep producing such movies. I wish there could be a little story for the audience to engage with. You can just call anyone from his past to make a rivalry and create chaos. Good luck for the part 2. Though people wont be waiting eagerly, they will just watch it when it hits the cinemas, I am not excited at all.

7.title: Don' think about it
7.content:
I went into this thinking Part 1, WTF! At least we only have to wait a year for part 2 (supposedly), unlike 2 years for part 2 of Fast X (2023). The steps in MI, I recognised from Fast X with the big ball. Shea Whigham (Briggs) was in the early versions on the Fast franchise.

Vacant characters Luther Stickell (Ving Rhames) and Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg) confused me somewhat, where's the team work. Hayley Atwell (Grace) I'm sure was put in the movie for some eye candy rather than a credible character - I got zero chemistry from her and Tom Cruise, maybe they tried to ignite some chemistry with Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson), which also failed. Hell, Vanessa Kirby (The White Widow) looked confused and probably put in the minimum effort. I'm sure that Esai Morales is a reasonable actor, but his character (Gabriel) didn't work as a villain.

Anyway, at over 2 and a half hours (and no post credit scene), this installment was way too long and lacked the polish of other MI movies. Some of the action sequences worked and locations are visually appealing. Maybe budget was the reason this didn't live up to the hype. Overall, I was entertained and therefore, I would recommend it.

7.title: Good concept but Overly Dramatic
7.content:
Movie is entertaining, the concept the movie revolves around is thought provoking. Tom Cruises involvement made it very acceptable. All the cast members literally carried the whole movie, Hayley Atwell is really good, her acting is really top notch. Action is 10/10

But the movie too much stretchable, every event thats happening is prolonged for no reason, entertaining as they are but they have stretch too much, the tone of the movie does not feel that serious moment to moment.

Movie is not face paced but the action sequences were fast. It kind of gives illusion of face paced movie but it isnt.
