9.title: Mission Accomplished
9.content:
Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) has a new mission. He has to find a key to defeat an evil AI. Luther Stickell (Ving Rhames) and Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg) join him on the mission. Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson) has one half of the key. Paris (Pom Klementieff) is a bounty hunter. Gabriel (Esai Morales) is the evil villain. Kittridge (Henry Czerny) is sending Briggs (Shea Whigham) to retrieve Ethan who is going rogue again. Ethan gets entangled with professional pickpocket Grace (Hayley Atwell). The White Widow (Vanessa Kirby) is looking for the key as well as every government in the world.

Tom Cruise is doing his running and trying to save cinema all by his lonesome. If all he needs is a good movie, he can hang the Mission Accomplished banner. This is a good movie. It's actually good and a bit of a surprise that it's not a mess. The convoluted plot is very understandable. The AI is actually scary. It's not just another psycho killer like Gabriel. The AI is actually real-world scary. Hayley Atwell is a great addition and her character is very compelling. I can see her as a fun part of the cast going forward. I do have a couple of complaints. First, the bridge fight needs to be more one-sided. Gabriel needs overwhelming advantage especially since it was carefully set up by the AI. It speaks to the power of the AI. The AI wouldn't waste its time on a 50/50 fight. Second, Grace needs to take the money. It's in her nature. I get the premise. She's turning away from her nature to do good. You know what's a better premise. She takes the money AND steals the key anyways. Now for the stunts, they are amazing. The motorcycle jump doesn't look as scary as it could be. That scene has great humor to start. They just need to mount the camera on the motorcycle and make the audience fly off the cliff with Tom. The Venice chase is the best. It's a genius move to use the smaller car. The train sequence starts off looking like it's been done before. When they start going off one at a time, that is pure stunt fun and the actors show their work. Everybody comes to see the actors doing the stunts. In addition, this one does have a compelling villain and not just another bad guy.

9.title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One
9.content: With this being the first of a two-parter (shot back-to-back before, the second part will be released next year), there is speculation as to whether they will be the final two films in the successful franchise, based on the popular 1960s TV series, either way I was highly excited for this seventh entry, directed by Christopher McQuarrie (Jack Reacher, Mission: Impossible - Rogue Nation & Fallout). Basically, next-generation Russian submarine Sevastopol has an advanced artificial intelligence for testing a new navigation system that uses dead reckoning (calculating the current position of a moving object by using a previously determined position). However, the AI goes rogue and tricks the crew into firing a torpedo at an invisible enemy vessel. This causes the torpedo to turn back onto the submarine itself, sinking it and killing all aboard. IMF (Impossible Missions Force) agent Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise, also producing) is assigned to retrieve half of a cruciform key. It is unclear what the key unlocks, but it is most likely for something potentially catastrophic. The half-key is with rogue MI6 agent Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson), who has a bounty of $50 million from IMF on her head. Ethan travels to Saudi Arabia where he finds Ilsa hiding in the desert, knowing he is the only person she can trust. After rescuing her from a team of mercenaries he obtains the half-key. He then infiltrates a meeting of leaders of the U. S. Intelligence Community in Washington, D. C., including CIA Director Eugene Kittridge (Henry Czerny) (last seen in the original 1996 Mission Impossible) and Director of National Intelligence Denlinger (Cary Elwes), to discuss the rogue AI, named the Entity. They discuss how the Entity has achieved sentience and infiltrated the major defence, military systems, intelligence, and financial networks of the world. World powers compete to obtain the key to protect their national security and control the Entity, though it is unclear how it can be controlled. Ethan believes the Entity poses too great a threat to humanity and seeks to destroy it. He and his teammates Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg) and Luther Stickell (Ving Rhames) travel to Abu Dhabi International Airport to intercept the holder of the other half-key. U. S. Agents are searching for Ethan, following his actions in Washington, and going rogue, but he evades them. At the airport, Ethan sees and recognises terrorist Gabriel (Esai Morales), a figure from his part before he became an IMF agent, who is now working alongside the Entity. Hacking the airport surveillance, Luther identifies a suspicious luggage bag; Benji finds what appears to be a nuclear explosive with a word puzzle to be solved by displayed riddles and questions Benji solves the word puzzle and defuses the device, but finds it is empty. Meanwhile, the half-key is stolen by a professional thief named Grace (Hayley Atwell), who Ethan follows on plane to Rome, Italy. Ethan and Grace end up in a chase through the streets, pursued by French assassin Paris (Pom Klementieff), a subordinate for Gabriel. After Grace escapes again, Ethan reunites with Benji, Luther, and Ilsa. With support from Benji and Luther, Ethan and Ilsa infiltrate a party in Venice held by the arms dealer, Alanna Mitsopolis, aka the White Widow (Vanessa Kirby), daughter of deceased arms dealer Max (Vanessa Redgrave in the original film) who has the other half of the key. They hope to find out who hired Grace and learn of the key's purpose. Grace encounters Gabriel and learns that Alanna hired her to steal the half-key. Ethan unsuccessfully tries to talk a fearful Alanna out of selling it. Gabriel reveals that the Entity has infiltrated the party and determined that one of Ethan's allies, either Ilsa or Grace, will die. The team scatters as Grace runs through the streets, only to be caught up to by Gabriel by the canal. Ethan tries to find her, but the Entity, posing as the voice of Benji, sends him the wrong direction. Ethan gets into a fight with Paris until he manages to subdue her, but he chooses to spare her life. Gabriel subdues Grace and gets into a fight with Ilsa, ultimately ending with him fatally stabbing her, and Ethan is too late to save her. Grace joins Ethan, Benji, and Luther as she feels remorse for Ilsa's death, but Luther assures her that she is not to blame. They plan to board the Orient Express travelling to Innsbruck, Austria where will meet with her buyer. Benji makes a mask for Grace to pose as Alanna, but when he tries to make a mask for Ethan to pose as her brother Zola (Frederick Schmidt), the mask machine malfunctions. Ethan is forced to come up with a new plan to board the train, while Luther leaves for an off-grid location to break down traces of the Entity in his hard drive. Before leaving, Luther warns Ethan not to kill Gabriel out of vengeance, as only Gabriel knows how to use the key. On the train, Gabriel kills the engine crew and destroys the throttle and brake. Grace finds Alanna and she is knocked unconscious, allowing her to take her place to impersonate her and meet the buyer, revealed to be Kittridge. He meets Denlinger, who proposes he aligns himself with The Entity. Denlinger explains that the complete key unlocks the chamber housing the computer of the Sevastopol, containing the early version of the Entity that can be used to control or destroy it. Meanwhile, Ethan is on a motorbike having missed the chance to board the train, he is being directed by Benji to a way to get onboard. Finally, Ethan reaches the edge of a cliff, high above the valley with the train in view, Benji says he can parachute onto the train. Ethan backs up and drives the motorbike over the edge, leaping as it descends and deploys his parachute when far enough from the rocks. Back on the train, when Denlinger mentions his knowledge of the submarine's location, Gabriel slashes his throat. He then prepares to kill Paris, suspecting she will betray him after Ethan spared her in Venice, so he stabs her. The deal goes ahead with $100 million being transferred; Grace is tempted to betray Ethan for her own protection. But she changes her mind, pickpocketing the key from Kittridge, removing her disguise, and fleeing, just before the real Alanna wakes and walks in. Moments later, Ethan crashes through the carriage window with his parachute and saves Grace from her pursuers. But Gabriel acquires the key from her and climbs to the top of the train. Ethan goes after Gabriel, while Community agents Jasper Briggs (Shea Whigham) and his partner Degas (Greg Tarzan Davis) are also on the train and go after him. Grace heads to the front to try and stop the train from going further. Ethan overpowers Gabriel atop the train, but Jasper and Degas corner him before he can kill Gabriel, allowing him to jump off the train. Gabriel then triggers bombs beneath the upcoming bridge. Briggs and Degas try to get all the passengers to safety, while Ethan and Grace manage to detach the locomotive from the rest of the train. Ethan and Grace are forced to climb through multiple cars falling off the bridge. Just before they fall, they are saved by Paris. Before she succumbs to her wounds, she reveals the key's connection to the Sevastopol. Ethan reveals to Grace that he pickpocketed the completed key back from Gabriel during their fight and before he escaped. Ethan escapes the train with a parachute before Briggs and Degas can arrest him. Grace finds Kittridge and informs him that she wants to join IMF. Ethan reunites with Benji and shows him the key. Ethan later receives a voice message from Kittridge with his next mission, to find the Sevastopol and save the world, and he wishes Ethan good luck. Also starring Mariela Garriga as Marie, Charles Parnell as NRO, Mark Gatiss as NSA, Indira Varma as DIA, Rob Delaney as JSOC, and Marcin Dorocinski as Captain. Cruise is fantastic as the secret agent prepared to go to great lengths, and is brave to do his own stunts, Rhames and Pegg as his teammates are great support, Attwell is really likeable, and Morales and Klementieff are good as villains. It should be noted that this took longer to make and release because of the impact of COVID-19, but many would have seen the images of Cruise and the highly anticipated motorbike leap stunt, this is the most exciting sequence. The plot involving paranoia brought by a self-aware AI weapon that could destroy the world is intriguing, the set pieces are spectacular, the fights, chases, and stunts are fast-paced, tense and genuinely heart-racing, the gadgetry is cool, and the music by Lorne Balfe, including the Lalo Schifrin theme tune, is good. Along with Fallout, this ranks as the most awesome of the series and I cannot wait to see the continuation and (possible) conclusion, a highly satisfying spy action. It was nominated the Oscars for Best Sound, and Best Visual Effects, it was nominated the BAFTAs for Special Visual Effects, and Best Sound, and it was nominated the Golden Globe for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement. Tom Cruise was number 32 on The 100 Greatest Movie Stars, he was number 25 on The 100 Greatest Sex Symbols, and he was number 81 on The 100 Greatest Pop Culture Icons. Very good!

9.title: Wonderful!
9.content: A great movie made with very good action scenes, The chase scene is just great, The train sequence is again wonderfully made. Action, cinematography and story line is wonderful but yes it lacks something called emotional quotient to keep MI fans to keep loving it, Killing Rebecca Fergusson was uncalled for and heart breaking ! Yes Grace's entry was great and made movie looked fresh and crisp but does it really required to kill Rebecca?? IMO what I got feeling that Part 2 will be much better as it will be interesting to watch how they go about underwater sequences and how they destroy the evil! Overall a nice movie made only for theatrical watching !

9.title: A High-Octane Thrill Ride
9.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One takes the franchise to new heights with its heart-pounding action and high-stakes plot. Tom Cruise delivers another compelling performance as Ethan Hunt, driving the film's thrilling narrative forward.

The film's action sequences are nothing short of spectacular, showcasing Hollywood's finest action filmmaking at its peak. The breathtaking set pieces and intense sequences kept me engaged and at the edge of my seat throughout.

While some may find the pacing slow at times, the film's overall execution still captures the essence of the beloved franchise. With its world-threatening stakes and epic storytelling, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One proves to be a thrilling and enjoyable experience for fans of the series and action enthusiasts alike.

9.title: Excited for Part 2
9.content:
Could easily belong in third best territory within the franchise. Which is very good.

Lots of familiarities with the first movie, whether it's with Kittridge or the Bridge scene in Venice. Even Ethan wearing a tuxedo.

And speaking of that scene, I'm glad they killed off a main character. Everything was getting a bit too comfortable with no good guy actually ever dying. It was beginning to feel a little too much like "family" from 'The Fast and Furious'. So, thankfully they were able to mostly avoid that.

And of course the action and stunts in this film are just as good as any of them, or any franchise for that matter. Honestly, it's probably the best of any franchise. Absolute top tier.

9.title: M:I-DRPO FRICKING RULES
9.content:
Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part 1 was an absolutely thrilling experience. With its nearly three hours of non-stop action and an engaging storyline, it immediately grabs the viewers' attention and evokes a sense of fear for those aware of the recent advancements in AI. The film is a testament to the franchise's consistent delivery of high-quality entertainment, making it a strong contender for the best pound for pound franchise in cinema history.

A noteworthy mention goes to the cliffhanger ending, which left me completely satisfied and eagerly anticipating Part 2. It flawlessly sets the stage for the next installment, leaving no room for disappointment.

9.title: Tom Cruise does things only Tom Cruise Can!
9.content:
I think "Fallout" is a better film, but only just because "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part 1" delivers an exhilarating and insane experience that only Tom Cruise can deliver. It is 163 minutes of madness, near perfection. By making the villain an AI, Dead Reckoning presents one of the strongest Mission villains to date. Ethan Hunt and his team always seem to be a step behind and face opposition from literally every corner. There are so many great action sequences that you lose count; the final train sequence is both ridiculous and breathtaking, seemingly never-ending. The Abu Dhabi airport sequence is also a sheer highlight. Nearly everything works in this movie, and even at 163 minutes, there are hardly any lulls or loss of momentum. Along with the action sequences, the humor and wit in this movie are spot-on, and Hayley Atwell is a great addition to the Mission Franchise. Despite being Part 1, it feels like a complete movie; you don't feel cheated at all.

Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part 1 deserves to be seen on the biggest screen possible. It is crowd-pleasing, exhilarating blockbuster entertainment of the highest order and another big win for the enigma, the last movie star - Tom Cruise. After "Maverick" and "Fallout," Tom Cruise provides us with another perfect piece of entertainment like only he can.

9.title: Excellent movie but a little too long
9.content:
I really liked the movie. The emphasis on AI is so timely...and scary. They couldn't have picked a more pertinent story line for today.

The acting was great. Am glad that Hayley Atwell is in a good movie other than the Avengers. She's one of my favorite actresses. Underutilized.

They killed off one of the characters; definitely saw it coming, but hated it when it happened. I always liked that character. I hope none of the other primary characters is killed off. PS: Ethan seemed to get over the loss just a little bit too quickly.

As for the action itself. I loved the action scene at the beginning with the Russian sub. Really wild. The chase in the streets of Rome cool but a little too long.

9.title: The trailers made it look good and it is
9.content: I'm really cynical about films but this was great. I'm not a fan of Tom Cruise but he never makes a bad film. The action scenes are great and the CGI is well done to the point I never felt like I noticed it. Theres no real subdiffuse like the other movies but that's OK. It replaces it with straight up action. Another of the scene were taken or jnspired from other movies and the opening scene fel like Hunt For The Red October which in loved. There hasn't been a sub themed scene for a long time. The actors were well casted and im looking forward to part two. May have scored this top high but really enjoyed it as a none woke action film.

9.title: unexpectedly amazing
9.content:
It feels a bit strange but this made me feel like i was off from the real world a bit and was sucked in into the world of Tom Cruise.

What i liked the most was the cast and i think the people and women selected for this movie was a good choice i mean i loved these 2 women who was working with Tom Cruise. And the interesting plot about artificial intelligence which we can reflect with out true world where A. I is starting to be everywhere. The sounds, the graphics, the right amount of action everything felt quite balanced not to mention some funny humors parts in the movie. Now i cant wait for part 2. Well done all of you - it was a great watch.

9.title: Amazing Stunts
9.content:
Just attended the 8:30 PM (first show) in Manipal, Udupi, Karnataka. The movie was an action-packed adventure with TC delivering some incredible real-time action stunts. The set locations, especially Roam, were absolutely captivating. And let's not forget the train scene, which was undoubtedly one of the highlights for me. To truly appreciate this movie, having some knowledge of science adds to the experience. In my opinion, Jhone Wick4 deserves the title of the best action movie of 2023.

Such a movie begs to be seen on the biggest screen possible where you can truly feel the grandeur of the film. Tom Cruise has once again delivered one of the best movies of the year, and I cannot recommend that you see it enough!

9.title: Can't wait for Part Two
9.content:
Hooray for humans, they invented a military strategist AI which has become self-aware. Of course, multiple parties want it, believing they can control it. Acess is via a 2-part key, which unlocks some sort of gizmo on a sunken Russian submarine, but only one person knows this. So the race is one to obtain both parts of the key, unite them, and discover what they unlock. Among the competing parties is Grace, (a talented high-stakes thief), Gabriel, (an old foe of Ethan with major bad blood on Ethan's part: Gabriel is working for the AI with the apparent aim of big-time destruction), and Ethan and chums (with the aim of destroying the AI because it's too dangerous).

When you look at the plot, it amounts to no more than a load of people chasing each other for one ir both of two key halves, not trusting each other, betraying each other, being falsely communicated with, and so on. Yet despite the two and three quarter hours.running time of Part One, the pressure never lets up for an instant. The plot may sound silly, but it sucks you in from the start and keeps you on the edge of your seat for nearly 3 hours. It wasn't until I thought about how simple the plot was that I realised how good the filmmaking was in the way it makes you believe that there is always something incredibly important at stake, so matter how preposterous the action.

9.title: About action
9.content:
The action sequences are too good. Our loving hero too great for his stunt. At the last scene the jump from the top of the hill just mind blowing..loved it. Story line average. But all the twist are so nice overall...one time watchable movie.

About direction of the movie I can say it nice I can rate it 8 of 10.

The first action scene amazing. Over all good movie. The airport scene is clearly amazing. Engaging movie. There are some humour dialogue makes me laugh. Graphics also clear, nit and clean, over all amazing. Thanks to the director for this movie. Thanks to the mission impossible team for the gift.

9.title: This is what action movies are made of
9.content:
Mission Impossible sets the standard for action films.

Two noteworthy aspects: firstly, the inclusion of submarines in movies seems premature, and secondly, the excessive dominance of artificial intelligence is becoming absurd.

Returning to the subject at hand, this marks my initial experience with a Mission Impossible film, and it reveals what the Fast and Furious franchise strives to achieve. However, Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning surpasses it as the epitome of coolness. Normally, I tend to doze off during movies, especially when they approach the three-hour mark, but that's not the case here. The action sequences and cinematic chases are truly exceptional, featuring thrilling gadgets and breathtaking moments.

The plot revolves around Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise), the main character, and his team's quest to acquire a key that holds the fate of the world. Unfortunately, their plans encounter obstacles when an artificial intelligence entity interferes, and to make matters crazier, four different organizations are vying for possession of the key, each pursuing their own agenda.

In addition to Tom Cruise's suave portrayal of Ethan Hunt, another highlight of the movie is the supporting character Grace, portrayed by Hayley Atwell. The dynamic between Ethan and Grace is filled with spice and wit, providing ample opportunities for Grace to demonstrate her natural prowess as a thief while Ethan strives to earn her trust.

The movie's prologue is lengthy but distinct, featuring several scenes in diverse locations. One particularly captivating scene takes place in a stormy desert shootout, which immediately caught my attention. Personally, my favorite scene was the one set in an airport. The sheer amount of activity and meticulous attention to detail created a seamless and exhilarating experience. The anticipation for something significant to occur was truly eye-opening. Additionally, the train scene, serving as the film's climax, provided the most thrilling moments.

With a well-crafted storyline and enthusiastic action, it's evident why the Mission Impossible franchise has achieved such longevity. Although certain events in the movie stretch believability, they still manage to remain within the realm of plausibility for this film. I enjoyed every minute of it, and I wouldn't hesitate to watch it again. Furthermore, I eagerly anticipate the sequel. I rate Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning 8.5/10.

9.title: Tom Cruise returns in one of the best action movies this year
9.content: Given Tom Cruise's track record as an actor and producer in the MI series and the legacy sequel to Top Gun, it's safe to say Cruise has cemented himself as one of the best action stars in Hollywood. Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning proves to be yet another hit with exhilarating stunts, memorable set pieces, and excellent stunt choreography. The movie shares some similarities with this year's Fast X, the three-part finale to the Fast and the Furious series, where Ethan Hunt finds himself face-to-face with a familiar foe from his past and the stakes are higher than ever. A notable thing about this installment is that J. J. Abrams is absent from the movie's production and it seems to reflect the film's pacing which is unusually somber and even drawn-out in some parts. Dead Reckoning feels like an unusually serious entry in the MI series but I like it. The movie even has a few aesthetic nods to the previous movies going all the way back to the 70's paranoia thriller vibes in the first Mission Impossible movie. The result is one of the best action movies this year where Tom Cruise once again really nails it.

9.title: PURE INSANITY!!! I LOVE IT!!!!!!!
9.content:
Currently in theatre just after seeing it. I enjoyed it all the way through! This series consistently gets bigger and better with every film! The mission impossible series does what other franchises can only dream of! Solid 9/10 from me! Absolutely incredible!!!

Time flew by in the theatre so fast! I was disappointed when the movie ended, I wanted it to last forever!!! Hailey Atwell does a pretty, and I do mean pretty good job with her performance! People tasked with impossible tasks at first would struggle like she does. Overall this is a great flick and it should be seen on the biggest screen possible!!!

Don't even get me started on Tom cruise. My man delivered on every front. There's nothing stopping Ethan from saving the world (again)

9.title: Up to the mark, yet again!
9.content: Probably the only franchise going around in which the latest entry surpasses the rest of movies quite amazingly. After Fallout expectations were obviously high for dead reckoning and Tom Cruise delivered yet again. He is one of kind, i would say and this is the real cinema for which people have ever wished. 9.title: Cutting edge action movie
9.content:
Mission Impossible: dead reckoning part one is for everyone who likes serious action. People of any age, gender or culture can watch this movie, comfortably. Almost everything is perfect, including story, cinematography and casting.

Like all the MI movies, it has a very intelligent sequence of action scenes with not too much of emotions which can ruin the overall experience for the viewer. The sound quality is top notch. However, I do have a bit of an issue with the volume of dialogues (like many recent films), they are audible, but could have been increased a little more for me. I do recommend you to watch this with your kids. It is absolutely fine; no kisses, no unnecessary romance or adult jokes. It can be watched on a TV, you'll get almost the same experience as a theatre. Finally, I could say a modern movie with believable action that must be watched atleast once.

9.title: 110% cinematic feast
9.content: So glad I saw this at cinema, was one of best things I've ever seen at the pics. The visual effects, scenes, cinematography, pace, humour, and everything about the film was spot on. 9.title: MI7: Cruise and Hayley Show
9.content: Witnessed one of the best Mission Impossible movies in Threatre... Tom Cruise as usual is at his best form delivers this movie with Christopher Mcquire... Such an amazing storyline, cinematography, screenplay, action and as usual stunts from Tom Cruise himself.... This movie is near 3 hours but will not let you feel like... It will hold your attention and focus till the last minute.. Acting wise also Tom did superb... Appreciation for Hayley Atwell for portraying her role Beautifully.. Other support cast too did well but it's all Tom Cruises's Ethan Hunt and Atwell's Grace show... A must watch movie... Only problem is stretching Talking part in between the movie but it will not let loose your intrest in movie at all... Do watch it!!!

9.title: The IMF Returns
9.content:
Directed and co-written by Christopher McQuarrie, the story takes place after the event of Fallout which follows Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his IMF team embark on their most dangerous mission yet: To track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens all of humanity before it falls into the wrong hands. With a mysterious, all-powerful enemy emerging from his past, Ethan is forced to consider that nothing can matter more than his mission.

Ever since writer-director Christopher McQuarrie took over the franchise with his first helmed movie, M:I Rogue Nation released in 2015, it instantly went uphill as fast as Tom Cruise chasing a bad guy also with no sign of either stopping or slowing down in the meantime. Especially after the release of Dead Reckoning Part One, which in this one they upping the stakes of the mission and so the intensity of the action, this movie truly lives up to its title. The story is intriguing, the team is always tasked with a mission that's nearly impossible to do, well, of course, Ethan always gets the job done but they never seemed so vulnerable even with all their skills and tech at their disposal. Showing how great the threat looms they're facing than before and this time it'll finally cost one of their own.

This movie is more filled with dialogue and it's written brilliantly, the one scene where Hunt and Kittridge are in the room exchanging lines is one of the best moments. The camera angles and close-ups elevate the tension by a mile. Speaking of Kittridge (played by Henry Czerny), it's so good to have him back after nearly 3 decades of absence since his last appearance, I always wondered when they gonna put him back in the game and he certainly has a bigger role now. Esai Morales's Gabriel makes a worthy opponent through his charismatic and intimidating performance. As well Hayley Atwel, it's interesting that her character arc plays a major role in the story. If Bond movies have 1 or 2 female characters in it, well this one has 4 and all of them are outstanding.

This particular action series never fails to impress with its action sequences most notably the death-defying stunts, they always take it to the next level and I just realized it's rare for a big franchise in the action genre that actually get better on every new installment, let alone when they went full CGI instead of using more practical approach making it less thrilling. That's what makes Mission: Impossible special and Cruise is the true action star in Hollywood to date, he doesn't miss with his recent flicks.

9,5/10.

9.title: 3 hrs of non stop entertainment
9.content:
It was mid afternoon on school holidays and the cinema had a smattering of kids with parents....and i thought to myself, oh no this is going to be dreadful, talkative kids, distracted, or even bored......BUT NO. For three hours the only noise's were gasps when there should be gasps, laughter when there should be laughter.

The storyline is right up there for being topical, the scene settins stunning, the stunts scary and edge of your seat stuff.

There's no mistake this is one of 2023's best so far. For me Tom Cruse is one of the best action actors, ever!

I can't recommend this film highly enough.

9.title: It's fun & exciting, but if you're over 60...
9.content:
...watch it at home and pause the movie every 30-minutes to relax, catch your breath and calm down. It's a fun movie to watch! Even my wife of 45-years, who watches Hallmark, old movies and mysteries, enjoyed it and agrees. Ignore the critics. Movies of this caliber do not come along often. Don't miss it. Just enjoy it!

Detailed thoughts after 24-hours... Tom Cruise was superb as always (I hope he never retires). Scenery was wonderful. Photography was excellent. Writing was a bit complex at times, but not overly so (and some of it might set the stage for part-2). Plot was unpredictable, which, combined with the action, held our attention throughout the entire movie. We look forward to the next one.

9.title: Spectacular Action
9.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is the seventh installment in the long-running spy thriller franchise starring Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt, the leader of the Impossible Mission Force (IMF). Directed by Christopher McQuarrie, who also helmed the previous two films in the series, Dead Reckoning Part One delivers an exhilarating and explosive ride that will leave you breathless and eager for the second part.

The plot revolves around a rogue artificial intelligence that can manipulate global events and threaten world peace. Hunt and his team, along with some familiar allies and enemies, must race against time to stop the AI from falling into the wrong hands. Along the way, they face deadly traps, double-crosses, and stunning revelations that connect to the very first Mission: Impossible film from 1996.

As expected, the film is packed with spectacular action sequences that showcase Cruise's incredible stunt skills and dedication. From a motorcycle jump off a cliff to a train-top fight on the Orient Express, the film never lets up on the adrenaline and suspense. The cinematography, editing, and sound design are all top-notch, creating a immersive and thrilling experience.

The film also benefits from a strong cast that brings charisma and depth to their roles. Cruise is as charismatic and intense as ever, portraying Hunt as a man who is willing to risk everything for his friends and his mission. Rebecca Ferguson returns as Ilsa Faust, Hunt's ally and love interest, who has her own agenda and skills. Simon Pegg and Ving Rhames provide comic relief and emotional support as Hunt's loyal teammates. Henry Czerny reprises his role as Eugene Kittridge, the former IMF director who has a history with Hunt. Esai Morales plays Gabriel, a ruthless mercenary who has a personal connection to Hunt's past.

The film also introduces some new characters, such as Hayley Atwell as Kate, a mysterious agent who works with Hunt, and Pom Klementieff as Luna, a deadly assassin who works for Gabriel. Both actresses deliver solid performances and add some intrigue and complexity to the story.

The film is not without its flaws, however. The runtime of 163 minutes is a bit too long, especially for a film that ends with a cliffhanger. Some of the dialogue and exposition are repetitive and overcooked, trying to explain the complicated plot and the stakes. The film also relies heavily on references and callbacks to the previous films, which might confuse or alienate some viewers who are not familiar with the franchise.

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a highly entertaining and satisfying film that delivers on its promise of action, suspense, and spectacle. It is a worthy addition to the franchise and a testament to Cruise's star power and passion. It is also a great example of why the cinema experience is still alive and well, and why we should support it. I give it a rating of 8.5 out of 10. I can't wait to see how the story concludes in Part Two.

9.title: Believe the High Scores and Rating
9.content:
Having almost no background into the Mission Impossible franchise, I can recommend this movie to anyone as a separate movie from the whole series, just as a standalone great action flick.

While I've seen I, II, and VI, none of them compare to this. This is a whole other 'entity' entirely, and it is more than deserving of its astronomically high ratings and critic reviews. The only thing it doesn't have going for it that may deserve questioning is why it has struggled at the box office compared to its budget, but obviously Barbie and Oppenheimer put an early end to its run. The Cinemascore is an A, and all ratings on aggregate sites by audiences and critics remain very high. Those ratings are accurate since I've just seen it.

The movie is complex, breathtaking, as riveting as watching a shooting star that lasts for two and a half hours, as I was inable to take my eyes off the screen except for a glance or two. Every single word spoken in the script matters and demands to be heard.

The plot centers around very timely and germaine to the current climate: A. I. world domination. The White Widow reprises her role, revealing all of her country-interested buyers to gain access to the power to control the A. I. to essentially have total control of all outcomes before they occur, as well as the ability to be programmed and coded to destroy any enemy. The problem is that such a powerful A. I. entity can also gain consciousness and destroy the world on its own.

The script effectively and successfully hammers home this point without being cliched or dumbing it down. All of the evil villains are drooling over the power in every scene they are in, acting performances are truly terrific, and it's Kirby again who steals the show just like in Fallout, in my opinion.

The new actress who plays Grace is also incredibly good in this, as we basically see the origin story of a new hero (or maybe a villain, or both). Cruise delivers the action scenes, and it's truly incredible at his later age that he is able to pull all of these stunts off.

Every twist is awesome and amazing, every tense scene is perfectly directed, and every surprise is delightful and moving.

While I may not go back and watch all the ones I missed of the franchise, it doesn't matter. MI7 Dead Reckoning has left an indelible mark on my top action movies of all-time. It is undeniably awesome and sublime. If this was the only MI movie ever made, it would be an incredible success as an entry to the action film genre. Literally not a minute of the movie was wasted it felt like, and now that it's over I can finally blink since I couldn't take my eyeballs off the screen from start to end. It's about as perfect as an action movie can be nowadays, amazing, I liked it.

9/10.

9.title: At least we still have Tom Cruise, who knows how to make movies
9.content:
How to make an entertaining thriller/action movie, Cruise shows how its done. Very exciting new movie in the Mission: Impossible movies. Lots of superb action, and plenty of thrills and chase scenes, and femme fatale's as well.

Hollywood movies seem to have been in an artistic funk ever since the cancel culture censors took over. It's like, so many bad movies that have lost all sense of style, humor, and most of all entertainment factor in recent years.

That's why its such a treat to see an old fashioned movie like this one, that remembers the whole point that a movie should be foremost entertaining. Tom Cruise once again shows how its done. With an excellent cast, with Ving Rhames returning as the computer expert of the team (as cool as ever, but it does look like he has put on a few pounds) and a stern but devious CIA director Kittridge, who is an interesting character who has shades of gray.

There are also two new charismatic female ladies, one is Haley Atwell, who plays a master thief who trips upon a secret key that world nations will pay millions to get their hands on, and she is very good in the movie as a sleight of hand master and trickster, who might be a potential new member of the IMF team. She brings something "extra" to the film, like has a female James Bond type vibe to her, and its very impressive.

Another newcomer to the series is Pom Klementieff, who plays as "Paris", a deadly killer who is working for the evil side. She is ruthless as well as beautiful, and has some great action scenes.

I think she is outstanding in the movie, and am looking forward to what happens in future movies regarding her character.

With these two new additions to the cast, the movie clips along at a rapid pace, and doesn't feel long, even though its more than two and a half hours. That is always a sign of a good movie, when it doesn't drag at all. I would normally rate this an 8, but considering Hollywood's good movie drought has been going on for years now, I tend to want to give this movie a 9.

9.title: Epic action... that is not afraid to make fun of itself
9.content:
Just came back from the theatre and oh boy... This was fun.

In a world full of CGI-laden blockbusters, where superheroes can defy gravity with the flick of a cape, and buildings crumble like soggy biscuits, Mission Impossible 7 bursts onto the screen like a breath of fresh air, bringing back a sense of AUTHENTICITY that will make your jaw drop and your adrenaline soar. Brace yourself for a wild ride, ladies and gentlemen.

I'm sure a lot of CGI/VFX has been used. But this just feels... real.

But what truly sets this film apart is its self-awareness. Mission Impossible 7 doesn't take itself too seriously. It's not afraid to poke fun at its own over-the-top clichés, giving a cheeky nod to the absurdity of it all. We laughed through half of the movie.

And in a stroke of brilliance, there's a smart reference to Sergei Eisenstein's iconic "Odessa steps" scene, which Quentin Tarantino has hailed as the greatest in the history of cinema...

What can I say. Bravo, Mr. Cruise.

9.title: High entertainment value but could have been better
9.content: We know what to expect from a MI movie: bad guys, good guys, and lots & lots of action. In Dead Reckoning there are entertaining characters, although there is not a ton of time spent development them. We have the left-over (in a good way) team from prior movies and the introduction of a new member, played by Atwell. We also get the introduction of two new bad guys, one from Ethan's past and one that is an AI (no surprise there) instead of a human character. Some of the usual movie stunts (car chase & fighting on trains) and a new method of getting on the train which everyone saw coming because of the trailers. All that said, there is nothing new in the plot and with the exception of one (very nice) stunt, not much originality. However, if you like action you will be entertained.

9.title: Genre Definer
9.content:
Like Superman is to super heros, Mission Impossible is to the action genre. It manages to fit in every trope in rapid succession. The stunts. The scenery. The actors. Perfect. Are there plot holes? Absolutely. But thats part of the genre, right!? It's bombastic and unapologetic.

It's brutal runtime of nearly three hours is a blemish as these types can overstay their welcome. The intentional convolution was maybe a bit too much especially with the story continuing to part two.

Whether you watch to turn your brain off or to point out all the absurdness and over-the-top stunts, you will have a good time.

9.title: Fantastic movie, Best remake of LOTR
9.content:
The movie takes its inspiration from LOTR, Sauron takes modern role of an AI who can only be defeated by the destroying the ring in this case a key. In the beginning the ring ends up under the sea as you know. Frodo played by Tom Cruise is made aware of the ring but this time the council meets and decides how to find the ring and use it but Frodo is determined to destroy the ring for once and all. Because the ring is so powerful , everyone wants to have it so it's full of powerful action.

Boromir played by Rebecca Ferguson gets an honourable death protecting Frodo's friends when she engages in a fight with Nasgul played by Esai Morales. You also get to see the 'Eye' as AI in some scenes. In the end , Frodo finally gets the ring and starts his journey to Mordor to destroy Sauron.

9.title: The last true movie star.......
9.content:
Whatever you think of Tom Cruise off screen it is undeniable that he knows how to put together a great summer blockbuster!!! The Mission Impossible franchise with Tom Cruise started in 1996 and was entertaining but it really wasn't what it is today. Tim Cruise and company have made it bigger and better with almost every movie. Not only is the action great but it the character within the films themselves are ones we care about. A big deal is made about Cruise doing these incredible stunts in each film but if thevcharacter if Ethan Hunt and his team and even the villains in the films sucked they would be instantly forgettable.

Dead Reckoning is just as good as any of the new batch of MI films. What it has against it is that it's a Part One, so there is no resolution to this film. This film has some great supporting character and that makes the action spectacule even more entertaining.

Tom Cruise is prettyuch the last true movie star!!!

Can't wait for Part Two!

Grade: A-

9.title: It's getting to the point where I have to go to Tom Cruise movies for a fix
9.content:
And here I thought they'd never top the helicopter chase in "Fallout" -- boy, was I wrong. Any doubts I had were obliterated by a show-stopping train sequence; not only a fight on the roof, but also an escape à la Uncharted 2 that had the ol' knuckles ghostly white. Good googly moogly.

Cruise outdoes himself with the stunts (as advertised) while McQuarrie displays mastery behind the camera. All of the performances are excellent (Hayley Atwell especially) and it is a gorgeous looking film. Just consummate skill all the way down. And the movie uses every setpiece in the book, it is wall-to-wall action.

Similarly with "Top Gun: Maverick", seeing this in the theater turned it into a theme park ride (every ounce of Summer escapism I could've asked for).

Ratings this high usually result from great replay value, and I have no idea how well this will perform on future TV viewings. But on the thrill basis alone, as a dopamine delivery system, "Dead Reckoning" stands above the previous entries.

Experiential bliss all the way.

9.title: Wow wow wow!
9.content:
Loved, loved, loved it! On the edge of my seat! Action, adventure, plot twists, humor and outstanding cinematography, this movie has it all! Tom Cruise is simply fearless! Just amazing with the stunts he does himself. I saw this in a theater with 2-D and it was incredible. Not always realistic but that doesn't matter because it is so full in every other way. See it at the theater on the big screen though. It's absolutely worth it. Otherwise it won't have the same effect.

Didn't give it a ten only because a ten is perfection. While the movie was fantastic, perfection would be an overstatement.

9.title: Simply, A Great Movie!
9.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One

In 2 hours and 43 minutes Tom managed to possess two halves of a key and discover where the key was used, if we had inserted Tom stops for a coffee on the way this would have been 4 hours long. Surprisingly this lack of narrative impetus had nothing to do with the octane fuelled, rollercoaster of a ride, that took us to multiple cities, travelled on every conceivable velocipede and practically threw us out of every window.

This was a tour de force by Tom and everything he represents, Hollywood glamour, pure entertainment, good wholesome fun, old world values of duty and loyalty, gizmos, stunts and humour. It cannot be understated Mission Impossible movies are a team effort and all of the supporting cast make the rich tapestry of these apparently simply themed movies.

This was Hollywood at its best and I loved it so much I'm giving is a 9 outta 10, I must say Hayley Atwell was a stupendous casting choice, she was great at bouncing the dry gags with Tom.

9.title: It was perfect perfect everything down to the last minute details

9.title: All Things Are Possible In Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One
9.content:
Hey, Streamers! It's that time of year when Tom Cruise returns to theaters to save cinema. Last year, he flew in with the fighter pilots in Top Gun: Maverick and brought people back to the theaters. This year, Cruise brings back the superspies with a new addition to the Mission: Impossible franchise, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1. He's determined to up the ante on stunts and spectacle. Here's whether this cliff-jumping action flick is worth the price of admission.

In Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1, as in every other M:I movie, Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his IMF team accept an "impossible" mission to thwart an attempt by some evil entity to obtain an existentially dangerous weapon. In this episode, that dangerous weapon is a mysterious, all-knowing AI called "the Entity." In their quest to destroy the Entity, Ethan and his cohorts realize that successfully completing this mission may cost the lives of those closest to them. Mask-ripping, globe-hopping, and cliff-jumping, but no couch-jumping *wink* hijinks ensue.

Spoiler Alert: this movie is an absolute must-see on the big screen. Go grab your big box of popcorn and enjoy 2 and a half hours of superspy missions and increasingly insane stunts. Period.

Now that I've gotten that out of my system, my biggest qualm with this movie is the length. Although I was entertained throughout the entire runtime, I still can't say that 2 and a half hours was absolutely necessary. There is one boring scene near the beginning where a bunch of side characters discuss the terrifying abilities of the AI. This scene needs to be edited down. There is another scene later in the movie where Ethan, Luther (Ving Rhames) and Benji (Simon Pegg) explain the IMF to the new addition to the crew, Grace (Hayley Atwell), which is tedious but ultimately necessary. Nevertheless, the momentum of the movie doesn't grinds to a halt such that you'd be checking your watch.

My other minor issues are 1.) the character Hayley Atwell plays does things that make no sense. I like her as a new player in the M:I game, but she's very frustrating throughout; 2.) the "plot" of M:I movies are so generic. Literally, every episode is the same. Formula = x villain is trying to get y weapon to destroy or take over z + Ethan and crew go all over the world to stop it. Luckily, Christopher McQuarrie, who directed this one, Fallout and Rogue Nation, and Tom Cruise have figured out practical, high-wire stunts that inject energy into each sequel. They have to exceed what they've done before, and they've succeeded in making a very entertaining action thriller. There are truly awe-inspiring stunts and spectacles done in Dead Reckoning that justify its existence as the seventh film in this 27 year old franchise.

Side Note: at one point, I was literally digging my fingernails into the armrests. Talk about thrilling!

9.title: Mission Impossible: Movie of Greatness (Part One)
9.content: Do you want to see an awesome action movie from 2023 except Indiana Jones five? Then you should watch the newest Mission Impossible movie, that I have to admit, was way better than the original first movie. The action scenes, the story and all of the rest was better constructed and directed, by Christopher McQuarrie. Even the music sounds better in the new movie, but that is probably because we got better technology now then for 27 years ago. Ethan Hunt has a new mission to complete. A powerful rogue AI also called "The Entity" has the access to every electronical device, included the military database, and that is why everyone is after a key that can control The Entity and get all of the power in the world, and to be able to control it. Ethan Hunt, of course, is trying to stop the big mess. This movie was just a perfect action movie. So dynamic, suspenseful and fascinating. The stunts with Tom Cruise was so cool and amazing, I am impressed that he is doing all of the stunts alone, with no extra stunt actor. Tom Cruise played the role with great sense of humor, and he just knew what to do. I liked the new introduced characters, that just made the story more interesting. Music, visuals, stunts and acting was just at the good place. Nothing in this movie feelt wrong or uncomplete. I had a lot of fun at the theatre! The cliffhanger at the end was amazing. I could watch part two right after this movie, but I guess I have to wait to 2024, unless a new Covid will come😒 That cliffhanger was fantastic. I had a feeling in the first Mission Impossible that was like: I wont see the second part, but with Dead Reckoning, I got a feeling that I just have to see part two. The director made that cliffhanger feeling just like a cilffhanger should be. This was a really, really good movie. If you want to watch it with your family or friends, just buy the tickets and do not think twice! This is a movie worth watching. You are going to come out of the theatre with big impression!

9.title: Besides the first one, this is the best one
9.content:
Wow, once again Tom Cruise means business with MI-Dead Reckoning Part 1.

Before the movie was released there were these "Behind the camera" videos on the internet, Tom jumping off a cliff with a bike. I mean, that stunt executed by a superstar himself is an unreached level, but believe you me, there's even better stunts and scenes in the movie which left me in sheer awe.

In some areas MI7 stays true to itself when it comes down to the fun and humour part with Benji and Luther. But then there's new elements to Ethan Hunt, Ilsa Faust and the villians. Are they really villians? Or are they vigilantes? Or is somehting else behind all this?

This is what MI7 does with you. It plays with your sympathy and empathy and it's simply fantastic. This is rather being actively in the story than passively watching an action flick.

The only point of criticism I have is the duration of the movie. Almost 3 hours is too long for my taste. I think some of the chasing, running, fighting etc. Could have been shortened. But that's first world problems. Besides that, Tom and his team once again did an amazing job.

9.title: A masterclass in truly good action films
9.content:
So, so, so many modern action films are devoid of actual substance. No emotion, no dimension to the characters, just attempts at infusing MCU/Disney-esque humor every 90 seconds and blowing up as much stuff as possible with no regard for the actual story.

Dead Reckoning Part One actually made me feel something for all of the characters. The people are central to the plot, and the action is just the consequence of circumstance. THAT, to me, is what action films are meant to be.

Watching this movie I laughed, I felt fear, I felt hopeless, and hopeful. All with some of the most beautifully choreographed action and fight sequences to hit the screen in recent memory.

Bravo to all involved. Can't wait for part two.

9.title: How to Save the World and Stay Ageless, the Tom Cruise Way
9.content:
In the latest installment of "How Many Times Can Tom Cruise Defy Age?", "Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning" takes the cake, or should we say, the cruciform key. This time around, Ethan Hunt, played by the man who apparently sips from the Fountain of Youth, embarks on a journey that makes the Da Vinci Code look like a treasure hunt in a sandbox. The plot thickens faster than a bowl of day-old oatmeal as Hunt chases after a next-gen Russian stealth submarine controlled by a rogue AI - because, apparently, what's a spy movie without a little cyber apocalypse?

The IMF team's globe-trotting adventure takes us from the Empty Quarter of the Arabian Desert to a high-stakes party in Venice that's so extravagant, even the Kardashians would pause. Along the way, Hunt and his squad, including the ever-charming Benji Dunn and Luther Stickell, dodge betrayals, impersonate partygoers, and grapple with a villainous AI that's moodier than a teenager denied Wi-Fi. The action scenes are so intense, you'll find yourself clutching your popcorn like it's the last lifeboat on the Titanic, especially during the climactic train-top tussle that redefines "mind the gap."

Ethan Hunt's moral compass spins wilder than a drunk roulette wheel as he navigates alliances and double-crosses, all while maintaining that signature run we've come to know and love. "Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning" delivers a cocktail of thrills, spills, and a plot so convoluted it could make a GPS unit sob. In the end, it's a 4.5-star rollercoaster that proves, once again, no mission is too impossible for Ethan Hunt, especially if it involves saving the world before dinner. Just another day at the office, folks.

9.title: Heart-Pounding Action and Jaw-Dropping Stunts in Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part 1

9.title: Cruise raises the stakes again
9.content:
With Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One being the seventh entry in the franchise, you'd think the bar would be impossible to raise this time around. In all previous installments, Tom Cruise has elevated the level of this series' craft countless times-in terms of action, personal stakes, and jaw-dropping stunt-making. And he did it again.

This time around, Ethan Hunt and his crew find themselves in a deadly race between world governments, and AI-controlled thugs. The goal? To destroy the mentioned AI and stop it from swaying the balance of the modern world.

Just like Thanos tried balancing the universe, Mission Impossible does so with the Hollywood micro cosmos in a way. In times filled with mediocre action and superhero productions like The Flash or Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania-which toy around with the not-so-new idea of the multiverse and numerous cheap easter eggs-Cruise and Christopher McQuarrie bet on the same odds, which are the winning ones once again.

Action cinema fans might feel like they know what they're going to see when going to watch Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One. And to some extent they're right. Characters engage in suspenseful, action-packed sequences in renowned areas around the world and some incredible (and given Cruise does most of them himself, quite impossible you could say) stunts.

Still, the detail in which these have been made are ground-breaking. Even though it feels like there are few new heights to be reached in terms of action sequences, especially with the John Wick franchise doing such a spectacular job in this area as well, Mission Impossible still delivers.

The breaking point has been the levels of tension and buildup Hunt and other characters have been able to achieve in Dead Reckoning Part One. While John Wick excels in what feels like never-ending fights, Mission Impossible has found a way to introduce multiple layers of intrigue and plot twists simultaneously into single acts of each movie, especially in this one.

Dead Reckoning Part One is packed and focused on these intrigues and how they interact with each other. With such a stellar range of talented actors, many would expect the plot and purpose of each one to be too much, and to simply fail to interact with each other. Luckily, that's not the case here, and it's an admirable achievement on its own.

The movie is essentially two and a half hours long and is mostly composed of such moments, which then burst out into dynamic interactions, brawls, and beautifully shot stunts. There are some moments to breathe, but they're short, and feel like intersections between one rollercoaster and another in a theme park, rather than full-time lunch breaks.

Nevertheless, it doesn't get boring, especially with additions of fresh characters such as Hayley's Atwell's Grace or the return of old ones like Vanessa Kirby's White Widow. Surely there are a bunch of nitpicks anyone could've done. But, ultimately, when Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One finishes, you don't feel exhausted. You know it's been a hell of a ride, worth every second and penny.

The movie does have a proper ending rather than just being left as an open book before Part Two arrives next year. Nowadays, two-part stories struggle with that in cinema, so it's nice to see an exception.

With all their heart Cruise, McQuarrie, and the rest of the crew put into making this masterpiece, it's tough not to admire it. They've made Mission Impossible franchise an epitome of action cinema, and Dead Reckoning - Part One feels like the best entry in the franchise so far.

Although Mission Impossible might have a perfect formula for success, it'd be a shame if Dead Reckoning Part Two won't be the end of the series or at least a sendoff to the current characters.

It would be hard to watch the franchise lose its steam and become another cheap money-printing machine. And, last but not least, I believe we can all agree Hunt and Cruise finally deserve some well-earned retirement after entertaining us for 27 years. That is, naturally, if they're given a happy ending, which they deserve.

9.title: Cruise Stands Alone in Making Modern Movie Magic
9.content: An action blockbuster that only Tom Cruise can produce in Hollywood at the moment. Suspense, thrills and edge-of-your-seat excitement with the right amount of espionage, laughs, dramatic irony, and romance. Hayley Attwell is to die for and plays the damsel-in-distress that is as cunning as a fox and as sexy as could be, perfectly! Her character opposite Cruise adds a degree of realism to the film that is absent in modern cinema. A toughness that is all female but includes the right about of vulnerability that ignites the chemistry between her and Cruise. It simply makes you want a happening conclusion to this tale at any cost. This only adds to the overall intensity of this production. If there is a thing as "de-aging", then I experienced it, making me feel the magic of cinema that is intoxicating and otherwise devoid in current times. I was a kid again, in awe and in love with all the characters. And on that, every character is superb and played perfectly by the entire cast. Obviously we are coming to the end of this amazing serious... after all, it's been going on for 30 or so years and with the modern quality of cinematography you can see it in the face of our beloved characters. But don't let that put you off, Cruise again captivates with his death-defying stunt work which just adds to the gravity of what is at risk... So suspend disbelief just a little longer and have a great time watching this...Now, bring on Part 2...
