9.title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One by Christopher McQuarrie
9.content: As Mission: Impossible - Fallout by Christopher McQuarrie has unexpectedly surprised the audience and the critics to have become one of the best movies of 2018 as well as one of the best movies ever made, there were no doubts about making the next chapter of Mission: Impossible film series. This time the cast and crew had to think on a much bigger scale to make the movie viscerally thrilling with new surprising plot twists. In order to completely explore the complexity of the next chapter of Mission: Impossible, they needed to make a two-part movie while shooting everything like one whole movie. Although during the shooting of the movie, the COVID-19 pandemic hit all around the world, it has been necessary to follow specific protocols to make sure everyone is as safe as possible. Even though there have been delays because of the pandemic, the budget of the movie increased until it resulted in being one of the most expensive movies ever made to have also pushed the release date, as it also happened with several other films. After a long time of work, in 2023 came out Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One by Christopher McQuarrie, with Tom Cruise, Hayley Atwell, Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg, Rebecca Ferguson, Vanessa Kirby, Esai Morales and Pom Klementieff. The movie's plot: Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his team of Impossible Mission Force (IMF) face off against the Entity, a powerful rogue Artificial Intelligence (AI) that shows to be a great threat to all of humanity, as they must track it down before it is too late, they have to be careful to not fall in the trap of the Entity that might predict on what has to happen, which will affect the lives of those Ethan Hunt cares the most. As the audience and the critics have been so thrilled with the next chapter of Mission: Impossible, after waiting for a long time, to see how the story will develop differently from the previous chapters and which new exciting action sequences have been elaborated to be seen on the big screen. At the same time, the audience and the critics were so much thrilled about watching the movie, especially to get the possibility of watching it on the big screen, after everyone around the world had to follow restrictions in order to not get infected by COVID-19, which is also a possibility to be able enjoying the movie on the big screen and feel the energy of the story from the beginning to the end. The movie has extraordinarily surprised both the audience and the critics for being a thrilling spy story filled with complexity and plot twists, which specifically shows the vulnerability of the main characters facing the most dangerous obstacles, while needing to be extremely cautious of what the next action will be taken from them without getting caught the greatest threat of the humanity. The production designer Gary Freeman has created the settings to have a specific look in which there is no safety wherever the main characters have to go, even these specific spaces might be claustrophobically small or viscerally gigantic, after they realize how much their task will cost more than they could ever imagine. The costume designer Jill Taylor has elaborated the costumes to have a specific look connecting on how the desperation of the main characters will increase when they face their greatest obstacles, while dynamically getting through everything until they find what they have been looking for, as the first step of the gigantic movie. The stunt team has created the action sequences to be much more expressive through the main characters' body language, especially when their obstacles become a bigger labyrinth by creating a much more intense atmosphere. The director of photography Fraser Taggart has captured the emotions, the suspense, the action sequences, and the plot twists, in every camera movements and in every angle shots needed for the story to be shown, by making the movie unforgettably thrilling with unexpected surprises as well as with intense atmosphere which elevates the tension of the audience and the critics until something unexpected gets shown. The editor Eddie Hamilton has created the narration's rhythm of the movie that tells the intensity and the complexity of the story without letting the audience and the critics get confused, about what is going to happen in the next step, especially when the main characters struggle whenever they take a definitive decision, as they realize they need to be careful to face their obstacles, emotionally and physically, which make the action sequences intensely thrilling. The visual effects have been elaborated to add furthermore details needed to make the story more spectacular in every pixel needed to be seen in every frame captured by the camera, while still showing the grounded practical effects that give a perfect mix of the story for the gigantic scope to be seen, without letting the audience and the critics being bored. The score by Lorne Balfe has been elaborated to create new musical notes than what has been heard from Mission: Impossible - Fallout while maintaining the basis of it, by letting the audience and the critics feel the thrill and the unpredictability with a none-stop rhythm that gets spectacularly loud. Tom Cruise did an excellent performance as Ethan Hunt, the IMF agent who will do anything to accomplish the mission with his team, even though he starts to feel more afraid of what happens next to the people he cares the most, after realizing how dangerous the Entity is. Hayley Atwell did an excellent performance as Grace, a thief who will soon become Ethan Hunt's new ally, when things get more complicated than what has been thought. Ving Rhames did a well done performance as Luther Stickell, the IMF computer technician, who, as a friend of Ethan Hunt, wants to make sure nothing happens to him or anyone in the team, while using all of his best skills to get their goal they have been looking for. Simon Pegg did an excellent performance as Benjamin "Benji" Dunn, the IMF technical field agent, who also will do anything to make sure nothing happens to Ethan Hunt and the team while using his best skills to face the most dangerous obstacles, not only as an IMF agent but also as Hunt's friend. Rebecca Ferguson did a well done performance as Ilsa Faust, the disavowed MI6 Agent who comes back to help Ethan Hunt one more time, until something will fatally happen to her, which will push Hunt and the team to finish what they have started. Vanessa Kirby did an excellent performance as Alanna Mitsopolis, also known as the White Widow, an arms dealer who solely focuses on her scope, which will soon be an important trace needed for Ethan Hunt and the team. Esai Morales did an excellent performance as Gabriel, a powerful terrorist who appears to be working with the Entity, and he is also an adversary of Ethan Hunt to have had a fateful encounter with each other prior to Hunt becoming an IMF agent, he will do anything to accomplish what the Entity commands him without letting anyone or anything blocking him. Pom Klementieff did a well done performance as Paris, a French assassin who works for Gabriel and will do anything to accomplish what the Entity has asked for, until something will turn into a different direction, which has been predicted by the Entity itself. Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a complex spy story filled with thrilling action sequences, unexpected plot twists, and intense emotions of the main characters, which makes it one of the best Mission: Impossible movies as well as one of the best movies ever made and one of the best movies of 2023.

9.title: Tom Cruise is incomparable as always.
9.content:
I adore the atmosphere of films"Mission:Impossible" because it's always a good thriller with interesting adventures. And it was cool that film directors did some reference to the first episode's Mission:Impossible.

What about a the plot? I like it. But have some comments. I think Ilsa's death was useless. I explain. I understand that one of these women must die. And everyone's life is matters . But if we should choose what woman will help save the world, that's absolutely clear, it would be Ilsa. Became she's a professional. And I don't understand the Ethan's phrase: "but I swear your life will always matter more to me than my own". OMG, Ethan, you have known her (Grace) for about two days?

I really enjoyed watching scenes with train. Firstly, the views of the Austrian Alps are breathtaking. Secondly, Ethan's jump off the cliff on a bike was jaw-dropping. And the fact that Tom did it in real life by himself...impress. Thirdly, I like the scene when the train was falling off a bridge. They shot it really well.

So, I shall look forward to the second part of this episode.

9.title: Masterful Filmmaking
9.content:
Compare this to any other film that has been out this year... oh no wait. You can't.

This film like other Mission Impossible entries is just brilliant. Not perfect, but brilliant (I still had a few gripes but I'll get into that later). This film puts other films to shame. It shows big studios like Marvel and Disney up big time and embarrasses them. The amount of time, hard work, effort and determination that Tom Cruise and the team put into this film is majestic, and you can see that on the screen. From the stunts to a clever and intriguing story, this film is just a masterpiece from beginning to end. The amazing set pieces that the crew built themselves to the daring stunts that Tom Cruise puts his life and soul into training for just makes this movie all the more memorable and what an experience this was in cinemas. It had the audience going wild, laughing and going 'Woah' the whole time and it was such an amazing environment to be apart of. That's what these movies are - an experience. And this piece of art deserves to be seen on the big screen. I mean, they built their own train to crash and burn! I don't see marvel making anything practical now!

This film just shows what true filmmaking should be and you can feel the love that the filmmakers have for these characters and the franchise as a whole. Hayley Atwell is a brilliant addition to the team and she works really well on screen - her chemistry with Tom is beautiful to watch. A well written, well crafted piece that deserves your time and money to be seen.

Now for the tiny irritating parts.

I wasn't keen on the camerawork in one particular scene, where they are fighting in the alley in Venice. It looks too shaky and all over the place you can't really see what's going on too much. I think this may have been the problem with filming this on location in a tight narrow alley.

Pom's character feels kind of unnecessary like she's just there to have a henchman of some kind she doesn't have any personal development in the film tbh and her change in character towards the end is quite sudden and doesn't make much sense.

Kittridges character doesn't make much sense throughout. You can't really tell what he's in it for, is he good, or does he have secret motives? That's what you would think from watching it, but honestly after looking back on the early scenes, you can't help but feel like they didn't really know what to do with his character and he felt quite messy.

I'm not a fan of this idea that the police or forces chasing the heroes of the movie just magically appear in every location the heroes do without any prior explanation as to how they were able to follow them and get there so quickly. I mean, by the time it takes for Ethan and Grace to get into the action, there are the same two cops who are after them throughout the whole film, just magically involved with the action in EVERY scene. Whether it's Rome or Venice, they are there at the same time. I don't like how it's done and we're just expected to believe they have some superpower that gets them there quickly and on time for the main event. They didn't need to be involved in every action piece in my opinion. They could have been left out for some and caught up with them later. It was too much and too convenient because 'the script said so'. So just wish they'd thought more about what they could have done with those characters. They felt very stereotypical.

My last negative is the plot can feel quite confusing at times, with several people saying 'I hired you' 'it was me all along' that you have to concentrate quite hard to think back on what happened in earlier scenes and think what that character may have benefited from doing that or making that particular choice. The twists feel very heavily used in this film and for me in some cases it works but in others it's just confusing. For example, Kittridge hiring bounty hunters to go kill Fergusons character AND hiring Ethan to go after her just didn't add up, why would you send people to kill her for the key and send the best IMF agent to go get her and the key at the same time? It didn't make sense to me. Again, Kittridges character doesn't feel natural in this story. But maybe I missed something. Definitely need to rewatch to make sure I get everything, cause the thing with a MI film is they can be so fast paced that sometimes to catch a twist or some context you have to pause and rewind, but of course in a cinema this can't be done. Another example of the confusing twists is the director being on the train talking to the villain. I'm not sure what he was trying to get out of that interaction, but he didn't last the rest of the movie. So was he good or bad? The twists just felt rushed and slightly forced at times.

All of that being said, it is still a great film and technically is a masterful film. Especially the train scene at the end. What a joy to witness in cinemas.

Overall, I'll give it a 9/10 because it's the most enjoyable movie that's come out this year so far.

9.title: Another Win for Tom Cruise!
9.content: The mission impossible franchise is a rare one, where the movies top the previous ones in story and stunts and action. This is just another great film where all the acting is great from everyone and the story isn't dull and reused. The stunts Tom provides for us and Keeps doing himself get better and better and for someone like me who keeps up on the way they do em and set it up for us it's exciting to finally see how it all plays out on the big screen for us. It's true when they say he cares about the craft and the quality of the movie he provides for us. I highly recommend people to see this movie!

9.title: Impossible - to find a flaw
9.content:
I've been a fan of this franchise since the first movie. This latest release is why I keep coming back. The subject matter is sooo timely as well. Anyone who has not been made aware of AI and its potential to overtake the world of information and disinformation might take note of the message that the movie conveys.

So enough of the doom and gloom. The other thing that I love about the franchise is Tom Cruise. He embodies to me what an actor should be. He has the ability to make you believe he is the character that he is portraying. I don't think when I'm watching a movie with him. It. Hey, this is Tom Cruise playing a character. I just see the character.

And the fact that guy does all his own stunts is amazing. From jumping the motorcycle off the top of the a mountain then Parachuting down, To climbing the side of skyscrapers, car chases, whatever. Not many people in hollywood have the balls to do that.

9.title: Tom Cruise Proves Age is Just a Number!
9.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning, Part One delivers an adrenaline-packed experience filled with flirtatious interludes, high-pitched drama, and a compelling save-the-world plot that does not disappoint. Tom Cruise once again proves his mastery of the impossible mission, captivating audiences while performing death-defying stunts that would intimidate actors half his age.

Director McQuarrie's signature style of intensely pressurized efficiency drives the film, steering the Mission: Impossible franchise away from espionage melodrama and towards a spectacle of function and action over emotion and impact. While some may argue that the formula feels familiar, the last 40 minutes of Dead Reckoning Part One present some of the most exhilarating action sequences seen this year, making it a standout for adrenaline junkies.

The movie's strength lies in its execution. The intricate play of identities and masks keeps the audience engaged, constantly questioning what is real and what is fake. McQuarrie ensures that the spatial information is clear, allowing us to follow the intense confrontations between the bad guys and the good guys with ease.

Though the film may not be entirely groundbreaking, it successfully brings back the magic reminiscent of DePalma's original, which many consider the best in the Mission: Impossible series. However, Dead Reckoning, Part One enhances this nostalgia with the relentless action and grand scale we've come to expect from the later movies.

For those willing to embark on this mission, be prepared for a heart-pounding and non-stop thrill ride. Despite some familiar elements, the film accomplishes its mission, leaving audiences satisfied and entertained from start to finish. Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning, Part One manages to strike the right balance between action and storytelling, making it a must-see for fans of the franchise and action cinema aficionados alike.

9.title: A nearly three hour film that flies
9.content:
I remember looking at my watch about what I thought was 30 mins into the film to find an hour had passed. This film goes so fast with so much going on you never notice the time.

The additions to the cast, as always only made it stronger, it was great to see Hayley Atwell (in my opinion criminally underused since her role as Agent Carter) given a role allowing her to be physical as well as vulnerable.

I have always loved Rebecca Ferguson as Ilsa her chemistry with Ethan Hunt has always been just subtlety perfect. Mission Impossible has always - but especially recently, been great at showcasing strong female characters which have more to them than "generic love interest"

The action as always is impeccable. I couldn't tell you which was my favourite but the fight scenes on the bridge had my heart in my mouth. So wonderfully choreographed.

Even though it was a part one, it felt like a whole movie. Can't want for the next.

9.title: 2hrs 45 mins of pure adrenalin.
9.content:
I'm old enough to remember when the first Mission Impossible film arrived in our cinemas in 1996. Ethan Hunt was hunting down the NOC List. Fast forward to 2023 and 7 films later and this is without a doubt the best film of the whole franchise since Ghost Protocal.

The action is non-stop from the start and takes in just about every city and country you can imagine. Norway, Venice, and Rome to name a few. Plus, that stunt! You know in the last hour of the film it's building up to it but, when it happens it still takes your breath away. At the age of 61 Tom Cruise is still pulling out all of the stops in terms of his own stunts.

The plot line centres around a key that has been split in half and whoever has the key controls a sentient AI being and controls the world creating a new world order.

Hayley Attwell is great as the new character Grace, Ving Rhames and Simon Pegg are both back as Luther and Benji respectively. Rebecca Ferguson returns as the MI6 officer Ilsa Faust and a character not seen since the original 1996 film makes a surprise appearance. Oh, and not forgetting Pom Klementieff looks as though she had an absolute ball playing Paris.

Please ignore the 1 or 2 * ratings who say the pace is slow, or that its the worst film they've seen. They've clearly not watched the film and just want to write a bad review for fun.

It is fast paced, with a great story line and definitely well worth putting the time in to watch it.

9.title: Typical MI film but great
9.content:
I am not a fan of action films generally, but do like the mission impossible series.

There are no surprises in the story line, but plants of action and lots of mind blowing effects and action. From car chases, fighting on the roof of a moving train to Tom Cruise looking cool on a motorcycle, all what you expect is there.

I like the supporting actors in his team, and the improbable ability of their technology to overcome all problems. You need to be able to suspend belief for 2 and a bit hours, but just sit back and enjoy the show. Don't be a nerd and point out any errors in the film, as this is not real life! Enjoy.

9.title: Nothing's Impossible !
9.content:
Totally over the top action, great stunts, production value, editing, everything "BIG WOW", and Tom Cruise himself of course doing what he does best, being Ethan Hunt.

In terms of action, this is an endless rollercoaster ride with a lot of humour here and there - brilliant - entertainment at it's best. That said, all the action comes at a price, I wasn't much into any of the characters, including Gabriel, and I felt he didn't really seem intimidating - more like George Clooneys unknown cousin - but maybe that's just me.

Anyway, I didn't give it a 9/10 score for nothing, this movie is GREAT, probably one of the 3 best MI movies - One of the best, if not THE best, movie of the year. Go watch it. Can't wait for Part 2.

9.title: A thrill ride with a hint of character development
9.content:
After this many films, there is not much to be said about Ethan Hunt nor his impossible missions. He is the maverick of the action film saga. Not many action films, if any, can say they hold up over a decade later but the entire series flirts with one disaster after enough and there is Ethan Hawk(Tom Cruise) delivering a smooth, believable but near impossible high risk car chase, motorcycle ride or falling plane. He is fighting on top of trains, in the streets, under water, whatever it takes to save people.

I am reminded of Jackie Chan who put his body on the line to bring us action scenes nobody else can replicate even today. Tom has matched that with an entire series of high risk stunts few would want to try yet alone do. This movie was no exception. Some of the scenes and cinematography will leave you in awe.

Was it perfect? No. Some characters were stereotypical and had little substance to them but the actors were on target despite the poor script they were working around. No scene felt like a waste because of it. It was a little bit long considering this is only part one but nothing you will regret sitting through.

9.title: An absolute thrill ride
9.content:
This franchise just keeps chugging along producing banger after banger. It's crazy how they keep managing to top themselves as far as impressive stunts in each successive film. While Dead Reckoning Part One is maybe a miniscule step down from the franchise high Fallout, it is still the undisputed action event of the summer.

Cruise and Co. Do a wonderful job of making this film and story feel like a big deal. It really feels like this is "the big one" for Hunt. Characters from the past are back along with some fun new faces. Atwell shines in her role, along with a returning Henry Czerny and newcomer Cary Elwes in another excellent use of his skills as a spy agency head this year. I also loved the callbacks to the first MI with the low angle dialogue shots and train set piece. The story feels quite relevant these days as well.

While this is a part one, I felt like the story had a nice conclusion, unlike some other unnamed summer film set in Rome intended to be part one of a bigger finale... but I digress.

Dead Reckoning is a thrill ride from start to finish with some of the most awe-inducing action scenes ever put to film. Bravo, Mr. Cruise for continuing to be crazy enough to do all of this for our enjoyment. I cannot wait for Part Two.

9.title: What Fast & Furious Wants to Be
9.content:
Apart from a small blip with "Mission: Impossible 2", this franchise is extremely consistent. The stunts are crisp, the mission is seemingly impossible, and Tom Cruise runs a lot. This film does not diverge much from that formula, nor does it need to. The established characters carry the same charm, and the new characters add to the complexity of the growing narrative.

The writing and story building in this movie are some of the strongest in the genre. A full range of emotions is experienced over the runtime, with a tense plot, emotionally devastating moments, and humor that packs a punch without being distracting. On top of it all, the film showcases a car chase that is one of the best that I have ever seen in theaters.

The first 20 minutes of the film are oddly shot and disorienting. When getting briefed on the mission, the camera aggressively zooms in on the characters and documents. The interesting choices in framing accompanied by an initial lack of score creates a very unsettling dynamic. It isn't until the title card hits the screen that the movie recovers.

In 2012, Tom Cruise met his cinematic counterpart in writer/director Christopher McQuarrie. Since their partnership began, every "Mission: Impossible" entry has been stylistically sharp, and purpose driven. These films are what the "Fast and Furious" franchise wants to be. Strong emotion, daring stunts, and a story that keeps attention for the full 2+ hours. Though flawed, this movie is one of the best of 2023 and I am eager to see "Dead Reckoning - Part 2".

Best Character: Luther Best Quote: "I swear your life will always matter more to me than my own." - Ethan Best Scene: The Choice Best Piece of Score: "I Was Hoping It'd Be You"

Written for the Gunnison Gazette.

9.title: Really good
9.content:
This latest Mission impossible has this impossible task of following the last one. Which was probably the best of the series so far. Luckily it sticks to what has made these later movies so great, with the edge of your seat action taking centre stage, and Tom Cruise (and the reat of this reliable cast) giving the audience what it wants with less green screen, and more stunts that are done for real.

The movies plot is topical too. Really pushing the tech of these films to the limit. But the stories just a bonus. We're really here for the action, and there's plenty of that. Fallout had pretty much everything you would want from an action movie. But this 1 has a unique car chase or 2 itself, and is really building up to a massively ambitious finale. The last half hour of the movie is really awesome.

Its a great movie but isn't as perfect as parts 4 and 6. Which i would say are both 10 out of 10 action movies. Well you can't give everything full marks, and this 1 does suffer just a little with its unlikely moments. The big surprise of the movie is forshadowed a little much and there are some questionable decisions made by characters in the movie. Who would surely not still be falling for the mask thing by now. Plus it is of course part 1 so ends on an inevitable cliffhanger.

9.title: You've gotta catch the big scenes in the movie theater
9.content: I'm sorry, I dozed off for 20 minutes in the movie theater because I'm really fed up with "Mission Impossible" delving deeper into why Tom Cruise's character fights. These inner conflicts seriously make me question if the director is hinting at Tom Cruise wanting to retire. In the latest installment, as you probably saw in the trailer, there are all sorts of thrilling scenes that won't disappoint you or me. Apart from Tom Cruise's intense performance, the abilities they have against traps and villains have really stepped up a notch. It's a classic that the villains always make their entrance with the strongest approach, which is quite the opposite of the "Fast & Furious" series. In the "Mission Impossible" series, the villains tend to be more cerebral, so you'll find yourself trying to connect the dots in the second half of the movie.

9.title: Close to a 10
9.content:
While I agree with some of the reviews about the lack of character development and drama, this movie does provide non stop edge of your seat thrill. The airport scene had my mind racing and provided one of the most intense moments I've experienced watching a movie. The whole plot about the villain being an AI program is both great but also not as good as a normal human villain. It doesn't stack up to other movies with great villains like James Bond, but the action scenes and overall intensity are a 10/10.

I do wish there was more drama, but we are also so far into the series that it's kind of hard to keep developing the characters. If you just want a great intense action film, this is it.

9.title: Another Great Instalment
9.content:
Back in 2006, I took a chance on seeing Mission: Impossible 3 in theatres without having seen the first two films. I really enjoyed it and went back to learn that the first and second instalments are just okay to me. However, I liked the third so much that I was eagerly awaiting the next film and since then it has delivered on all fronts for me. It's going to be very hard to top the greatness of Mission: Impossible - Fallout, but I will say that Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning: Part One comes close. Here's why I believe this latest instalment is one of the best in the franchise.

Just like all of the previous films, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning: Part One begins with Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) being offered a mission that he chooses to accept. This one is a little more personal to him though and directly connects to his past that we have yet to before. The plot has him searching for two parts that form a key that will unlock something that the audience is unaware of. This mystery, along with the very clever spy sequences and bombastic action scenes made for an incredibly enjoyable viewing experience. It's also nearly three hours long and doesn't feel its length at all, which in my opinion came down to the screenplay by Erik Jendresen and Christopher McQuarrie.

McQuarrie has directed three films in the franchise now and most of them are the best ones in my opinion, so that trajectory just continued on here. The screenplay that he wrote with Jendresen was the highlight for me here though, even though the action was thrilling as well. The clever dialogue kept me on the edge of my seat, and even with this being a Part One, it never felt unfinished when the credits began. The objective is completed, but there is clearly more to come. This film does such a great job entertaining you and leaving you wanting more. I can't wait for Part 2.

Yes, you get what you come for with this one. Action, stunts, unique spy scenes, and most importantly to me, a villain that's not really just a person. There were moments when I found myself genuinely concerned for our own planet because I don't think this film is that far off when it explores the dangers of Artificial Intelligence. I was sucked in and had a blast from start to finish and I believe (especially if you're a fan of the franchise) many others will too. Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning: Part One is now playing in theatres and I highly recommend checking it out.

9.title: Metaphoric with an important message.
9.content:
With Dead Reckoning: Part One, Mission Impossible returns to the visual style of its original 1996 remake. This movie's compelling and timely plot and well written script have become extremely rare qualities in film in this age of industry desperation, abuse, greed and partisan political rhetoric. Dead Reckoning: Part One accurately portrays the noble qualities of humanity in juxtaposition with its selfish chaos while simultaneously presenting the very real and rising threat to our entire race in the form of an extremely advanced and, perhaps, unbeatable opponent: Artificial Intelligence.

Lorne Balfe, whose Hollywood credits are endless, delivers a stunning musical score. Perfection does exist in cinema, and many Hollywood titles achieve it. Dead Reckoning comes strikingly close, with clear and concise dialogue, Hollywood's greatest acting talents, and exceptional cinematography from Fraser Taggart. Direction here is astute and timely; moving the plot along briskly and keeping the viewer engaged and concerned. Some pacing mistakes are made as well as hiccups in believability and realism. Overall, Dead Reckoning: Part One continues the tradition of premiere spy thriller excellence in the Mission Impossible franchise.

The little known truth about the Universe, is that its qualities are that of generosity and patience. Our planet has always nurtured life, offering a boundless wealth of sustenance and nutrition. As children of Earth, mankind's nature is also one of giving and forgiving; a fact that so many millions (especially those in power) refuse to acknowledge; deciding to, instead, consume, destroy and exploit for personal gain. How appropriate, then, for this movie to have failed at the box office, despite its incredibly important message and moving performances. Selfishness is truly the root of all evil, and an uncaring, cold and calculating A. I. makes for the perfect villain, as well as a clearly impossible mission.

9.title: Very good action movie
9.content:
I really enjoyed this film, it has some enjoyable action moments and the plot is being developed well throughout the movie. The action is over the top and really exciting.

The opening sequence is a very long scene which is fantastic and it introduces us what the movie is about.

It should have more action of course but it is a great film to enjoy watching. I watched this in the cinema and I was really impressed and surprised by the experience.

The first half was excellent but after that it becomes a bit boring and pointless.

It ends very unexpectedly and you have to wait for the next one that is worth waiting because I really want to see how it ends!

9.title: Best Film of 2023
9.content: Reading some of the reviews I think they have missed the point. No it's not Fall out but it does not disappoint. The scene is set well as a story and you get the reasoning behind the old and new characters, this loved up to the franchise and I am surprised it did not do better at the box Office. This film did not disappoint, on the contrary was action packed full of Great funny scenes. As always well written directed. As with all MI films well acted and a rare thing nowadays well written. My wife and I loved it and am looking forward to seeing part 2. I have bought the film recently and I can honestly say without a doubt this is the best film I have seen this year.

9.title: THE CINEMA IS BACK!!
9.content:
The cinema is back!!!

I watched it in IMAX theater, the biggest screen in Japan (Grand Cinema Sunshine Ikebukuro) for the first time in my life and it was such a game changer.

Tom Cruise never misses. He was great in every scene in every possible way. He does acting, running, flying, saving, loving, and producing (but not directing which is strange for us all.)

I must shout out to who played Paris!!! Who's she? I must knew but I didn't. She's sooo gorgeous. She looks like female version of Joker (in a good way.) And she tells everything in her eyes. It felt almost equal (or more than that?) to Tom's acting.

I am so curious about how Part 2 answers towards the AI threatening. (Or maybe this movie is the answer idk.) Tom does things that AI never come up with, and that's true meaning of "the cinema is back!!!"

I felt so sorry for Rebecca. She's outstanding in this new M:I. She is the reason I watched this...I hope she come back in Part 2.

And I can't wait to watch Part 2 (titanic version).

(plus, I saw Dune 2 trailer and it was far more better than I watched it on YouTube. Sorry but I'm glad that the theatrical release will be delayed in the US because no one can spoil it before I watch it. I should watch it in IMAX to experience Hans Zimmer's music.)

9.title: Second best of the franchise after Fallout
9.content:
In Top Gun Maverick Tom Cruise acknowledged, he may be the last of the lot but he's still here and will keep going on for some time. And now here he fights a war against digital entity (even though the film itself is shot digitally).

Not as good as Fallout but still better than all the other entries in the franchise. The action is spectacular and impressive as always. Characters and emotions are given enough space, just like McQuarrie's previous entries in the franchise. Haylee Atwell does a fantastic job as the new entry in the franchise. However, I was disappointed that Rebecca Ferguson is sidelined here. There's a bit of a problem being too many characters and this being just the part 1 but the way it still managed to be this good despite that makes me think part 2 is gonna be the best in the franchise.

9.title: Unapologetically Awesome
9.content:
Given that I saw the trailer for the first time half an hour before I went to the cinema (and squeezed in a YouTube series recap), if it wasn't for a co-worker mentioning this film was about the sacrifices made by friends for each other, I really would not have been interested in this film at all.

Without resorting to hyperbole - this movie is freaking amazing. It's the kind of 2.5hr plus movie that doesn't feel that long at all, engaging the audience with incredible action sequences, subtle yet impactful character moments, and all-round excellent performances by all.

As noted above, I hadn't kept track of the most recent MI films so wasn't attuned to the comradery and friendship that developed between Ethan, Luther, Benji and Isla. Dead Reckoning allows the cast to shine in their roles and their chemistry is wonderful to watch.

Grace, the newest member of the team, is well-written and perfectly cast as a skilled international spy, but is completely out of her depth when her life - and the fate of the world - is on the line. Her growth is natural and cathartic and the audience is rooting for her to succeed.

Tom Cruise truly is one of the few action hero superstars of our time. In the last couple of years, he has helmed two of the most entertaining blockbusters audiences have seen in a very, very long time. Both films take legacy characters and build upon them, upping the stakes and allowing our hero to make choices consistent with their character and arc. And with both critical acclaim and smashing the box office, maybe the film industry could take some notes from Mr. Cruise.

It goes without saying the stunt work, location filming, and grand scale of this film is breathtaking. There are some pacing issues and awkward leans into comedy, but overall, Dead Reckoning is the exhilarating tension-filled ride we've all been aching for and a welcome departure from the rushed CGI worlds we've endured in recent times.

Although it's a two-parter, the film has its own ending, and sets up perfectly for the next one.

And I can't wait.

Dead Reckoning Part One" is about Ethan Hunt reconciling how he got to this point in his life, and wants you to remember the first movie-how Ethan Hunt became an agent and the price he's been paying from the beginning.

Last summer, Tom Cruise was given credit for saving the theatrical experience with the widely beloved "Top Gun: Maverick." One of our last true movie stars returns over a year later as the blockbuster Dead Reckoning Part One" is a ridiculously good time. Once again, director Christopher McQuarrie, Cruise, and their team have crafted a deceptively simple thriller, a film that bounces characters off each other While this series essentially rebooted in its fourth chapter, changing tone and style significantly, this seventh film very cleverly ties back to the 1996 Brian De Palma original more than any other, almost as if it's uniting the two halves of the franchise. It's not an origin story, but it does have the tenor of something like the excellent "Casino Royale" in how it unpacks the very purpose of a beloved character. "Dead Reckoning Part One" is about Ethan Hunt reconciling how he got to this point in his life, and dir McQuarrie and narratively recall De Palma's film repeatedly. And with its sweaty, canted close-ups wants you to remember the first movie-how Ethan Hunt became an agent and the price he's been paying from the beginning.mcq really knows how to bring hunts character to the forefront Venice is the beating heart of the film a creepy night shot the is like a London Gothic and atmospheric With a maze of running through Venice little streets

Brings the story and new choices It's not just visual nods. "Dead Reckoning" returns former IMF director Eugene Kittridge (Henry Czerny) to Ethan's life with a new mission. Kittridge informs Hunt that there's essentially a rogue A. I. in the world that superpowers are battling to control.and so Ethan and his team-including returning characters Luther (Ving Rhames) and Benji (Simon Pegg)-have to not just intercept the key but discern its purpose. The key only matters if IMF can figure out where and how to use it.

After a desert shoot-out that ushers Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson) back into the series, the first major set piece in "Dead Reckoning Part One" takes place in the Dubai airport, where Hunt discovers that there are other players in this espionage chess game, including a familiar face in Gabriel (Esai Morales), a morally corrupt mercenary who is one of the reasons that Hunt is an agent in the first place. Gabriel is a chaos agent, someone who not only wants to watch the world burn but hopes the fire inflicts as much pain as possible. In many ways, Gabriel is the inverse of Ethan, whose weakness has been his empathy and personal connections-Gabriel has none of those, and he's basically working as a broker

At the airport, Ethan also crosses paths with a pickpocket named Grace (Hayley Atwell), who gets stuck in the middle of all of this world-changing insanity, along with a few agents trying to hunt down the rogue Ethan and are played by a wonderfully exasperated Shea Whigham and Greg Tarzan Davis. A silent assassin, memorably sketched by Pom Klementieff, is also essential to a few action scenes. And Vanessa Kirby returns as the arms dealer White Widow, and, well, if the ensemble has a weakness, it's Kirby's kind of lost performance. She has never quite been able to convey "power player" in these films as she should.

With all the talk in Hollywood about ai

There's also something fascinating thematically here about a movie star battling A. I. and questioning the purpose of his job There's also something fascinating thematically here While good old Ving Rhames and good not-quite-so-old Simon Pegg remain in the van, distaff talent carries out the majority of the secondary ass-kicking. Rebecca Ferguson is back behind the sniper rifle as old chum Ilsa. Vanessa Kirby reprises her role as statuesque princess of malignity. Newcomer Pom Klementieff, Newcomer Hayley Atwell joins the fray as Grace, a thief who finds herself in the middle of all the scheming and double-dealing and violence. Esai Morales plays Gabriel, the diabolical avatar of The Entity. Shea Whigham goes big with agent Jasper Briggs, a man hot on the pursuit of Hunt who "always goes rogue."

Ethan and Grace zip around Rome in one of the funniest, most exciting car chase scenes I've ever seen in a film. I don't remember ever laughing so hard during a car chase.because of the Fiat 500 chase scene in Rome the car is a character and driving handcuffed is spectacular in car chases In an exciting train scene we not only get one of Simon Pegg and Tom Cruise's funnier conversations, we also get a massively tense scene that feels straight out of Uncharted 2.

If that's a lot of video game comparisons, forgive me. I play a lot of video games! I watch a lot of movies and play a lot of games and this one feels like a fun intersection of the two.

Since I'm trying not to spoil too much, I won't say much more. I was highly entertained from start to finish. Morales's Gabriel is a compelling villain and the European locales-Rome, Venice, the Austrian Alps, etc.-are gorgeous and fun to spend time in, even if it's often just backdrop to brutal fight scenes Bring on the final.9/10 well worth it.

9.title: Worth Your hard earned money

Firstly, I would highly recommend watching this in IMAX. I saw it in Dolby Atmos, and I slightly regret not forking over the couple extra dollars to see this in all its IMAX glory.

Tom Cruise... This guy is truly insane in the greatest way. I came into the movie excited for the stunts, which are phenomenal (there really is no one else who makes movies like Cruise), but I was surprised that I came out of the theater enthralled with the plot. This movie is nearly 3 hours but it felt like it was barely 2 because Christopher Mcquarrie has done an excellent job pacing this film. I didn't want it to end. Of course, this movie has amazing fight sequences; it's a Mission Impossible movie. However, as mentioned before, I was surprised to find out that the action was not what I enjoyed the most about this film. The story is very well crafted, and the action set pieces support that story to make this an epic experience.

9.title: They have done it again!
9.content:
I laughed, I screamed, I jumped, I grabbed my seat, I had my heart pumping so fast, and I cried. Ethan Hunt and the IMF team must track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens all of humanity if it falls into the wrong hands. With control of the future and the fate of the world at stake, a deadly race around the globe begins. Confronted by a mysterious, all-powerful enemy, Ethan is forced to consider that nothing can matter more than the mission -- not even the lives of those he cares about most.

Now you probably won't feel all the emotions I mentioned earlier, in fact, you might not even feel half of them, it's just that I've been following Ethan Hunt's adventures and re-watching the movies multiple times since I was a little kid, making me build a huge emotional connection with everysingle character in the franchise. The mission impossible franchise has established itself as the epitome of what an action movie are. The action sequences were out of this world; from every stunt to every fight scene and the chase scenes.

The cast was wonderful and, other than obviously Tom Cruise, Haley Atwell definitely stands out. The story was also very interesting and attention grabbing as it was a bit different than other stories as it explores the immerging AI topic (keeping in mind that the movie was filmed in 2020 meaning that the writers saw this matter even before it had its widespread.)

Score:9/10.

9.title: I reckon that's the movie of the year
9.content:
Wow. Totally worth staying up till 1:30am to see it on opening night. And I'll definitely be seeing it at least a couple more times in theatres - this movie was built to be watched on the big screen. So, definitely go out and see it! Give them as much of your money as you can, to show them just how much we support them making more of these movies!

I don't know what constitutes a 10/10 movie, but Dead Reckoning P1 is probably as deserving of that score as any other I've seen. If you were worried / wondering if / how Tom and the crew would manage to one-up Fallout, you'll be happy to hear they somehow manage to ten-up it. And I loved Fallout! The man just DELIVERS.

One of the best action movies I've ever seen. But it's not just the action that's great - it keeps you on your toes with twists, it evokes all sorts of emotion, it makes you laugh, it makes you jump, it makes you think, it makes you contemplate possibilities, it parallels our own world in many ways, it has you falling in love with Hayley Atwell (she's my new favourite actress - I hope to see her in many more roles going forward), it makes you grip your arm rests in suspense, it maintains that nostalgic MI feel... I really can't say enough good things! And as I sit here reflecting on the experience I just had, I'm finding myself wondering how much thought they put into every single moment of that movie. There was SO much going on the whole time, yet it was impossibly well composed.

Just go see it. Even with how high this review sets your expectations, you won't be disappointed.

9.title: Tom's amazing action vs Writer's lame writing.

First of all, I'm going to tell you that I am a very, very big fan and admirer of Tom Cruise, one of the greatest film stars in the Hollywood. If it wasn't for one and only Tom Cruise, who even tries to put his life on the line for the mere entertainment of fans, I would've rated this movie as low as 5. Really, as people say, Tom Cruise saves the Hollywood, if Tom is not in this movie no critic will ever praise this movie like they did now.

The movie has one of the best and amazing action sequences, if not THE best. Also, the score gives me chills. The acting part is also pretty awesome. I believe, the drawback of the movie is that it has so many plot holes or flaws in the storyline. Like, how can US make the most powerful AI and plant it in Russia's submarine without even retaining the copy of original source code. Why would the US official in the train just gives all the information regarding the Entity to Gabriel just like that knowing that if he gives the information to Gabriel there is no defense against Gabriel killing him. Also, why is Ethan is morally inclined towards woman? In the narrow lane fight, he left Paris to survive but will he leave a man to survive in the same situation? Also, Grace is so much annoying in the movie. Why would Ethan take her everywhere he goes in the Airport? Why don't he just take the Key away from her and leave her? Also, why is she always ditching Ethan when he is trying to save her? Why doesn't White Widow kill Gabriel, just like that? There are even more flaws. The writers are being excused because of the amazing charisma shown of Tom Cruise with his stunts along with the special effects team making such visually appealing movie.

9.title: Absolute masterpiece with most depth in vision and story
9.content:
I loved this installment, too pity it is in two parts, and thank god it is as it is a complex story that needs proper unfolding. At the same time it is an analogy of our world today and that took guts, which I admire and give it even extra credits for!

It didn't miss a beat in being a proper MI movie, amazing stunt work as always, so much so we even get a bit blase about it at times; "oh, he jumped of a ridge with a motorbike" or a locomotive plummeted to its last resting place several hundreds of feet below, vertical climbing within train wagons etc. But nothing feels contrived, everything has a function in the story, adds to the tension without ever being overblown despite the massive undertakings. It is really well done and those who complain about character development, we have come to know Ethan Hunt over the previous installments of MI, now we see him apply all his skills, and an added bonus of human interest with his female characters including the loss of life and his internal burning desire to finish it all once and for all. And we get to know the rest of the crew and their sacrifice as well, so overall I found it very rewarding, both in character, motivation and perseverance to be a believable undertaking and I eagerly await the second part of Dead Reckoning! Absolutely stunning and rewarding film to watch!

9.title: IMF's Key to Success
9.content:
While Ethan Hunt was battling his latest nemesis, AMC acted like my own personal enemy. More on that later. This review is about the best Mission to date.

It's hard to say now, as they clearly say "Part One" in the title, but as tradition, this series ALWAYS gets progressively better. Easiest Franchise Ranking Ever: Just start at the newest chapter as number one best and work your way backwards.

This is also probably one of THE most suspenseful movies I've ever seen. From minute 1 to minute 163, this is a nailbiter/edge of your seat thriller. And yes, it's about 3 hours long and is also one of THE most well-paced movies I've ever seen. This did NOT feel this long and when we got to the climax, my group and I felt that was the mid-section.

(Technically, it is. Again, Part One of Two.)

Outside of this movie, I've recently added A. I. to my list of possibly irrational fears. It started with Elon Musk's concerns - if he's concerned, then it's probably worse than we thought and led to the Writer's Strike with A. I. being able to construct perfect screenplays. And what's next? All of our jobs?

This movie didn't help. The film's about the use of technology/intelligence and how the world would be when it falls into the right/wrong hands. Also, it's about another McGuffin. When IS this series about anything than a McGuffin the team keeps acquiring and losing and acquiring again and so on?

I LOVED this movie, which is something I say a lot about these Mission: Impossible movies. What this one brought to the table was really letting us, the viewer, take a crack of what it would be like to be a super spy. You literally feel like you're part of the action and not just watching a movie. I do NOT know how they pulled that off. While we don't have free will, à la Choose Your Own Adventure, you'll be side-by-side with Ethan and you'll feel every bit of the danger, punches and near-death experiences he has.

Without spoiling anything specific, and I'll get to how everyone was trying to spoil this for me, a tragedy occurs in this movie that did make me very sad, indeed. But, luckily and mercifully, I can see this was the path of this character. I don't really see any other way. At least I have acceptance. Plus, I did like the direction the film took after this incident.

Awful we have to wait a full year for the second part. I know by then I'll have seen this at least three more times. In fact, from what I'm about to write, you'll know I earned a free AMC ticket for my HORRIBLE experience with my friends. So, without hesitation, I believe I will go see this again very soon.

***

Final Thoughts: WOW, thank GOD this movie was excellent. This was one of THE worst experiences at AMC I've ever had. Before the movie even started, the garbage cans entering the theatre was overflowing to the floor. All three of them.

Then, the A/C was off and/or not working properly as it was incredibly hot the entire 3+ hours including previews and that dang Nicole Kidman outdated ad. Further, speaking of that garbage they show before the movie, unbelievably, they had one full spoiler-heavy press string of clips from this very movie AND Director Christopher McQuarrie/Actor Tom Cruise "introduce" the movie with a thank you for coming. While I didn't care about the latter, that spoilery clip show had no business before the very movie we're about to see.

Also, the screen was noticeably dented so that was distracting during the movie. And probably worst of all, about 30 min in, the movie suddenly went mute and eventually, it abruptly stopped. They tried to fix it, but ultimately/accidently fast forwarded to a scene with a key death they now spoiled for all of us. They finally rewound to the beginning so we got to see Christopher/Tom's greeting, albeit now they were shaking back and forth like it was Drunk-vision. We laughed, but we really didn't want to fully start over since this movie was already 3-hours and it was getting late. Thankfully, they managed to find the section 4-5 min before the muted part.

Arg. I hope AMC was just having an off night.

9.title: A Glorious, Larger Than Life Action Spectacle
9.content:
Man what an adrenaline rush of a movie this was. Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One proves why this is one of best franchises to have ever graced the silver screen and the 7th installment in this franchise was no exception. The story is exhilarating, faced paced and full of unpredictable twist and turns and the stakes are always high. The action and stunt work, as you'd expect is mind-blowing and intense. It has set the bar so high for future action flicks that it wouldn't be easy to surpass it. On top of that the gorgeous Cinematography and the fantastic direction makes it even better.

Tom Cruise is perfect as Ethan Hunt, jumping off a cliff with a motorbike and fighting on the roof of a moving train. The movie also explores his relationship with his teammates and Ilsa. The best new addition to the series, Hayley Atwell as Grace is one of the greatest aspect of the movie. She gets most of the screentime and is absolutely fantastic. Her chemistry with Ethan, from the moment they meet, is electric and the movie gets more and more exciting whenever they're on screen. Though some of the side characters lacked development and were provided with very little screentime.

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a really enjoyable action flick that breathes new life into the franchise. With exhilarating action, great performances and a solid story, this a must-see. Tom Cruise once again proves why he's one of the greatest action stars of our time. Highly recommend it.

9.title: Mission to Remember
9.content:
Ethan Hunt is back, and this time, he's taking us on a rollercoaster ride that's nothing short of exhilarating. "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" not only lives up to the hype but surpasses it with a breathtaking fusion of action, suspense, and intrigue. This latest installment in the iconic franchise is a resounding success that keeps the adrenaline pumping from start to finish.

1. Tom Cruise at His Finest: Tom Cruise reprises his role as Ethan Hunt and shows us why he's the undisputed king of action cinema. At 60 years old, Cruise performs stunts that will leave your jaw on the floor. From death-defying freefalls to intense hand-to-hand combat, Cruise's commitment to his craft is unmatched.

2. Heart-Pounding Action Sequences: "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" boasts some of the most heart-pounding action sequences in the franchise's history. Whether it's a high-speed motorcycle chase through the narrow streets of a foreign city or a skydiving stunt that defies gravity, every moment is a visual treat.

3. Intriguing Plot and Twists: The film keeps you guessing at every turn. The plot is a labyrinth of espionage, double-crosses, and high-stakes missions that will leave you on the edge of your seat. The unexpected twists and turns add depth to the story, making it more than just a series of action scenes.

4. Strong Supporting Cast: The ensemble cast, including Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg, and Rebecca Ferguson, delivers standout performances. They bring depth and humor to their characters, adding a layer of camaraderie that has become a hallmark of the franchise.

5. Incredible Locations: "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" takes us on a global journey, featuring stunning locales from around the world. The cinematography beautifully captures the essence of each destination, enhancing the cinematic experience.

6. Pulse-Pounding Score: The musical score by Lorne Balfe elevates the intensity of the action sequences and keeps you engaged throughout the film.

7. High-Stakes Espionage: The stakes have never been higher, and the IMF team faces a truly menacing antagonist. The cat-and-mouse game between Ethan Hunt and his nemesis is nothing short of a cinematic masterpiece.

8. Mind-Blowing Gadgets: The film is brimming with futuristic gadgets and espionage tools that will make James Bond jealous. Each gadget plays a crucial role in the unfolding of the plot, making for a fun and gadget-packed adventure.

9. The Legacy Continues: "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" pays homage to the franchise's legacy while pushing the envelope for what action cinema can achieve. It's a testament to the enduring appeal of the Mission Impossible series.

In conclusion, "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" is a mesmerizing blend of action, suspense, and intrigue that keeps you hooked from the opening scene to the closing credits. With Tom Cruise at the helm, the movie reaches new heights in the action genre. It's a breathtaking, high-octane thrill ride that cements the franchise's place in cinematic history. Don't miss this electrifying installment that deserves every bit of its 9-star rating!

9.title: Mission Impossible Movies are the Best!
9.content: Mission impossible movies are action packed! I wasn't not disappointed one bit in seeing another fine addition to the six movies already made. Each one brings its new challenges to Ethan hunt and his team and they do not fail to deliver visually satisfying car chases with just the right amount of white knuckle escapes that make you feel like your in the back seat of the escape. Awesome directing and overall an exemplary production. Definitely recommend you see this movie. The visuals are incredible and the sounds/ music and sound effects are amazing. 9.title: Thrilling Action and Outstanding Performances
9.content: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a thrilling addition to the franchise, packed with the plot twists you would expect. Clocking in at close to 3 hours, the film manages to hold your attention from start to finish. Director Christopher McQuarrie masterfully weaves a complex narrative that remains surprisingly easy to follow, ensuring that you're fully immersed in the story. Tom Cruise's performance is nothing short of exceptional, showcasing his commitment to the role. Despite being part one, the movie tells a self-contained story that feels satisfying, yet it leaves you craving for more. 9.title: Tom Cruise is aging like fine wine.

The rest of the supporting cast does what the role asks of them to, to support Tom Cruise and fill some space while he does some awesome things on screen that blows our mind off.

The story is predictable, With all the AI talk in the real world, reel world MI takes it up a notch. The stunts are anything but predictable and there was a surprising amount of comedy added that sat quite well with me.

9.title: And this was just part 1!!
9.content:
Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning (2023)

Mission Impossible: Fallout is undoubtedly my favorite entry and while this one didn't reach those heights, it managed to stand well enough as it's own film while dedicating a big portion of the narrative for setting up Part 2. What I find most incredible about this entry is how they managed to land the film smack in the middle of all the A. I. craze. They began filming back in 2020, when there wasn't a whiff of Chat GPT and now as the whole world is obsessed with A. I. taking over humanity, we get this action packed adventure with world ending stakes.

In this Mission Impossible, Ethan Hunt and his team must recover a set of specific advanced keys that hold the secret to a highly sophisticated Artificial Intelligence. All the powerful countries and criminal organizations are eager to get thier hands on this super-tech, making the mission all the more deadly.

It was very easy to mess up this story and to make it convoluted but the creators managed to strike a good balance between building the narrative and energizing the experience with fantastic action. Everyone is anxious about the motorcycle "trick" but best believe that after the jump, there is an equally heart pounding action sequence. What's more, the action here is actually realistic and unpolished in terms of fighting, driving and choreography.

At this point we are familiar with the cast that got natural chemistry and works as a solid unit. Fortunately, the newcomer Haley Atwell is delightfully charismatic in her supporting role and manges to flawlessly fit into the team. What surprised me about the film is it's use of on point casual humor where it didn't feel overbearing and actually felt funny.

From the weaknesses, the film does feel stretched out at times in terms of explaining things. Also the two agent characters felt like a nuisance instead of adding tension or value to the story. Asides from that, the movie looks beautiful, the action is well filmed and as always, the music is spot on. Special props for Tom Cruise to be doing all this at the age of 60. Cinematic experience is highly recommended!

9.title: An incredible experience that words won't be able to describe.
9.content:
Tom Cruise has done it yet again.

I honestly doubt we should be surprised by his ingenuity at the point, he's THAT good.

The Mission Impossible movies have been around since I was 6 months old, and have never once failed to entertain me.

In 2001, I was in awe of Tom riding a bike across a flaming bridge, hair and jacket blowing away in the wind like there's no tomorrow.

In 2010, we were all gossiping away about seeing glimpses of Tom as he did the Burj Khalifa stunt, and it was my first real memory of seeing a movie being shot.

And now in 2023, I am CUSSING myself out for being too lazy to go to downtown toronto for the premiere screening, as Tom himself decided to show up at that specific location. DAMN IT LOL

MI-Dead Reckoning Part 1 is not only a fantastic movie, but somehow manages to retain the impossible element of the movie's title, even after 27 years.

The direction, visual style and plot are all perfectly in sync with one another, and while there are times when it felt slightly rushed, I was too invested in the movie to be bothered at all. (It is part 1 of 2 anyway)

Tom still has his incredible stage presence, and so do the other characters in the film.

It does feel like this franchise is coming to an end, and I cannot wait to watch the next one.

Unlike Spiderverse 2, which got only kids excited, this nailed the cliffhanger storyline it was clearly aiming for and kept us all on the edge of our seats throughout.

I don't want to talk about the plot, I feel you should experience this film without knowing anything about it.

The only negative thing I would say is that it isn't the best mission impossible film. When you bring in a cliffhanger, it leaves things unresolved(as they should be), but that also makes you feel like there is much more to be seen, and as such the movie will feel incomplete and a little rushed at times as mentioned above.

It doesn't mean the movie is bad by any means though. It's downright incredible, and Tom is shining brighter than ever.

Please go and watch this movie, you will not be disappointed unless you think marvel = cinema.

9.content:
After having watched successive "blockbuster" failures during the summer, we finally have one that delivers in every category.

Mission Impossible is once again at the top of its game as it is packed with incredible action sequences never seen before, an intriguing story that leaves you on the edge of your seat, great cast and great CGI that has been lacklustre on so many recent big budget films.

9.title: Best Mission Impossible yet.
9.content:
I slept on this and am writing the review the next day... but this was fantastic.

I'll get some negatives out the way first, it starts off REALLY slow, and I was worried as to where this was going. Also, wasn't a massive fan of some of the camera work, way too many extreme close ups in every talking scene.

Tom Cruise - Ethan Hunt is back again for another mission, and it seems as if age is finally catching up to Cruise. He still does his fair amount of action and stunts, but doesn't have anywhere near as much to do as previous installments.

Hayley Atwell - Grace is introduced in this film as a talented pick-pocket, and Atwells performance is fantastic. Beautiful woman with a great performance and has really good chemistry with Cruise.

Pom Klementieff - She plays Paris, a French assassin who works for villain, Gabriel. I LOVED her performance in this, but she hardly said a thing. She said maybe three sentences, and just grunted, barked, and groaned throughout her crazy performance. Now, Paris 100% feels like someone you would see in the John Wick films, she has a very unique style which I'd love to see more of, and I was so relieved when I heard the worst "there's a pulse". Really hoping she has much more to say and do in Dead Reckoning part 2.

Simon Pegg & Ving Rhames - They're not in the film much, the do have a few scenes but not massively involved.

After sleeping on this.... I loved the film, but... I do think on another day I might have been frustrated with it.

All that being said, this is by far the BEST Mission Impossible film to date. This franchise gets better and better.

9/10.

9.title: McQuarrie and Cruise hit the bullseye dead on
9.content:
Watched this in IMAX. Brilliant experience.

Tom Cruise and Christopher McQuarrie deliver again with perhaps their most accomplished work yet; Dead Reckoning Part One is a glorious spectacle of pure adrenaline shot through with emotion and a dreadful sense of mortality that elevates this from the typical popcorn action flick. One of the great problems of the modern thriller is how to adopt the international superspy to a time where technology is king. McQuarrie's screenplay deals with that with aplomb, twisting together plot threads with increasing complexity and pulling everything right with suspense. It is perhaps one of the great screenplays, a perfect combination of ruthlessly efficient dialogue, flowing action sequences that naturally introduce themselves and move with the emotion of the characters, and a pace that takes one in the hand and blasts off until you can never let go. Star-studded throughout with great performances, Tom Cruise nevertheless stands out, if that were ever in question. Subtle emotion, comedy, all-out action, he does it all, so much so that you wonder if, at this point, Tom Cruise is Ethan Hunt in reality as well. The visuals are death-defying, quite literally, although the necessity of CGI to remove the stunt team's safety equipment is perhaps one of the only minor gripes with this movie. Action sequences are staged with a manic joy and a steady hand all in one, and the only major issue this movie has is the length of one or two such set pieces, where the shock value wears off and the occasional quip has flown past. This is not to say that the movie doesn't have proper slower beats, it does, and handles them quite well, although it must be said that those scenes rely more on the emotional rapport we already enjoy with old characters, and on the considerable skills of Rebecca Ferguson, Ving Rhames, and Hayley Atwell. These scarcer moments are perhaps one of the few weaker points in the movie, where it feels that maybe some action would've been better off traded for more character work to improve the emotional complexity of the characters. Christopher McQuarrie's direction occasionally hams things up just a tad too much, with several scenes that felt just slightly too silly and the occasional lapse in editing, but these are minor issues in what is perhaps the best action movie Tom Cruise has ever made. And to think it's just the first half of the story.

9.title: This film has set the expectations very high for Part Two!!
9.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is an action spy film directed by Christopher McQuarrie. The film stars an ensemble cast of Tom Cruise, Hayley Atwell, Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg, Rebecca Ferguson, Vanessa Kirby, Esai Morales, Pom Klementieff, Mariela Garriga and Henry Czerny.

Ethan Hunt and the IMF team must track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens all of humanity if it falls into the wrong hands. With control of the future and the fate of the world at stake, a deadly race around the globe begins. Confronted by a mysterious, all-powerful enemy, Ethan is forced to consider that nothing can matter more than the mission -- not even the lives of those he cares about most

This film is the seventh installment of the Mission Impossible series.

Mission Impossible is probably a film series which always sets the expectation very high and never disappoints and the same is with this film. The film has some top notch action scenes, heart pounding stunts, stunning visuals and a captivating story line which will keep you engrossed from the start till the very end.

When it comes to Mission Impossible the first and foremost expectation is it's action scenes and the film no where disappoints be it rooftop chases, car chases or the most iconic jumping off from a cliff on a bike. All these adrenaline pumping scenes will keep you on the edge of your seats.

The plot of the film is great and execution is superb, the film will keep a very tight grip on the viewers and will not like to even blink the eyes in anticipation of not missing anything.

Acting is another strong aspect of the film as all the characters were very impressive and will keep you engaged.

Screenplay of the film is top notch with superb cinematography, superb music and great VFX. The climax of the film is equally great and sets the bar very high for the second part.

A must must watch film.

9.title: He did it again!
9.content:
Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning (Part1) - The 7th instalment of the globe trotting IMF team with Ethan's loyal returning team Luther & Benji, even Agent Eugene Kittridge makes a return who appeared way back in Brian De Palma's first movie in 1996.

We now have a new foe turned alliance with Grace 'Hayley Atwell' putting in a brilliant performance.

The plot is smart and sophisticated, action is fluent, a little gritty and a feel of the first movie, it's brilliantly well paced throughout with the usual Cruise doing all his own death defying stunts, it's the perfect Summer Blockbuster, brilliant!

9.title: True sense of the Summer Blockbuster
9.content:
The people raving about this film have said what I'd like to say already. Mainly points that Tom Cruise had kept cinema alive two years on the bounce now. The hype around these films are so well done on press tours and the biggest selling point is that this action star is somehow performing incredible mind bending stunts 40 years into his film career.

Dead Reckoning is a very busy film in terms of plot devices as well as its action. I won't delve far into the plot although just to say essentially the main villain is A. I- which considering the script was written before all this chat gpt stuff, seems incredibly prescient in todays times. Really scary actually!

We have returning characters who are all on top form and they all seem to be revelling their roles, most of which Pom Klementieff. Her role is a caricature of a antagonist/hench-person but she really is menacing it's fantastic.

When the title card appears 25 minutes into the film, part of you thinks, is this going to be a slog and run out of steam. But as the train sequence begins in the latter third of the movie it's almost a metaphor for this film picking up pace more and more and running along like a freight train- it more accurately- An orient express that hasn't got brakes!

What's so refreshing about these films and the partnership of Tom Cruise and Mcquarrie is that you know what you're watching, or at least a lot of it is all practical. They're all on location, performing their own stunts, ads minimal cgi added to make it all look as real as possible. It's truly exhilarating. Not that I'm about to slag off other big films and franchises, but oftenly the last 15 or so years a lot of action films you see, a lot of what you're watching is blue/green screen and cgi, it looks often like a mess and so much is going on you can't even focus properly.

I'm going to seek this out a second time so I can watch it on an Imax screen! I hope everyone else tries to see it on the big screen as well.

9.title: Had high expectations which were definitely met
