6.title: This might self-destruct
6.content:
There is such a thing as doing too much.

After Fallout which was tantalising with some tender moments, Dead Reckoning feels like colour by numbers with Tom pretty much in every frame.

The action sequences seem to need the the flimsiest of excuses to get going. Sure, there are some cool bits but we are well into John Wick-Italian Job-Bourne-Fast&Furious-Bond territory with rehashed Mission antics.

What's new? An attempt at pathos (Death in Venice) with a convoluted, self-important script.

I still hope they bring it home in Part 2 but am now prepared for Mission to stutter towards the finishing line.

6.title: Weak and complacent directing
6.content:
I am not going to watch part 2 of this double. During the whole movie it's pretty clear the actors are not in the same room. One in focus and others in a haze, close up after close up never a wide shot. Sometimes the proportions don't even match. And what to say about Tom Cruise. Botox rubber face galore, his face looks paralyzed. I sat through the whole movie hence the 6 albeit a weak six.

This weak and annoying way of making movies with no wide shots and once there is a wide shot, it's computer generated. I must say, The CGI is pretty bad in this movie. How come a movie like The Fifth Element, one of my favorites, has equivalent cgi or better even. It's from 1997 for freaks sake. Spend your money on something else.

6.title: Poor story/ writing! However Action, filmography and stunts (Most) were amazing.
6.content:
Love the franchise, filmography insane, characters are amazing (Par Miss Captain America - good acctress just poor writing).

So many loop holes and just ruined the focus on the story.

They are the best minds and strategic team on the planet but they couldn't even think to hide a couple of guns close to operation locations?... So use a sword instead, and to add spin in circles fighting too!.?!

Then no one ever wanted to use a gun again in the movie, which would have stopped or solved most problems. Even a guy holding a gun says to his mate kill her!? You have the gun in your hand!

Never written a review before but damn this movie just really failed for the franchise. Shame about the writing, love all other parts and massive respect t to the team but seriously, it was like watching a standard 80s movie full of holes.

Hope they fix it for the next one. P.s please don't over do the motorbike cliff stunt on advertising. It's awesome we get it but doesn't need to be the only thing we see for 6 months before it is released.

6.title: Tedious
6.content:
In a nutshell: Car chase would never end. Tedious Plot ridiculous. So many plot turns you finally give up.

Scene at beginning where all the players get cryptic, short sentences. No one could stream together a paragraph of dialogue?

How many villains were there? I lost count and stopped caring. Who is doing what to whom?

Train scene: see car chase comment.

Women were super good at fighting every bad guy there was. But uh oh, couldn't beat the middle aged slow villain.

Dead come back alive to save hero. Obviously writers boxed themselves into a corner.

Editing. Do they know the definition? Long movie and repetitive.

And the famous scene of riding off a cliff and opening a parachute....done 30 years or so ago in James Bobd movie. Except skis were used.

6.title: Put a Ch1ck In It and Make it Lame!
6.content:
Sat down with my husband to watch this much awaited movie on Paramount+ and we were so disappointed.

A meandering script with pacing issues and even as a woman I found there were far too many poorly chosen, uninspiring female characters coupled together with Ethen Hunt's character being purposely weakened to accommodate all the women makes this the weakest and least cool movie of the franchise.

I have loved every previous Mission Impossible movie but sadly this one is overly long with poor characters, a weak storyline and comedic misses. Paramount took a beating at the box office and I can see why.

Let's hope the final outing is much better and a return to form.

The last hour is the better part but still not enough to rate it more than a lackluster 6/10.

6.title: A basic action film with spectacular stunts.
6.content:
Disappointed with the classic action movie scenario where the protagonist still has to defeat the threat. The feel of the previous Mission Impossible was much better, and I just couldn't get into the film. The fight scenes with the film's antagonist were a dud for me, far too slow and lacking in fluidity.

Nevertheless, the stunts performed by Tom Cruise are truly impressive. I literally got shivers when he fell into the void with his motorbike. The one-handed driving is also a very good scene. It's always impressive to see an actor of his age doing all that. I'm still looking forward to the next instalment in the saga, hoping for a film with a better plot.

6.title: Reckoning Mission!
6.content:
Like the missions before it, Mission 7 promises a lot, but things are slower this time. The movie almost hits 3hrs runtime and the plot seems promising, but the action scenes are not as great as the last few movies.

Tom Cruise manages to once again prove an exemplary stunt man, especially in the final sequence, involving a train, which is probably one of the greatest I've seen.

I feel this overlong plot could have been told in one movie, but Part II comes out next year, so it's not quite the end. The plot mostly revolves around chasing down keys that make up one, which is the start of something possibly leading into Part II, but the pace is very slow in this lengthy movie, which is why I feel the second part could have just been squeezed into this one.

This movie is another example of why making sequels longer does not always work. There is nothing worse than rushing a plot, but the same can be said for slowing a plot down.

6.title: Don't expect much and you'll enjoy it.
6.content:
It was okay. WAY too long at 2 hours and 43 minutes. Too much hearkening back to previous movies and unnecessary melodramatic dialogue. Easily could've shaved a half hour off the run time with better editing and a tighter script. Still, the action scenes were fun and I did enjoy myself for the most part. The villain being an AI was both novel and topical. The new female characters stole the show, especially Hayley Atwell, the thief with a heart of gold, and Pom Klementieff who plays a psychotic assassin. It was a decent piece of summer "turn your brain off for a couple hours" spectacle that you'll watch once and never think about again.

I gotta say, though... Christopher McQuarrie has become such a disappointment. When he made his directorial debut in 2000 with "The Way of the Gun", I was blown away. To this day, I love that little film. If you had told me, back then, that he would go on to write and direct a bunch of unimpressive action fluff like Mission Impossible, Jack Reacher, the Top Gun sequel and the Mummy reboot? I would've been like "pffft, that sucks." And it does. It really does, because he could've been a great auteur director instead of just another paint-by-numbers studio hack.

6.title: Lost in spectacle: Did not meet the bar for an MI series
6.content:
"Disappointing Deviation from the Series' Essence" Ethan Hunt's transformation from a covert agent to an infallible savior is emblematic of the issues plaguing this installment.

Regrettably, despite my deep affection for this franchise, this film exhibits a plethora of missteps.

Excessive mindless action, manipulative attempts to evoke emotion through shallow relationships, subpar writing, and a lackluster plot progression all mar this film. It could have been much better if they had focused more on Character building instead of the futile and stretched action scenes. There were particularly scenes which didn't deserve so much time like the car chase scene and the train fall.

Overall this movie tarnishes the once-authentic Mission Impossible series, casting a shadow on its reputation. It's so painful to give a 6 star to Tom Cruise movie.

6.title: I feel insulted by the childish plot
6.content:
Yes yes, this movie packs great action scenes, jaw dropping car chases, and mind blowing scenery. But the back story is really stupid. My 4yo could have come up with a better story.

The AI villain "Entity" blurring the reality and fiction is somewhat relatable. But how it was released and how to kill it with a key are like a really bad joke.

Some of the characters and their actions also do not make any sense.

Even though this is an action movies some scenes contain longer dialogues about the stupid story that you get bored to death.

Overall, I wish the screenwriters and director would have spent a few more percent of their time to develop a better story and more relatable characters.

6.title: Ilsa Losing Fight On Bridge Was Impossible!
6.content: I know it was in the script for Ilsa to lose that fight, but it was a ridiculous scenario of writing to suggest me to believe it! When those very writers wrote her kicking dozens people @$$ with ease! I'm sorry but its like Black Widow losing to Robin! I didn't like this at all! What a let down of hope for a simple emotional tug at the heart for ratings! 6.title: Yet more of the same, but more bling
6.content:
Im sorry that I went to see this film. It is a couple of hours of my life the I wont get back again.

It is much the same as all of the rest of these films. Once again Ethan Hunt and his crew get shot at a million times and magically none of the bullets seem to hit them. Improbable car chases and crashes never seem to hurt them for long. No broken bones or whiplash for our action heroes.

Im tired of this sort of rubbish coming out of Hollywood.

This film is ok for teenagers who are only looking for action and special effects. Anyone else should definitely look elsewhere for a good better film, one with a plausible plot and some actual character development and realistic drama.

6.title: Not done it dirty
6.content:
I'm really conflicted about only giving MIDR 6/10 but that is only because, after having never seen any of the IMF films previously, I've just watched them all prior to watching this latest on at the cinema. The 4th, 5th and 6th instalments are so incredibly brilliant that Dead Reckoning had a very high bar to jump over.

On the plus side, the humour was spot on when it needed to be. The car chase through Rome, although overly long, was fun and the Pom Klementiofs character had bags of menace chasing the little Fiat in that Hummer. The main antagonist, Gabriel, was an intriguing baddie and, like others have said, would have been much, much better if he'd been a material manifestation of the AI. Having Gabriel as a pseudo-human would have been a great piece of sci-fi/tech writing and would have been in line with how the IMF films have pushed the envelope with avant-garde technology and gadgets.

On the negative side, it is too long. Considering this really is a 5.5hr film split into two, that's preposterous. It's either a blatant cash-grab or it's very poor writing and editing. I found the character of Grace really poorly written and acted, but I think the acting was poor because the character was poor and we spent a LOT of time with Grace when we wanted Ethan, Ilsa, Benjy and Luther if we're being honest.

So yes, plenty of good with a few bad bits. I'd say this one was my least favourite if you exclude everyone's least favourite (John Woo's Impossible Mission II) but I am more excited for the final part of this than say, Dune II.

6.title: After the Mcguffin !
6.content:
They dont even try anymore... they just assume that Tom would carry the tension with his intense stares and run fast enough to catch our attention.

The scenery, costume, music, direction, action are all top notch, as we would suspect from a MI movie. They are on rails to deliver something entertaining. But they rely way to much on the Cruise effect and the story is weak at best. The villain is way less interesting than than the last one. He is generic bad with pure hatred for humanity. No twist, no reveal, he is just after the eradication of everything for the sake of it. The famous stunt was so marketed that we only wonder when it will happen and when it does we say ''Oh... there it is.... nice''.

Tom assemble his crew and they all run for an hour after a Mcguffin. The fact that this is a two part movie is playing against itself. We dont have the usual payoff.

The MI franchise is usually a machine so well oiled , we forget how ridiculous it can be and we let our self being carried by the action. Here however, this movie is just the setup for the part 2 and we feel we didnt had the whole pie. This story isnt worth to be tell in this new anticlimactic format. It is basic at best. And there is enough downtime to let us think about the plot. Which is bad.

I am still curious about the end, but i hope it will be better than this generic action movie. Without the MI brand and the Cruise effect, it would have been lost and forgotten, and fairly so.

6.title: Decently Entertaining
6.content:
Mission Impossible's Dead Reckoning Part One brings back the iconic Tom Cruise as the fearless Ethan Hunt, joined by an exceptional ensemble cast including Hayley Atwell, Rebecca Ferguson, Vanessa Kirby, and a host of other talented actors. While Tom Cruise's performance continues to be exemplary, the film's story falls short of its potential. It delves into a familiar topic that has been explored countless times before, leaving us yearning for something fresh and unpredictable to reignite the franchise's excitement.

Amidst the film's shortcomings, one cannot overlook the brilliantly executed action scenes that do make an impact. While there are fewer action sequences compared to the previous instalment, the ones present leave us on the edge of our seats, especially the heart-pounding car chase that adds an adrenaline rush to the viewing experience.

However, not all aspects of the film deliver on their promise. The scenes set in Venice, which held great promise, fail to reach their full potential and could have been more thrilling and engaging. Nevertheless, the film manages to retain its allure, thanks to the unwavering charisma of Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt.

One of the film's most significant drawbacks is its excessive length, as it could have benefitted from tighter editing to maintain a more captivating pace and keep the audience fully invested in the unfolding events.

In conclusion, Mission Impossible's Dead Reckoning Part One offers a mix of highs and lows. Tom Cruise's stellar performance and some standout action scenes add excitement and spectacle to the film, but the repetitive storyline and lack of fresh ideas dampen its overall impact. Despite its flaws, fans of the franchise will likely find enough enjoyment to appreciate the latest instalment.

6.title: MI turns into Fast and Furious until it finally comes back
6.content:
I mean, you have to love the final act. That whole last sequence that lasts for about an hour is breathtakingly great. Everything about it works so well it makes me think there was a perfect action movie here, with a little more self-restraint.

But as it is, the 2h47m runtime gets in the way, with way too long scenes of boring exposition, flat characters that the actors never find a way to make interesting with the poor dialogue they are given to work with, and a villain that by design can't possibly be amazing.

Regardless of the score, it is a movie that does justify paying to see it on theaters though, and that already means a lot nowadays.

6.title: Lord of the Impossible: Dark Fate
6.content:
The action sequences of the movie was reasonably good, although seen before in film, tv or documentaries like say Jurassic Park/World or Evel Knieval. However, the movie was way too long, had draggy sequences of meeting dialogs of intense men giving expositions as well as poor excuses or slap stick to lead to action sequences.

The tech in this MI movie does not feel smart and not keeping up with or ahead of times. Its feels old school with a bit of slight of hand which felt awkward and misplaced like clowning around. The evil entity corrupted AI is poorly visualised (a little like a rip-off of the face of robot in Lost in Space), explained and defined.

The editing was not tight and script and visual storyboarding of scenes did not seem well produced. Everything seems to be going everywhere and everybody is chasing around something like an artifact in a Indiana Jones movie. Some characters seem unnecessary and too many damsels in distressed and goofy duh moments rather than smarts when dealing difficult situations. The characters also did not seem to gel together well or not appear invested in the moment like always dressed prim and proper and in view like they are in a talk show.

I am not too sure this is due to COVID-19 messing the production. Also, the close ups of Tom Cruise were a bit painful with his hair not appearing properly made for the close shots like dry and poorly trimmed and styled.

It had the parodish feeling of Terminator: Dark Fate and the length that felt like an extended Lord of the Rings film DVD/Bluray release.

Maybe, I haven't got over the Top Gun: Maverick's surprisingly refined production that I blew my mind which I unfortunately had expected from this new Tom Cruise release.

6.title: Drops the ball for me
6.content: It's not a bad movie. The action is terrific. It's slick. However, the whole thing feels very contrived, as though the action scenes were conceived first and then the plot warped to encompass them. I guess this is an approach frequently adopted in this genre of movies, but in the case of 'Dead Reckoning' it is so 'clunky' that you can easily identify the welds. As for the "who's got the key" storyline? More like a 60s episode of The Man from Uncle. 'Fall Out' was a masterpiece - this falls well short of that for me. And as for the decision to kill a certain individual? I'm sure they had their reasons but the franchise is weaker for it. When the MI ride finally ends, I predict 6 will be the flagship. Hopefully 8 will improve on 7 but it has a lot of misconceived baggage to carry forward...

6.title: Ssshh
6.content: Lots of whispering. Solemn tones. Hopefully part 2 will be better. The middle sequence was quite dull, and the gravity of the entity was not lost on anyone. So much so that they couldn't raise a voice higher than a whisper. The film wasn't great but watchable. And there was too much sleight of hand going on. And I wish I could visit the landmarks featured in this film at the times they visited, instead of being stuck in massive traffic jams and interminable queues. But Tom and Co seemed to get around it ok. The start of the film was actually quite silly and the Cillian really quite predictable.

6.title: Predictably entertaining
6.content: This is not a bad movie, in the sense that none of the movies in the series are bad. But aren't they all sort of the same? Like - almost EXACTLY the same? Plenty of action, maybe too much. Nice to see Esai Morales and Cary Elwes getting 2020's work, as both are quality actors. But Hollywood, for the love of God, can you stop forcing the "tough chick" character on every action movie??? It's just not realistic to watch these 110 pound ladies taking out men twice their size or more. It wouldn't happen and it makes the film lose a lot of credibility. Trained or not it wouldn't help against men who are also trained and physically a LOT stronger. That's just fact and observation. Having stated that this is all fiction and there are plenty of other ridiculous things in the movie, but for the most part it works (or is at least slightly north of watchable). Could and probably should have been 15-20 minutes shorter.

6.title: What you see is what you get.
6.content:
Please forgive me for stating the obvious, but this is a franchise movie, number seven in one of the most successful movie franchises of all time. The Mission franchise wouldn't have been as successful as it is without Tom Cruise, and, after seven installments, it is probably fair to say that Tom Cruise wouldn't have been as big a star as he is without it.

Unless you have been living under a rock, you know what this franchise is about, and thus you know pretty well what you are going to get. Complaining about the fact that you're getting exactly what the posters, the trailers and the previous six movies would have you expect seems not only pointless, but almost unfair.

I'm not a fan of Tom Cruise. I have always found him to be a way bigger star than he is an actor. But he is a true professional, and you can rest assured that he's gone all-in to deliver a movie that the fans will love.

You could say that the characters are fairly one-dimensional, even cartoonish in some cases, and that some of the one-liners reflect that, but that is true of most franchise films. And while there's room for male actors who are not lookers, there is no room for women who aren't gorgeous. Again, this is not specific to the Mission franchise.

You could also say that you have seen almost all of the scenes before, in other movies. Think of any action movie cliché, and you're likely to find it in this movie. But done better and more expensively than in many other films.

So while this is not my favorite franchise, it is a very well-made movie, and I think the fans will love it. It kept me alert for two hours and forty-three minutes, and that's certainly not bad. And then it's over. You don't think about it afterwards. What you see is what you get. But what you see is quite impressive, and, sometimes, quite enjoyable even for people who are not huge Mission fans.

6.title: Franchise Fatigue
6.content: Again starring Tom Cruise, Dead Reckoning is the 7th film in the Mission Impossible franchise. The film is the first of a two part end to the franchise, but at nearly 3 hours long it feels far too long. The action scenes and stunts as always are exceptional, and there are a lot of them. The problem is the plot. The script is convoluted, badly paced and far from gripping. Esai Morales of NYPD Blue fame is a good actor but is sorely wasted as the main villain and i never got fully involved in the supposed personal battle between him and Cruise which is meant to drive the emotional core of the film. There is nothing here we havn't seen before in previous Mission Impossible films and the whole venture feels like film making by numbers. Ultimately Dead Reckoning feels like a big disappointment and is as memorable as a computer printout. Hopefully the 2nd part will end the series on a high.

6.title: Ethan Hunt - or James Bond??
6.content: MI is becoming increasingly like the James Bond movies. There's too much endless chasing, and I'd like to see more of the quieter intelligence and espionage element that we saw in the very first MI film. The plotlines are very repetitive now, and a bit stale. The chemistry is still solid between the three main characters (Ethan, Luther, Benji) though, with some witty and fun banter, so all is not lost! While I'm at it - the MI theme tune is one of the best in the business; it drives the story forward very nicely - but that's practically disappeared now too. For me - more atmosphere, investigation, and intrigue, less racing around the streets with the obligatory female hanging out of Hunt's character... that's so last decade.

6.title: All Seemed very rushed I blame Covid
6.content: Not your typical mission impossible all seems very rushed and poorly directed which is strange as it's the same director from fallout which was the best one of the series, can only think that the constant shutdowns due to Covid are to blame for the final outcome, still a good watch but nowhere near what the previous 6 movies produced. A complete lack of chemistry and direction in most actors performances they all seem to take turns in producing their dialogue and it just doesn't have the same energy or tense moments as fallout it's like u know what's gonna happen and it's all very predictable unlike all the others which keep u on the edge of ur seat throughout.

6.title: Good, not great
6.content:
I suppose I should preface this by stating the inevitable where if your going to split a film into two parts your always going to have a job making 'part 1' feel justified in being a standalone, recently we have seen a film do this right - Dune, and a film do it wrong - Fast X, and this is somewhere down the middle.

I'll give credit as I know the film encountered some great difficulties during production, owing to covid lock downs, so I can understand that the finished product may not have been exactly as Tom and Christopher invisioned it, alas there are quite a few jarring things that cannot be excused by production issues.

Tom is of course great as always, and as has been mentioned a million times over his stuntwork and acting is once again second to none, Atwell was great as the newcomer and stole every scene she was in asides from those shared with Kirby, having Kittrich back was good and I feel like he was one of better placed characters returning from previous films, played well once again by Czerny.

Unfortunately Benji and Luther felt like side characters here, ultimately due to the premise of the enemy actually bring a computer AI, which pretty much puts them out of the game by default. Fergusons return is very underwhelming and almost felt forced, after the end of Fallout where Hunts wife essentially gives him permission to go off with her, the advent of Grace suddenly seeming to establish herself as of equal standings to Hunt didnt land with me, and it of absolutely no surprise whatsoever when she was eventually killed off in what was a very poorly choreographed fight scene, which to be honest didn't actually make much sense and was badly shot.

Gabriel was good, but thus idea that he is somehow working for the entity, almost in sync with its "thought process" really didn't land for me, I think the idea was that we viewed them as counterparts to one overall enemy force but instead it felt like both were actually rather hindered by each other instead of complimentary which really took the edge off any real feeling of threat.

The two american cia guys (at least I think they were cia) were very jarring and didn't need to exist at all outside of the airport scene, I enjoyed Greg Davis despite his small part, but Shea Wighams character was terrible and totally miscast (was he supposed to be taken seriously?)

Talking of not making much sense, there was an over abundance of exposition where it wasn't required, one of the greatest things about the mission impossible franchise is that it DOESNT spell it out for you, and this makes figuring it out for yourself far more rewarding, and queues up great twists, there is none of that in this, intact I dont think there was a single plot twist whatsoever, or at least nothing that wasn't instantly obvious a mile off.

The car chase sequence was cool for stunts, but didn't actually need to be in the film whatsoever, it just served as a platform to setup Gabriel's henchwoman Paris and to get away with some stunts, also if they really did drive that armoured truck off the balcony why the hell didn't they show it?

Circling back round to stunts, the main stunt of the movie (which is great) you have already seen in its entirety in the trailer, which jarred me quite a lot, I think one of the best things about the stunts in the previous outings was that you follow them from beginning to end, in this one it's 10 minutes of occasionally cutting to Tom riding up a mountain on a bike, to the stunt you have already seen, to him (completely out of the blue) being on the train at exactly the right place and time, I know this is mission impossible but that jumped the shark.

The train sequence is good, particularly the last bit, but it's too long, also if they really did crash that train the choices of how that were shot were terrible, sure a single snap cut to an on-board of it heading down mid-drop would make sense, but not having a wide shot was a really bad decision.

The alleyway fight that seems to be getting a lot of praise failed to capture me to be honest, you couldn't see what the hell was going on and Tom could of very easily got out of their almost instantly, also there is no reason why he didn't kill Paris, its purely because its required that she be alive at the end.

Maybe I'm being overcritical, but I'm being honest, this is a good fun action film, it isn't a mission impossible film though and unless there are elements in part 2 that relate to unforseen elements of this one its essentially filler, while we wait for the grand finale, this entire film could of been condensed into 30 minutes pretty much and stuck on the front of part 2 and it wouldn't of made any difference.

Where John Wick 4 was two films cut down and condensed into one, this is what should of been one film strung out into two, and it shows.

6.5/10, and I would rank it 5th out of the 7 films so far.

6.title: The length ruined it for me
6.content:
It started off terrific!!

I was engaged and loving the storyline which was compelling. Even the car chase was highly entertaining in the tiny yellow Fiat.

I usually go to the movies for the story and not for the big action scenes and here it worked for me, until it didn't.

At 2 hours and 43 minutes, i enjoyed the first 2 hours and would have rated this a 9.

The last 45 minutes move this to a 6 for me. The train action sequence was the demise and that's not to say it didn't have creativity and marvel at what was created, but it just keep going and going and going. I needlessly so, but I am not a teen or 20-something that probably ONLY cares about the action sequences.

So for me, this trend of 3 hour movies will keep me from going to more movies at the theatre. It really is impossible to sit that long no matter how captivating the movie. I know a lot of hard, hard work went into this and I do applaud everyone's efforts. This all may be a moot point with the writer's strike. I do love going to the movies.

Final thoughts, Haley Atwell is probably one of the most stunning female leads and a great addition to the series. Hopefully she has better luck than the other females in this franchise.

6.title: Gets a six for my reactions to some hackneyed (Octoberish) stuff
6.content:
The Red Octoberish submarine scene was predictable. And horses? In the desert with high-tech gear? C'mon, it should have been ATVs. But I guess the film needed traction in the "Arab" meme.

The "device" gadget that's key to saving humanity (once again) is boring and course it's a tried-and-true analog object. T Then the required crazy car-chase through Rome? With stairs and tiny old streets.

I actually exited before the finish - I mean, we know how this will end, right?

The film loses its way hopscotching all over and never locking in a time frame. The only constant of course is the immortal T Cruise. Kudos to production and Cruise for going film and theatrical opening. Hopefully part II will close the gaps.

6.title: Spectacular, But Plotless
6.content: There's an argument to be made that the Mission Impossible is the most consistently enjoyable franchise of its era, the second film notwithstanding. That having been said, this film does show signs of weariness despite the spectacle. The plot is scarcely worth bothering with, which is admittedly not the point fo these films; and it's trying to be of the moment with a focus on A. I., and allusions to post-truth politics. That the A. I. is imbued with what is close to quasi-mystical powers shows just how little we understand one of the big issues of our age; that the film doesn't understand either doesn't seem to matter. It's directed with a degree of flourish, and there's no doubt that the action sequences are viscerally thrilling and spectacular. But without any real stakes that we can relate to, it can feel a bit like Marvel's jeopardy-free excursions into the multiverse. The director said that when he and Cruise met to plan the film, they did so by deciding on the two biggest stunt sequences, and stiched the film around them - and it shows, in the film's lack of structure and genuine tension. But all that matters little when it looks so good and thrills so much. It's a blast, despite the faults.

6.title: The Sexy Sexagenarian hot on his heels
6.content:
The franchise standing on it's 7th installment, lot has changed, but one thing didn't ,Tom Cruise. Tom at the age of 34 started his iconic role of Agent Ethan Hunt on MI: 1 is now a sexagenarian at 61 and at this age his sheer will and enthusiasm to perform death defying action sequences all by himself is indescribable.

Now coming to the movie , the story is a bit weak and it didn't excite me personally.

I think, as Dead Reckoning was plagued by COVID they were unable to shoot all the intended scenes and hence decided to split it into two parts. But still due to the lack of proper editing the runtime of the movie was a bit longer than it was meant to be. Also speaking of editing the jump cuts of Tom Cruise on the motorbike that leads to the hyped jump from the mountain seemed to be very boring and lengthy

Coming to the story, The theme of AI going rogue began way back in 1968 with 2001 A Space Odyssey and later Age of Ultron. I watched the movie today and it's not even sticking to my mind. When I left the theatre I almost forgot that I just saw a movie,not even a memorable scene. But that was not the case with MI:1 and Ghost Protocol.

Eventhough I watched MI:1 and Ghost Protocol from TV the amount of excitement that it delivered was huge. Still I remember most of the scenes from those movies. Those are my favourite movies in the series.

The screen presence of the villain done by Esai Morales was commendable.

The action scenes especially the train sequence with Tom Cruise and Hayley Atwell was too dramatic and the VFX on those scenes were very evident.

It was the usual age old edge of the cliff sequence and one of the scenes reminded me of Paul Walker running on top of the bus that was about fall from a cliff on F&F 7.

There was no thrilling hand to hand combat scenes in this movie and the one on top of the train was too short. Most of the time the train was inside a tunnel . The fight sequence between Hayley Atwell and Rebeccca Ferguson with the villain also was very weak.

Overall part one is a watchable movie. Nothing exciting in my personal opinion.

The movie as a whole can be evaluated only after part two.

6.title: Disappointing, except the stunts
6.content:
There's some good things.

The stunts are great as always. However, some of them are great only because you know Cruise did it for real, not because what is on the screen in super inventive of fresh. Like a fight on the roof a train, a car chase in Rome, motocycles... I think we've seen all this. The only really fresh action scene is right at the end.

As a big plus, the theme is very current from the real world, a threat to humanity caused by AI.

List of bad things is far longer:

It's too long and filled with convoluted bad guy monologues, you can't keep track of their motives and eventually you'll just start ignoring the whole plot and waiting for the stunts.

The new character...by Hailey Atwell. I didn't like her. Nice face, cringey acting, annoying character. She didn't deserve Ethan Hunt's loyalty, after doing nothing but betraying him, over and over again, for small gains. I read Tom Cruise dated her in real life, I think this has clouded Tom's judgement. She shouldn't have gotten the part, or at least not this much screen time. I prefered Rebecca Fergusons character much more.

The worst thing, Atwell's character displaces the old team almost completely, and they are put to the sidelines. Also lines and scenes that were written to Simon Pegg for example, aren't as witty as usually. He had far less funny scenes or lines, than in previous parts.

Some parts are obvious CGI. I mean obvious to the eye.

Writers did a bad job, it's too silly (yet taking itself seriously), convoluted, artificially complicated and outlandish, even for a MI movie. They were never realistic, but they made some sense until now

Bad guys are not memorable at all, compared to Rogue Nation and Fallout.

Actually I hated this movie, mostly. Even when I loved MI series, minus part 2. MI series was on endless winning streak since part 3, I guess it had to end at some point.

They filmed during Covid restrictions, perhaps it had a negative effect on the creative energy on the set... the only movie worse in this franchise is part 2.

Perhaps Dead Reckoning Part II ties everything together, but I don't think it will. But now people can say the lack of satisfaction when the credits roll was due to it being just the first act. I'd say it's because of bad writing and Hailey Atwell messing it (and Tom's head) up.

6.title: A low point for the franchise
6.content:
Other reviewers have already pointed out everything that's wrong with the story and the characters and the writing in general.

Let me add this: the camerawork and editing in many scenes is simply terrible. The 180-degree rule is broken countless times during conversations, the camera cuts between differently angled shots of the same character while he's speaking (without intercutting reactions of other characters or anything like that) because why the hell not, and there are dutch angles everywhere and for no good reason... This is film school 101 stuff, really.

Solid action, but everything else feels subpar compared to the previous movies. It's the worst installment since M:I 2.

6.title: Good points and bad points
6.content:
I don't regret watching this blockbuster that delivers grand sequences. It's just somewhat ponderous at times. The entity - whatever. Too convoluted.

The good points. The train sequence towards the end is quite spectacular. The Rome car chase incorporates some familiar landmarks. How did they do it? Haley Atwell has some personality. Like to see her in the future.

Tom has aged naturally. No botox even!

Bad points: Takes itself too seriously. Entity is incomprehensible. 2 movies are unnecessary, just one would have been enough. Lengthy.

The way Rebecca was killed off seemed unnecessary. Why fight him? Why not have a better weapon?

6.title: The fellowship of the key
6.content:
The movie lacks interesting characters and character development. The directing is worse than in the last two installments, with sub-par camera work. There are less set pieces and they are not as well done. The action felt a bit over the top at times and the plot was hard to follow (or did it just not make any sense). This key seems to spawn in someone else's pocket whenever you blink your eyes.

I really enjoyed Fallout and I tried to like this one just as much but I just couldn't.

Regardless of all of that, I wasn't bored while watching as the close to 3 hours of runtime flew by quickly, which means I must've been entertained.

6.title: Lots of whining about a key.
6.content: All the ingredients for an action movie are there: chases, explosions, guns and some familiar hot spots. But now also endless whining about a key and an artificial intelligence in a submarine. This "entity" is described as supreme, but throughout the film remains little more than an abstract animation on some screens. It is not the supercomputer from Terminator 2. Characters are not given time to show the audience who they are. The viewer certainly does not have to think with this film, the storyline and characters are prefaced the entire time by the monologues of one of the omniscient actors. This movie is a heck of a long sit. Rarely did I find myself in the theater wishing the movie had ended.

6.title: Not bad but not good either...
6.content:
Let me just preface by saying that I've never watched any of the Mission: Impossible films prior to this one, so I'm not a fan (nor a hater) of the series. My review might be a little skewed due to me going to a late showing. I was honestly starting to fall asleep around the midway point, but was able to wake myself up and power through the rest of it. I might consider re-watching this in my local theater again or maybe when it comes to a streaming service, but I'll make sure to watch it when I'm not wanting to nod off.

Now, onto the actual review. This movie in short is... OK. I mean everything about this movie is just mid-tier at best; the acting, the action, the cast, etc. The biggest problem I have with this movie is that it felt incomplete. Of course, Dead Reckoning - Part 2 is supposed to be coming out so hopefully it gives me a sense of closure. I guess the setting/scenery is nice and I will hand it to Tom Cruise, him doing his own stunts is pretty cool.

6.title: I wanted to love it so much....
6.content:
MI has offered us everything the Bond Franchise hasn't over the last decade. Jaw dropping stunts (IMHO), favourable characters, better plot lines and villians and most importantly more entertainment.

All but one MI (I'll let you guess which!) has bumped up the expectation of a Summer Hollywood Blockbuster but MI:DR pt1 has fallen over it's length and demand for action set pieces. I love this franchise and was SO looking forward to the next (and final?) installment spread over 2 parts.

However, characters you have grown to love over the last few films are cast aside when this was an opportunity to round them off and say Goodbye. Hayley Atwell is thrown into the mix with little to no backstory. She is no Ilsa whom I am trying to recollect having more than 10 lines.

The club scene looks to been lifted from John Wick, during the same scene the dialogue is similar to that of the Matrix 2 (as in "what the hell is going on?").

I can't get behind the concept of the villian or their henchman despite how many times it's explained. There is a moment someone explains how he has made himself indepensible to the villian by holding onto a secret, which he then tells the villian's henchman...

20-30 mins could have been shaved from this movie with little to no effect on it's outcome. If anything I think more may have gone to see it at the theatres who might have been put off by it's length. This was the same opinion of others in my group.

Should you still go to see it? Yes. The effort taken over these set pieces is phenomenal. Some are very memorable. There are comedic moments you will enjoy too but for me Ghost Protocol remains the best in the franchise.

6.title: The weakest so far
6.content:
I'm a huge fan of the Mission: Impossible series, and while some movies are clearly better than others none of them have been outright bad. And this isn't either, but it swings closer to that precipice than any of the other films.

Dead Reckoning doesn't feel like one story split in two films, rather it feels like one movie streched into two films with no reason other than making twice as much money on it.

The characters are decent, but neither the central conflict or the stunts come across as especially impressive compared to earlier entries in the series. This movie commits the greatest sin a Mission: Impossible film could ever do: it's boring and void of tension or awe.

Again, this is not a terrible movie, but we've seen much better from this franchise in the past. As the end credits roll on this movie, I can only hope that this is a rare weakpoint and not the beginning of a downward spirals for a series of films that have always managed to stick the landing.

6.title: Huge MI fan, but this one is poor! Due to Covid?
6.content: Huge MI fan but this one story wise is poor, the AI supernatural aspect is just lame. You can tell because of the pandemic restrictions this film was maybe held back, hence loads of scenes of just awkward talking and not enough action. The previous MI fallout was absolutely amazing, peak of the franchise I think. This the script is poor, the story isn't good, and action isn't enough. However it has some good locations like Birmingham, Rome and Venice and many more. For city holidayers this is a treat, especially seeing Venice and Rome scenes. Also, Tom had a double serving of chicken tikka for this movie in Birmingham , and doubled his efforts to keep movie industry going during the pandemic and therefore I've added additional stars.

6.title: Action packed nonsense with Cruise as the new Bond
6.content:
Cruise is back, and he's almost as awesome as always.

First - the stunts are superb. Cruise took it upon himself to fill in the void that the Bond franchise left 20 something years ago (forgive me for not counting the Craig films) and he's doing an excellent job.

Second - don't look for intelligent dialogues, smart humor, or an interesting plot. This film's story is mostly coherent and that is enough. Especially when you have such shallow characters, which are mostly busy explaining to the audience how the action parts connect.

Third - although there were some nice talented additions to the cast, they were not really needed and felt like marketing stunts. Furthermore, one of the characters was artificially planted, and the plot twist which brought her in was really stupid and completely uncalled for.

Last but not least - The soundtrack was too much of everything: Far too loud, much too aggressive, and ridiculously melodramatic.

Altogether - 5.5/10. (I would have given a higher rank if the dialogue wasn't so infantile)

6.title: only for Tom Cruise
6.content:
I suppose, this is probably the first MI film that has brought in the concept of a sentient/AI and the last stunt sequence (which was anyway published on Youtube already) and the car chase sequence and the fight sequences in the train in the climax, that's all the film has and in between they just talk & talk for long periods of time.

The movie would've worked very well if they would've cut down the film by at least 20+ mins of sluggish talking sequences.

It's a watch for the man who isn't afraid to take risks with his life to entertain & thrill the audiences of his films even at the age of 50+, which is much appreciable.

Overall, it's a must-watch if you're a Tom Cruise fanboy but otherwise, it's an easy skip.

6.title: What Walt's Watching
6.content:
I think Simon Pegg's character, "Benji Dunn" summed up the 7th instalment in the Mission Impossible franchise best when he uttered these words, "Details get in the way".

And it's true with "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One" details do get in the way of this almost non-stop action, adventure, thriller under Christopher McQuarries' direction.

The McGuffin in this movie is a key made of two parts that unlocks a sentient computer called "The Entity" which is nefariously destroying the digital age.

Problem is your McGuffin is usually an object, event, or character in a story that lacks intrinsic importance, but serves to set and keep the plot in motion.

Meaning it can't also be your stories antagonist.

All I can say is I'm glad I wasn't playing a drinking game with the words "Key" or "Entity" in it or I would have died from alcohol poisoning.

Yeah it's not the greatest script from McQuarrie, Bruce Geller and Erik Jendresen, but it does feature some of the most amazing stunts.

Sure they've been done before in oooh let me think "The Great Escape" with Steve McQueen jumping fences on a motorcycle, the car chase in Rome, Italy in James Bond, Fast X etc, the latest Indiana Jones fight scene on top of the train, Jurassic Park cliff scene and lots of other movie references.

Talking trains even Agatha Christies stylings are up for grabs on this Orient Express train ride to hell.

By the way, train spotters don't cry for what happens to the train that appears to be a preserved Britannia class steam locomotive (curiously disguised as a French engine) in fact, it's actually a specially commissioned non-functioning stunt replica.

And if you get confused on how Rome suddenly becomes Venice with boats etc, it's because filming started in Venice on the same day Northern Italy locked down for COVID-19.

Production was hastily moved to Rome, only to be shut down again.

Gotta love a pandemic for messing up a movie shooting schedule.

The frequent delays caused by COVID-19 ballooned the budget to $290 million, making it the most expensive Mission: Impossible film, and the most expensive film of Tom Cruise's career.

Is any movie worth more than the capital value of a third world country?

I don't think so, it feels like an obscene amount of money.

Watch out for: BMW product placement at an all time high, including blowing the bloody doors off an M5 CS, but the best stunt involves a Beemer motorcycle in one of the series most elaborate stunts yet.

With a runtime of 2 hours and 43 minutes "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One" will test your bladder and makes it officially the longest MI movie to date.

Will "Dead Reckoning Part 1 and 2" really be Tom Cruise final portrayal as Ethan Hunt as well as the final main instalments?

Only time will tell.

Whatever happens Ving Rhames ("Luther Stickell") is the only actor who has been by Tom's side for the entire run since 1996, when even Australia's Prime Minister was trying to get the dance moves right to "Macarena" by Los del Rio.

The IMF or Impossible Mission Force is just like the Expendables only slightly younger...not much with Cruise blowing out 61 candles in Sydney for his Red Carpet promo tour.

The fallout with this instalment is it's no "Fall Out", but it has its merits and will still pack cinemas for people keen for the cinematic experience of massive screens and sound systems.

6.title: Nice Movie
6.content: Brian De Palma is an incomparable genius. I've seen every film in this franchise and nothing comes close to this first installment. Textured, muted, paced, mysterious, intelligent, authentic, original, inspired. Incredible film making that respects the viewing audience as much as it challenges it to remain attentive and invested. It's truly a beautifully crafted film that towers over every subsequent iteration. Strap in, get comfortable and experience some of the most masterfully entertaining cinema you're ever likely to see. This is unrivaled cinema. De Palma Delivers in spades! Enjoy! Nice movie hai.

6.title: Watch but with little lower expectation
6.content:
Undoubtedly, "Mission: Impossible" stands out as one of the most successful ongoing spy movie series. It continues to surpass expectations, with each installment improving upon the last. However, in this latest edition, there is a noticeable hiccup.

Tom Cruise delivers a brilliant performance, showcasing his limitless capabilities-the very essence that defines "Mission: Impossible." Yet, this particular installment faces a setback in terms of appreciation, primarily due to its storyline. The narrative unfolds at a slower pace, hindering the overall momentum, a departure from the dynamic established in the previous installment, "Fallout."

This happens to be my least favorite entry in the entire series thus far, primarily due to the story's development. However, I hold onto the hope that the groundwork laid will lead to a satisfying conclusion in the final episode.

It's important to note that the last hour of the movie features some compelling action scenes, while the rest of the film largely serves as a foundation for the second part. Approach it with patience and a genuine love for the series.

6.title: Just seen with my kids - respect for Tom Cruise
6.content:
Just yesterday, my younger, Norwegian-American children and I went to see this in Kilden Kino on Tønsberg (- Norway's oldest community, thanks to the cylindrical plateau alongside the town which was a natural ancient fortress).

The volume was too loud, but then I am hard of hearing, so .... I had only gotten a couple of hours of sleep the night before and was concerned Dad would fall asleep during the movie.

NO WAY.

I'm becoming repulsed by James Bond but have enjoyed the Jack Ryan and Jason Bourne series. I haven't kept up with MI, but since there was much filming in Norway, we had to see it, and the train scenes certainly were in beautiful Norway. (LOTS of lightly or un-settled dramatic terrain like that here.) I've seen car chase and train scenes before and that gets a bit old, even if these were spectacular. (My favorite is the Moscow scene in The Bourne Supremacy.) Why not a kayak or sail board ... or hang glider ... chase scene?

The characters were interesting, and I thought Elias Morales was excellent as Gabriel. Sorry to see brainy Elsa eliminated for the transition to light-fingered Grace. Henry Czerny is as excellent as he was in Clear and Present Danger.

Tom honestly looked his age, and that doesn't disfavor him. My kids both knew he does his own stunts - and of his scientology quirk - and I'm coming to think of him as a real-life Indiana Jones ... or Ethan Hunt. But 57 now 61 *is* pushing it, and we don't want to lose him.

I wonder how the sub-marine/sous-marin sequel will face off with the submarine scene in Pierce Brosnan's The World Is Not Enough - real turn-off, though: Bond should never have killed a woman.

My kids said they liked the film. None of us fell asleep. :-)

6.title: Mission Impossible 2: Sons of Liberty
6.content:
This movie was like Mission Impossible 2, Metal gear solid 2, Uncharted 2, Tomorrow Never Dies (2nd Pierce Brosnan James Bond) combined.

Ethan must team together with the woman he is now handcuffed with while driving the James Bond car, fight a ninja and figure out how to disable the evil ai which soon will control the world but not before jumping out of the train car dangling from top of the cliff just in time.

+ Positives I liked that they brought back Kittridge and started to touch a little bit on Ethans backstory pre IMF.

Lorne Balfe delievers an ok soundtrack and the sound mix during the train sequence had punch.

Negatives
First movie since MI2 which was a let down. The cinematography felt not as grand scale as Fallout and the story and pacing was less nail biting than usual.

In Fallout they started to touch on sending Ethan more down the path of grey morality and making it "darker and grittier". I felt like this was gone and everbody was sadly reduced to 2d characters. Except maybe one little gesture towards the end. Ethan also felt overpowered once again like in MI2. It was the little moments in Fallout which made it so good, showing Ethan as a normal human being, struggling and vulnerable, failing the jump, not beating up 5 guys in a row with no effort but actually struggling to take down even one guy.

The evil ai plot felt a little out of place for MI movie, I hope the next final movie will make it work.

I believed that the film would end on a huge cliffhanger making me want to see the next asap, as this is part 1, but the ending felt really anticlimatic. I guess expectations has once again wrecked a movie for me.

6.title: Great action with at times jawdroppingly insulting script.
6.content:
First of all the good things, which are those that everyone mentions. Some of the best action scenes in the cinema ever. It's obviously also good to see the whole team back together, even though they don't get as much screen time as some of us would like.

However. Some scenes (and the whole premise for that matter) are just straight up ridiculous. The scenes which probably should shock the audience you can see coming from a mile away (Ilsa - honestly the most nonsensical close quarters fight scene ever choreographed, I wanted to be screaming. The Director of National Intelligence who's literally begging to be killed by orchestrating a proposition of an alliance to the one party that has no interest in being allied, people routinely forgetting that guns exist). Finally the whole objective of the baddie could be smed up to "why though?". The AI could just nuke Sevastopol and be unstoppable. Anyway, most of the action was decent. Plot wise the second worst MI.

6.title: 6/10 - Entertaining but Lacks Depth
6.content:
"Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" is the latest entry in the iconic action series, offering a globe-trotting adventure with high stakes and thrilling sequences. Tom Cruise reprises his role as Ethan Hunt, who faces off against a new, formidable threat while navigating a perilous mission that could endanger the future of mankind. Joining him is Hayley Atwell as Grace, adding a new dynamic to the team.

While Tom Cruise delivers his usual charismatic performance as Ethan Hunt, the film suffers from a lack of depth in both its acting and storytelling. The acting, though competent, doesn't reach the high standards set by previous installments. The villain, Gabriel, is a weak antagonist with a tacked-on backstory, failing to evoke the menace and intrigue expected from the series' villains. The hand-to-hand combat sequences, notably the Venice bridge scene, lack the finesse and excitement of past films, making the choreography glaringly obvious.

The direction and cinematography are visually impressive, but the film struggles with a sense of realism and emotional impact. The climax, featuring a dramatic train crash, is visually striking but feels more like a spectacle than a thrilling conclusion. While the Venice car chase scene is amusing, it veers more into the realm of comedy than tension.

The film's greatest flaw is its generic plot and lack of high stakes. The storyline feels recycled, with predictable beats and an overemphasis on Ethan Hunt's romantic entanglements at the expense of his friendships with Benji and Luther. The film's tone is light, bordering on absurd, and it lacks the grit and suspense that fans might expect from the series. It's more a flashy display of action set pieces rather than a tightly woven narrative.

Despite its shortcomings, "Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" is still a decent action movie. It delivers exciting visuals and some entertaining moments, even if it fails to bring fresh elements to the franchise. If you're a fan of the series or enjoy high-octane action, it's worth a watch, but it falls short of the series' best offerings.

6.title: Your Mission............Should You Choose to Accept it.....
6.content:
.... Is to want to like this latest MI instalment more than you can.

I am a huge fan of MissImp and have been since I was a boy watching Jim Phelps, Rollin Hand et al pull of the impossible with style and aplomb on TV I have loved all of these - not so much the second - and what Tom Cruise has done with the action spy genre, but I feel 'cheated' with this one.

It feels like all of the previous instalments have rolled up into this one - and not very well.

Dialogue throwbacks from Kittredge and Luther (MI1), Atwell is the new Nyah Nordoff-Hall (MI2), Ethan training recruits (MI3), being chased by a team of goodies (MI4) the same train roof punch up, same BMW cars and bikes getting mashed in the same car chase as.. yawwwwnn.

I'm still trying to work out why the 'mind-reading shape-shifting agent of chaos' that is Ethan Hunt HAS to ride a motorbike off a cliff and parachute onto a train - he has breached the CIA dressed as Fireman Sam and stolen a NOC List for gods sake!

Ethan's self-righteousness is starting to wear a bit thin too.

Disappointing..... but I'll watch it again - and again - and Part 2 also because 'We live and die in the shadows to protect those we love and those we may never meet'.

6.title: Incredible - but formulaic
6.content:
I love Mission impossible movies. 4 thru 6 just got better and built upon themselves. I rewatch them once a year or so and always catch something new. Dead Reckoning looked incredible from the trailers but something held me back from seeing it in the theatres. The reviews all seemed to say "I know I just saw a Tom Cruise Mission Impossible Movie and the stunts and action blew my mind but there's something....missing." So I didn't see it in theatres. And I'm kinda glad. After watching it at home, I feel the same way. It's not...quite up to the bar set by 4 thru 6 from an emotional or character development standpoint.

And after watching it twice, a few things annoy me.

1. A few too many head cocks. Seriously, does every person have to cock their head to convey emotion in this film? There were at least 5 of them. I have the key (head cock). I just outsmarted you ( head cock). I just showed up when you didn't expect me (head cock). I pulled off a mask and turns out I'm someone else - bet you didn't see that coming (head cock). You've gone to the well too many times with this gesture and it's annoying. Stop. Stop.

2. And a few too many conversations when 4 different people complete one part of a full sentence in sequence without missing a beat. It's completely unbelievable. I can't have a conversation with ONE person without accidentally talking over them and these people can have fully complete thoughts and decide who conveys that thought in a complete sentence sequentially MULTIPLE TIMES in a movie. It's lazy and overdone and honestly something you see on MANIFEST or something. Maybe once in a movie but not 3-4 times, and every time something complex or incredibly emotional is explained. We're smarter than that - please trust your audience to figure out what's going on.

I do hope the second one is better. I do hope this franchise doesn't go the way of the Matrix or other franchises like it where they sell out on action and forget that their audiences have brains.

6.title: Go on...
6.content: ... if you don't mind plotholes large enough to sink an atomic submarine into and if you don't mind female characters that are either aggressively stupid or stupidly aggressive then this is the right movie for you. Good action. You will be taken to nice places all over the world, as usual. Ethan has never been to Venice (Spoiler!), who would have guessed. I did not know that. Do all Venice parties look like the remains from the Eyes wide shut set? Pew. And the Orient Express, really? There is so little going on and so little to sy here, that it is hard to meet the remaining 130 characters for the minimum length of a review posted in this forum. 100 left, o.k. Did I mention that every single woman character in this movie is a nuisance?

6.title: A spectacle of senseless humor, straying from its essence of pure adrenaline.
6.content:
In the latest installment of the renowned franchise, Mission Impossible 7, a discernible shift is evident as the film appears to prioritize elements of comedy and drama over its trademark action-driven narrative. The series' earlier successes lay in its straightforward yet compelling plots, revolving around the classic conflict between antagonists, protagonists, and the indomitable Ethan Hunt and his team. Notably, the action sequences were known for their intensity, paired with seamless choreography that refrained from incorporating excessive comedic interludes that could disrupt the flow.

However, with Mission Impossible 7, there emerges an appreciable emphasis on grandeur, exemplified through a captivating screenplay and visually striking action scenes. While this approach has its merits, a noticeable yearning for the mature essence exhibited in the preceding films becomes apparent. The pursuit of a broader audience appeal seemingly comes at the cost of sacrificing the inherent charm that once defined the franchise as a paragon of pure action.

In conclusion, Mission Impossible 7 ventures into uncharted territory by delving into comedy and drama, granting the film a new dimension of grandiosity. Yet, some fervent followers of the series may miss the resonating impact of the former action-centric experiences that Mission Impossible movies were celebrated for.

6.title: What is up with the dialogue?
6.content: Since Ghost Protocol I got into the MI films. They have been hit and miss going back to MI #1 which was not that good. But this new installment, despite the great cast, edge of your seat action and stunts, excellent special effects and photography, the dialog is ridiculously wooden. It's like they are each taking turns reading the tele-prompter and each actor was promised to have a minimum number of lines. I thought I might have just been too sensitive about this but my wife totally agreed. It distracted from what was a pretty good film. This is really strange to me because I never noticed this in the other films. Ruined it for me.

6.title: The world doesn't know it, but they're counting on you.
6.content: I wondered how this franchise's still going last time and here we are again. I mean, Cruise, Ferguson, Rhames and Pegg are all much stronger actors individually than the roles they play within this series. However the film contains good action, cinematography and has more comedy elements than any from the past I recall, with the cheeky likeable Hayley Atwell as Grace. Ethan vowing to put her before himself, after all she'd put him through is endearing as well. Though the plot in these are a bit of a wash and never a fan of a super computer concept. Not sure how I feel about this film as a whole though, certainly doesn't engage throughout, clocking near three hours and not all of the parts work, but it's decent.

6.title: Solid Mission Impossible. Not great, but good.
6.content:
You know the drill: non-stop action, several magnificent stunt scenes, sumptuous locales, and a lot of Tom Cruise running after some MacGuffin. That's Mission Impossible. If you like the formula, you will be well served. If you don't care about it, this movie won't convince you, either. Same old, same old.

I always go watch a new Mission Impossible when it premieres, and this year it doubled as a nice birthday entertainment for me. I wasn't disappointed.

But one thing is certain: unfortunately, I think Tom Cruise is already past his prime. And it's good to see him wrap things up while he still can. Top Gun Maverick was a great surprise, and Dead Reckoning Part 1 was outrageously entertaining. It's amazing how this formula has held up since 1996. Tom Cruise should be proud of this achievement. This was never meant as Oscar material. It's an unapologetic popcorn blockbuster. It never takes itself too seriously, and they have fun while doing it. And I think that's the whole point of an action flick. It remained true to itself, unlike similar franchises such as Fast and Furious, which went too far out of line and it's totally unrecognizable. Mission Impossible is recognizable at its core, in every instance. I say, Bravo.

That being said, as someone deeply embedded in the real-world technology space, whenever a normie tries to write about "hacking" or "artificial intelligence" and such, it's obviously very, very wrong. Though I have to be fair and say that it would be very boring to root technology in reality too much. But yes, the nemesis of this chapter is none other than ChatGPT. They did it. OpenAI was successful in placing AI in the zeitgeist as the new action flick villain of this era.

And yeah, an AI so sophisticated, capable of replicating itself over the internet, but with a super obvious flaw: a key that can unlock its "original source code" (whatever that means), and this key is the MacGuffin that everybody is chasing after. It used to be the key to deactivating a nuclear football, but this time it's an AI. Yeah. Same old, same old. They should have called Angelina Jolie and Rami Malek for a cameo.

Reality checks aside, it's an action flick. The details don't matter. It's like Thanos going after Infinite Stones. We get it. A "world-ending event" is the motivation for the protagonist to perform the most outrageous stunts ever. And they deliver. Car chases, knife fights, alley fights. Guns, lots of guns. And nothing less than a train and precipice sequence.

Newcomer Hayley Atwell was a surprising and refreshing addition to the team. I think she and Cruise had great chemistry together, and she was great in every scene. I love Rebecca Fergusson and every movie since Rogue Nation; I think she could do so much more, but they never actually unlocked her full potential. But Hayley was great from the get-go and much more well-utilized. It's unfortunate that, again, Rebecca didn't receive enough action sequences, but her participation was great nonetheless.

Another newcomer, Guardian's own Mantis, Pom Klementieff, was here as well. Unfortunately, she received a very poorly written-character to play. Another wasted potential. At this point, the story has more characters than the McQuarie knows what to do with. Even though Hayley was great, I wouldn't cast her and instead use Rebecca a whole lot more to crown her character arc. And I wouldn't have Pom as well. Esai Morales was more than enough as the relentless antagonist.

Vanessa Kirby's character was never meant for action sequences, but at least this time, they gave her a lot more to do, so that was a good thing. She had to flex a bit more of her acting skills; it was good to see.

The soundtrack is nothing to write home about. Serviceable but not memorable. Directing and editing were normal, nothing spectacular. It's a very well-polished action flick, no more, no less. They perfected the formula at this point. And everything points to an explosive finale. The Part 1 aspect works well. I don't think the movie was too overextended. As I said, they could've trimmed the story a little bit, trimmed some of the cast, and made better use of the time and resources. But it's nothing to the point that it's unbearable to watch. It's good enough to not get boring. And the story wraps up nicely for a satisfying first chapter. It doesn't end in a cheap cliffhanger. It does feel like a complete episode with an overarching arc for the last chapter.

I don't think you need to go see it in the theater unless you don't have a good home theater at home. I would be equally satisfied to watch it on my 75" TV.

Enjoyable but not memorable. A solid 6 out of 10.

6.title: Bloated
6.content:
This is the longest film in the franchise so far. And it is a two part one as well. So there will no doubt be another almost 3 hours to this storyline.

I understand that they want to go out on a bang and have the last couple of films seem like some big epic. But this annoying trend of splitting the last movie in a franchise into two parts is starting to annoy me.

The plot itself is definitely the most ridiculous so far. Which is fine... this series thrives on the ridiculous.

The problem is that a lot of the decisions that seem to have been made didn't make much sense from a plot or character perspective... almost like they just wanted to throw things in to motivate Ethan.

Having Ilsa come back, just to fake her death and vanish, then having her come back again, just to start an ill advised sword fight and die. The character has been all about the guns previously... why the sudden desire for a sword fight? Other than dramatic death purposes, of course. It just felt like a waste of Rebecca Ferguson.

The cast are great and the action is over the top as always. The writing just felt rather lazy this time around. Like they were just trying to kill time between action sequences until they got to the second film where they can actually start resolving things.

Hayley Atwell's character for example. She repeatedly does the cliché of running away from Ethan when he is clearly trying to save her life. She ends up putting herself in danger and having to be saved repeatedly instead of just being like "oh right, in over my head here, maybe help would be a good thing." This would be alright if it just happened initially... but when it keeps happening it is just like... come on... stop stringing this out now.

Don't get me wrong. I like this franchise. But this film just feels lazy and stretched out in order to justify it being in two parts.

6.title: Wanted to love it. Really did... but
6.content:
I really tried to love this movie. Swear I did. I haven't gone to a normal movie theater where I paid money to sit next to strangers and watch a film since - The Northman(big robert eggers fan).

I've been a huge Cruise fan for as long as I can remember and I love that he respects and appreciates the audience as opposed to the rest of Hollywood which seems to believe they are entitled to our money sans our opinions and wants.

It's always fun to watch Cruise do his thing. Yeah, he looked a little old but not like Harrison Ford in that latest Indiana crap fest - looking like Joe Biden in that hat. Cruise, here, is a bad a$$ older dude who still looked like he could beat the crap out of a much younger person but was nearing a time to hang it up.

Which leads me to the things I did appreciate in MI:DR - Cruise may have a massive ego - understandable being that he's been consistently one of the top 5 biggest movie stars ever for his entire life. But his ego isn't offensive. It doesn't sabotage him or his work. He's too smart for that.

So in this film I saw Cruise consciously put together a younger class that seems like they're being set up to take over some time down the road - Hayley Atwell and the young black man that found himself admiring Ethan Hunt.

Cruise is still a lot of fun to watch. And no doubt the action was fun. Hayley Atwell was super sexy, fun, sneaky, and clever. I absolutely loved that she was actually feminine. She wasn't going hand to hand with 280 pound guys. I bought her character.

Rebecca Ferguson is easily one of my favorite actresses working today. She's just phenomenal in everything I've seen her in and can truly make fairly measly and forgettable role into something concrete - Which is what she did here. She wasn't given much but still managed to stand out.

Vanessa Kirby had next to nothing to do.

Ving Rhames and Simon Pegg... love these guys. Just wish the script loved them as much.

Esai Morales was apparently cast directly from his role in Ozark. He's one journeyman of an actor and a real talent... i was happy to see him in a movie of this size and scope. He deserves it. Again I think the script let him down.

Speaking of the script letting someone down... Pom Klementieff. My god, "look what they did to my girl". So, Pom is perfect as the femme fatale - she has the look, she's gorgeous but we can still buy her kicking some butt. Problem is that they did nothing with her. She spoke like 3 times in the whole movie. Personally, I think she deserved better. This could have been an opportunity for her to do some actual acting as opposed to the marvel drivel and other stuff I've seen her in.

All of the above aside, the number one issue with this movie is the script. I mean was this written by a person? Or did they experiment with AI to write this? I'm seriously asking... but this script was awful. A film school freshmen would do better than this. It honestly felt less like MI and more like a Fast and Furious movie. I half expected Ethan to say he had "Family".

I kept thinking through the film that if you hadn't seen the last few Mission Impossible's then you wouldn't know or care about anyone in this film. Some of you might say... well they should watch those other movies. Wrong. It's on the filmmakers to make each story accessible to new viewers each and every outing in franchises. They failed on that here.

Also, in my humble opinion, I really wish Cruise would can Christopher Mcquarrie who is for all intents and purposes a by the numbers director... Barely above average and bring back John Woo - one the most legendary action directors to walk the earth. To me MI 2 is by far the most memorable. I remember seeing it as a kid and to this day those gorgeous shots and action sequences are imprinted in my mind.

I gave this a 6 and It's only because of the respect I have for Cruise and the supporting cast but considering the writing - this rating is generous.

6.title: Where did it go
6.content: I remember when I used to get the chills from the name mission impossible, that vibe was the reason I fell for it, that same thrilling vibe was the same reason I dragged myself out to see this movie but guess what, I asked myself where did it all go, scenes were like cars running and Tom doing a lot of foot running no drama no sensational belonging no relatability they denied reality to some machine and that's where it all started, am not going to lie I really digged the scene when he approached grace that move was like fire in my head others were just same ai Bull crap, the sequel the only thing they did was betray the mission and to the critics if they don't fix this in the upcoming movie then i guess it really is impossible.

6.title: Tom Cruise's Signature Spy Action Thriller Sets the Path For A Better Follow-Up
6.content:
Mission: Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One (2023) : Movie Review -

Tom Cruise and Christopher McQuarrie's pair bring another thrilling adventure in the MI series with Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One. If I am not wrong, then Cruise and McQuarrie's collaboration (in any way) hasn't gone wrong except for "The Mummy" (2017). Rather, Christopher McQuarrie is responsible for writing and directing one of the best films in Tom's filmography. Mission Impossible 7 is anything but a failure. My faith in this pair remains intact as they deliver what's promised. Actually, they don't do anything else, and that's the major issue here. All those previous 6 films of MI have made us acquainted with almost everything that's possible in a modern spy-action drama, so naturally they were out of new conflicts this time. MI 7 is an utterly honest and trademark Mission Impossible film, but that's all there is to it.

Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One starts off with an unknown "AI" device deceiving and destroying a submarine. Ethan Hunt is given a task to find a key from his friend, Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson). In the next scene, we travel from the ocean to an Arabian desert, where Ethan confronts Ilsa and eventually gets the key. The key has to be traded, so Ethan shakes hands with a pickpocket, Grace (Hayley Atwell), who is actually working for the opposite party. After quite a thrilling SmackDown session at the airport, Grace takes the key to Venice, and as expected, Ethan, Luther (Ving Rhames), and Benji (Simon Pegg) follow her there to get it. Ilsa, who was supposed to be dead (for how long? Nobody knew anyway) joins the party as they meet at Alanna's, aka The White Window's (Vanessa Kirby) den, where they also encounter the mastermind behind the entire thing, Gabriel (Esai Morales). Gabriel has some plans written that Ethan has to deal with, but it's pretty difficult this time since the AI thing, the Entity, knows it all. Will Ethan and his team get what they want? Or is it just the beginning of a massive war?

Mission Impossible 7 has fewer thrills compared to its predecessor, Mission Impossible: Fallout, which is arguably the best MI flick. Actually, MI 6 has raised the bar so high for contemporaries that it's very difficult to match the kind of thrill, suspense, and excitement with a similar set of characters and surroundings. MI 7 suffers from an insufficiency of novelty and unusualness. It's been so many MI films that we have seen the face mask, so it's an impossible mission for the writers if they think they can provide some thrill with it. We know that whatever happens, the hero can't die or even get hurt. So it's impossible to imagine that Hunt might not get out of that situation.
