8.title: Cinema worthy & heart-pounding
8.content:
Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1" delivers an exhilarating experience that makes it well worth the trip to the cinema. The action, pacing, and beat of the film are what truly keep you hooked from start to finish.

While the plot dives into the AI zeitgeist, the tech play is a bit overplayed, but it's the relentless action sequences and perfectly timed pacing that stand out. Tom Cruise, as always, brings his unique brand of intensity to the role. Despite my reservations about his off-screen persona, there's no denying his ability to anchor these films with compelling presence. Though his character may seem a bit whiny at times, Cruise manages to pull it off with a charisma that draws you in.

One of the standout aspects of this film is its sheer cinematic scale. With a top-notch home theater setup, it's easy to distinguish movies that truly deserve the big screen treatment, and "Dead Reckoning Part 1" is undoubtedly one of them. The action sequences are bigger, bolder, and crafted to be seen on a vast canvas with booming sound.

The movie keeps you on the edge of your seat, delivering a series of heart-pounding moments and intricate stunts that are a hallmark of the franchise. The impressive visuals and pulse-pounding soundtrack enhance the overall experience, making it a thrilling ride from start to finish.

In summary, "Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part 1" is an impressive spectacle that lives up to its name. It's a film that demands to be seen in the cinema, offering an immersive experience that's hard to replicate at home. If you're a fan of the series or just in the mood for some high-octane action, this movie won't disappoint. Enjoyed every moment!

8.title: Another great part
8.content:
"Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One", although not the best part of the series, has a lot to offer:

Christopher McQuarrie returns with his great direction. His script (co-written by Erik Jendresen) is strong, although the story seemed a bit disjointed to me. The jokes, however, were good and well placed, as were the tense moments. Fraser Taggart's cinematography is incredible, so is Eddie Hamilton's editing, and the brilliant score by Lorne Balfe.

Tom Cruise's performance is strong, one of the strongest in the series. However, others like Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg, Rebecca Ferguson and Vanessa Kirby are also outstanding.

So overall, while I don't consider it the best of the series, it's a really good installment in the Mission: Impossible series.

8.title: Another M:I movie full of ideas, and another winner for Cruise
8.content:
I was surprised to see this playing at the cinema this weekend in Poland, before its official release date. I decided to check it out since the early reviews have been so good and since I was in the mood for some fun action.

The M:I movies have really surpassed Bond films in terms of action, ideas, and even fun. It's probably the best running franchise now. And ideas are where this movie really excels.

In the movie, an AI "virus" of sorts has slowly been overtaking the existing global tech infrastructure. It is becoming so powerful that it can control and alter outcomes, affect humanity in drastic ways, and even affect individual actions in a given moment. This is a cool idea and very relevant given the context of the world we live in today. This virus appears to have more sinister intentions for humanity. The IMF team, US intelligence, defenders/enforcers of the virus, and other world powers are all interested in a key that "opens something" and with which the virus can supposedly be controlled. And so you have the basic storyline as all of these sides will battle each other to get to that key first, which Alanna Mitsopolis, a black arms dealer, is looking to sell.

The way that this is set up is great, as there is a feeling throughout the movie that the stakes are very high. At different moments, the movie seems to have this eerie, almost surreal, Matrix-like feel to it, that is created by the complex reality of the story and the tone of the film. The standout stars in the movie are Cruise and Hayley Atwell, who plays Grace, a thief that at one point gets her hands on the key and gets pulled into the action. They are great as a duo throughout much of the film. The banter and comedy is also quite good as I had a couple of actual laugh out loud moments. There was a little more "lightness" in this MI entry in general.

Esai Morales as Gabriel, the main defender of the virus and also one of the pursuers of the key, was also quite good. Throughout the movie he acts as if he is a medium for the virus or in some way controlled by it as his actions essentially channel what the virus wants. I was a little confused by his character or how such a character would even come to be, but some of the logic can definitely be checked at the door. Essentially, he, as well as the other dueling sides, has interest in the power of the virus. I also really enjoyed Henry Czerny back as Kittridge and Shea Whigham as Jasper, who spends most of the movie trying to chase down Ethan and his team.

The other stars in the film are the ideas and executions in the action and set pieces. There is a marvelous battle in nighttime Venice. A surprisingly entertaining and funny car chase sequence where Ethan and Grace try to get away in a janky little Fiat. And an absolutely ridiculous final train stunt sequence. Its one of those that make me go "oh come on!" in disbelief while simultaneously not being able to look away due to the amazing and captivating execution.

Overall this one is action-packed, with great ideas and execution, and is a lot of fun. It feels a bit more "classic" in tone with a lot of the themes and plot developments resembling the first M:I movie. I really enjoyed that. There is more intrigue and mystery than outright action. As I said, there are a lot of funny, more lighthearted moments as well and Cruise is the one delivering a lot of them. I guess it's a bit disheartening that with all that said, I still felt bored at moments during the movie. Perhaps this was just the state of mind I was in. Perhaps it is a statement of how high the bar has already been set by all the M:I movies and ideas in the past. And perhaps it is also a result of being a bit jaded by all of the action and CGI films of the past decade, which have left me with a feeling of riding one roller-coaster after another, with each one trying to outdo the previous one. It didn't blow me away and take me by surprise as much as Top Gun Maverick did, for example.

With that said, there are plenty of clever ideas here, inventive action, and funny and lighthearted moments, along with an overall more classic espionage movie tone. It's good and people will not be disappointed, even if it is a Part 1 of 2. It leaves you with a feeling of closure as far as the events that transpired, but also with a knowledge that more will come and that it could be quite spectacular. It's value might also grow on a repeated viewing and once the second part completes the story.

8.title: A Great Installment-Even With Cliffhanger
8.content:
Viewers seek out MI films for two reasons: the crazy stunts, and a "won't strain your brain" popcorn movie. This movie checks both of those boxes.

Cruise does fewer dramatic roles in favor of splashier action flicks of late. And not surprisingly, they're pretty darn good. But not always perfect.

When you go to a Mission movie (much like Bond or Bourne) you're watching for the thrill ride and excellent supporting cast and twisty story. All are present in this film, but it's missing one thing that would make it a nine or a ten: a strong villain played by a capable actor. The "big bad" is a rogue AI program called The Entity, so no on-screen villain in that regard. The Entity's human chess piece-avatar is played by Esai Morales (replacing Nicolas Hoult), a very middle grade actor who is unable to inspire any true tension or fear. By comparison Henry Cavill as Fallout's chess piece bad guy was phenomenal.

The other new performers: Pom Klementieff, Hayley Atwell and Henry Czerny all acquit themselves well. Fringe returnees Vanessa Kirby and Rebecca Ferguson (who I guess isn't really' fringe') are also terrific.

Cruise, the ultimate performer delivers numerous edge-of-your-seat stunts that are amazing. His jaw flexing, minimal dialogue Ethan Hunt still carries the emotional weight we need to see from the lead actor in an action series.

But, that villain, or villains, as the case may be, and the demise of one of our favorite players, for me, left the ending feeling hollow and flat. So to was the silly scene with Morales staring at the sky screaming "Hunt!!!" a la captain James T Kirk bellowing out the iconic similar scream: "Khan!!!" I'll see the next one for sure. Just hoping for a rousing wrap up since Cruise has said this will be his last Mission film.

8.title: Amazing Action as usual, Story a little bland...
8.content:
Let's be honest here, we're here for the Action and the thrills, right? And Dead Reckoning Part 1 really delivers on that in great fashion, just like Rogue Nation and the phenomenal Fallout did before.

It still somewhat irritated me to be so 'not' intrigued with this massive stake story that is set up for a Finale of one of americas greatest Action Franchises. Should we not be allowed to expect something maybe more deep or just let's say not too ridiculous? ... Don't get me wrong, I know the Series has been full of bizarre and over the top ideas, but in this case I really think Chris McQuarrie went a little bit too far. It's one thing to create a big atmosphere by setting up massive stakes and YES, of course this Finale should feel big and massive. But it's another thing just making the wrong and maybe just too simple decisions. Bigger doesn't always equal better and in the case of the Story here (A. I.), I just felt like that's a very bland and boring idea to bring up for such a massive Finale.

Of course that's also subjective, but I just never found myself really feeling intrigued with what was going on with the story. I just really didn't care about it. And the big issue is I didn't even want to care, because the way the Film goes deeper into the story, progresses and takes time with actual dialogue I just really felt more and more annoyed with it. I had the whole opposite feeling while watching Fallout, I was intrigued and wanted to know what they're doing next. Because it was more serious in tone, you could take everything seriously and the characters really got some time to breathe for at least some short emotional moments. Of course the emotional moments are here aswell, but they're just not as well executed or written.

And besides the invisible enemy (A. I.), we arguably got the most bland and annoying villain of the Franchise. A character that just cheaply got a little backstory so it makes sense putting him there. But honestly i was just bored with that character. It's such a one-note character. A typical bad guy look. And the worst of it is that the story seems to not get enough of him now.

You might be thinking now why is it still an 8/10 for me, well i think all the rest can still somehow make up for everything that's bad or bland here. It's still an epic feel film with a lot of awesome action set-pieces and it has many longer action sequences that are so much fun and so well paced. The car chases in Rome here are the most exciting and hilarious the franchise has ever had. And the main cast truly delivers. Hayley Atwell is a great new addition and in general you really have to highlight how much great stuff McQuarrie has accomplished with all of these female characters. Pom Klementieff is a showstealer, the action with her character is really refreshing. And in general with the visual, technical and the location departments they arguably outdone themselves yet again.

It's surely not the best of the franchise, I think Fallout & Rogue Nation was the point this franchise found its peak but it's still an incredible fun ride that's surely not feeling as long as it could. The Positive still strongly overweights, but I can see why people including myself have some issues with it. If your scope is bigger than just Action Films, you'll definitely not feel like this is the big masterpiece.

8.title: The Epitome of the Theater Experience
8.content:
You will not see many action movies better than this one in your lifetime. The immediate comparison for many would be its predecessor, but this one surpasses Fallout in a number of ways for me.

You could have told me this film was double the budget of Indy 5 and I would've believed you instantly. This film is 2 hours and 43 minutes of perfectly made action in some of the most incredible areas of the world. Some of the specific scenes from this film, and you will know which scenes I am talking about if you've seen it, are possibly some of the best action sequences in the history of cinema.

It's everything you would expect out of a Mission: Impossible movie, but happens to be the best of the seven. You cannot watch this movie anywhere outside of the theater. That would just be a cruelty to this film and the theater.

8.title: What an action movie should be.
8.content:
Although the story seems a little lackluster and is filled with typical action movie clichés, they feel completely in place in what is the best Mission Impossible film to date.

Tom cruise delivers once again with some white knuckle set pieces and stunts that keep you on the edge of your seat. And the great thing is that they don't stop coming throughout the films almost 3 hour run time.

Pair this with the comedic quips, an amazing car chase sequence as well as a decent serving of hand to hand combat and Christopher McQuarrie has directed exactly what the dictionary definition of a popcorn action movie should be.

Overall a great movie that looks amazing on the big screen with its stunning set pieces and locale choices that has some weaker story elements and is very predictable yet the non stop thrilling action will have you overlooking it's shortcomings.

8.title: This is what espionage films should strive to be!!!!
8.content:
My "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One" SPOILER Review:

PROS: -The Action and Stunt Work is Top Notch!!!

-Cruise always commits.

-Hayley Atwell is the breakout star.

-The "Villain" is unlike anything the series has done before.

-The airport sequence is an exercise in building tension.

-The idea of "The Choice".

-The Rome car chase is pure fun!

-The 3rd Act is like a movie within a movie and kept me on the edge of my seat!!!

-I need Part Two right now.

CONS: -It's about 20 minutes too long.

No other franchise does action and espionage like Mission Impossible does. Seven movies in and these movies continue to surprise. This series is the best at using action sequences to build the characters, show their relationships and motivations. The airport sequence, the car chase in Rome and the train sequence are all built on the choices the characters make in them and kept the audience on edge of their seat throughout. Tom Cruise commits to the stunts as always and it's glorious to behold. Hayley Atwell really surprised me as a thief who gets caught up in the adventure. She was a true wild card here. Having an A. I. be the villain is both a unique and current day choice. It's a terrifying force and its presence is felt throughout, leading to one of my favorite moments in the film. The 3rd Act on the train is really special, operating on multiple levels of deception, betrayals, hand to hand fights, culminating in a spectacular crash. I had a blast with this film. Even as a "Part One", it felt like a whole movie. I love this series and the filmmaker's commitment to practical stunts and their ability to keep the audience guessing. This is what espionage movies should strive to be. I had a great time at the theater. 8/10.

8.title: Tom cruise is still a action star over 2 decades...!!!
8.content:
Tom Cruise once again proves why he is the heart and soul of the Mission: Impossible franchise. His portrayal of Ethan Hunt is as captivating as ever, showcasing his dedication to the role and his willingness to perform his own stunts. The rest of the cast, including Rebecca Ferguson as Ilsa Faust, Simon Pegg as Benji Dunn, and Ving Rhames as Luther Stickell, deliver solid performances, adding depth and humor to the film. Additionally, newcomers such as Hayley Atwell and Pom Klementieff bring new energy and intrigue to the story.

Especially Hayley is a show stealer making me go through her filmography Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning does not disappoint when it comes to action and thrills. From breathtaking chase sequences to death-defying stunts, the film keeps viewers on the edge of their seats throughout. The action is expertly choreographed and filmed, showcasing McQuarrie's mastery of the genre. Whether it's a high-speed motorcycle chase through narrow city streets or a daring heist in the heart of an enemy stronghold, the movie constantly raises the stakes, leaving audiences craving more... Christopher McQuarrie's direction in Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning is exemplary. He knows how to balance intense action sequences with character development and plot twists, keeping the audience engaged from start to finish. The film's pacing is well-executed, with each scene building on the tension and leading to a satisfying climax. McQuarrie's attention to detail and commitment to practical effects make the movie feel authentic and grounded, enhancing the overall viewing experience... Despite minor loopholes and illogical questions rise while watching but the racy screenplay makes u forget and patch up to themovie... Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning is a thrilling addition to the Mission: Impossible film series. With its gripping plot, stellar performances, and jaw-dropping action sequences, it is sure to satisfy fans and newcomers alike. Christopher McQuarrie once again proves why he is one of the leading directors in the action genre, delivering a film that is both entertaining and thought-provoking. If you're a fan of high-stakes espionage thrillers, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning is a must-watch.

8.title: THE REASON TO GO TO THE THEATRES

The same old crew returns in their respective roles with some fascinating additions like Hayley Atwell and Pol Klementieff and both of them have done fascinating jobs in their roles. The Fallout was definitely a better movie experience than this in my opinion, then again it's subjective. Fallout had better choreographed action scenes with much better pacing and a tight plot. On the other hand this is one of the finest experiences with very much dialogue driven and more story focused in recent times regards to the action genre with the movie divided into two parts (the next year coming next year) but unlike John wick and Extraction franchise (which are more action focused than story).

Tom cruise is charismatic as always with TOP GUN breaking the box office records last year and continuing this trend is the MI7 which is definitely here to entertain and in an old fashion and connecting the very 1st MI movie to this one and has a story which is relatable in today's technological and AI world more than ever.

Well can't wait for the second one to come any sooner and hope next year too MI will once again ignite the box office on fire.

8.title: I love tom cruise and all his movie's

8.title: Not as great as Fallout but no doubt an incredibly solid action summer blockbuster.
8.content:
Whilst Fallout felt like a fresh direction in a 20-year-old franchise, Dead Reckoning - Part One suffers from hints of repetitiveness and a bit of an over convoluted plot, but is nevertheless a great time at the cinema, and it does not disappoint where it is meant to deliver, the action stunt sequences.

The main stunt is of course the highly anticipated bike jump from a cliff into a parachute, a feat so incredible that I will never forget how everyone in the theatre was completely and utterly silent and focused as Cruise jumped off that cliff on the motorbike, and that is what makes this film worthy of the cinematic experience, pure movie magic.

I'm really interested in the approach they took to the story, and while it is still the first part, it felt like the stakes were raised as intended and set up well for the second part. The way A. I. and futuristic digital technology were integrated to the main plot could've hindered the elegance the franchise has upheld for decades, but I actually enjoyed how the story unfolded and its consequences. Some bold choices that I hope they don't overwrite when the second part is out, they provide a lot of weight to the events.

However, at times, the McGuffin of the two keys became a tad bit annoying because of how much it kept on being mentioned and repeated. I feel like there are some sequences that would have benefited from being trimmed down. A small amount of wonky CGI during the train sequence, but nothing too distracting. Also, not a fan of how the film starts, up until the title drop it feels like a total editing mess.

The locations are as beautiful as ever, but I do wish that action films in general quit doing the same high-speed car chase sequences in Western Europe, it's become really overdone lately. I swear I've seen it done in the last five big action blockbusters. Despite that, the film does try to provide a different take on that overdone sequence, with Cruise either driving with one hand or in a small Fiat, which spares it from becoming boring.

Overall, it's worthy of the cinematic experience, a great time at the theatre, and another great instalment in a franchise that much like Tom Cruise, does not look it's age.

8.title: Great Action Film
8.content:
Tom Cruise is probably once of the greatest action stars ever. At age 60, it is fascinating that he performs the stunts he does. You know its him and its incredible to think of the danger he puts himself in to get the shot.

MI: Dead Reckoning is drawing a close to the series of films. Ethan (Cruise) is tracking down two pieces to form a key that unlocks something. He is joined by his team of Luther (Ving Rhames), Benji (Simon Pegg) and Ilsa (Rebecca Ferguson). There is an AI software that has become sentient and infiltrated all the security services on the planet. Every country is trying to get the key so they can control it. Esai Morales is the nominal villain, Gabriel, who is working for the AI. The White Widow (Vanessa Kirby) has one piece of the key and is going to sell it to the highest bidder. Pom Klementieff (Mantis from Guardians of the Galaxy) plays an assassin, Paris. She is fun and menacing and a nice addition. Finally, Hayley Atwell joins the cast as Grace, a pickpocket/thief, who gets in over her head by stealing one of the key pieces. She is a positive addition and they gave her character lots of screen time.

The movie's plot jumps around the world and moves at a pretty brisk pace. At 166 minutes, this movie never drags. The action sequences are some of the best in the series. The one drawback is, much like the Fast and the Furious franchise, they have lost the human aspect of the show. The characters become just props in the action sequences and their motivations don't really have much to do with anything. I've also never liked the fake masks they make to impersonate people. That gimmick has been part of the series from the beginning and its always seemed silly to me since Cruise is always shorter than the people he is impersonating. Still, everyone is game and I was never bored watching it. The final action on the train sequence going through the Austrian Alps is amazing starting with Cruise's motorcycle jump off a cliff. Just breathtaking.

I look forward to Part Two.

8.title: Nice Movie
8.content:
Probably one of my favourite action films ever, i just finished watching this for the first time in about 20 years. Full of action, suspense and great stunts, Tom Cruise plays young spy Ethan Hunt on the run after a failed mission where it sees his team killed off after a suspicious set up. Cruise plays his character with a limp wrist and an incredibly unique walk. According to sources he cut his own hair on set and refused to be handed food by anyone that was born in march.

The brilliant Jon Voight also stars, who turns out to be the antagonist, turns out Voight didn't know how to wear hats properly which transpired to the screen as you can see in most scenes. In an interview he actually said - quote "i gave up trying to figure out how to put hats on, so i made it a character trait" The action sequences are unforgettable, especially the tense "cable drop" scene, where it sees Tom Cruise lowered down into a secure room full of all kinds of security sensors, that was almost an impossible mission... but not quite. The scene is shot perfectly, no music, hardly no sounds, almost pure silence. I was so captivated by this scene, my cat meowed which startled me flipping my dinner off my lap into my face, i got so much mash potatoe and beef in my hair i spent 2 hours in the shower trying to get it out.

The film ends with another terrific action sequence involving the helicopter chase through the channel tunnel, it was pretty crazy and over the top but it worked and i loved it. If you look closely in this action scene you can see there's bits of lasagne on Jon Voights clothes, which he always ate before shooting a scene. The director decided to keep it in, saying it gave his character depth and meaning.

I have to give 5 stars for this, always a joy to watch.

I'm going to watch mission impossible 2 next and.

Overall it was a solid movie to watch, especially if you're a fan of the older MI movies.

8.content:

8.title: It's not your relaxing, easy to watch action movie
8.content:
Trying to describe this movie, I instantly think of the phrase "Very well done Tenet". To be clear, Nolan's Tenet is a tragedy for me, potentially the dullest action movie ever made, a terrible waste of potential.

And the comparison comes from the fact that in both cases in the center of the story we have a very interesting concept with pretty much unlimited potential + the music is extremely specific, unusual for action cinema. It is silent almost all the time, only in the background.

In new M:I, it never builds up clear excitement, but it builds up the tension brilliantly, making you stressed out from the beginning to the end of the situation on the screen. In Tenet, it's seemingly similar, but terribly monotonous, which almost makes me fall asleep during the main action sequence. On this basis, you can see that such procedure is easy to spoil, so all the more respect that they managed to do it right.

Additionally, this film gives an exceptional amount of time to the characters, their relationships and the whole variety of dialogues, none of which is any faster than it should be. Sometimes their even suprisingly slow. It's hard to expect something like this from a movie in this franchise, but it works.

The acting is great, the humor works rather well, the action is great as usual. The plot is not perfect, you can have some small accusations towards it + we have some "strange" directorial decisions here (for example in some scenes the camera angle was very different from what we usually see and expect and it wasn't necessary, it didn't work for me that well), but overall it's a great film. Possibly the best of this franchise, but I'm not sure if it's better than Ghost Protocol.

8.title: Action Packed

Tom Cruise continues to deliver top-notch performances even in his 60s. His acting and stunt-making are still the same. Excellent!

The story is straightforward, it takes place in three to four locations at most. Desert (Saudi Arabia), Venice, Pub and Train.

The movie received a beating from Oppenheimer and Barbie, which is why its box office collection decreased. I remember watching Oppenheimer and seeing posters for Mission Impossible in theaters. I wish I had seen MI in the cinema halls at that time. Would have been quite a cinematic experience.

The coincidence is that I saw Shaun of the Dead today, in which Simon Pegg is in the lead role, and he is also in this movie as Benji.

I have had a great time watching this movie.

8.title: They did it again!
8.content: Every time I think "Ok, please stop making these before you jump the shark" they managed to keep this franchise more James Bond than Fast & Furious. Ghost Protocol was excellent and while Dead Reckoning Part One is not quite at the same level it is still pure fun action entertainment. Say what you will about Tom Cruise as a person, it's undeniable he is just tremendously good at what he does as an actor, and this one is no exception. 8.content:
Rating: 8.0 Overall, a very entertaining watch that is fueled by good acting and great action scenes as Tom Cruise delivers another action-packed Mission Impossible movie, though it is a bit story dense given its runtime and it being one of two parts.

Good Direction (Does a good job in moving the story forward and getting the most out of his actors; does a very good job in the action sequences as they are well choreographed and shot very well), Good Acting (Good to Very Good from Tom Cruise (Plays a lot from experience not only in the character but as an action star as he feels like the biggest charisma in all his scenes and works off of the other characters very well), Good to Very Good from Hayley Atwell (Works off of Tom Cruise very well and does a good job at showing a range of emotions being the female lead (while also holding her own in the action sequences)), Pretty Good to Good from Ving Rhames, Good from Simon Pegg (Continues where he left off as the comedic relief character), Pretty Good from Rebecca Ferguson, Pretty Good from Vanessa Kirby, Pretty Good from Henry Czerny, Pretty Good from the rest of the cast), Good Story (Follows the Mission Impossible Template as it sets up the conflict and has Ethan Hunt and crew try to solve it (though it is a bit more story dense given it is one of two parts); has elements of the story that due build suspense and uses the action sequences well to help with telling the story; the conflict is a bit convoluted (but not that much)), Good Screenplay (The dialogue is good and flows well (pretty typical of other Mission Impossible movies (though this makes it a bit corny at times)); the jokes were weaved in very well throughout the movie and hit most of the time; the symbolism was kinda shallow (not really the purpose of the movie); foreshadowing was pretty prevalent and used well in helping build suspense)), Good Score (Carried a lot of the traditional Mission Impossible motifs and was used well in the movie to create suspense), Very Good Cinematography (Used very well in establishing the scenery and the fighting scenes (but there is one POV shot they kept on using that felt very out-of-place/amateurish in comparison to the other angles)), Very Good Sound, Very Good Editing, Great Visual Effects (More about the practical effects and the stunt coordination as they did a great job in going above and beyond (helping continue the legacy of Tom Cruise outdoing his own stunts)), Very Good Production Design (More about where they shot but there were some good sets), Plot Structure was very typical of it being the first of two parts but they did a good job in separating what the conflict of this movie is and what the conflict of the next movie is; the movie is a bit story dense and could have been cut a little bit as some of the scenes were longer than they needed to be, Pacing was a bit on the slower side given that it has a lot of time to play with given its longer runtime and it being one of two parts (The runtime could have been shorter but then some of the action would have been taken away (though some of the scenes definitely could have been shorter)), Climax was executed very well as it has the best stunts of the movie and is an anxiety rush in adrenaline in what is happening on-screen, Tone was very similar to other Mission Impossible/Spy-Action/Tom Cruise movies.

8.title: Tom Cruise doing what he does best
8.content: I have been a huge fan of the mission impossible series and this movie was a really nice addition. I will say, it's not as good as fallout but still very pleasant to see. The movie starts at a slow pace but kicks up in the latter half. The last 40 minutes were thrilling and had me at the edge of the seat. Tom cruise was doing what he's always been doing. The best thing in this movie for me was Hayley Atwell. She absolutely killed it with this movie but it was very weird for them to move on from Rebecca Ferguson. They shouldn't have killed her as it was a great character that was intact with Tom cruise. The other two characters benji and the other guy were sidelined which I thought was a missed opportunity. Overall the movie was a fun watch but could've been better.

8.title: Time Flies.
8.content: Ever since I was kid my favorite to see on TV is the Mission Impossible series, from MI1 to MI6 I watch them all on TV. Now I'm finally old enough to enjoy the seventh in the cinema. But when Tom shows up in the movie, the first thought that came to my mind was time flies so fast, the history of time had been curved of his face, but surprisingly he's still that glorious and charming Ethan Hunt belongs to IMF. His typical greeting with people by biting the cheeks is here again too lol that's really a subtle movement but reveals his charm again and again. It's a little bit absurd that when Luther said he was analyzing all the facial characteristics at the airport that was collected by a pair of sunglasses weared by Ethan while at the airport, that's a little bit far-fetched because I don't really think a small pair of sunglasses has got that level of computing functions or stuff like that but anyways I feel that French-speaking agent has got a more mysterious story to reveal but not actually said in the part 1 of this movie. So, looking forward to the 2 part. Cmon Ethan and Benji.

8.title: Tom Cruise does Tom Cruise
8.content:
Whatever you think of him as a person, Tom Cruise knows how to make a blockbuster movie. Is there any requirement for him to do his own stunts? No. Could someone else have done them cheaper, and quicker? Probably. But he's Tom Cruise, has Tom Cruise money and influence, so does whatever he wants in this industry.

And it works. The motorbike base jump makes absolutely no sense in the context of the film, but it's a glorious, old-fashioned, practical stunt with minimal use of CGI.

I'm bored of Marvel's 2hrs of green screen - give me more like this. Tom, please go on being Tom Cruise for many more years.

8.title: Carefully crafted and at the same time adrenaline pump rush movie
8.content:
Carefully crafted and at the same time adrenaline pump rush movie that will keep you at the edge during first half, then builds slowly in the second half, and again the pump rush at the end.

This movie hits the mark on various fronts. The plot is unique, deep and well explained. The director takes time to untangle various threads on the WHAT and WHY it's happening.

The locales and cinematography is breathtaking - from Empty Quarter (Abu Dhabi) , Spanish Steps (Rome), Venice and Kylling Bridge/ Helsetkopen Mountain (Norway).

Tom Cruise does his usual best with his death defying stunts, including car chases, jumping off the cliff, and even while the train falling off the bridge. Get ready to hold your breath during various occasions.

This movie yearns for more as the plot is so well weaved and provides a good path for part 2 that could end with a big bang.

Watch it on Dolby screen as Mission Impossible takes stunts and sound effects to a new level.

8.title: So good! Each second something crazy is happening
8.content: Mission Impossible is proof that people don't mind long franchises, as long as the story is good, and the action is not overly obnoxious. Personally found Tom cruise in this movie very low key tbh such a smooth humble performance he's there with a bang when you need him in the movie but that bang is so silent and powerful at the same time!! No flashy dialogs or over the top acting in any way which ultimately gives other actors and there are so many of them and its true and everyone shines in the movie equally and that's a total win win + The direction of the movie is soo retro! What a classic vibes full on best action movie from start to finish.

8.content:
Tom Cruise proves once again , he sits on a Hollywood throne and he has no plans in letting anyone taking his place anytime soon.

This movie is brilliant. The action, the riddles, the legendary Tom Cruise!
