Great production and storytelling. Thank you!

8.title: Another Tom Cruise Blockbuster
8.content: I remember growing up through the 90s and seeing blockbuster movies every summer. Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning had me feeling like a kid again with the action and suspense that doesn't disappoint. Tom Cruise once again knows how to get the attention of the audience with stunt after stunt. He knows how to deliver to his fans. Of course you need to have some suspended belief with this film. There were some plot holes that may have you scratching your head, but that is going to happen with most action movies. I do think the film could have been edited down because it is long at 2 hours and 45 minutes. I also think this didn't need to be a 2 part conclusion to the franchise, but these days money comes first and art comes second. Overall, I enjoyed Dead Reckoning Part One. I will definitely see what is in store for Part 2 whenever that comes out.

8.title: I don't accept that.
8.content:
A wise critic (me, right now) once said that action is the universal cinematic language, and Tom Cruise is living proof of that. If the startling revival of Top Gun in the worldwide box office didn't already signify this, then the Mission Impossible franchise, now 27 years long, all but cements it. There's an early scene in Dead Reckoning Part One that is emblematic of all that this series is about, stylistically: the American bigwigs sit in a room and unspool exposition for the audience after the cold open. A rogue AI is on the loose and threatens the national security of every world power. They're the heads of the CIA, IMF, NSA; you name it. It doesn't matter who they are, but what they represent: men (and sometimes, occasionally, women) who are all keenly aware of their near-approaching chance to seize absolute power, men who would sell their souls for that level of control, men who are, in short, not Ethan Hunt. What should be a simple group conversation is shot in the most maximalist way possible, with the coverage frequently breaking the 180-degree rule, pushing in and showing us every gleam in their eyes with extreme close-ups, tilting into a Dutch angle as much as the camera allows, and, when a certain suit slips in, always framing him in the background to practically draw a red arrow to his presence. Never has shallow focus been so in your face. The longer they talk, the more his statue-esque figure haunts the screen, and the more the tension simmers, until finally the scene pops, the mask comes off, and we audibly gasp and laugh and exhale. Not many action movies can make you feel all of those emotions, nevertheless simultaneously. Dead Reckoning then proceeds to do precisely that that precisely over and over again.

In a modern world of living computer programs sabotaging entire nations and drones able to invisibly execute from thousands of miles away, you'd think that plastic masks would have been discarded long ago for slicker, more advanced tech (remember when a dropping into a vault via cables was the peak of this series' stunts?). Not the case for Mission Impossible, which not only steers into the skid, but doubles down repeatedly, and those reveals hit every single time. It doesn't make sense for a sentient artificial intelligence, or, to be honest, any living person with eyes, to not notice a skin crease or stiff cheek. It doesn't have to. IMF sounds like and is a name made up by a 12 year old for the zaniest, coolest action sequences that take you to the limit, and then keep going. For years, the Naughty Dog's Uncharted franchise was heralded for their ability to capture movie-scale blockbuster moments on the smaller screen and let the player experience every explosion and death-defying stunt for themselves. Its second instalment literally drops you into a train carriage hanging off a cliffside in medias res, asking you to jump, climb, and dodge falling furniture to survive. Dead Reckoning more or less recreates this sequence in the midst of its climax AFTER the infamous motorcycle BASE jump, adds two more carriage cutscenes after you think it's over, and then makes Hunt escape from the train AGAIN in a skywing parachute. The theme music swells. We're onto Part 2.

Dead Reckoning is the franchise's funniest film, too, because of the sheer earnestness that it commits to each and every moment, unwilling for even a second to consider becoming a parody of itself. They shot it, so it is in the film. They shot it, so it exists and happens. The train carriages tumble over, and then again, and again. The entire chase in Rome is a masterclass of slapstick action ramped up to 100, high-octane stunts performed by Fiat and tactical jeep alike. Just see Pom Klementieff's maniacal glee as she squashes scooter after scooter in her pursuit; that's all of us, tracking the runaways by spotting the dented cars. I was giggling each time the pair of CIA grunts inexplicably ended up at the scene of the action, and then cheering them on because they're ultimately harmless and only want to witness it all with their own eyes like we do (it can't be a coincidence that one of them resembles Harry from Home Alone). When Hunt runs across the airport's roof in plain view whilst the two scratch their heads? Perfect. The train landing is improbable and hazardous and has Cruise's name stamped all over it, and when the shot reveals a convenient ramp-shaped rock formation, everyone knows what is about to happen. These aren't mere ironic subversions; the franchise has reached a point where it isn't afraid to poke fun at itself, so why hold back on anything? We're not laughing at it for being ridiculous and overwrought, but with it and along with every other member in the audience because it is delivering exactly what we want and are often too embarrassed to admit we want. In a media age where sincerity is poison and everything needs to be obscured by layer upon layer of irony and cynicism, there's a lot of value in that.

The plot and characterisation are often ancillary, although given the main objectives of the series, this isn't the biggest sin. Sometimes, one needs to serve the other. Listen to stunt coordinator and unit director Wade Eastwood sum it up: it's not merely about shooting what is on the script, but needing a character to go from point A to B, and devising the most entertaining means of getting them there. Newcomer Grace is breezily inserted as a small-time accomplice before very suddenly becoming a bigger piece of the puzzle that is the global arms race, and the script does as good a job as it can in endearing us to her as Atwell and Cruise sell us on her importance. If there's one casualty (perhaps self-inflicted due to her rising career, or for some, an instance of fridging) to this it is Rebecca Ferguson's Ilsa, who has been as constant as a love interest in this franchise can be over the last three editions. I'm almost impressed at the ease in which they swap the old model for the new, as if the move was a pre-ordained, Entity-foretold sequence that needed to happen for Part 2 to come into fruition. It's a classic example of the plot prioritising fresh spectacle over emotional heft (I still don't understand why he had to make a choice between the two or how it came to be), and whilst the traditionalist in me should criticise this, my heart was already racing towards the next scene. Another example: Dead Reckoning Part 2 is reportedly the farewell to Ethan Hunt for good, and yet Tom Cruise has also mentioned that he wouldn't turn down an opportunity to return in another film. I'm kidding myself if I said no to that for the sake of the franchise's narrative integrity.

Let's be honest. The film is at its clumsiest when it is trying to round the story's edges; I thought I had completely forgotten about the pivotal scene where Gabriel kills the brunette from Hunt's past, only to realise that it's basically a retcon to beef up his tragic backstory. Given the former's proximity in the race for the magical Macguff-err I mean, very important key, it's hard to be truly frightened of his presence. The AI portion of the premise provides the script with enough convenience to ramp up the tension at a moment's notice, able to morph into any digital threat that the scenario requires. But what more appropriate villain for Ethan Hunt, for Tom Cruise? Much like the Entity itself, he has always risen to the challenge, described aptly as "a mind-reading, shape-shifting incarnation of chaos", and in an era where technology increasingly threatens the very existence of the movie star, he shifts and morphs and goes to another level. When we see Hunt hurtle off a cliff with only a parachute, it is an iron-clad guarantee with the audience that it is him on that motorcycle; you can use CGI to simulate any impossible stunt, but nothing replaces the natural and emotional edge of it actually happening before our eyes. When he runs, it is with every cell in his body, as if to stop running is to cease to exist altogether, the new age of filmmaking nipping at his heels. When Ferguson has been dispatched and Atwell herself seems to lack confidence in her own importance, Cruise looks her in the eye with the utmost reassurance. We can scarcely believe it a mere hour after her introduction, but he wills it into existence. When he says he will be on that train, we KNOW he will be on that train, one way or another. In the age of the cinematic universe and IP battles, you have to respect the work ethic, the sheer desire, of the last genuine Hollywood action star, the last leading man. Tom Cruise is his own brand. Sorry, Jeremy Renner.

8.title: good one FOR REAL
8.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One (2023) Review

Tom Cruise returns as Ethan Hunt in Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One, delivering another high-octane thrill ride that solidifies the franchise's reputation for breathtaking action and jaw-dropping stunts. Directed by Christopher McQuarrie, this installment raises the stakes with a gripping story, a formidable new villain, and some of the most spectacular set pieces in the series' history.

Plot & Execution The film follows Ethan Hunt and his IMF team as they race against time to track down a powerful AI weapon known as "The Entity" before it falls into the wrong hands. With global security at risk, Hunt faces off against shadowy forces, including the enigmatic Gabriel (Esai Morales), an adversary with ties to his past. The story is packed with espionage, deception, and moral dilemmas, giving it a sense of urgency and relevance in an era of digital warfare.

While Dead Reckoning Part One lays the foundation for the grander conclusion in Part Two, it still manages to be a complete and satisfying film. The pacing is relentless, keeping audiences on edge from start to finish. The screenplay balances high-stakes drama with well-placed humor, never losing sight of its core emotional themes-loyalty, sacrifice, and the weight of Ethan's choices.

Action & Stunts The Mission: Impossible franchise is known for its practical stunts, and this film does not disappoint. From a white-knuckle train sequence to a mind-blowing motorcycle jump off a cliff (performed by Cruise himself), the action sequences are nothing short of breathtaking. McQuarrie's direction ensures that every moment feels immersive, with crisp cinematography capturing the tension and spectacle.

Performances & Characters Tom Cruise once again proves why he is one of Hollywood's last true action stars, bringing unwavering intensity and charisma to Ethan Hunt. Hayley Atwell, as the enigmatic Grace, is a standout, offering both charm and unpredictability. Returning favorites like Simon Pegg, Ving Rhames, and Rebecca Ferguson bring warmth and familiarity, while Vanessa Kirby and Pom Klementieff add intrigue and menace to the mix. Esai Morales delivers a chilling performance as Gabriel, a villain who exudes quiet menace rather than over-the-top theatrics.

Verdict Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a masterclass in action filmmaking, blending exhilarating stunts, gripping storytelling, and strong performances into an unforgettable cinematic experience. While it ends on a cliffhanger, the film never feels incomplete-it's a thrilling ride that leaves audiences eagerly anticipating Part Two.

⭐ Rating: 8/10 ⭐ A must-watch for action fans and one of the best entries in the franchise.

And BTW, This review was written by AI........

8.title: Miles better than anything else out there, but...
8.content:
Not as good as the previous movies.

Here are the pros: It doesn't feel like over 2.5 hours, these movies never do feel long. You're also not being lectured to, you're not being scolded, you're not being subjected to the rantings of an identity and race obsessed leftist at any point. You're watching a great, well crafted movie.

Cons: First, you can tell this movie was filmed during the panicked overreaction to covid, because the world this movie takes place in doesn't feel populated. It feels like everyone's moving around in a unpopulated dream world that gives off post-apocalyptic vibe. But I can't fault the movie for that, it was probably a challenge to work under such absurd conditions.

Second, Vanessa Kirby is not a good actress. Her idea for a character is to do the non-blinking, wide-eyed and staring thing while slowly sauntering across the frame. Obviously the filmmakers think that, because she has an interesting face, letting the camera linger on her will make up for the lack of an interesting performance. It doesn't.

I'm sure the second installment will tie it all together and elevate this one, I've yet to be too disappointed in anything this franchise has done.

Those are really the only negatives I can come up with.

8.title: THRILLING, the best M: I yet.
8.content:
There's a winning formula they keep reusing, and they keep on making it work, there are a set of known aspects to it, such as: disavowed mission, your own government coming after you, the impossible mission, Benji and Luther on coms, etc. And then there's a set of unknown aspects, that with brilliance and creativity, they fill with light-hearted comedy, drama, captivating action and thriller.

The new characters are refreshing, the dynamics between Ilsa and Ethan had long become exhausting. Two friends taking a break from saving the world to save each other, please, I'm starting to yawn again. Benji on the field was fun but it was ridiculous. I always wanted to see more of the white widow, and Pom Klementieff's character is a total badass.

I was not instantly sold on the idea of "the Entity", it sounded ridiculous until they slowly present it to you in a way that makes sense, in a way that it becomes a scary adversary.

Thrilling, why? Some of the previous movies were fun but incredibly ridiculous and predictable, there was but one route to follow and the destination was always successful completion of the mission, with minor setbacks but rarely any proper opposition. In this movie the characters are presented with choices that could genuinely take them anywhere. "Choice" is an important concept in this movie. But there is also a lot of fun, these action sequences are much more dynamic and actually make you hold your breath.

What some are forgetting is that this is only the first part, there are many things that will be dived into in the second movie, it's satisfying to know that they've taken their time to tell an interesting story.

8.title: The Hunt continues its upwards trajectory
8.content:
Typing this at the end of the movie in the theater: Ethan Hunt and his team continues an ever exciting and nerve wracking journey to do the work that no one else dares to do. The movie has a very solid pace: returning characters did a solid job fluffing up the story while introducing new ones. Hayley Atwell in particular put in a solid work as the new member of the IMF. Being part one, development for the new villain appeared somewhat lacking, but I trust that Part Two will answer all the questions.

With perhaps the last action segment taking a bit lengthy, the movie kept me on the edge of my seat throughout, and I think it's a must see in theaters.

8.title: An Action Film With Soul
8.content:
In a time where cgi is the star and studio executives care more about coin than ever before it is so refreshing to see a film such as Dead Reckoning.

Seeing live stunts, which used to be so mainstream, performed again is so refreshing. Younger audiences don't know what they have been missing.

The story is strong and the characters have plenty of back story and connectiveness due to the prequels allowing the movie just just move ahead with the story.

Its quite a long film but it never actually feels like it, there is plenty to keep the mind entertained and distracted. Its a perfect movie to get a way from it all .

The only negative was the use of Rhames and Pegg, there characters seemed to lack a little energy, but its a small complaint :)

8.title: My Review
8.content:
A Cruise-ing Triumph with Wheels

Tom Cruise returns as the ever-defiant Ethan Hunt in the seventh installment of the Mission: Impossible franchise, Dead Reckoning Part One. Buckle up, because this film is a high-octane thrill ride that will have you on the edge of your seat.

From the opening moments, Dead Reckoning throws you into the action with a breathtaking motorcycle stunt that sets the tone for the rest of the film. Cruise, as always, commits fully to every death-defying feat, and the film's stunt team deserves a standing ovation for crafting some of the most pulse-pounding sequences in recent memory.

The Grand Prix of Car Chases

But the crown jewel of the action is undoubtedly the car chase sequence that takes place through the winding streets of Rome. This masterfully choreographed ballet of screeching tires, near misses, and hilarious one-liners is both exhilarating and laugh-out-loud funny. It's a sequence that could be ripped straight from the pages of a James Bond novel, and it's sure to be talked about for years to come.

A Familiar, Yet Timely Story

While the core plot of Dead Reckoning might not be the most groundbreaking, the film cleverly spins a familiar yarn into something that feels refreshingly relevant. The themes of global threats, technological warfare, and the price of loyalty resonate in our current climate, adding a layer of depth to the adrenaline-fueled action.

Cruise Controls the Show

Tom Cruise is, as always, the anchor of the film. His Ethan Hunt is a charismatic blend of action hero and vulnerable soul, and Cruise delivers a performance that's both thrilling and emotionally resonant. The supporting cast, including the always-excellent Rebecca Ferguson and the delightful newcomer Hayley Atwell, provide able backup, but it's Cruise who truly owns the screen.

Verdict: A Must-See for Action Fans

Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a non-stop thrill ride that delivers on all fronts. The action is jaw-dropping, the humor is spot-on, and the story, while familiar, is well-told and timely. If you're looking for a film that will keep you entertained from start to finish, then this is the mission for you. Just remember to hold onto your popcorn, because things are about to get bumpy.

Rating: 8/10.

8.title: Dead Reckoning 1
8.content:
I might have missed the Cruise/McQuarrie spectacle at the cinema, but I don't regret it. It was not as good as Fallout, but it was still a great-great film. One of the best of the year so far.

Look, there is a lot to say about what the story says (with the A. I. and world-ending feel) and what the actors did with the material but I have a beef with the editing. I dunno, there were a lot of moments that felt jarring and cut in a weird way. Of course, in the action set pieces it was all great, a non-issue.

All in all for the last hour I have only one thing to say: I like trains. And can't wait for part 2, which I will see at the cinema.

8.title: Breathtaking, visually superb 7th franchise film - with only half a story
8.content: As a 'Pt 1' suffixed, 163min, 7th franchise film, "Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" drags - BUT is visually superb with some terrific performances. So props to Christopher McQuarrie's excellent direction - tho with Erik Jendresen he couldn't even write a whole film. This time Tom Cruise, Simon Pegg, Ving Rhames, Rebecca Ferguson & now Hayley Atwell (strong) battle baddies Esai Morales, Pom Klementieff (both great) & Vanessa Kirby (and cop Shea Whigham) across the likes of Venice & The Orient Express to stop an all-powerful AI taking over the world (sigh). Cary Elwes, Chris Parnell & others support a wild roller-coaster ride. It's breath-taking... for half a story.

8.title: Mission accomplished
8.content: I mean it's mission impossible! You know what to expect. Still, I thought there was a nice twist to it. I didn't expect the story to turn out this way. Made me scared about the future in technology (just kidding of course hihi) The stunts were great! Tom Cruise what can't he do?! You see that the movie has a big budget. After so many mission impossible movie's you expert that they run out of ideas. But they kill it every single time! And loved the running scenes the iconic Tom Cruise run. Absolutely lovely and also a little bit funny. When the second chapter comes out i will definitely go to the theater to watch the next movie.

8.title: Amazing Movie
8.content:
Probably one of my favourite action films ever, i just finished watching this for the first time in about 20 years. Full of action, suspense and great stunts, Tom Cruise plays young spy Ethan Hunt on the run after a failed mission where it sees his team killed off after a suspicious set up. Cruise plays his character with a limp wrist and an incredibly unique walk. According to sources he cut his own hair on set and refused to be handed food by anyone that was born in march.

The brilliant Jon Voight also stars, who turns out to be the antagonist, turns out Voight didn't know how to wear hats properly which transpired to the screen as you can see in most scenes. In an interview he actually said - quote "i gave up trying to figure out how to put hats on, so i made it a character trait" The action sequences are unforgettable, especially the tense "cable drop" scene, where it sees Tom Cruise lowered down into a secure room full of all kinds of security sensors, that was almost an impossible mission... but not quite. The scene is shot perfectly, no music, hardly no sounds, almost pure silence. I was so captivated by this scene, my cat meowed which startled me flipping my dinner off my lap into my face, i got so much mash potatoe and beef in my hair i spent 2 hours in the shower trying to get it out.

The film ends with another terrific action sequence involving the helicopter chase through the channel tunnel, it was pretty crazy and over the top but it worked and i loved it. If you look closely in this action scene you can see there's bits of lasagne on Jon Voights clothes, which he always ate before shooting a scene. The director decided to keep it in, saying it gave his character depth and meaning.

I have to give 5 stars for this, always a joy to watch.

I'm going to watch mission impossible 2 next and I'm really hoping to see more cardigans worn.

8.title: I liked it
8.content: I have seen every Mission Impossible movie and the only one I really liked was Ghost Protocol. This movie was the second best. Though I was a little annoyed with the train scene since I know there is no way the cars would have kept moving with all of the cars brakes engaged at back of the bridge that was still on level ground. I really liked Hayley Atwell the only other movies I had seen her in was Captain America and she has been working out since she has never looked this fit before. I only watched this movie since it was available for free on Prime right now. In fact I have seen all of the movies for free except I purchased the Ghost Protocol Blu-ray.

8.title: One of the best of the series
8.content:
I won't explain too much in this latest instalment of the popular spy franchise, partly because it's very complicated, (Maybe a little too much), but also not to spoil anything as the story is quite a unique one as spy movies go.

What i will say is despite the long running time, this film rarely feels slow, due to a lot of fast-paced stunt scenes, which will all get the adrenalin pumping. The train finale is particularly noteworthy, with although some very farfetched elements, delivers big time on the climax we never got with Fast X.

Tom Cruise is also on top form, with his usual charismatic, humourous yet determined drive as Ethan.

Some films have got tired by their multi-sequel cash-ins, this is not one of them, this is as good as any of the previous outings, if not one the best.

8.title: Worth the wait!
8.content:
Mission impossible delivered! Was one of the few movies I was eager to watch at a cinema this year and I very much enjoyed Dead Reckoning part I a lot just like I hoped I would. The humor worked which is a very big deal for me as I was extremely burnt out from the goofiness in recent releases ( yes marvel humor is trash ). Spectacular cinematography through out, awesome and captivating action scenes, matured and likable characters, breathtaking stunts and did I mention the witty humor? I was truly entertained. Been a while since I enjoyed my day at the local cinema this year. Thank you Tom Cruise for keeping this grand and terrific franchise alive! May you never age!

Tom's dedication has always amazed me since his Burj Khalifa stunt in ghost protocol. Another death defying one here, jumping off a steep cliff into a sheer drop. Not only once but 6x. A stickler for perfection. Even the magic trick with the key is performed practically. A point to that. His devotion and enthusiasm at his age needs a praise. He breathes life onto this franchise.

Also I loved the fact Ethan was not fighting in service of any of the factions whether the CIA, MI6 or Kremlin but to destroy such cataclysmic weapon as it does not belong in the hands of power hungry politicians. His struggle was not for the sake of nationalism or personal gain but in furtherance of human life. A hero for all. A movie for all.

I enjoyed my time a lot. Nevertheless, that doesn't mean Dead Reckoning part I is flawless. The writing was very much cliched and was bored a lot on all the chatting scenes. Craziest and most implausible villain so far. An all knowing, clairvoyant, God like AI. There are scenes where a display of an eye or some bubbles on a screen embody the treacherous computer program and it's supposed to be terrifying but came of as just silly. Fights felt too unrealistic and choreographed. The Japanese girl was not even a tad bit intimidating. She was a weird choice in an all matured cast. Some dragged out scenes. The Russians should've spoken in their native language instead of English in a stereotypical accent. Awful Hollywood trope. Benjie and Luther were almost missing after the first act. The airport scene with them was delightful. The rest of the movie would have been cooler if the old cast was there.

The biggest disappointment was the passing of Elsa. She was a capable and a likable character. Her role as a mercurial secret agent matched Ethan's, so they were perfect for each other. She was awesome on the last 2 movies and replacing her was a blow to the sack. Her new substitute is likable and fun indeed but uninteresting as she's a mere thief who lacks the enigma and warrior spirit Elsa possesses. The villainous Jap had a longer period of grief than Elsa. After her death, the crew immediately went straight to business. That was just wrong.

Taking everything into consideration, Dead Reckoning part I was an extravaganza. Another great sequel. Not the best for sure but a thoroughly pleasant experience. A seal of approval from me.

8.title: An Enjoyable 2 part finale on the MI series.
8.content:
Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1 is a 2 parter sequel and a follow up to Fallout.

Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise)and the IMF team(Ving Rhames and Simon Pegg along with Rebecca Ferguson) team up with a theif named Grace(Hayley Atwell) and together they must track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens all of humanity if it falls into the wrong hands.

With control of the future and the fate of the world at stake, a deadly race around the globe begins. Confronted by a mysterious, all-powerful enemy, Ethan is forced to consider that nothing can matter more than the mission -- not even the lives of those he cares about most.

Overall this was a good film. The subplot is AI as the villian creates things that aren't there e.g in the opening scene we see a submarine that isn't there at all. Some people might not like this one but at least it's better than Mission Impossible 2.

8.title: Tom cruises the MI Ship
8.content: Ever since I started watching English movies, I have come to know that there is the most handsome guy on the planet who plays a spy in movies and does awesome action sequences. That guy is Tom Cruise in the "Mission Impossible" series. I guess he is in his sixties, and I am in my forties, but even someone in their twenties still thinks the same. The movie has the most generic "MI" script with a pinch of Artificial Intelligence element in it. However, it compensates for the script with astounding action sequences as always, successfully making people eagerly await the second part. It is a glorious visual treat.

8.title: Cruise continues to defy and still entertains....
8.content:
8.0/10 (Highly Recommend)

For a first time watch through this film is spectacular, but admittedly I would rather sit through a four plus hour film to see it through to conclusion than to be left wondering if and when the second part truly gets released. However, when part two is eventually released I hope it's the end of the franchise. Eight films would definitely see the conclusion of a great franchise.

I had been looking forward to see this film for ages. I'm sad I couldn't have seen it in theatres, but my own home theatre slightly makes up for that. The action is awesome and while there's a few finicky parts that lack realism it doesn't detract from the concept of the story as it's replaced by other realism that's a little too real.

I continue to love the acting especially when new faces are added or old ones return. Every time the mask part shows up I'm enthralled. Imagine if it were so simple to disguise one's self. Of course the adage of don't get too attached to a character rings true. There's so many that I don't feel it's a spoiler.

The cinematography continues to be outstanding. It captures the action, the emotions, and the story in a way that you feel you're an accomplice to everything. It's also nice to finally see a character not actually be able to drive a getaway car as if it's part of their everyday life.

Overall, I hope this movie is second to the end. It would be nice if the next film closed out the series. It's been a great ride and adventure as everything has built on the next. Tom Cruise knows how to entertain and bring the big without being unrealistic about it. While the story is new some of the characters aren't so you could start here, but it may get a little confusing to some.

That's all for now. Thank you for taking the time to read my review. Until next time.... Enjoy the show!

8.title: IT'S WORTTHHHHH NGLL
8.content: In Mission: Impossible - Fallout, Henry Cavill plays August Walker, a CIA agent with his own agenda. The film is one of the best in the Mission: Impossible franchise, with thrilling action sequences, breathtaking stunts, and high-stakes espionage. Cavill holds his own against Tom Cruise, and his character's moral ambiguity adds a layer of tension to the plot. Cavill's physicality is on full display here, especially during the much-talked-about bathroom fight scene, which stands as one of the most brutal and well-choreographed fights in recent action films. His portrayal of Walker brings an edge to the character, making him a formidable opponent to Cruise's Ethan Hunt. Cavill's performance helps elevate the film, which is filled with twists, turns, and some of the best action set-pieces of the last decade.

8.title: Another exciting half-entry in the Mission: Impossible franchise.
8.content:
When it comes to the Mission: Impossible movies, you know what you're going to get. Tense countdowns. Action set-pieces. Tom Cruise running. Even though the Impossible Mission Force (IMF) has overcome many obstacles in the past, there's always a question of whether this latest mission will be too much for them. With Mission: Impossible-Dead Reckoning (Part 1) (2023), the threat is so large that this movie only covers half of it. As long as you're OK with not having a conclusion to the full plot, this movie is fun and full of action.

With Artificial Intelligence (AI) being a current hot topic, using it as the antagonist of this film felt like it fit right into the cultural zeitgeist. Not that AI has been a new villain by any means (as 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) has shown). Considering the (fictional) power of this AI, the Maguffin of the two-piece key to control it was a great way to drive the plot and the action. The ebb and flow of the double and triple crosses provided just enough twists to make the friends and foes always in a state of limbo.

Of course, a Mission: Impossible movie is always going to be a Mission: Impossible movie. I've enjoyed them for many years for all the reasons stated above. However, if it's not your thing, then you'll probably be bored with the same old car chases, just in different foreign locales. At the very least, the female lead (Hayley Atwell) for this film was an excellent addition to the team, as it came with some weighty decisions on her part. I'm definitely interested to see how they conclude this two-part movie when Mission: Impossible-Dead Reckoning (Part 2) comes out next year.

Another exciting half-entry in the Mission: Impossible franchise, I give Mission: Impossible-Dead Reckoning (Part 1) 4.0 stars out of 5.

8.title: Mission Impossible and Tom Cruise do not Miss!
8.content:
First and foremast MI7 is an adrenaline filled action film. It's relentless from start to finish causing the 2 hours and 43 minutes runtime to fly-by. The action feels real too, Tom Cruise does not cut any corners. You watch every twist, turn, jump and fight as if it is somebody you know. This is partly down to how well these scenes are shot and partly down to the depth of the characters.

Speaking of characters, there are loads in this film! There are returning fan favourites and some excellent new additions from Hayley Atwell who was fantastic in every scene to Pom Klementieff who plays a villain that would not be out of place in a Kill Bill style action movies. Each character brings something fresh to the table.

The story partly focuses on rogue AI and misinformation which is topical and interesting given the current state of AI. Whilst one may get confused with all the characters and call-backs to previous films, the story does feel more straightforward than some of the others in the franchise.

Finally, this is the third film in recent memory (Fast X, Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse) to effectively be a part one of two. However, by the time you come the end of MI7, you feel that you have embarked on a satisfying journey in spite of the fact that they overall story is incomplete. If you are going to watch an action film in the cinema this year, it should be this one.

8.title: a thrilling ride, can't wait for part two
8.content:
The mission: impossible franchise continues to deliver high-stakes, heart-pounding action in dead reckoning part one. This latest installment brings back Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt, and it's packed with the kind of intense stunts, intricate plots, and global intrigue that fans have come to expect. The film is filled with twists and turns, and from the very beginning, it grabs your attention and doesn't let go.

What makes this movie stand out is its ability to maintain a constant sense of suspense and excitement. The action scenes are brilliantly choreographed, with Tom Cruise once again performing his own stunts, which adds an extra layer of authenticity and thrill. The plot is engaging, with a well-written script that keeps you guessing until the end. The film sets up high expectations for the second part, leaving you eagerly waiting to see what happens next.

Overall, dead reckoning part one is a strong addition to the mission: impossible series. It's exciting, well-acted, and delivers on its promise of non-stop entertainment. I give it an 8/10 for its thrilling action sequences, engaging story, and solid performances.

8.title: Full of great action sequences, the dynamism of "M:I 7", combined with the complexity of the central theme, prevents it from being tiring despite the long duration
8.content:
In "M:I - Dead Reckoning: Part 1", Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) faces an Artificial Intelligence that started as an assistant to the American government, but ended up learning on its own as it worked and transformed into a deadly sentient creature, willing to predict future panoramas and find ways to eliminate them, guaranteeing their existence. And for those who think this is exaggerated, it's worth remembering that we live in a world where everyone carries a phone all the time, there are digital locks, traffic is controlled by computers and the main armed forces on the planet depend on technology to attack. Hunt needs to gather his usual collaborators, as well as a talented thief (Hayley Atwell) to reach his opponent Gabriel (Esai Morales), who may hold the two halves of a key capable of opening the new global weapon. Simon Pegg, Rebecca Ferguson, Ving Rhames and Vanessa Kirby return to their roles from the previous films.

The seventh chapter arrives to be ambitious, obvious, starting from a simple base and triumphing around the action. And in fact, "Settlement of Accounts - Part 1" succeeds, it is an "M:I" film seeking to be increasingly longer even in terms of duration, but it also brings a different result when the characteristic style of the saga now inserts trends that make the average with the public. A good example of this is the escape scene between improvisations and changing vehicles that ends with a comical number between Grace (Hayley Atwell) and Ethan driving in circles in a Beetle through the streets of Rome and Venice. The point here is: what movie doesn't want to make its moment funny? And "M:I" used other means to bring humor in its own way, but here, it is evident the pauses that the film takes to insert jokes beyond the usual. However, what disguises this is because McQuarrie does not lose sight of the tension in the middle of the action, and does not have the characters self-confirm that they are in the "joke moment" of the narrative.

"M:I Part 1" presents all the ingredients that have made this franchise derived from the eponymous TV series one of the most popular for decades. Ethan brings together the usual team, is faced with puzzles that are practically impossible to put together and once again becomes the key to saving the world. Especially in the first third of the feature film, things work very well, never reaching the level of its predecessor "Mission: Impossible - Fallout (2018)", it's true, but also never ceasing to surprise. McQuarrie reaffirms his quality as a director of action scenes, giving the expected intensity to car chases, to the moments in which the lack of time adds tension to naturally dramatic situations, avoiding that feeling prevalent in recent blockbusters that absolutely everything was done beforehand. Of a green screen. It is worth highlighting the attention to detail, such as the sweat appearing to signal the nervousness of the submarine crew about to be hit by torpedoes. Having made the positive considerations, it must be said that the script written by McQuarrie and Erik Jendresen does not have much breath, something perceived by the obvious facilities frequently used to situate the viewer and manifested by the dramatic emptying of this web of movements and twists on the screen.

One of the main problems of the seventh adventure of "M:I" is the use of excessively expository dialogue to explain to the viewer the technical details and conspiratorial particularities. More than once, Christopher McQuarrie allows the film to slow down just so someone can explain the details of what is happening and what could result from the Entity's growth. In fact, speaking of the villain, AI could be better explored as a practically invincible enemy, as it has the ability to alter any digital situation - for example, erase cronies from security monitoring circuits and cover their tracks digitally. The confrontation in this virtuality could even allow the very clever Benji (Simon Pegg) and Luther (Ving Rhames) to be more than just luxury supports appearing every now and then. However, the director chooses to make the Entity almost a McGuffin, that is, an element that moves the story forward, but that loses in importance to other figures. McQuarrie decides to elect Gabriel (Esai Morales), someone who hurt Ethan in the past, as a bodily extension of the Entity. The result is that neither artificial intelligence is elaborated as a global threat nor the rivalry with the flesh-and-blood nemesis is convincing on a dramatic level.

That said, the film is built around this epic clash between man and machine, showing that Tom Cruise is willing to face computers on and off the screen. And he does it like no one else at 61 years old. Previously considered just a Hollywood heartthrob, Cruise has established himself as the main name in current action and makes every second on screen count. His Ethan Hunt comes naturally and continues to impress with his sense of escapism. Now, however, he shares the spotlight with a supporting character who is equal to the protagonist. Grace, played by Hayley Atwell, is an international thief who crosses Ethan's path for the object needed to intercept the machine. But she's not interested in using the weapon for global destruction or anything like that. Like all good movie thieves, she just wants to get paid. Now, together with Hunt, she needs to escape henchmen who are really looking for the A. I. for evil. And so, a relationship emerges that is built organically. It's impossible not to root for them, even though they spend the entire time fooling themselves on screen.

Starting from this relentless duo on screen, the plot takes the audience towards 2h45 of pure adventure and adrenaline. Paranoia is the feeling that dominates "Dead Reckoning Part 1", and is the driving force that ensures that the film is always in constant movement. The action does not just arise from the need to complete the mission, but rather from being able to carry it out in increasingly adverse conditions. At 2h43 long, the audience loses their breath with the constant emergence of new problems, headaches and moments of tension in quick succession. In this regard, director Christopher McQuarrie does a great job of showing the action happening, without quick cuts, clearly showing the effort of those involved in trying to make everything look as realistic as possible. Obviously, there are digital touches in some moments, but nothing that takes the focus away from seeing stuntmen or Tom Cruise himself actually throwing himself off a cliff, as this man increasingly makes me believe that he wants to die in front of a team of filming, but just don't know how.

At one point, for example, Hunt and his allies need to intercept a suspicious sale at an airport, and the mission is to find the target, recover the item (a piece of a key, related to the Entity) and escape without being noticed. But the group is being hunted by the police, which complicates movement through the terminals. And then the thief Grace (Hayley Atwell) appears, who steals the seller's key, without knowing what she's getting into. When the police siege tightens, she is forced to cooperate with the protagonist, and the two attempt a bombastic escape from the place. Ah, in the middle of all this, Benji (Simon Pegg) needs to defuse a nuclear bomb hidden among the luggage. The entire excerpt symbolizes the film's approach, always seeking to create progressively more complex, intense and suffocating situations, which do not seem to have a solution. For almost three hours, "Settlement" offers constant tension, and it is even necessary to take a breather when leaving the theater, especially due to the megalomaniacal scope of the sequences.

Since the third chapter, the franchise has become defined by Tom Cruise's insanities. This is very evident here, in a work committed to creating action spectacles with as little computer graphics as possible. In recent years, the figure of the actor (and producer) has become the target of discussions when he joined the fight over the importance of the cinematic experience, given the growth of streaming and home sessions driven by the pandemic. Seeing him run, jump his motorbike off a mountain peak, escape in a compact Cinquecento through Italian streets, or even climb onto the top of a moving train, are great reminders that Cruise is willing to do anything in the name of the crazy grandeur that only cinema can deliver. The partnership with director Christopher McQuarrie, who supports and carries out many of its crazy things, is one of the reasons why this franchise remains relevant and full of life even after 25 years on the big screen.

The "M:I" saga has always focused on the present. No matter how much continuity there was, each film brought its own set of dilemmas to be explored and resolved within the work. "Dead Reckoning" sounds like a rather abrupt turn in emphasizing the past, with a plot full of nostalgia and analog technology, and preparing a future beyond its second half, but with little attachment to the now. Interestingly, the film proves the quality of the saga and is among the best releases so far, given its excellent cast and commitment to high-level action. It's almost three hours of pure intensity, leaving you eager for Part Two and regretting the end of one of cinema's best sagas. This first part could just have been less self-congratulatory and expository. Even so, this chapter presents what was already expected, remaining faithful to the structure seen since the 1996 film. However, the dynamism of the story, combined with the complexity of the central theme, prevents it from being tiring despite the long duration, at least On the contrary, it promotes spectators' involvement with the story by generating expectations around the resolution of the problem and the future of the mission.

8.title: Another Solid Mission Impossible Movie
8.content: An amazingly directed successor to the increasingly epic sequels with impressive stunt work, expertly choreographed action sequences, charismatic performances, clever espionage set pieces, and nail-biting tension that keeps you at the edge of your seats. My only gripe has been consistent with the other sequels is the vaguely underlying misogyny with the seldom female characters often being relegated to either being "untrustworthy", lacking much positive agency unless they're being traitorous, being bad at driving, in frequent need of rescue by Tom Cruise, and/or being fridged after they've served their purpose for Tom Cruise. Luckily all 3 female characters have at least some redeeming qualities (mostly their performances), so it doesn't drag down the movie too much. This movie is still an exciting action thrill ride that makes me so excited for part 2!

8.title: Mission (almost) accomplished
8.content: With the seventh chapter of the Mission Impossible saga we are taken back a little to what were the beginnings of the saga itself, both from the point of view of the characters, the direction and the narration. From a directorial point of view, in particular, Christopher McQuarrie confirms himself as one of the most capable action moviemakers of recent years, managing to put together an extreme variety of action scenes that are different from each other in a memorable and adrenaline-filled way. Nonetheless, however, the direction also seems to want to emulate the style of Brian de Palma, already director of the first chapter, and the insistent use of Dutch angles and close-ups turns out to be a mere exercise in style rather than a truly inspired choice. From a narrative point of view the plot becomes more understandable after two or three viewings of the movie, since at first it appears to be excessively convoluted but once unraveled it acquires a very high degree of entertainment. The choice to divide the movie into two parts is unjustified and this is noticeable due to the unnecessarily long duration of this part one. Numerous action scenes last longer than they should and some events are extremely dilated in time. Nonetheless, the movie is in no way boring and the stunts, which are now an integral part of what elevates the Mission Impossible saga above the average of other action franchises, always keep the viewer in suspense and are worthy of be appreciated in style at the cinema.

8.title: Some Faults, Yet Always Entertaining With Tom
8.content:
Tom Cruise has to be one of the most consistent Hollywood superstars there is. Seemingly every summer he gives adrenaline junkies something to get excited about. Although the plot for this story is using a pretty standard modern day topic of AI taking over the world, Tom's action stunts and effort he puts into the movie really make it worth the watch. As he always says before the movie starts now "they made it for you" and is very adamant that it is made for the big screen.

Although it runs long there's no section that loses the pace. There's certainly a lot of characters to keep track of and it's not always clear who is working for who and why , but that's a bit of Mission Impossible's modus operandi. Luther and Benji fit perfectly as Ethan's friends and partners in crime. The scenes when they're all on camera together is soothing. The actors have a good natural chemistry that makes their bond believable. Vanessa Kirby is excellent in her role , but wasn't totally sold on Hayley Atwell. Esai Moralles was fine as the villain , but not spectacular.

There's some loose ends to the story no doubt , but we can hope they're tidied up in part 2. The biggest one for me being : what is the nature of Gabriel's relationship with the entity and how does he communicate with it directly?

All in all it's a nice summer flick. If you've liked Tom Cruise in previous work you ll likely enjoy this too. I didn't like this movie as much as last years Top Gun: Maverick , but still happy I hit the theatre for it.

8.title: You Should Choose To Accept This Mission
8.content: Tom Cruise has another solid hit with Mission: Impossible 7. Dead Reckoning Part 1 brings the action and death defying stunts that Cruise is well known for. The story is perfectly timed for an era of ever growing technology. AI has become a topic of interest here as of recent. This is something that should not be taken lightly. The team of writers wonderfully crafted a story around a hot topic issue in today's society. This pays off for the cast and crew of this film. The story, action, and cast make this a solid film. However, this being my personal opinion, would have liked to seen the team lose in some capacity at the end. This would have made the film more interesting. This could have set up a nice rebound for the sequel. This is just my opinion and I overall enjoyed this sequel.

8.title: Entertaining action fantasy.
8.content: The films in the Mission Impossible franchise border on self-parody and Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One (2023) is no exception, All those bombastic speeches about the end of the world being imminent, and only Ethan Hunt and his band of covert rogue operatives can pull it back from the brink. Having said that, you've gotta admire the set piece action sequences which are often very impressive on a technical level and for their sheer spectacle. The crashed train sequence here is a case in point. Hayley Atwell is very strong in a much deserved lead role, and there is also great support from Rebecca Ferguson and Vanessa Kirby (as The White Widow). Tom Cruise does his usual schtick but does it very well in an overall entertaining piece of action fantasy.

8.title: Great start that fizzles with self-absorption
8.content:
A middle-aged man facing a mid-life crisis who starts out with energy and vigour, but eventually tapers off to a tired and drawn out self-absorption. Describes both the film and the star.

I was rocketed back and forth by the fast-paced early scenes with twists, and humour. But then the Viagra but have worn off for this initial stand-up production and things got very limp.

The turning point was when one of the key characters decides for the 5th time to double-cross Cruise despite almost getting killed all the other 4 times she did so.

And then there was the train scene. An apt metaphor for staging an endless series of action scenes as contrived as they were confined. The writing team had too many Red Bulls in the brainstorming room coming up with all the ways they could milk this device. Unfortunately, the facilitator must have opened with "there are no bad ideas" and all of them made it into the film.

Meanwhile, Cruise probably didn't even bother scrutinising the action shots of him riding, jumping, fighting, parachuting, grappling, etc. "Keep 'em all in from all angles...I did all those stunt myself you know so let's milk them and get our money's worth from those expensive insurance riders." he must have said. And we're only in PART ONE!

Great film for watching with your partner who falls asleep halfway through every film because they won't miss a thing.

8.title: Great Action Movie But...
8.content:
Loved Tom Cruz, love the comedy in it, the supporting characters and loved the action! Lots of good action scenes, keeps you excited to continue watching.

The storyline is good enough, even scary because we live in such a high tech world and everything one says and looks at is being taken note of.

That said the return villain is not very exciting but what was a let down was the annoying new protagonist, Grace, that made much of the movie annoying, not a the actress's fault just the role she plays is super frustrating. Couldn't wait to skip her parts, if only they had her less dumb in her decisions , the movie would have hit the mark a bit more.

Still worth the watch.

8.content:

8.title: Great film, maybe a little overhyped tho....?
8.content: Hello again film lovers! Ok sooo MI-7, those of you reading are probably looking to see if the film lives up to all the overwhelming hype its got and let me say in some ways yes, in some ways no. Before I continue let me try and save you some time first by showing you what I rate the other films in this series. Then at least it will give you an idea of if your gunna read the rest of this review lol ok so MI:1-7/10, MI:2-10/10, MI:3-9/10, parts 4-6 all 11/10! So read on, should you chose to do so lol I'm a lifelong fan of Mr Cruise(seriously the guy only makes a questionable film every few leap years and has been doing so since the early 80s!)and this series of films, I still remember getting all hyped aged only 13 to see the original mission impossible and then falling asleep in the cinema as I was so bored! Lol but then part 2 was just my kind of crazy spy vs spy action film, plus I'm a VERY big fan of John Woo! And so I was back on board and have been a LOYAL fan ever since. As is popular opinion with fans of the series, these films have just gone from strength to strength, particularly with parts 4-6, Fallout being especially EPIC filmmaking at its best! I've even seen the last three in the London IMAX costing me a total of £75 each time just to ensure I watched every second of them exactly how Mr Cruise and team wanted us to. So to say I was excited to see this latest instalment, especially after the pandemic delays etc, was a HUGE understatement!(I even had trouble sleeping the night before, can you blame me after how AMAZING Fallout was?!) So I did my best Tom Cruise run to catch my train, constantly thinking of the train stunt in this one's trailer I may add! Lol And excitedly me and my brother talked about how epic this new film was as literally EVERY single review at that point had said basically it's the best movie ever! And after the last 3 being arguably that high in quality we had no reason to doubt it! Soooo my first impression was, honestly, a little underwhelmed I'm sad to report, and my brother felt the same. Don't get me wrong it is great and very entertaining, but my expectations were maybe a little too high to live up to? But the other thing that really bugged me was that they really did show ALL of the best bits in the trailer, the big bike stunt for example, if you've seen the trailer you've seen the whole stunt already. The film just feels like one big chase scene, everyone is chasing everyone else, my brother actually complained that he felt a bit dizzy afterwards lol Something just felt a bit....off? It didn't feel as clever or as tense as previous instalments, but that could just be me. Let me also point out that some friends of mine went to see it and they hadn't seen any of the previous ones, they thought it was AMAZING! Like literally one of the best action films they'd ever seen and those friends do have VERY good taste in films also. So naturally I then watched all others from 4 onwards with them, very interested to see if they still thought this one was the best one even after having now seen parts 4-6, and I have to admit they actually still do! And yes they did LOVE parts 4-6 especially, like the rest of us lol So that's why I said yes and no to the film living up to the hype, me and my brother felt it wasn't as amazing as parts 4-6 unfortunately(even tho we desperately wanted it to be better, but maybe that was asking a bit too much tbf?), but other friends of mine do think it is the BEST instalment yet so it really is up to you to make your own call on it. By Hollywood standards it does, as most other mission impossible films do, stand out a MILE in filmmaking excellence! You know with these films you are getting unbridled entertainment for sure so you will definitely have a blast watching this latest instalment. But as us film geeks can't help but always do, is it the best one yet?? The decision is up to you! Lol I'm hoping that once we get part 2 I will want to re-review this part one as I'm sure I will be the one after all is revealed saying THESE ARE THE BEST ONES YET! Lol I won't even be mad or embarrassed because it will hopefully be down to how multi layered in writing both parts are which I will love! At the end of the day the thing that REALLY makes this series of films so damn entertaining is how brilliantly written they are. Nothing kills an action film quicker than dumb writing, Endgame and The Predator I'm talking to you! Grrr still mad about how much potential both those films had and just blew it with TERRIBLE writing! Anyways, I hope I have helped you fans understand that this part one needs to be seen to really get your own feel for it and see where you place it in the order of 7 films in the series. I'll still be doing my best Tom Cruise impression running up to London to see part 2 on opening day and will write my review on that the same day, I left this review until I got the digital copy of this part so I could watch it again before committing to this review. So to summarise, this film is GREAT, but if like me you are a long time fan of the series you may find it's been a little bit overhyped and not as good as previous instalments. So thanks again for listening and until the next time wishing you and your families well, stay safe and May the force be with you.

8.title: Best Action Scenes Executed to Perfection👍🏻
8.content:
Scintillating action project ever made in Hollywood so far. A pack of four adrenaline rushed sequences made an epic action flick by Tom Cruise with his age daring physical fitness.

Tom is acting and supervising everything in the action sets to perfection with an expenditure of $280 million for stunts alone!

When you settled that this action scene must be the peak moment of the movie then there comes another one! Wow!

Gods bless all the extras and the time taken to shot the action sequences thousands of times to get such a marvellous product.

Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One, as suggested by that ominous "part one," seems to care a bit more about its plot, and it's not hard to see why. This time, Cruise's Ethan Hunt isn't fighting nihilistic terrorists or vaporous international-espionage networks but an all-powerful artificial intelligence known as "the Entity" that has instant access to any and all online networks and can effectively dupe the world's tech-reliant militaries into fighting one another. It's a variation on the man-versus-machine theme that Cruise and McQuarrie pursued in last year's Top Gun: Maverick and a rather compelling metaphor for their well-publicized dedication to old-school action film-making and real-life stunt work. It also happens to resonate with our current moment: You can easily imagine the Entity standing in for any number of modern society's (and modern cinema's) high-tech bogeymen, from dead-eyed disrupters to algorithm-obsessed visionaries.

There's an Easter-eggy quality to much of Dead Reckoning, but McQuarrie & Co. Escalate matters effectively. Alec Baldwin's Alan Hunley once memorably called Ethan Hunt "the living manifestation of destiny"; this time, Shea Whigham's Jasper Briggs, (yet) an(other) intelligence agent tasked with bringing Hunt in, describes him as "a mind-reading, shape-shifting incarnation of chaos." Everybody is set in their usual roles. Rebecca Ferguson's Ilsa Faust is once again a cross between love interest and mysterious outsider, a rogue spy who has to save Ethan and be saved by him at key moments. Vanessa Kirby returns as the White Widow, an arms dealer who plays all sides. Among the latest additions to the main cast, Esai Morales brings an impressively chilly hauteur to Gabriel, a death-obsessed terrorist working for the Entity. Hayley Atwell's Grace, a professional thief who winds up entangled in the attempt to retrieve two halves of a mysterious key that everybody's after, makes for an energetic audience surrogate, and she and Cruise have excellent chemistry. It's also hard at times to tell if Grace was just in the wrong place at the wrong time or if there's more to her. A number of these characters seem like they'll get their true moment in the sun in part two.

Within the context of the film, the stunt (and our awareness of its approach) also works as a clever bit of distraction. So much time is spent setting up the motorcycle jump that we might start to think that's going to be the climax of the movie. But what comes afterward - an extended train sequence that culminates in what might be the most hair-raising derailment ever put to film, full of seesawing train cars and dangling movie stars - is even more unforgettable. That is, in many ways, the enduring charm of all these films: They feel like magic tricks, built as they are on anticipation, familiarity, misdirection, and spectacle. Whenever it gets down to the business of making Tom Cruise run and jump and drive and fly in and out of things, Dead Reckoning manages to astonish.

8.title: If plot holes were pot holes
8.content:
You could lose a train in these.

Right off the bat I loved the movie. I loved the balance of action with nuanced interaction, I loved the stunts - more so because most of them were practical and not CGI.

But (and it's a big but) a couple of plot holes were so insultingly stupid and unnecessary it was like finding a rat's tail in an otherwise gourmet meal.

Insulting plot hole 1: Steam trains are inherently more interesting than diesel or electric right? They have smoke and steam and whistles all going on at once, carting that big coal hopper right behind the engine to intensify the grime factor - all good for movie making. So, the bad guy invades the engine carriage and kills the two guys frenetically shoveling coal into the firebox, maxes out the speed then breaks off the throttle control and brake handle, and the train just keeps going at full speed for a really long time despite the lack of shoveling? Magic coal is much worse than infinite bullets.

Insulting plot hole 2: The bad guy maxed out the train speed before a curve where the train was supposed to slow down and give our hero the chance to get on board. Naturally it didn't slow down but hey no derailment (or even an edge of your seat moment when you thought it might) so why was the train supposed to slow down in the first place?

Insulting plot hole 3: This whole movie was about finding a key, which was in two parts, both of which were needed to open the lock. The evil AI's objective was to get the key first so no one could locate and destroy it. The evil AI gets the first half and keeps looking for the second half. Why doesn't it destroy the first half immediately, if it did the second half becomes worthless and the evil AI is safe.

Now there is no way the movie makers didn't know this; they just didn't care which is why they are so insulting. Every movie has plot holes granted but the shameless disregard here is at another level.

What could have been a 9 or 10 is therefore reduced to an 8.

Still going to watch part 2 though.

10.title: Best franchise currently going
10.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One confirms that Mission Impossible is the best franchise currently going and possibly ever made. A 2 hour 43 minute adrenaline rush that contains some of the best action sequences put to film, embarrasses the majority of the competition out there and sets the stage for a magnificent part 2 whilst still being a satisfying adventure in its own right.

This is possibly the most open and obvious a Mission film has been with its deeper meaning for cinema and what aspect of Cruise's career is being dissected this time with a film that focuses on Ethan's relationship with women and basically outright declares AI to be a soulless monster and how the human element is always needed (perfect film to release during a writer's strike).

Tom Cruise is perfect as Ethan Hunt and the strongest aspect this time round is when the film explores what made Ethan who he is and reminds you he genuinely cares about his team but that comes at a cost. Physically, the madman is still going strong with his stunts, driving a bike off a cliff in truly breathtaking fashion.

Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg and Rebecca Ferguson remain the best IMF team and all play to their strengths here. The longer this series goes on the more authentic their growing friendship feels. Shea Whigham and Greg Tarzan Davis get more than expected and their buddy cop antics are a lot of fun.

With Esai Morales' charismatic yet terrifying Gabriel and Pom Klementieff's terrific henchman of few words, this franchise finally has more good villains than bad. The return of Henry Czerny as Kittridge is glorious and he remains as gleefully despicable as his first appearance.

The best new addition is easily Hayley Atwell. She plays a type of character never seen before in these films which makes her character and dynamic with Cruise fresh in comparison to everyone who's come before and their chemistry is magnetic. Instantaneous from the second they interact.

Christopher McQuarrie's direction is phenomenal. The action sequences are suitably practical (this is how you spend $290 million), and the camera gets as close to the action as humanly possible, he remains one of the best in the business working at this scale. There's plenty of canted angles as a nice homage to De Palma's original and it helps give this one its own style in comparison to McQuarrie's previous entries.

The pacing is really impressive with the film feeling like it's in a perpetual third act from its first airport heist (which is so much fun). Lorne Balfe does the music once again and yet again it's a highlight of the film, he knows how to elevate everything so well and really hammers home the emotional beats.

10.title: Mission on the Orient Express!

The Orient Express is trashed (in a way) in both films and I know which one I prefer! A few things intrigued me - the engine is a steam one, which is no longer the case in real life. The current incarnation of the train has a new and different logo, but it is nowhere to be seen. Instead we have the art deco WL logo of the 1930s, and I loved seeing it on screen. In short, there was a bonus for me, but besides that it's a great thrill ride everyone will enjoy!

10.title: Adrenaline Pumping, A Heart-Pounding Cinematic Masterpiece!
10.content:
From the very first frame to the last heart-stopping moment, "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" delivers a thrilling cinematic experience that grips the audience and never lets go. This action-packed thriller is an adrenaline-fueled rollercoaster ride that takes viewers on a journey filled with suspense, intrigue, and mind-bending twists.

As the lights dimmed in the theater and the iconic theme music began, I knew I was in for a treat. The opening scene instantly catapulted us into the heart of the action, setting the tone for what was to come. The plot follows Ethan Hunt (played brilliantly by Tom Cruise) and his team as they face their most dangerous and enigmatic adversary yet. The stakes are higher than ever, and the clock is ticking. Every scene is meticulously crafted to keep the audience at the edge of their seats, and it succeeds masterfully.

One of the film's strengths is its captivating characters. Ethan Hunt, as always, is a charismatic and compelling protagonist. His determination and unwavering commitment to his mission make him an inspiring and relatable hero. The supporting cast, including Rebecca Ferguson as the enigmatic Ilsa Faust and Simon Pegg as the tech-savvy Benji Dunn, adds depth and humor to the story, making for a well-rounded and engaging ensemble.

The mind games played throughout the film are nothing short of exhilarating. The plot twists and turns like a labyrinth, keeping the audience guessing at every step. Just when you think you have it all figured out, the movie throws another curveball that leaves you questioning everything you thought you knew. It's a testament to the screenwriters' skill that they can keep the suspense building until the very last scene.

As an action film, "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" does not disappoint. The breathtaking set pieces and jaw-dropping stunts are a visual feast for the eyes. Tom Cruise's dedication to performing his stunts is evident in every heart-pounding moment, and it adds an authenticity that is often missing in other action movies. From high-speed motorcycle chases through bustling city streets to death-defying leaps off towering skyscrapers, the action sequences are a spectacle to behold.

Beyond the action and intrigue, the film also explores deeper themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and the blurred lines between good and evil. It delves into the complexities of the characters' moral choices and the consequences of their actions. This added layer of depth elevates "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" above the typical action blockbuster, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant experience.

The movie's pacing is relentless, never giving the audience a moment to catch their breath. The tension builds steadily, and just when you think it might let up, another pulse-pounding set piece ensues. I found myself so engrossed in the story that I hesitated to take a bathroom break, fearing I might miss a crucial revelation or action sequence. The film's ability to keep me fully invested speaks to its compelling storytelling and captivating performances.

The production values are top-notch, with sleek cinematography and a dynamic score that heightens the suspense. The attention to detail in every aspect of the film is evident, from the intricately choreographed action scenes to the elaborate set designs. Director Christopher McQuarrie's vision is masterfully realized, making "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" a feast for both the eyes and the mind.

In conclusion, "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" is a heart-pounding and exhilarating cinematic experience that is worth every single penny. It sets a new standard for action thrillers with its captivating characters, mind-bending plot twists, and adrenaline-fueled stunts. Tom Cruise's dedicated performance as Ethan Hunt is nothing short of awe-inspiring, and the supporting cast complements the film perfectly. This movie is an absolute must-watch, leaving you eager to unravel its mysteries until the very end. If you're a fan of action-packed thrillers that keep you on the edge of your seat, "Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" should be at the top of your must-see list. Strap in for an unforgettable cinematic ride!

10.title: Dangerous Impossibilities Await-We Accept.
10.content:
Never doubt the power of dedication to the craft, patience to persevere adversity, and Tom Cruise running. They've done the impossible once again, at this point it's safe to say the IMF is a valuable asset to the world-and for our own sake of nonstop joyous entertainment.

Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One picks off nearly five years from the masterpiece of Fallout to bring us the penultimate movie of a grand two-part farewell for Ethan Hunt and his team. It's not only the longest film in the franchise so far but also the most daring and, surprisingly, the most humorous. Throughout the movie, we were brought to the edge of our seats with on-the-ground car chases through Rome, brutal fight sequences atop of roaring trains and intimately between tight alley ways, and of course, in the air as Tom Cruise tops his previous Evil Knievel-inspired stunts with a motorbike jump off a two-thousand-foot Norwegian cliff. The action movie of all action movies is here among the greatest ever made, in the same franchise. We are lucky to have the likes of Cruise and his longtime collaborator, director Christopher McQuarrie.

Cruise and McQ produce this highly intense spy thriller to another level, by choreographing a perfect blend of excellent directing, cunning writing, huge stunts, clever production design, and superb acting. Everyone clearly brought their A-game-as the IMF team always does-to execute the best of what this franchise keeps doing, making better movies. This is the very definition of a blockbuster. The CGI-filled dumbed-down movies with inflated budgets, some of whom came out around Dead Reckoning, are hopefully a short-lived studio misread of what audiences really want-a good movie. This is a damn good movie.

At a run time of 2hrs 43min, M:I 7 is a lot to take in but from the opening scene with that rapturous theme music-shoutout to the excellent score by Lorne Balfe-we are taken on a mission that doesn't stop. McQ's writing and directing takes on a slightly different tone, interweaving more humor, subplot, supporting character depth, and influences from the original 1996 movie-the dutch angles and Kittridge playing big roles. Yet, no scene drags or action set piece feel out of place because the writing and editing keep it all synced, following the rhythmic beats of the iconic soundtrack. Not even when the credits roll do we get a breath in, due to the obvious one-parter aspect, but they have made a cohesive and compelling story which satisfies us more than enough.

When the film does end on a clear cliffhanger, we can all agree-and accept-that it will be well-worth the wait for Part Two. Now, whether Tom Cruise can top-off the franchise with the greatest movie with the largest stunt yet, it's a fairly safe bet-yet, of course, it can neither be confirmed nor denied until the mission is complete.

-TE (7.10.23)

10.title: An Impossible Masterpiece
10.content:
I cannon describe with words how happy I was when I left the theater today to see that Tom Cruise has done it again and better than ever before with Dead Reckoning Part 1! This film has everything I crave from a modern action blockbuster and does it better than everything else, yes even Fury Road, this has a better story.

The stunts by Cruise in this movie were absolutley jaw dropping and insane, with an incredible motorbike stunt that is unparalleled by anything else in the industry, with a fight scene on top of a train that I'm still unsure is 100 percent practical but would be utterly mind blown if it was over 95. Every film right from the first one in 1996 has always upped the ante every single time without failing, which is already a challenging task, but after finishing this, I am extremely optimistic that not even the sky is the limit when it comes to making films like this and that the fronter is truly infinite.

So yes, the action is incredible, but so is the story. It is very interesting and complex while not being convoluted enough that it's difficult to follow or will leave you feeling confused like the 1996 film. The MacGuffin in particular used in this movie is actually a very clever one for being an almost unavoidable cliche, but this one is actually designed really well. A two piece key shaped like the Christian Cross that perfectly fit into one another. I thought the story that they spun around this was really clever and the film has many emotionally justified moments throughout where it constantly feels convincing and never breaks realism.

Every actor in this movie had their time to shine and all play great performances off one another. Every character except the villain had a believable motivation, I guess one complaint I had was that the villain was actually pretty simple when you think about it, but I can see why the movie kept him shrouded in mystery on what his true motivations were, which will probably be revealed in the next movie to be nothing more than pure evil and wanting to destroy society.

Overall, I liked the performance from every actor, even the villain who I'm sure will have a much more diabolical part to play in Part 2 which I'm interested to see. This was just a very professional production from top to bottom with exceptional stuntwork and choreography. Tom Cruise is a beast of an actor with ruthless passion to make the best possible action experience for his audience and I couldn't be any happier to consume it in all it's glory!
