Such a movie begs to be seen on the biggest screen possible where you can truly feel the grandeur of the film. Tom Cruise has once again delivered one of the best movies of the year, and I cannot recommend that you see it enough!

10.title: Very good movie
10.content: This movie was very well done. Although I'm not a fan of Tom Cruise, he is very good in this movie and all of the mission impossible movies. The story is complicated but if you watch carefully, you can follow the story pretty easily. I enjoyed the tech gadgets in the movie and they use in the story. The action scenes are incredible. Compared to James Bond, Ethan Hunt is way way more believable and more interesting. 007 movies are just garbage and very outdated and super sexist. Mission impossible is one of very few movies I would go to movie theaters to watch. I look forward to part two of this movie and all of the sequels.

10.title: ETHAN HUNT IS BACK!
10.content: I like it when Ethan disappears in the smoke, it makes him invisible. The intro of the movie is like every spy movie. Ethan is going to a lot places like Paris, London, France and Switzerland. Ethan tried to catch a thief while getting chased by bad guys. Ethan and Grace were driving a car while being handcuffed to each other, Grace didn't know how to drive. It was sad when Elsa died to Ghost man. The train fight was a amazing final battle scene when Grace stolen the key without Ethan. He rode a bike to a tall mountain and jumped off a cliff and got in inside the train to stop Ghost Man from getting away with the key and to escape the train. At the end of the movie I saw the submarine from that was from the beginning of the movie. I wonder what is going to happen to Ethan...

10.title: Unbelievable season
10.content:
Approaching this film with a modicum of doubt that Tom would still be able to deliver. Unbelievably, this epic actually manages to top the brilliant Fallout. Tom is literally going to die if he keeps doing these stunts. The motorbike sequence is utterly ludicrous. Intriguing plot with actual stakes and some familiar faces ably supported by brilliant new allies and villains. Sets up Part II perfectly with a sensational finale that homages Back to the Future 3, MI:1 and Speed. It is funny, action packed, polished and exhilarating. Harrison was great last week, but Tom is still the King. 9/10.

T.

5.title: Very disappointing
5.content:
After the first 30 minutes that promised an intellectual action thriller, the film starts its nosedive into mediocrity by introducing a thief who constantly indulges in disloyalty, for petty gains, towards the IMF and Hunt, but is held in high regards by Hunt. For the life of me, I couldn't understand why. The film also doesn't bother with it.

Neither is it concerned with the so called action set pieces. _Fallout_ had plethora of those, one after the other, tied together by a cogent story line. For all its hype, it has 2-3 in a run time of close to 160 minutes, which tested my patience.

Reading it's critics' reviews post viewing make me feel as if they have been written by the Entity, the AI behemoth at the center of this. The perceived entertainment value implied by them is not even remotely connected with the reality.

It is no wonder that it is faltering at the US box office. It is no Top Gun- Maverick. Crowds are going to turn up, especially outside the US, because of Cruise's star power. But I don't believe this will please most of them.

Disappointing.

5.title: Your high expectations will get a beating...
5.content:
4 considerations for those with high expectations and who want to avoid severe disappointment:

1 THE NEW ACTORS LACK CHARISMA

I NEED a vicious bad guy, to really pull me into the thrill of the moviie, but none of that! There isnt even one bad guy in particular, because there are now numerous supposedly "bad" guys / girls and they all FAIL to impress me.

Haley Atwell is not my cup of tea either. She unfortunately does get a lot of screentime.

2 IT LASTS TOO LONG

There is WAY too much superfluous (explanatory) talk that really slows down this movie. It lasts WAY too long because of it ( 2hours and 43 minutes). Half an hour could have been easily cut out of it!

I started looking at my watch, halfway through...and I got BORED. There I said it. I say it again, I got blipping bored. That's the last thing I want to experience during an action movie!

3 THE STUNTS DONT LOOK REAL

There is such a heavy layer of ADDED CGI effects, that the REAL stunts actually stop looking real at all. The real stunts look WAY more impressive in the behind the scenes footage, than they do in the actual movie.

4 THE JOKES FALL FLAT

Simon Pegg looks like a really old man now and he somehow has lost his usual wit and charm, which were a delight in the earlier MI movies. Without a witty Simon Pegg, GONE are the jokes as well. I didnt laugh out loud once. I smirked a few times...

This MI movie is definitely one of the worst editions, if not the very worst, because it BORED the heck out of me. THAT has never happened to me before watching a MI movie!

Despite this disappointing conclusion I still wanna thank you for reading my 2001 th review on Imdb.

5.title: Not the best one of the franchise
5.content:
No matter what most people say in their reviews this film is not the best one of the franchise.

Did we really need another mission film, not really but they are fun to watch though.

So as I settled down to watch this film, I came away from watching the movie not over thrilled as I thought I would be.

The main bad guy wasn't much of one, being back Harries for the last one at least his bad guy had some balls to him.

The alley way fight scene was awfully done, heck I could have filmed a better fight scene than that and Ferguson's sword fight scene was dreadful, it didn't suit this style of movie.

Then we had the very weak storyline. Most of the characters in this movie were very one dimensional, which didn't help with the film runtime.

The bike jump that has been on the internet for weeks has made the scene when you watch it in the film, as oh I have seen it already and didn't bring as much thrills as it should have.

Over all a very disappointing movie to the franchise, will I watch the next one, yes I will as I am a fan of these films.

Cruise has recently said he may keep on making them, well if they are going to turn out like this one, don't.

5.title: Dead stupid.
5.content:
Mission Impossible is one of those rare franchises that has been getting better and better with each installment. Until now.

The plot can be summed up in a few words -- Ethan Hunt must find a special key to save humanity from an AI entity -- and yet the writers make matters so unnecessarily convoluted that the film winds up at an incredible 2 hours and 43 minutes long, a large percentage of which is far from white-knuckle action. This leads to some serious pacing issues.

One of the film's key set-pieces -- a car chase in which Ethan and the newest IMF member Grace (Hayley Atwell) careen about in a yellow Fiat 500 -- is played for laughs, which is at odds with the general tone of the franchise. Roger Moore was just about able to make this kind of nonsense work in For Your Eyes Only (his silly yellow car being a 2CV), but in Dead Reckoning, it's just embarrassing.

The deactivation of a bomb by Benji (Simon Pegg) is a pointless piece of padding: he must solve several well-known riddles in order to do so, with seconds to spare at the end. The final piece of the puzzle could easily be solved by simply rotating the last dial through all the remaining options, but that doesn't occur to brainiac Benji. This entire scene could have been cut from the film without detriment.

Cruise's much-touted motorcycle jump off a cliff sees Ethan riding his bike at high speed over rough, rocky terrain towards the precipice. I'm no expert, but wouldn't hitting extremely uneven ground at that speed cause him to crash? (in reality, Cruise pelted along a specially constructed, very smooth ramp, the rocky ground added digitally in post).

In one of the most ridiculous scenes, Hunt rescues Grace by parachuting through the side of a moving train (this carriage built from balsa wood?), right into a gun toting henchman -- what are the chances?. Equally unlikely is how bad guy Gabriel (Esai Morales) departs from the speeding locomotive: by falling backwards off the train onto a crash mat in a waiting truck, a feat that, realistically, would have less chance of success than me asking Hayley Atwell for a date.

And as a graphic designer, I hated the fact that when Grace's various crimes flash up on a laptop screen, each misdemeanour is in a different font and point size. Why would that be a thing? A bored programmer with an interest in typography?

Preventing the film from being a total disaster are a great turn by Pom Klementieff as blonde henchwoman Paris, the actress stealing every scene she is in despite having next to no dialogue, and an incredible finale in which Ethan and Grace must race through several of the train's carriages that are dangling over the edge of a bridge, director Christopher McQuarrie reminding us a little too late that he can put together an effective action scene.

5.title: Disappointing *Warning: Spoilers*
5.content:
This franchise has been amazing to follow and each movie was better than the last, but this penultimate instalment? I'm sorry, they got it wrong. Can't win them all. Fallout was a tough act to follow. I thought this movie would deliver, but it just didn't. And that's ok. That's life.

Too much ceremony and really forced emotional depth. It didn't feel natural. Felt very staged. The camaraderie and character development of each team member is usually flawless and weaves smoothly in and out the story. This time, it seemed forced and 3 hours was indulgent.

Of course the car chase scenes, the motorbike stunt and the train scene were amazeballs. The locations were spectacular.

The way they killed off Rebecca Ferguson's character was so haphazard. She deserved a better send off than that.

Did not feel like much was at stake with the villain. He didn't seem like a real threat. Or maybe his full identity needs to be unfolded more. I think Solomon Lane was a much better villain.

The AI concept was clever but it was told in a too convoluted way. Just felt like it could have been simpler. The riddle and bomb scene was really good suspense. And you felt the pain because we all love Benji.

Ok that's enough. I may be the only person who thinks this movie was average. It got such high praise.

5.title: If you are a true M:I. fan just like me, you not gonna like it.
5.content: Bad scripting, bad villain, many bad things, not even closer to fallout (one of the best modern action movies ever), more closer to the 2nd movie (terrible). Without a doubt the amount of High reviews its from people who probably dont see the hole saga or previous movies, if you are a fan and your heart was pulled off in Fallout with tense and inteligent scripted scenes you will agree with it and i even want to continue because i have expectations and let out with a generic action movie. With the 3rd movie the saga is getting better and better reaching leveis of details And action like pure music, unfortunally ends up in Fallout.

5.title: An M.I. movie that fits the formula of its predecessors, but feels like a lazy written sequel for money grabs.
5.content:
"Dead Reckoning" (Part One) has the same old MI formula: The apparently difficult and intricate mission, the funny and witty dialogues with Benji and Luther and, of course, the hot resourceful (and traitorous) girl (plus, the sexual innuendos). But it feels like the same old script with nothing more to give.

There's too much plot armor for an action movie. You know, the convenience of poor aiming from the bad guys, the easy get out spots in situations that doesn't seem like it (or, in other words, predictable coincidences), superpowered protagonists (or enemies if it fits the same plot armor), bad guys who doesn't intervine in fightings waiting for the protagonist to get his way, people in the surroundings that doesn't seem to care what's happening, predictable "unsung" heroes or, in general, deus ex machinas everywhere.

We know it's called Mission IMPOSSIBLE, but on the majority of the earlier movies, there was a plausible impossibility, with attention to detail and buildup. In this one it's just mediocre.

It gets a little bit better after the 70 minutes mark with the reappearance of Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson); although, she as a love interest seems off. However, the plot armor is still very much there; even with ironically an overpowered villain with a pocket knife to justify a pivotal moment for Ethan Hunt (if you've already see the movie, you know what freaking scene I'm talking about).

Besides, there's constantly bad acting (it seems like a parody of action cliches) and bad casting for the main villain.

And the CGI is not that good everytime. There are several scenes where is too evident that is computer generated, and not in a good way; like the car chases (where there are several continuity errors) and, also, in the last survival mayhem, which is pretty cool, but the CGI is so evident that it throws you off about the credibility of all that is happening.

So, in the end, with this Mission Impossible, you get the same formula, but nothing more. And, for that, is better to waste your time in rewatching the good classical ones.

5.title: Terrible writing and below-average in spectacle for the MI series
5.content:
Wow this had problems. Weakest entry since MI2.

1. The Entity is a never-ending supply of plot conveniences. Covers up sloppy writing as needed. Total get-out-of-jail-free card.

2. Grace had the most irritating character writing I'd seen in years. She's the stereotypical "thief you can't trust" character who will conveniently pickpocket someone as the plot demands. Ethan's unexplained attachment to her is obsessive and nonsensical. I wanted her gone as soon as her character was introduced, and not in a good way. TERRIBLE character.

3. Waste of Ilsa Faust. Grace just neatly replaced her. Pointless death.

4. The final act involving the train was lifted right out of Uncharted 2. Completely unoriginal.

5. Pom Klementieff's character was ridiculous and unnecessary in every sense. Existed for "deus ex machina" moments and nothing else.

6. Consistently overplays the "this was part of my plan all along" card trying to make its audience think it's clever.

7. Gabriel made no sense at any point. He wasn't threatening or anything. Silly.

8. When Ethan reveals he swapped the key for the "lighter" in Gabriel's pocket at the end, I audibly groaned. Absolutely ridiculous how lazy that writing was.

9. The action scenes were a step down from the previous three movies in every way. The chase scenes weren't as well-done, the fights were over-choreographed and made no sense (e.g., Ilsa literally had a sword but insisted on choking Gabriel TWICE), and the stunts were underwhelming.

10. The dialogue feels so artificial. The scene where the various national security officials are explaining the circumstances to Cary Elwes's character was the most clearly scripted thing I'd heard in years.

5.title: What a disappointment
5.content:
I had taken a short break from this franchise and when I saw Fallout I was pleasantly surprised how entertaining it was. As a result I really looked forward to this installment. Guess I should've kept my expectations in check.

It's hard not to notice that this is a Mission Impossible movie that's 2h 43 min long, AND there's a part II coming. Seriously? I feel like we're already breaking a golden rule of a good action/adventure series: about 2 hours is perfect for these movies.

This wouldn't be a bad thing if the movie actually delivered and it turned out the story was just so amazing that we needed two long movies. In reality the story isn't even good and even if it was, they somehow manage not to use the long runtime so flesh out the plot. Instead there's just a lot of long action sequences that could've been cut shorter, as well as some pointless fat that could be trimmed such as multiple scenes of Cruise & company just staring at the sunrise or something. To put it succinctly: I've never had any interest in making a "fan edit" of a movie until I saw this one.

I missed one or two of these movies but there wasn't always an overarching plot, so I have no idea if I'm supposed to know who these other characters are like Grace and Gabriel. The movie either thinks I should know them or isn't interested in telling me much about them. Also, the big bad is a faceless computer program. Jesus, guys. Really?

It's a bloated version of what the franchise has managed to do in the past with a tight run time, simple story concepts and characters that stand out, but then get out of the way for Cruise and the action. I can't imagine anyone watching this and being left on the edge of their seat, unable to wait for the sequel.

This falls completely flat and while they allowed themselves more runtime, they don't take advantage of it. Maybe the weakest in the series that I've seen.

5.title: As good as MI-2 by John Woo
5.content:
Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning is a very different movie than the past 4 entires. For one, it doesn't have a well defined awesome villain. 2- the film leans hard into Dutch angles and Closeups of actors. There's hardly moments where you can take in the scenery or get yourself used to the geography of the locations. This was never the case in previous entries. 3- What are the motivations of the characters to do the dangerous things they are getting themselves into? It's on thin ice motivations-wise. 4- There's a lot of Tell, not a lot of show going on. Things are being described to us as opposed to being shown in a clever way. 5- Other than the climactic train stunts, there are no memorable action sequences as compared to previous entries. 6. The film is too long. The content in this movie could have been 2 hrs. It is a really bloated movie. 7. The hand to hand combat is not that great in the film when compared to other great action scenes that have n presented in other films this year.

The good stuff: 1. Ethan Hunt character is great overall.

2. Some of the effects work is really great.

Cut the movie down to 2 hours and I would think it's a 6 or 7.

5.title: A MASSIVE step down from its predecessors...
5.content:
Simply put this was a massive let down and step back from the highs achieved in Fallout in many regards.

The action sequences where far less creative than seen previously seen, with only the car chase in Rome and final train crash standing out.

The main nemesis being a unoriginal AI system and a lackluster man with little compelling motive hold nothing to the fantastic Solomon Lane in Fallout (who you can actually sympathise with)

And finally the worst offence was the outrageous downgrade from Ilsa (a fan favourite with depth, connection to Ethan/the audience and actually use to the mission) to Grace, one of the most useless, annoying side acts who runs away 3 times before finally understand the depth of the situation (leading to Ilsa's death!) and is then instantly forgiven and basically handed a spot on the team in place of Ilsa.

We are then expecting to go on and just accept that Grace has somehow earned the audiences respect despite being given every reason to hate her.

Overall very disappointing but it was always going to be hard to live up the the peak of it's predecessors.

5.title: All icing no cake
5.content:
Rather than "Dead Reckoning" this entry in the franchise should be called "By the numbers"

The scenery and locations they've chosen for Cruise to sprint through are stunning, but that's all that really happens and there's nothing to differentiate the film from any of those that have gone before.

Glamorous villains, expensive clothes, balletic unrealistic fight scenes, rubber masks, bomb threats, panicking comedy sidekicks, double crossing government officials, pickpocketing, outlandish and impossible stunts and lots of cliched dialogue while ominous music plays - we've seen it all before. It's not terrible, it's just been done lots of times before and the plot events are more sign posted than a theme park.

What plot there is, is riddled with holes which are ignored at the expense of trying to build tension - yet at no point did I have any concern that Cruise's character would not prevail, much less die. The same could be said of his sidekicks - apart from the one who is replaced - an event which can be seen coming from further away than Christmas.

The scenery is beautiful and the action well shot, yet the central premise is Cruise sprinting between fist fights, long monologues, tricking people interspaced with overly long foot/car chases.

The fight scenes are too choreographed and look completely unnatural. Most would not look out of place on a dance floor. For supposedly "elite" operatives, none seem to grasp the premise that guns are the best way to kill someone quickly, instead resorting to knives for some reason.

The story ends pretty much where it started and it left me wondering what the point of the film was - aside from making the studio a large amount of money.

5.title: This movie is an insult!
5.content: Oh, absolutely, this movie is a blast, a real edge-of-your-seat, popcorn-munching extravaganza, right up there with the best of the Mission Impossible series. But, let's talk about the character Grace. The writers must be geniuses, right? They've managed to craft a character with the intelligence of a teaspoon, and they named her Grace. It's like watching a masterclass in character development! Every scene she's in, you can't help but marvel at how they've redefined the limits of human intellect - downwards. It's a stroke of sheer brilliance, or should I say, anti-brilliance. And amidst all this, the movie still manages to be entertaining. I mean, who wouldn't find amusement in witnessing the most spectacularly brainless character ever written? Hats off to the scriptwriters for pushing the boundaries of character IQ - to the very bottom. Bravo!

5.title: I'm just confused now.
5.content:
Mission: Impossible - Fallout is one of my favorite movies of all time. I will never forget watching it in theaters for the first time. I love all the movies and the overarching storyline.

But with Dead Reckoning Part 1, I'm just confused now. Why are these next two movies being made? It doesn't have anything to do with the previous films, so it feels like everything we previously saw means nothing. Sure, they mention a few names from last time, but the 4th movie directly affected the events in 5, and capturing Solomon Lane directly affected the events in 6. But here, there's basically nothing except for the White Widow returning. This feels more like a glorified spin-off with Ethan Hunt than a full sequel.

I am fully aware this is the first half. I love me a good cliff hanger. As long as it's done correctly... but this isn't. The movie literally just stops abruptly and thinks that having a monologue with music is a good outro. It's not. There's no big reveal at the end to make you excited for what comes next. No surprises, no characters returning out of the blue, nothing. When Dead Man's Chest ended, Barbossa coming back from the dead was extremely cool. And it was built up from the beginning. But here, the movie just stops. Not cool.

But what about the action scenes? They unfortunately leave a lot to be desired. They hyped up that motorcycle jump to ABSOLUTE DEATH... and in the movie we get to see it for a whopping four seconds. FOUR!!!!!!! I don't care if he did the jump himself. It doesn't feel like it when you cut it so hard and only show me a small part of it! The Halo jump in Fallout was so great because it was all one cut. That showed that they really did risk life and limb for this stuff. Same with Tom on the outside of the plane in Rogue Nation. We got to see that happen in real time for at least 10-20 seconds. But they just gloss over this so hard in Dead Reckoning... WHY?????

The pacing is absolutely atrocious. The reason why Fallout and Rogue Nation were amazing is because they trimmed the fat and cut to the chase... literally! Those movies had a lot going on, but they got straight to the point. In this movie? There isn't a lot going on, but it's the longest of the movies so far. So we have overly long sections of people talking about nothing and extended scenes of people staring or spouting what's going to happen before it happens. It's lame. The dialogue in Fallout beats the dialogue in this 500 times over.

We have literally no idea who Gabriel is. The actor who plays him isn't menacing or stoic at all. And the movie chooses not to tell us anything about him outside from the fact that he killed a girl when Ethan was younger. HOW DOES THAT MAKE HIM MORE EVIL THAN SOLOMON LANE???? Solomon Lane was going to detonate 2 nukes in the middle of Kashmir in the name of creating world peace, and you expect us to believe this motiveless brick of a person named Gabriel to be even more evil? Without giving us any reason to do so????

Don't get me wrong, the movie isn't entirely bad. But much like The Dark Knight Rises, it's hard to appreciate it when there's so much wrong with the movie. I haven't even gotten into Grace joining the IMF, Kitridge returning, Ilsa dying in the most emotionless way possible, it goes on.

I'm not mad (well, maybe a little). I'm just confused. After the masterpieces that were Rogue Nation and Fallout, we were all hoping that Christopher McQuarrie and Tom Cruise would just knock it out of the park. But that hasn't happened yet. We'll find out next year if they did or not. That's what frustrates me the most.

5.title: True MI Fans won't like it: Due to lack of depth
5.content:
A lot of us have pretty much grown up while loving this franchisee - one installment at a time. And it has been wonderful to see the franchisee evolve (specially last two movies) with changing times and taste of audience. But latest 'Dead Reckoning Part 1' turned out to be very disappointing due general lack of depth in plot, characters and dialogues.

'Sense of Urgency' has been one of pillars of MI but throughout this movie, none was felt. Everyone was just going about sitting and talking in long scenes revealing little and repeating the same points. After initial 30 minutes, I thought may be movie will pick up pace but there was absolutely NO build up or edge of the seat scenes. Multiple times, I found myself waiting for scenes to get over during later part of the film.

Villian was kinda inconsistent and non-threatening and come onnnnn ----> 'he loses the key to ethan and he just shouts his name in frustration like this was a scene in home-aloneee' !!

Tom's character seemed sympathetic or caring towards new female lead but they never showed any reason why he should be!!! In the climax, Tom spent way too much time on bike while alot of action happened in the train.. eventually he jumps but then again climbs on top of train and villian actually ran towards him to fight!! Seriously ....????!!

Action and stunts are top notch with healthy dosage of trademark humour but overall too thin on plot line, characters or relationships!!

And I dont know when I will get over the scene where female lead is worried if he will leave her alone on the train and he says "I will be there!!!!!!???!?!?!"

Alas.... so much wasted potential and money!!!

5.title: I don't get the hype
5.content: My wife is a big Tom Cruise fan, so we went to see this movie as part of her birthday celebration. I don't get the hype. The plot felt very forced to me with contrivances and bizarre explanations for things rather than true exposition and plot development just to be able to get to an action sequence. The action sequences also felt very stale as we have seen people running on trains and car chases through European streets many times in the past. The storyline was also very convoluted. Overall, I did not find this one very interesting. While my wife is looking forward to the second part, I will go just to support her but I'm really not that interested in what happens next.

5.title: Good action/horrible writing
5.content: Over all it was entertaining but the writing was very cheesy. At one point there were 8 people in a room and each person spoke one line and then another person finished that sentence and it went on like that for 5 minutes. What really did it was when the main "bad guy" was fooled by Ethan and in anger he yells out "Eeeeeettttthhhhhaaaannnnnn" to the air as the camera pans away. It was a good action movie and there were some redeeming qualities like Simon Pegg and Haley Atwell and Tom running a lot but I could have watched the movie on silent and still got as much out of it. Entertaining but really cheesy.

5.title: lacking in so many ways
5.content:
Not enough Simon Peg, and not enough of the team solving problems.

The fun in these movies is from the characters different strengths and them playing off of each other. And that was missing here.

It starts off pretty good, I was thinking "Yeah! A good action movie" and then it ended up feeling quite long.

While at times Pom was quite good, at other times she felt like a 90's Bond villain; which was just out of place in this movie.

Ilsa wasn't bad but I didn't see any real chemistry between her and Ethan and the way she died seemed silly and forced for the story line. With a fairly long sword she lost to a guy with a short knife.

Gabriel seemed like he was computer generated rather than just bossed around by a computer.

Briggs, while good, sounded silly complaining how Ethan always goes rogue, because he seemed to forget that he always gets the mission done that way.

And don't even get me started on why Ethan told Kittridge up front that he was going rogue, he could have pretended like he was going to get the key and return it to him for awhile.

While impressive, the real motorcycle/parachute jump was made odd by Ethan whining about it. His entire career has been stunts like that and he never whined about them before.

The tiny car chase was funny, but it felt like the movie switched to Inspector Gadget for awhile. It just didn't fit.

Also, a signal being analog doesn't mean a computer can't interpret it and even alter it. It would just switch it to digital then back to analog. Fun fact: when a 'digital' signal is transmitted over wires like network cable it is actually an analog sinewave where up is on and down is off.

And finally, if I had to hear them say "The Entity" one more time!!!! At some point they would just say "It".

5.title: Weak Stakes, Weak Villain Side
5.content:
Weak villain They should have showed why the villain guy is listening to the entity or why he hates hunt so much.

The entity isn't organic, but at least it's unique it's like it was forced into the plot this is because everything just suddenly happend, the movie could have been about a stopping the bad guy creating the entity and failing (but that is already done)

The Stakes are weak They should have showed what the entity will do after destroying the key, fake atomic bomb is not enough. (In the movie they just told it by saying it hacked into important places)

They should have showed the bombs in the bridge earlier in act 3 so that the stakes are a little higher.

Too lucky I know they need luck in order to beat the entity, atleast make it so that hunt didn't look confused after crushing into the train and make him react to the enemy, make it that he opened the parashout on purpose to tackle the enemy, make it more him rather than luck.

Ps, i honestly wanna rate 1 star because i saw a review with 10/10 saying it it was soo good he could cry.

5.title: I wonder how many times KEY is said in the film?
5.content:
A 2 hour and 45 minute film about a key and people talking about said key !

Have I got the key ? Do you have the key ? Who has the key? Does anyone have the key ? I actually don't care anymore and would like whoever has the key to use it as a weapon and put me out of my misery !

Aside from that the action scenes are great fun, Tom Cruise does lots of running and plays Russian roulette with his life.....although I'm pretty sure he's made a deal with devil and is immortal. He's certainly aging slower than most 61 year olds ! 5/10

Also side note: why do these reviews require 600 or more characters ? So annoying.

5.title: It felt like a downgrade of the franchise
5.content:
This was the first movie of the entire M:I universe that I couldn't finish. I tried, but after 2 hours of watching it, I just couldn't stop thinking about what went wrong with one of my favorite - if not THE favorite - movie franchises.

The action is still good, Tom Cruise is still a flawless Ethan Hunt, and well... There's more CGI in this one to my uneasiness, it had everything to deliver, and yet, after the first 90 minutes I saw the same old traps that movies are falling curse to: bigger, harder, stronger, faster, but no better.

The premise of exploring Ethan's past is interesting, but the main villain is cartoonesque, smug, with questionable fashion taste, being an incredible hand-to-hand fighter while looking in his 60s (yes, I know the actor and Tom Cruise are of the same age, but I guess Tom has much more money to spend on cosmetic procedures) and this unstoppable force to match Ethan's skills, but wait... Didn't we have that portrayed majestically by Sean Harris? The anti-Ethan plot thing?

I get it, movies need that momentum, but I couldn't bear with this plot. Portraying an AI as an "Entity" is a bit bland, but it fits the current world, having henchmen be its voice was generic and that may be the word to describe the feeling I had while watching it: generic.

It's a very well-executed action movie, but there's no heart in it. They had to dumb down the characters in order to create a climax, the Ethan from the previous movies, the one thrown in impossible choices, and still thinking outside the box was just a plaything in this movie. Oh, right, they also had to introduce a new annoying-as-hell femme fatale in the most uncreative James Bond fashion that simply fails to see who is really trying to help her as she always backs off to save her skin, creates more trouble, is saved by Ethan, rinse and repeat while killing a character who had a thousand times more connection with Ethan.

I swear, the dumbness level of screen and character writing was above the charts with this one. You have a BMF agent with a sword versus an old dude with a knife, and she simply lets go of the reach advantage to engage in physical combat that gets her killed. Great writing, seen that a million times. In fact, you could say that to the entire second half of the movie, that's why I didn't bother myself with watching all of it, I was truly done after 2 hours and 5 minutes.

Fallout was the perfect setup for a much better movie. You had a team, you had an Ethan finding a bit of peace... And they ruined it. I honestly regret watching this.

5.title: Mission Predictable: Dead Reasoning
5.content:
You'll have to really blindly love Tom to get around the sketchy and predictable dialog in this repetitive thriller.

Planning for the mission doesn't make sense.

Vingh gives the predictive line and Simon plays his typical beta roll.

But, you get to see Ton in multiple running scenes, obviously his favorite. Especially in Venice where he runs and runs. Venice isn't that big for all that running.

Rebecca's character winds up without purpose. Who choreographed that bridge scene?

The train scene is absolutely adolescent car after bleeping car.

Overall, one of the worst movies Tom has been a part of....right there with Cocktail.

This could have been 60 minutes and then I would have felt less pain.

I don't even care about part 2.

I wish AI wild have written the dialog.

Let the submarine collect barnacles.

5.title: Long, boring, not interesting
5.content:
I cannot stretch my suspension of disbelief that far... nothing in this movies is remotely credible.

Every MI movie went bigger than the previous one, and I started to let go a few movies ago. This one reached the same level than Fast and Furious reached a while ago: no traces of brain left, complete non-sense.

The story is uninteresting, dialogs are so boring they're hard too follow. It's too long, the chase with the little car was so long and uninteresting, I was looking at my watch, knowing there was still about two more hours of movie to go...

The motorbike/base stunt is great, but actually looks much better in the Behind the Scene video, so don't miss this one.

5.title: Is this a Marvel movie???
5.content:
I don't get it! Even after being stabbed for twenty minutes, she reached the falling wagon (so no one would notice) and lifted the weight of two people? That's how? Like in Marvel movies, why didn't you give him wings and unlimited power?!

With parachutes, how did he get on a train at that speed? Then he just hit that guy with a gun! Each wagon fell one minute at a time, then the last wagon was suspended for five minutes! Was the resistance of the connections stronger or what? It is not a locomotive that pours coal into the train, but the speed of the train did not slow down a bit! And another bug, how did it come to your mind?

It was really hard for me to like this movie. I used to justify the miracles of Mission Impossible series to myself, but this one was not logical at all. There's probably something wrong with the direction that caused Mission Impossible to lose its line of thought. There is no doubt that Tom Cruise's acting and stunts made for an enjoyable viewing experience. Let's hope the second part is better.

5.title: Great action movie, but ultimately ruins the franchise
5.content:
There is so much for me to say and yet nothing at the same time. As an avid M:I fan, I experienced many sleepless nights waiting for the 8th when I got to watch this movie in cinemas. After seeing countless trailers and shorts of the stunt, I had a great feeling about this. But after walking out of the cinema, I ultimately feel robbed and empty.

Firstly, this movie puts the M:I franchise to shame. Although many will review this movie with high ratings, I feel that if you have watched the rest of the franchise, you would begin to understand where I am coming from. Every Mission Impossible is about doing the impossible; missions that are far too dangerous, and stunts that would kill your average person. However, this is exactly why M:I is so so good. It gives you a rush of feeling and hooks you in for every second of the movie. This movie, although still great with beautiful scenery and a decent and relevant plot, does not convey that.

The movie felt incredibly forced and unnatural. The scenes were extremely jolty, and the smoothness viewers had experienced in all the other movies was not met. There was way too much storytelling in this movie, almost making sure that you could understand every little moment. However, the fun of this franchise is being shocked within a second and having to piece together what you just witnessed. The comicality in the movie became increasingly frustrating and annoying, and Ethan Hunt was simply trying too hard to be funny (again, not at all like his character in the other 6 movies). In all the other M:I movies, Ethan does not think and make a comical comment about the dangerous situation presented to him, he just does the thing. In this movie, I think I developed a slight hate from this new personality that had overcome him for the entirety of this film.

The stunt that would change cinematic history was in fact shocking and extremely impressive (including the fact that Cruise did 6 takes too get it perfect), but only lasted a short time before he genuinely teleported into the window of the train. How he got there? I am really not sure. This was the only major stunt performed during the whole film, and is simply not great enough or long enough to make the whole film great.

From unnecessary storytelling to a forced comical dialogue to 'lighten the mood', this movie honestly looks embarrassing compared to the rest of the M:I franchise. Extremely disappointed with this movie, especially since it was built up so much in advertising.

I'm sure as people read this, they'll heavily disagree. Haters will say this is a gross exaggeration of a review, but real fans will know this is exactly how it was.

5.title: Cruise as Clown
5.content: This is a poor addition to the library of MI movies. Cruise is played for laughs, with slapstick stunts that aren't funny and all of his edge is removed as he is constantly one-upped by the new additions, who themselves have precious little charisma. Tinseltown Tom also looks jowly and botoxed and seems to have been slightly manipulated at points by CGI or AI or de-aging-God only knows. The action scenes are eternally long but don't ratchet up the tension. It felt in some ways like a swan song for hapless Ethan Hunt and a franchise looking to extend itself with new young lackluster characters.

5.title: Great techno wizardry but Cruise's weird face is distracting
5.content:
Why is this film 2.5 hours long and it's only half a story?!

Why does Tom Cruise's face look like it's AI? (Not a pun or spoiler) His features are melting into his waxy face.

So much exposition and not enough time to appreciate the beautiful locations or build enough meaning into the relationships.

Far too much talking and not enough left for the audience to work out.

Fab set action pieces, especially the yellow car and the chase in Venice and lets face it (pun intended) , this is why most people choose to watch any movie with Ethan Hunt as the main character.

Whizz, bang, exposition, exposition, and one Hollywood action star with a strange, smooth, barely moving face and a long wait for the exposition to pay off in the next film.

5.title: Not as great as the hype or the stunts
5.content:
The whole film seems to be based on an adrenaline seeker getting his thrills by doing stunts & building uo to a big stunt that we all had seen before the movie was even released.

The action scenes seem to choppy and shakey cam & lens flares are used so much it tends to take you out of the movie.

I was also very surprised to see some very poor special effects & models towards the end of the movie,l.

The movie is set in sone lovely locations but overall the whole movie just seemed lacking of something.

Its watchable but its far from great and I think it got way over hyped. Also its kind on a Matrix 4 which is just a trailer & build up for the next movie. It could have been great but fails on too many aspects to be a hreat movie.

5.title: Underwhelming 7th film of the franchise
5.content: After the impressive "Fallout", which oozed stunts and style in abundance, Dead Reckoning gives the impression that the M-I franchise has peaked. From unoriginal fight scenes ( fight on the roof of a train, anyone ?) to the clunky attempts to explain the plot to camera by the actors talking it through with each other, and the good old "rubber mask" ruse, there wasn't much to write home about here. But the biggest issue to me is the Elephant in the room ( Spoiler Alert ) ; The producers see fit to kill off the awesome Rebecca Ferguson ( as she approaches 40 ) and replace her with another beautiful, but younger model, while all the ageing blokes keep their jobs ! I left feeling uncomfortable that nothing has really changed in Hollywood.

5.title: Meh...
5.content:
Let's see the saving the Universe has already been done. Saving the Metaverse. Saving the quantum realm. Saving the animated universe. Saving the all things everywhere, all the time etc etc etc.

Hmmm. What can we save next that's bigger? Now we need, oh wait, right, a super AI !!

Ok, here's the idea, you're going to love this: There's a super duper device that multiple groups are chasing, and it keeps changing hands, and there are car chases in Italy, and there is a female thief stealing the device, and the male lead keeps trusting her, and she just keeps stealing it and the male lead keeps trusting her, wait!! I just saw this movie! It was called Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny!

5.title: Disappointed
5.content: Felt like watching one of the Taken or John Wick sequels instead of a Mission Impossible...... Tom Cruise did put up pretty good action scenes, but unfortunately they did not give me the thrill of classic "Mission Impossible twists". Some action scenes are meaninglessly over-extended, which actually made me feel exhausted instead of attracted. In a word, the amount of content is just not enough to fill 150 minutes. Besides, I have always expected MI series to be somewhere between Jason Bourne and 007, meaning the plots have at least some sense of reality for me to empathise, but unfortunately again, this one failed my expectation. The NEW AND OLD characters are not well portrayed at all: the death of an important character did not make me feel anything much; and the AI supervillain setting brings out too much unreasonable plot(just for the most basic part I mean why the AI wants to acquire that key rather than destroying it since it is the only thing that can threaten the programme). To conclude, I just feel Ethan Hunt and his team deserve a much better ending movie than this. Hopefully part two can be better, after all MI is the only blockbuster serie that still interests me.

5.title: Worst of the franchise
5.content: Probably a testament to the drivel coming from Hollywood today that this film is being received rapturously. Either that or chatGPT is being employed to write reviews by PR agencies. It is easily the worst of the franchise; absent is the fast pacing, the tight editing and the novel and creative chases, stunts and heists. Instead we get tired retreads of previous ideas. The actors look, to a man and woman, bored out of their minds. And how could they not with a script written by children...seriously, who is writing these things? Have they ever read any samples of good scripts? Or at least watched films from bygone eras when the studio could not rely on visual effects to entertain and thus had to come up with interesting dialog? Are we really so short of intelligent or creative writers that no one could be found to come up with something resembling a professional product? Or was there no slender piece of the $219 million budget or whatever the figure was to pay a professional? OK, I am going on too long about the script, I mean we don't watch MI for snappy dialog, but it was really atrocious. I mean, I was looking at my watch during the long segments of nothingness, which is to say about half the film. The plot was a confused mess and really prevented me from connecting with any of the characters, even though they are almost all old acquaintances. What a sad effort! I am unfortunately old enough to remember the charismatic original (I mean the de Palma film), which could really be enjoyed by a adult. This latest MI is made by children, for children. I'm not sure what I'm going to do for entertainment anymore.

5.title: Is this action film for you?
5.content: I watched with focus for about 40 minutes. I didn't think I understood the mission. Venice was shot beautifully. Then I found myself wondering about Tom Cruise's skincare. Has feminism got us to where the women in the film all get attacked and beat up. The women don't wear fun clothes. Could Hayley wear black knit top and pants like Tom, instead of a vest? How did they conveniently find a coal-fired train for the long action sequence? I sat through whole thing, but too expensive for me. I am going to start watching the old MI tv show. I liked how they chose a team at the beginning based on what skills were needed and it was a caper.

5.title: Same director, same writer. WHAT HAPPENED?
5.content: Felt like this was written for a 6th grader. So many obvious explanations about the plot that weren't needed. So many out of character goofy moments for Ethan Hunt, whose usually always even keeled. So many moments where physics didn't matter and shock value was prioritized. So many cheesy one liners where the shot lingers on the character, making it even cheesier. I never comment on any movie and try to embrace them for what they are, but I am baffled at how the same team that gave us incredible films ended up with such a shallow movie. Attempts to make the viewer care about the characters or be intimidated by the villain just didn't land. I guess no one is perfect, and the team missed the shot on this one. Hoping part 2 is a bounce back game for Tom Cruise and the gang!

5.title: Too long.... Feel asleep during uninteresting scenes
5.content:
I was so excited to watch MI7 and I had very high expectations. Especially after TG Maverick which is one of my all-time favourite films by Tom Cruise.

The best mission impossible for me is MI4 Ghost Protocol. Each MI movie after that had to exceed what I felt with MI4. The overall cinematic experience- suspense, action, story, dialogue, character development and just the thrill of it all - was top notch. In fact, I had watched MI4 numerous times!

The following movies MI5 and MI6 were great. But sad to say, MI7 was a huge let down. Although kudos to Tom Cruise and the rest of the cast and crew - one can truly tell how much heart and soul were put into making this film. However, in terms of how it connected to me as an audience, it just fell flat. And it was too long... stretched by dialogues that felt repetitive. I slept through those parts. Especially as they kept on talking about "the key". My goodness gracious - it became a bit annoying.

Even the stunts - I've seen them many times before like in fast and furious movies. The motor bike scene jumping off the mountain, that was pretty cool, but when Ethan lands, it felt a bit abrupt. It should have been more exciting if we saw him trying to land on the train from the top view. I'm not a film maker, but I'm looking for breathtaking, edge of your seat moments that we have yet to see. I think that's what made MI4 so special, when Ethan was on top of the tallest building in Dubai. No one has ever done that.

MI7 felt like a James Bond movie, but the American version. Would I watch MI7 part 1 again? Maybe a year or two later. I have to forget how it made me feel sleepy and bored. Well, I hope Dead Reckoning Part 2 is waaaaay better. Crossing my fingers.

5.title: I used to think the 2nd IM movie was bad...
5.content:
I get that it was shot during COVID. It had lots of money and lots of hard work that went into making it. I've worked years in film production and I know exactly what that is about.

BUT the story is just plain awful and, to me, the most glaring are ALL of the female characters. All that work with Ilsa, wasted. Hayley Atwell's paper thin introduction-then replacement for Ilsa. Vanessa Kirby's presence was ill conceived and pointless. Pom Klementieff part was very thin. Pom's fight scenes were pretty cool though. Her character was just thin. Very few lines and one of the most under developed antagonists in the movie. I haven't got a problem with any of these actresses. They are incredibly beautiful, charming and gifted actors. But the writing is super bad. There is also the imbalance of so many love interests, as well as the imbalance of too many antagonists and this is just the first half of the 2 part story to play off convincingly to Cruise. Again, good actors, crap writing. I would also add that the fight choreography with Esai Morales is "off". I'm not sure if they were struggling to make him look good and he wasn't up to it, the editing, the choreography or the shot design but it just doesn't hit the right beats and suspension of disbelief suffers. The chase scene with the mini Cooper is overworked and lame. The lead up to and the "big"(?) marquee stunt of Cruise riding over the cliff is overwrought as well. I did like the shot of him crashing into the train in a timely fashion but it's nothing that would save the movie for me.

I used to hate the overly stylized IM 2 with the preposterous end fighting scene where the motorcycles kept changing, the tires kept changing, physics kept changing, etc.,... (Nothing to do with the actual movie really but I heard that Dougray Scott lost the part of Wolverine because of him being in this movie and Cruise's inflexibility. The same inflexibility that lead to strife with reshoots with Henry Cavill on one of the superman movies. All over his mustache.) For an "action movie" it barely has a pulse, IMO.

5.title: Blah
5.content: I really wanted to like this movie; I've been a fan of the franchise for years, and the last two offerings were quite entertaining. But this one fell flat for me. The character development was lacking... The deaths were ridiculous at times; it felt more like a comic book movie. Don't get me wrong, this was Tom Cruise, doing everything we have come to love about Tom Cruise... But I really wish they would've spent more time and money on script development, rather than on the stunts. Having said that, it was entertaining... And re-introducing old characters and integrating old timelines certainly helps prop up this teetering work; but even with all of that, I'm not sure I'll tune in for part two.

5.title: Cinematics Great, Plot Mind Numbing
5.content:
The action scenes and locations are amazing. The actors all did a good job. The movie should have been amazingly entertaining. The story and plot ruined it. Contrived. Confusing. Mind numbing.

I think this is supposed to to be a twist on Lord of the Rings, but it just doesn't work. There is this one key to command and control everything in the world, it holds all the power. Everyone wants it. Rather then wield it, Ethan Hunt and his gang are going to go on a journey to a harsh environment (deep under the sea) to destroy it.

How this doubled up looking house key is so powerful is that it can control or destroy a rouge AI called "the Entity". The "source code" of the Entity is stored on a sunken sub. This AI though has permeated into systems outside of the sub and has appointed a devout psycho to carry out its wishes to stop Ethan Hunt and his friends. Of course not just stop, but mentally screw and toy around with in the process. Even though the Entity exists outside the sub, somehow destroying the source code on the stored drive in the sunken Sub will kill it off for good.

I wish they didn't have this AI bad guy. It obviously was very hard to cnopd.

5.title: Nothing impossible about this mission.
5.content:
I love Tom, especially after Top Gun 2, however this movie was just meh. Formulaic plot, one item of interest changing hands.

Irritating close up shots of face, subpar dialogues, predictable plot armours. Notch down in the level of stunts, moreover the showstopper stunt had already been put on Yt, killed the whole experience of Tom jumping off the cliff. Female characters were all over the place and why was Pom's character there even, the faces she was making during the car chase were CRINGE.

I loved Ilsa as she had more depth. Could have killed off Benji or Luther as the writers are anyway not giving them much to do apart from being present in the movie.

Was expecting more.

5.title: Mission Impossible meets John Wick 4
5.content:
Good plot. Started out with great execution but ended up following the John Wick model of endless idiotic chases, fight scenes, car scenes, implausibility and 2.5 hours of what could have and should have been a 90 minute movie.

Ethan Hunt vacillates between between a super genius spy, assassin super hero and a complete bumbling goober idiot head over and over and over again.

And now we get to wait a year to see the second half of the movie that shouldn't have even been it's own separate movie.

But, I'm pretty sure Tom Cruise wants nothing more to be able to look in the mirror and see his dashing image in the makeup room as they produce another way too damn long movie.

I honestly don't know if I'll have the energy or desire to sit through another 2.5 freaking hours.

I definitely won't pay to watch it.

5.title: Disappointed
5.content:
I can honestly say that I was very disappointed with the new addition. Waited so long for this. It was very eyecatching and the stunts were great. But it seriously lacked in storyline and some of the stunts seemed unnecessary and drawn out. I'm hopeful that the second part will have more substance to it. It's great for a visual experience but fell really short of substance when it came to a story and cinematic experience.

I am hoping that the franchise will step up their game and have a proper script and not just use it as a shock factor of stunts.

Tom cruise is a brilliant actor and I felt this cheapened his ability.

5.title: A massive let down
5.content:
Where do I even start? One of this year's biggest blockbusters, and certainly one of the most anticipated films of the year. Overshadowed by it's close release to Oppenheimer and Barbie, most people expected huge drop in box office sales. Nonetheless, I still went to watch this movie with an open mind and a considerable excitement. After all, the latest installment in the series before this movie, Fallout, was arguably a fan-favorite. Little did I know that I was in for a less-than-pleasant experience. I thought I had to start by talking about the plot and the casting. It is exactly what you think it is if you've read the short summary on IMDB. A goose chase for a dangerous weapon that everybody wants to control. As well as the risk being obviously the fate of the world which hangs in the balance. A recycled and overused premise that we've seen a million times before. The whole sequence through the streets of Venice felt pretty familiar for some reason. I soon found out, and I kid you not, that this car chase was set in exactly the same place as Fast and Furious X. And I'm not just talking about both of them being set in Venice, both car chases in both movies actually end up in the same place where the cars had to go down the flights of stairs. You've got to be at a new level of desperate if you need to rip an entire scene from the Fast and Furious series. Funnily enough, that doesn't even come close to how bad the casting was. Grace's actor, Hayley Atwell, is without a doubt the most unlikeable character to ever come out of the series. Backstabbing Ethan all movie only for him to completely forgive her every time with zero repercussions. She is literally the reason Ilsa Faust died, but on the very next scene, Luther plays it off by taking all the blame from Grace and comforting her by saying that "Ilsa died so she could save you". Like, am I missing something here? Another honorable mention is Vanessa Kirby's character, Alana, who honestly felt like it could have been played by any unknown actor and it would still have the same effect. Paris's character should have taken her place but even she had her flaws. We understand too late in the movie that she is working with Gabriel, simply because it genuinely seems like she's just a mercenary throughout most of the film. The only thing that saved her character for me was the fact that we find out that she isn't dead at the end of the movie, so who knows how that turns out. And finally, Esai Morales's character, Gabriel. Now, I'm not trying to blame that performance solely on Esai, but what in god's name was that? Talk about a villain falling short. The way the writers created him may have set him up for failure. But that still gives no excuses for how Esai missed the mark completely. Even Dante in Fast and Furious X felt like an actual, fully fledged villain. And that's saying something. Horrible cast, horrible plot, and sub-par performances all around to say the least. I was eagerly waiting for the ending, not just because I wanted the movie to end as soon as possible, but also because it was the movie's last chance at redemption. One redeeming scene at the end could've saved it for me. But alas, this is the way the movie industry works now. As expected, the ending left me feeling like I had just wasted almost 3 hours of my life watching an unfinished mess. Marvel was the first to do it with Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame. But at least Marvel's writers did it the right way. Infinity war felt like a fully fledged and coherent movie on it's own. It captured your interest and immediately hooked you as well as leaving you begging to know what happens next. Then came Spider-man: Across the Spider-verse which couldn't quite accomplish the same feat. And now with this movie which also failed to do a two-part movie the right way. Moral of the story is, if you're going to split your movie into two separate movies, you should at least put some effort into making that first part seem like an actual completed movie. And not just what seemed like an unfinished project.

With all that being said, I can still confidently say that the cinematography and Tom Cruise with the help of his team are the only things that make this movie worth watching. The action scenes, however lacking in effect, are pretty enjoyable and should be enough reason for you to check out the movie for yourself. Only for Tom Cruise though.

5.title: Overhyped, not worth it
5.content:
I don't quite understand the ratings, but this movie suffers from poor direction. The loud sound and fast pace keep it going, but most scenes lack emotional connection with the characters. The performances by Simon Pegg and Esai Morales (Gabriel), the new antagonist, are somewhat commendable. However, Tom Cruise and the female cast members fail to leave a significant impact. Take, for example, Guardians of the Galaxy, where the female characters possess strong personalities and deliver compelling performances.

The main issue lies in the mediocre action sequences. A good action sequence should strike a balance between realism and impossibility, something the previous Mission: Impossible films accomplished. Unfortunately, this installment falls short. The action scenes lack danger and appear fake and nonsensical. The train scene, in particular, suffers from jarring jump cuts. It's disappointing to see the characters engage in impossible feats but not witness the creative ways they save themselves.

Furthermore, the overall plot and dialogues are confusing. While I appreciate complex movies, this one leaves me perplexed. The writers take too many liberties with who is chasing whom and which side characters are on. The threat of AI as a dramatic element no longer captivates; it's just a code running on electricity. The concept of outsmarting AI and doing the unexpected feels tedious.

In summary, I can give it a maximum rating of 6, but it deserves a 5 due to the weak direction. Even if everything were executed flawlessly, the movie would still fall short of being mind-blowing, perhaps reaching an 8.5 at best.

5.title: The missions seems to be getting easier
5.content:
Don't know why but the mission was too easy in the movie. The AI entity is so intelligent to control the whole cyberspace, calculate all possibilities but couldn't figure out that killing Ethan might be the easiest solution instead of doing time pass with other ladies. Also they just conveniently gave location to their next meeting to everyone as if it's public info. It just seemed very linear and dragged a little.

My biggest issue is the lack of chemistry between characters and just genuine conversations between them. The background score was constantly playing irrespective of what is the situation. Felt like Tom was in some trance and was just there to do action scenes. In the whole movie I didn't see a single good emotional scene from him. If he wants to do just stunts then he might as well start a YouTube channel. The stunts although good were maybe unnecessary. They could have got an easier way get Ethan on train for example then to jump from a cliff.

Hopefully in next movie they do concentrate on the story and plot line and not just action scenes. This might be the worst MI in the series.

5.title: Mission: Impossible 7 A Disappointing Entry That Falls Short of Expectations
5.content:
I am deeply disappointed with the excessively long wait for the seventh installment of the Mission Impossible franchise. The initial allure that emerged from the breathtaking first trailer has completely faded after watching this film. Unfortunately, all that remains is a profound and bitter sense of disappointment. The convoluted dialogues veiled in violence, coupled with action scenes overly focused on visual spectacle, fail to deliver the desired impact.

Benji and Luther indeed push their boundaries this time, while the hastily developed relationship between Grace and Ethan, considering their backgrounds as cunning thieves, is implausible. It is regrettable to see the minimal meaningful dialogues given to Pom Klementieff's character, Paris, despite her agile performance. She appears silent and tragic. As for Esai Morales, let's not forget, he merely replicates the antagonistic character from previous films. His acting is remarkably poor, and he fails to grasp the meaning of the lines he delivers. Even in fight scenes, it is evident how awkwardly he struggles. How can Ilsa meet such an absurd fate? Just moments before, she nearly took the life of the formidable Salomon Lane in previous films, yet now she falls at the hands of someone far more feeble. And how can this team display such high spirits after Ilsa's departure? It all feels like watching a comedy disguised as Mission Impossible-an entry filled with recklessness, devoid of existential concerns, lacking meaningful conflicts or substance, with only Tom Cruise's aging and forced daring actions.

Nevertheless, I appreciate the chemistry that develops among the cast members, their genuine camaraderie. However, I am perplexed by the sudden emergence of consciousness in the AI. As witnessed, the film's genre abruptly shifts into science fiction, while the nonsensical use of Halloween masks only adds to the confusion. Honestly, I hold greater regard for the prosthetic makeup used in the fourth film. Yet, as the film progresses, the insanity and implausibility become increasingly apparent. I am certain that in the eighth film, they will repeat the same mistakes, perhaps even leaping from helicopters in the Arctic.

Of course, I understand that crafting a complex story is no easy task, but the narrative in this film feels severely unbalanced and weak, like a monkey losing its way in its stride. It is difficult to comprehend how Eugene Kittridge could become the CIA director after previously serving as the head of IMF in the previous films. And the scene with the exploding submarine is entirely nonsensical. How could their bodies remain intact after being exposed to a nuclear blast? This is an incredulity that is hard to believe.

The film attempts to defy progress by employing Halloween masks, but in my opinion, it is nothing more than a foolish and forced science fiction fantasy. Although I acknowledge that the film tries to connect with the present era, the excessive delivery in blaming technology as the ruler of humanity is nothing but an irrational science fiction delusion.

5.title: One of the most lame screenplays!
5.content:
MI has joined the league of the action hits of the 80s, 90s(Terminator ,Die Hard, Rambo, and so on)that were inscrutably dragged, thereby, turned into a suffering! These stars, and their fans (I'm guilty myself)don't know where to retire a franchise!

It has one of the most lame screenplays I have ever seen for a movies with so immense star value. I ain't even writing about the other pathetic aspects of the movie. I was so bored even by the action sequences that were the only distraction for the audience from the ridiculous plot, and inept direction.

Avoid the wastage of time and resources by going to a multiplex or so.

5.title: Just The Average
5.content:
Mission impossible 5 was seriously the best in the recent one following it,there was so much plot twists, mystery and Nobody knew who had what.

The AI plot was weak,the scenes where he just walks on and conducts a deal with the woman having the key was unrealistic,the car being hit by the train was expected,I don't know why he had to run on the roof,we get it man,you want everyone to know she doesn't limit you,cruise but this is a movie.
