5.title: Run geriatric Tom Cruise run
5.content:
Had a bit of a hard time with this one. On the one hand some action scenes were really good, the desert scene in the beginning and the never ending train scene in the end were engaging. But as a whole this installment felt like a step backwards from the previous ones. Weaker in some way.

We get to witness that Tom Cruise at 60 still can run and do impressive stunts. But at the hefty runtime this movie has you would expect more from the story. The idea of an AI adversary is intriguing, but it became a hollow bad guy. Despite the movies length it somehow still felt rushed. Like that they tried to do too much and too little at the same time.

The choreography in the Venice fight scene felt really off, didn't look good at all.

Hayley Atwell was kind of a miss for me, didn't really fit in and her chemistry with Cruise wasn't there. Feels like they forced her in so they could take someone else out.

Good to see Henry Czerny back as Kittridge, he's a solid actor although he didn't get too much screen time here.

Remains to be seen how they tie this thing together in the second part, but it feels like they could have been content with this if the pattern is the same.

5.title: It's okay but nothing more
5.content:
*MILD SPOILERS*

First off I have to say that I love Tom Cruise and his films. I've defended the guy even when it wasn't fashionable and The Last Samurai is in my top 3 favourite films. Maverick was epic and I respect his commitment to his craft but having seen MI: Dead Reckoning I do have to say that it was just okay.

I totally appreciate that the film wasn't woke and there wasn't any messaging being thrust down our throat though maybe Pom fighting evenly with Tom is a bit of a stretch. And so for that reason I do understand that it is important that the film does well at the Box Office to show Hollywood the way forward.

But with that in mind, let's not get too carried away because it still suffers from some real problems. The sense of peril for any of the characters has all but vanished because we've seen what the characters are capable of and we remember the other films.

I mean did the bomb in the airport really have any tension behind it at all? We know the franchise. We know they won't detonate a bomb in an airport in the first act. So it seems false and treating the audience as if they have never seen an MI film before.

And having an audience that knows the characters leads to other problems. Having seen Tom and Ilsa kick the literal crap out of room loads of guys before, having her run away when presented with the unnecessarily dramatic scene in Venice seems really forced.

Let's be honest, no one really presents a credible physical threat to those two (because of what they've shown us in the other films) and hence to have them split up and run away just feels really pointless or rather clearly foreshadowing a lazily constructed and unsurprising moment of apparent drama. Why would you do that? Why would Ethan shout run when they could fight their way out of the situation with ease?

And likewise the makers really do need to pay attention to the marketing that they do for these films. When they splash memorable images of Tom and Hayley in the train everywhere pre launch, it kills any tension in the second act of who might die. It's patently obvious who will die because you've previously shown me who is on the train at the end.

Similar to this is the never ending fixation with the need for amazing stunts. The bike jump is impressive but is it REALLY that more impressive than the Bond ski jump at the beginning of TSWLM which was nearly 50 years ago? And in turn it can't just have been me that felt like they thought of the stunt first and then crammed in a kinda pointless scene to facilitate it? An obvious stunt for stunt's sake is not conducive to building tension. I might as well watch the X Games for that.

Yes the film was fun but like John Wick, when there is too much action and the main character has despatched bad guys with ease for the last 90 minutes, seeing them do it for another 30 minutes is just wallpaper.

While the film was okay, the acting was good, the music was great and some of the action was kinda cool, it did feel generic, a little lazy and a little 'going through the motions'.

What I really fear, and I saw this with the glowing praise of Wick 4 and Extraction 2, is that we become like the Left and just because a film is 'on our side' (i.e. Isn't woke) that we give it a free pass when it is, well a little bit boring.

PS Can we also acknowledge with sadness that the thing that made Hayley Atwell so hot (you all know what it is) has been lost with the push/pressure to make her lose weight.

5.title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning: Part One (2023, Christopher McQuarrie) Decent standard Cruise action but the script is bizarrely bad
5.content:
Eric's Grade: C 'Dead Reckoning' is the seventh installment in the Tom Cruise led 'Mission: Impossible' franchise. Once again this sees Cruise teaming with director and co-writer Chistopher McQuarrie who has been solely in the Tom Cruise business since 2014. Since 2012 nine of the twelve movies McQuarrie has worked on have been Tom Cruise films, and McQuarrie has really found a career defining niche with the most recent set of 'Mission: Impossible' films directing 'Rogue Nation', 'Fallout' and now both installments of 'Dead Reckoning'. In addition to Cruise this latest entry features many returning actors from the franchise including Ving Rhames, Rebecca Ferguson, Vanessa Kirby and Simon Pegg with new additions such as Esai Morales, Pom Klementieff and Hayley Atwell. While 'Dead Reckoning' has cleared over $500 million at the box office that figure becomes a tad less impressive when compared to its $291 million dollar budget which ranks it as one of the most expensive films ever made.

The plot here is chaotic and features a new high tech terrorist that Ethan Hunt, played by Cruise, and his IMF team must hunt. This new supervillain is none other than a computer program. Nearing the realm of science fiction and comic book plot lines an advanced war program on a Russian submarine gains sentience. Now it threatens the safety of the entire planet as it can control anything digital, and its predictive modeling makes it a doomsday prophet for a new age. This prophet comes complete with human disciples in the form of Morales' Gabriel and Klementieff's Paris among others as apparently it still helps to have some humans to usher in Skynet and Judgement Day. Once again Ethan and friends must go "rogue", which they even sort of wink at in this film as it does happen in pretty much every 'Mission: Impossible' film, in order to put an end to this next generation enemy as it becomes apparent that all the governments of the world want to possess the Entity to control and use it whereas Ethan's small force determines it should be destroyed and are striving to that end. To start the adventure they must hunt down a key split into two parts. Off to the Arabian Desert they go to track down key half one which is inexplicably being held by Ilsa Faust who is now the primary love interest of Hunt as well as a disgraced former British spy played by Rebecca Ferguson. They track the other half to Abu Dhabi and then Rome where somehow a thief played by Hayley Atwell enters the mix as she gets the key loses the key gets it again.... it's easy to lose track. She spends a great deal of time running away from Ethan Hunt before, predictably joining up with his cause. They figure out the Entity, as this sentient AI is called, can pretty much do anything, see anything, manipulate anything connected to computers or satellites or the internet so they have to go old school analog to get the drop on this thing. The whole thing culminates in big action set pieces, a runaway train, questionable allegiances with revelations about the location and nature of the Entity as the heroes square off against the villains for all the marbles.

So I have greatly enjoyed the 'Mission: Impossible franchise'. This includes the first three films which, for the most part, aren't as well regarded, but the franchise leveled everything up starting with 'Ghost Protocol'. Since then every installment has tried to feel bigger with more audacious action and higher stakes. While this installment has a lot of tension, and the stakes are higher than ever, I don't feel like the action here is anything better than we have seen before. The Burj Khalifa sequences in 'Ghost Protocol' are eye popping. The helicopter chase from 'Fallout' is dazzling spectacle. I feel like they are almost at their creative limit with attempting to come up with action to astound and amaze the audience. The action here is still enjoyable, however, and not the downfall of this film. The writing to me is very all over the place. I am thoroughly confused regarding who wants what with this Entity as well as what the Entity can and cannot do. We have no data on how it recruited humans to do its dirty work or even what its intentions are. There are many problems when it comes to trying to dissect the enemy and all of the moving pieces surrounding it not to mention its limitations if it, in fact, has any. As presented it is ostensibly an omnipotent presence that can manipulate the present and foretell the future? The entire inclusion of the Hayley Atwell's thief character is nonsensical. It is like the film makers wanted some new blood and they found a way to shoehorn someone into the story logic be damned. Not only does her whole presence not work for me, but once she is in play almost every action she takes makes no sense. She consistently attempts to run away from Ethan falling into malevolent hands each and every time she attempts to flee. Rebecca Ferguson is finally freed up to be a more a part of the story after the events of previous films, instead they just sideline her, and seemingly replace her with Atwell? I greatly enjoy the action 'Dead Reckoning' offers even if it is not breaking new ground, but this is the most convoluted plot and confusing character development that the series has ever had, and we haven't even brushed on the fact that the bad guy the Entity has at its beck and call is a nefarious figure from Hunt's past. Of course he is, and on and on it goes. Turn off your brain and enjoy some action as Tom Cruise runs and runs searching for the latest widget to save the world, but engage your brain at your own risk as 'Dead Reckoning part One' is a fun, but problematic hot mess.

5.title: Disappointing
5.content: I wanted to like this movie but unusually as I love MI movies I lost interest. The role of Grace (Hayley Atwell) I found annoying and her acting was bad. I didn't understand why the Tom Cruise character keep saving her. The start of the movie was excellent, then along came Grace. The character development was weak and the only parts I really enjoyed were the interactions with the old team, these were excellent funny, exciting, clever. The two excellent actors Rebecca Fergusson and Vanessa Kirby were under utilised and tokenistic such a waste of talent compared to the Hayley Atwell role, that got screen time but did little to impress. I'm hoping her role won't continue in next movie but if it does I'll wait to view when free to air.

5.title: Back to MI 2 standards
5.content: It was going strong, but sooner or later you run out of story. This has all of the most boring, been done a thousand times scenes that now cost double the money. Getting rid of Ferguson and going with the new thief, not my cup of tea or something that should be in M:I. They've clearly exhausted their ideas. This is like fast and furious. Super boring now because it's just rinse and repeat. If they don't get back to what works, I think this will die out like fast and furious. Hopefully, it will recover. There is part 2. But let's get some team action back in there. Get some cohesive stuff going on. Bring back the impossible mission. Raise the bar and steaks. Tom don't show your awesome stunts a thousand times before the movie. I'll watch the next one. But let's hope for something better. Still a huge Cruise fan.

5.title: Tommy Wiseau as Ethan Hunt
5.content: I loved Top Gun Maverick. I loved Born on the 4th of July. I love Minority Report. There are some parts of Color of Money that are brilliant. This new MI installment was a disappointment. It was as if they were making a mockumentary. I thought they wpuld break character and outtake the whole movie. Tom Cruise's lines are delivered with an overly dramatic, nasally, inhale. The setups are procedural at best. The lumbering scenes with disappointing comedic beats fails at every level. I yawned at least seven times throughout the film. I want to come back to the theaters and see big movies on the big screen. This was barely a reason to leave the home. Let's do better next time.

5.title: Confusing and Way Too Serious
5.content:
My movie-going rating is always determined by the number of times I look at my watch and I did that repeatedly throughout this. I will concede that some of the action stunts were great but when they weren't happening the movie plodded.

I realize that logic needs to be suspended during action films. But really----Cruise rides his motorcycle off a cliff, parachutes down right through the exact spot on the train when one of his femmes fatales is just about to be shot??? And didn't I just see Indiana Jone have a car chase though the cobblestones streets in Europe. Do keep in mind when you are in a foreign country, it's always very easy to find the car you are chasing.

Finally both Henry Czerny and Ving Rhames need to lighten up.

5.title: MI: 1, MI: 4, MI: 3, MI: 5, MI: 6, MI: 7, MI: 2 Best to Worst
5.content:
MI: 1, MI: 4, MI: 3, MI: 5, MI: 6, MI: 7, MI: 2

In that order. Seriously had high expectations for this film, but I was uncertain of the direction of this series since the 5th movie. When it was announced that MI:7 was a part one. I rolled my eyes, it should of been left as MI:7 and then just continue on to MI:8, that's was pointless and it almost separates the film from the rest of the series; which is weird considering you can usher a whole new cast and still not have to call it a two-part.

Since a kid I loved this series watching the first Mission Impossible and buying it on VHS, even the N64 video game. Yes that old. What I love and miss from MI:1 was that serious spy thriller. Very little laughter, if any out of Hunt. The suspense and dialogue in MI:1 is so good you have to rewatch it several times to understand what the motives were for several characters. And there's a reason the director is a legend it shows in MI:1. And I believe MI:4 is the perfect version; if you were to go the action adventure route. MI:4 I can truly appreciate the flow and adventure of that film. Brad Bird did a fantastic job. Everything about the fourth movie is great, you can feel the suspense till the last second. And the hanging out the tower scene still raises my anxiety. They should have kept that medium for the franchise. I can literally continue this review all about MI:4 because I can see the attempted balance of that style to what Christopher McQuarrie was trying to do with his Dark Knight Nolan style of view since MI:5. Which I didn't like because it was a copied style, pasted to this franchise. Like many other franchises. And it was working for MI:5 & MI:6, but for this film it seemed forced, not enough salt or sugar in the recipe. MI:7 feels watered-down.

Let's begin...So much appreciation for the other films now that I've seen Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning. Lots I didn't like about the film and things I did. I'm not a big fan of Christopher McQuarrie's version of Mission Impossible but I still favor MI:5 & MI:6 over MI:7 by several stars. Sorry Chris. This movie like others said feels flat or empty. The beginning was kind of slow and not as clever compared to all the other MI intros. The villain is so terrible, really so another repetitive character-arc plot. He's basically John Cena in Fast and Furious 9, long lost associate of Hunt who caused everything to happen. Who we've never heard about in first six films. Not featured or mentioned in any of the previous films; And he knows Ethan's every move. Didnt we get something like that with Solomon Lane. Barf. Why was the woman in the white face in the movie? Ohh...I forgot we need a female antagonist because I have to be a mindless noob and follow trends that others follow without thought. Her character seemed so pointless.

Things I liked: Grace was a fresh-hot face to the series, the music was really good; better than some of the previous. *Watching this in IMAX was cool, soundFX were great. Mostly everything I didn't critique I enjoyed*

So are all directors and writers sitting together and saying to each other create the same films. Because the plot to this is weak and redundant. Really an artificial intelligence machine capable of controlling everything and potentially destroying the world or controlling the world: Eagle-Eye, Fast and Furious: 6, A. I., Ready Player One, Free Guy, Matrix. And the countless A. I. based movies. This made the movie drop several stars itself. The real MI:7 was part of a British intelligence branch that dealt with misinformation in media and sabotage. There alone is good source material. Seeing it thru AI is boring and is just a repetitive plot. In MI:4 the Kremlin was exploding in the first half of the movie. MI:2 the intro, MI:5 airplane takeoff intro.

The only reason I ranked MI:7 above MI:2 is solely due to that fact that they created a love story sequel, right after the fact they created a blockbuster spy action thriller that catapulted the whole series. Did not make sense to create that version of MI:2 at that time. NO ONE WANTED TO SEE A LOVE STORY right after the amazing movie that was Mission Impossible.

Hope MI:8 brings it back! Or bring back Brian De Palma(at 82) or Brad Bird!

5.title: Average. Here's my complains.
5.content:
It's not a bad movie, but it's kind of a let down. Perhaps the worse M. I. film since M. I. 2.

The dutch camera angles give it a cheap feeling.

The exposition dialogues are long, tedious and boring: Submarine exposition, then office exposition with people laying back on their chairs and no tension, then exposition by Ethan's briefcase (followed by the most overwhelming message distraction)

In many scenes (in both exposition and action) the camera changes sides and it's hard to follow who is looking where.

The car chase is treated as a joke for far too long, which diminish the seriousness.

The A. I. story (although interesting) doesn't do anything groundbreaking.

Ethan is wanted by everyone and walks around without a mask on? Come on!

Girl and supervillain fight alone and Ethan runs to save her, but he is far away. Guess who loses.

And the 2 big stunts of the movie (bike and train) are spoiled by the trailer.

Also, we spend 2,5h chasing a McGuffin, which is boring.

We don't even know what the villain wants or what happened in the past between him and Ethan.

This movie has MANY flaws. Boring, predictable, and the pacing was off. Especially at the start, before the airport scene.

What I liked?

Some of Italy's scenes, because I've been there and I recognized the landmarks.

And most of the final scene with the train. Even though the villain shouldn't have survived that fall, due to velocity.

5.title: 🙈🙈🙈 A very well-shot full-length film about ridiculous pretentious nonsense
5.content:
"Imagine being an experienced professional writer tasked with revising a text to enhance its uniqueness while retaining its core meaning:

A masterfully directed feature film unfolds, exploring the realm of absurd and pretentious escapades. It delves into the lives of enemy shooters located in the hinterland who, despite incessant automatic firing, fail to hit their targets and perish in clusters. The film commences with a fantastical twist, as a Russian artificial intelligence assumes control of a submarine, injecting amusement into the narrative. Our protagonist's encounter with a messenger yields comedic moments, as the ludicrous and pretentious script was penned by someone one might consider an amateur. Within this whimsical tale, we immerse ourselves in the study of an invulnerable 'essence,' examining its defining attributes: immoral, godless, and omnipotent. It encompasses a cosmic, visionary realm of unfathomable absurdity, so much so that even 'The Expendables 4' pales in comparison, appearing like a grounded documentary. Astonishingly, the creators amplify this nonsensical saga into two separate films! Only by temporarily suspending rationality can one truly appreciate this bewildering spectacle, as lacking intellectual engagement may result in cerebral atrophy.

Agree or disagree, disliking my opinion holds no consequence-a mere ticket purchase will suffice for the creators, who perceive their audience as passive consumers."

Please note that the revised text aims to capture the essence of the original while imbuing it with a more polished and professional tone.

5.title: Disappointing Movie
5.content:
You know when the reviews are lying when this movie gets an 8/10 in IMDb but the experience was totally flat. I actually felt asleep at some of the scenes and it felt too long. This Part 7 is prob equal or lower to Part 2 of the series. Whereas Parts 3, 4, 5 and 6 were just stand out action films, topping the previous parts, Dead Reckoning is disappointing and dead. Where did this movie get wrong?

Story was stretched out. This could have been just a 1 movie but I think the producers got so greedy that they decided to have a Part 2. It's the same style of the Hunger Games before and the Spiderman Across the Multiverse, and these movies fell flat too.






Dead Reckoning tried to be Mission Impossible but failed miserably and ended up being a B-grade action movie. And I believe this is due to the Producer's greed. Well, they will not take money for Part 8.

5.title: Five stars for Tom, but the gals disappoint
5.content:
A movie of this length demands a good, cohesive plot, strong characters, good dialogue. Well there was none of that here. After a poor opening sequence, of a submarine being blown up (a Russian submarine, manned by a crew speaking English with funny accents) the rest of the film did not improve much.

In a movie of this type - escapist fun - I like to see at least one beautiful sophisticated woman in lovely clothes. There were four females playing Strong Women (all the subordinate roles were taken by men) and each was boring and badly dressed. I'm female and if I want boring and badly dressed I can look in a mirror. Is it so wrong to expect a little glamour when I go to the movies? Rebecca Ferguson can look gorgeous, and she's a good actress but she was seriously wasted in this film. She sort of hung around looking depressed before getting killed. And why on earth Hayley Atwell was cast is a mystery - at least to me. She has zero star quality, and there was no charisma between her and Tom. But the worst casting was Vanessa Kirby as the White Widow; there is simply no way this person was believable as a mob boss.

You also need a good villain and that was missing too. The guy playing Gabriel just wasn't striking enough.

Good action sequences, although nothing that hasn't been done many times before, and the car chase could have been shortened considerably without any loss to the plot.

Tom continues to amaze. He's 61 and yet could pass for late forties, even in close up.

In summary, pretty entertaining, but far too long. My vote is five - but those five stars are all for Tom.

5.title: As a deep M:I fan, hugely letdown
5.content:
Hey guys, for me it seems like I've seen a whole different movie than you, obviously, M:I Dead Reckoning Part 1 is rated highly. And while I understand that as a standalone action movie it is very well executed and solid, it is imho very disappoint as a part of the Mission: Impossible franchise. I just want to share my 2 cents on it.

For me, it was a 5/10 at most. And I live and breathe the M:I franchise over everything else, like Star Wars, LOTR, Potter, whatever. I also love and admire Tom Cruise for his incredible work. I am a male in my thirties and have seen every M:I movie on the big screen as it came out, except for the first one in the nineties.

But for me, this new installment in the franchise just falls flat. Let me explain why.

First off, it is far too comical. There were always small jokes or light moments during the franchise, but the whole beginning part of this movie felt more like a Marvel Love and Thunder dumbness. The car chasing scene in the first half was incredibly hard to watch, complete opposite from the one in Fallout in Paris for example. How many times will you recycle the "woman can't drive" joke. The movie theater laughing for 10 minutes straight is not what I expect when going to a MI-film, at all. This already has wrecked me completely to the point I almost started crying to what they had done to this part of my favorite franchise.

Not "dark" enough, goes along with my first point. There is no feel of real danger or menace, like in M:I 3 or Fallout for example. Ethan was always ahead of the situation or everything turned out great after every scene. The scene from Fallout with the heist on Solomon Lane's truck, to catch him right in front of the Police eyes? Planned and done perfectly.

The only "dark" moment was when Gabriel kills Ilsa, but again, that happened just for the plots sake, to tear off some emotion from the audience. Of course it was Ilsa to die, we wouldn't care at all if it would have been Grace instead.

This theme gets even worse with the main villain. Gabriel was a wet towel, compared to Owen Davian or Solomon Lane. Esai Morales played well, don't get me wrong, just the character itself was very shallow. Those guys were a real threat for Ethan and the IMF as a whole. In contrast to that, Ethan plays with Gabriel the whole movie and defeats him twice in Part 1 already, one by having the opportunity to kill him easily if not for Gabriel's plot armor, the other by stealing the key in the end. Where is the tension going into part 2 if the main villain is no threat and just a joke to be played with?

The whole AI thing is also very hard to grasp. I get it why they've chosen it, to give the story a 70s vibe with the analog technique to be used, as a nod to the original M:I series. But AI going rogue and people trying to abuse it for power feels so sucked dry and seen millions of times already.

There is no real Mission: Impossible moment. That one is the biggest one for me I suppose. Like no moment in the movie lets you sit on the edge of your seat watching Ethan do a crazy stunt or activity for minutes. No tension. Every movie had that kind of moment:M:I server room sceneMI:2 Entry into Biocyte tower, exchange of Chimera and BellerophonMI:3 Ethan interrogation with Davian and death after electrocution, resurrectionMI:4 Burj Kalifa climbMI:5 Underwater Server RoomMI:6 Halo jump, Solomon RescueMI:7 tried this with the bike jump, but it was already dead on arrival, seen it so often on Instagram, trailer, general movie PR. Also, it was over like in seconds and while I can imagine how hard this stunt was to pull of, just watching it felt "meh, whatever."

You didn't even see him flying towards the train and aiming at it, that would have provided some tension at least. Also, the CGI of the rocks, which meant to hide the ramp was done incredibly poorly.

Also, the opening of the movie with the submarine stuff felt more like a James Bond, instead of M:I. In every film of the franchise the opening would include Ethan and his team doing things to kick off the plot. The screen time of Luther and Benji felt too short, I especially love Luther's character.

Easter eggs or recalls, plot repeats:

So many, especially to M:I 2:

Gabriel shouts "Ethan" at the end, like Sean shouts "Hunt" when Sean finds out he replaced his right hand Billy and got him killed.


The "parachute is only for one" thing is straight up repeated form the same plot line in the end of M:I 2 Biocyte tower, where he leaves Nyah with Sean and escapes by himself with his parachute.


Whole train sequence felt like already seen, because we actually did see it exactly like that in M:I


Mention of a collier of Bulgary if I recall correctly, like the one Nyah tries to steal in Seville in M:I 2


The whole mountain drive up scene was a homage to Fallout, where Benji guides Ethan through London's roofs and misses to activate the 3D-view, so he does not know Ethan has to jump down to get on a lower level to pursue Lark. Here, while you wait for Benji to say the same, he actually was aware of the height difference and guided Ethan straight towards it


Sloan picture in the government room in the beginning


"you've never seen me upset"-reference between Kittridge and Ethan.


Mask machine breaks, already seen in Ghost Protocol.


the sleight-of-hand tricks from M:I


They were many more, but I've forgotten some after sleeping the night after witching it yesterday

There are many logic errors or plot holes for me, but maybe I got them wrong, so please feel welcome to educate me.

AI whole plan goes shambles just if Ethan won't kill Gabriel? In MI:1 he had a whole campaign running for not killing or harming anyone, even in this film he saved Paris and did not kill her. Was it really so unlikely for Ethan not to kill someone? Doesn't make sense. The AI sees millions of different outcomes like Dr. Strange in Infinity War, but this one crucial point to not kill Gabriel would save the day?


Ilsa dies form Gabriel's knife, but Paris, wounded exactly the same, goes on to save Ethan and Grace, pulls them up the train carriage and proceeds to survive? Wow.


Ethan gets a "he was a baddie" before joining the IMF prequel story all of a sudden? Really? In M:I he already seemed like a decent person with morals, parents to care about, where is the character development coming from? It shocked me that Tom Cruise approved this, just so Gabriel's whole character had a reason to exist. Why did he need to? Lane was introduced completely from scratch and it worked out fine.


Gabriel standing on top of the train, waiting for his escape point. Then, Ethan confronts him, making them fight on top of the train while dodging light signals and a tunnel. What would have happened if Ethan would not have been there? Would Gabriel just played jump and run on that train's roof by himself while waiting to arrive at his planned escape point?


How many times will Grace betray Ethan and straight up leave him to die in the subway? Why on Earth did the writers seem it would be plausible to write her character like that? How dumb does she get to be to not understand Ethan to help her. Even Ilsa got this quicker and she was even more hostile towards Ethan at first. Tiring, to say the least.


Gabriel's escape point. He calculates the exact acceleration and speed of an old steam-powered train, to know exactly when to jump and land and his prepared truck? How would you know the exact peripherals of the machine to do that? Did the AI calculate this? So it has to be mentioned in the movie.


Also, who kept the train running and shoveling coal into the combustion chamber? The train should go slower, instead of full speed the whole time.


The whole plan to board the train with a motorcycle, resulting in driving up a mountain and a base jump into the train. Meanwhile, Paris just stands on top of a bridge and jumps down to the train. Really, the whole Ethan's IMF super-intelligence guys would not have thought of that?


AI sets itself into a submarine and destroys it, so the original code needed to stop it would get destroyed as well? Transfer yourself into a house, trigger some systems to cause a fire, burn down the house with the original code. Why would the AI risk that the original code to delete it would still be retrievable?


The key has infinite power to glow the jewels or what? Or do they have to put it into a charging station from time to time or whatever?


Ilsa gets defeated by Gabriel? Like, have you seen her fight in Rogue Nation or Fallout, the guys she defeated there?


Car chase in Rome: Paris just walks away after wrecking half of the police fleet with her Hummer and nobody minds? It is not even shown how she escapes. Just another "Somehow, Palpatine returned"


-Too predictable. What is Part 2 going to be? Start sequence, Ethan dives down to Sevastopol, tries to delete the AI, that goes wrong, AI loads itself into a satellite in orbit, the whole rest of the movie is going to be about flying into space to delete the AI on that satellite?

Then all the other characters, what happened? I wouldn't mind if it was just "some" M:I part in the middle, but Dead Reckoning is meant to be the final installment to the franchise, so there are some ends to tie together.

No mention of Solomon Lane or the Syndicate? CIA director Sloane just gets a picture on the wall? Is she dead? What happened to her after Fallout? What happened to William Brandt? What is Julia up to? Maybe all these actors were not meant to be hired to create the next parts of the M:I franchise, I get that. But at least mention them, so it does not feel like they were all meaningless and the plot lines completely forgotten.

What a terrible disappointment. Like a famous comic book guy once said, this was so bad, I will only watch it 6 times more.

I just hope it was some kind of a build up for the grand finale and it will redeem Part 1 in hindsight.

5.title: Disappointed
5.content: Only expectations to have while watching this movie will be the stunts besides that story is a letdown, the antagonist was plain boring and story was supposed to make him look like Ethan Hunt's greatest for. The antagonist looks like a model with smoldering, that was all the portrayal of the character I can remember. Movie is cringey at times, the chemistry between actors is almost nonexistent. The movie can be said to be a stuntman tutorial for newbie action stars. Such a letdown compared to the other sequels, the movie looked abit rushed as well. I think the Covid restrictions while shooting the movie might have played a part in it. I felt robbed of my time and money. The score of 5 is just so that I am a big fan of the MI series. I am not trashing this movie in no shape or form, for a movie of that magnitude and budget it was heavily lacking in story and script.

5.title: A good action movie but not an M:I movie
5.content:
I watched the latest installment at the Australian premiere this week and Mr. Cruise was there himself. I am a hardcore M:I fan and have watched all the entries countless times. So, I was so looking forward to this one, but it doesn't feel like an M:I spy movie but rather an action thriller. This movie let me down and I came out of the premiere with so many questions and complaints. The opening intro is not as impactful and punchy as the previous ones. Ethan Hunt in this movie is not as clever and 'ahead of the curve' as we've seen him in the last six entries. The first half is rather slow. There was very minimal use of fancy gadgets (maybe cos of the plot).

**SPOILER ALERT** Ethan Hunt doesn't infiltrate any highly secured building to steal anything highly classified or extract anyone using smart tech, great team work and innovative yet dangerous plans (hence, impossible). All the promoted action sequences clearly come across as forced and don't blend naturally in the situations shown. McQ said in intereviews that they develop action sequences first and then figure out how they fit into the story and situations later and it's clearly apparent in this movie. If Ethan Hunt had to escape with Grace in Rome, I am not sure why he would let her drive when he knew she wasn't an IMF agent. It was just to create the sequence with unnecessary comic situations at the expense of action sequence intensity. It feels like that whole sequence was created to bring something new, but does not fit well for Ethan Hunt's character. The train sequence is way too long and again, not still sure why everyone went up on the roof to fight. In previous M:I movies, Ethan was kind of compelled to engage in risky stunts cos there was no other way (hence, impossible). That is missing big time in this movie. The biggest disappointment was the so-called 'biggest stunt in cinema history', which lasts only a min in the movie and that cliff jump, which they have been showing off for months is pretty much the stunt - nothing much after. They haven't even shown how he managed to pinpoint his landing right through to the train window. All the previous stunts he did were shown end to end, so you know how he did it and how dangerous it was so, you're completely engaged with that stunt (e.g. Burj Khalifa stunt, underwater stunt and plane stunt in Rogue Nation). The villian is also very weak and doesn't come across that brutal. The only positive is the plot, which is really good and relevant to what's happening today. Overall, quite disappointed.

5.title: A Tedious Rehash of the Same Old Formula
5.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a disappointing addition to the iconic franchise, delivering a lackluster experience that can be succinctly described as both boring and a rehash of the same old stuff we've seen countless times before.

From the opening scenes to the final credits, the film fails to inject any fresh energy into the Mission: Impossible universe. Instead, it relies heavily on tired tropes and predictable plot devices that have become all too familiar in the series. It's as if the filmmakers took a checklist of successful elements from the previous movies and mechanically reproduced them without any attempt at innovation or creativity.

The narrative, which should be the driving force of any action-packed spy thriller, is painfully unoriginal. The plot unfolds in a predictable manner, with clichéd twists and turns that do little to engage or surprise the audience. The attempt to build suspense falls flat, as the storyline lacks depth and fails to provide any meaningful stakes for the characters.

Despite a star-studded cast led by Tom Cruise, the performances feel uninspired, as if the actors themselves are aware they're going through the motions of a tired script. Even Cruise's charismatic presence can't salvage the film from its own mediocrity. The chemistry between the characters, a crucial aspect of the franchise, feels forced and lacks the genuine camaraderie that made earlier installments enjoyable.

The action sequences, once the hallmark of Mission: Impossible, are surprisingly decent. While there are moments of intensity, they are overshadowed by the sense of déjà vu that permeates every frame. It's evident that the filmmakers relied on the formula that worked in the past, neglecting the opportunity to push the boundaries and offer audiences something new and exhilarating.

In summing up, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a prime example of a franchise resting on its laurels. It fails to deliver the excitement and innovation that fans expect, offering instead a tedious and formulaic experience. If you're seeking a thrilling and fresh take on the Mission: Impossible series, look elsewhere, because this installment is just the same old stuff.

5.title: I just don't get it....
5.content:
Yeah, so that was my first actual thought... "I just don't get it". Am I seeing things nobody else sees? Why are my experience of this movie so utterly completely different from others? How come this movie has a raiting of 8(!) (as of writing), when I just felt like leaving the theater during the movie? I just realized: I suck at understanding the brilliance of movies these days. I used to have a pretty good understanding before (or I think I did), but I have totally lost it.

Ok, so back to the movie. Let me begin by saying that I love the MI franchise. Watched the series before any of the movies, loved what Brian De Palma did with the first movie, the intense, the mystique, the action. Rest of the movies I found very (VERY) entertaining (except perhaps John Woo's interpretation which was a little bit too much... well... John Woo). And the common denominator for all the movies was an intriguing story: they got an Impossible Mission that was to be handled by a team whose only imagination set the limits on how to complete it. It was cunning, well thought through and thrilling.

And then this... so disappointing... Well the action was there, the entertainment was there, but that was it. The story sucked so bad I even found myself uncomfortable watching this. I sometimes looked down on my phone during the movie just to avoid hearing any more of the plot of the movie. The dialog between the characters was even worse, one cliché after another. And a lot was said during the movie that was so obviously "over scripted" that it lost all meaning and feeling. While I was watching I actually found myself playing with the thought: what would the dialog look like if the characters were not allowed to use the words "entity", "key" and "AI"? (we probably could shorten the movie by an hour or so). Jokes aside, it was not the experience I was hoping for. Probably will see the follow up, but only when out on streaming.

Hoping for a new retake of the MI franchise in the future cause this was not good...

5.title: Go back to the roots, seriously
5.content: M:I really needs to go back to its roots, at this point. Remember the 60s and 80s TV shows ? Random passers-by pointing the agent to secret spots ? M:I 6, the previous movie, still had that spirit. Backstabbing in secret undergrounds. Venician boats passing by. That's what M:I needs to reverse to. Not James Bond. Not car chases. Not Evel Knievel moped stunts. And if you include screen crashing insane stunts into a secret agent show, it needs to blend in. It doesn't any more. Did any script writer even notice that real-life police got insanely invasive since 2018 ? Even before covid ? A secret agent who can't avoid 2020s police is dead. In fact, M:I needs to go even more secretive than the 60s and 80s TV shows. Look at the "Matrix" franchise's Agent Smith police. That's the kind of police you're dealing with now, in the 2020s. Personally, I'm wondering whether the movies need the TV shows' M:I teams back. Take the action down a notch, and include some cleverness. Humour is good, but this not a comedy film. You're not going to escape Europe's police. If the movie shows a car chase of 20 Italian police, and Tom Cruise escapes, my guts wrench.

5.title: Enough With Tom Cruise et al in the MI Series!
5.content:
It is time to let go of the Tom Cruise era of the Mission Impossible series:
Cruise is over 60 years old
Hayley Atwell is over 40 years old
Ving Rhames is in his mid 60s
Simon Pegg is over 50 years old
Rebecca Ferguson is over 40 years old
Vanessa Kirby is in her mid 30s
These actors are all great. The writing was good. The actions scenes were executed to perfection. The plot line is so-so. My problem is that I cannot suspend belief when I'm looking at these old people who have the fighting and physical skills of a person who is decades younger. Listen ... I'm an old person myself. I was an good athlete in my younger years and have kept up my training. And I work out ALL THE TIME. Enough is enough. Move on. Yes, I know it is a movie and I'm usually pretty good at suspending belief because it really is just entertainment. Yet now? We're in the Twilight Zone of a nonsensical action movie.

5.title: Boring
5.content: Lots expository dialogue, plus ridiculous action/fight scenes. Lacks any kind of human connections. Add on to this, the main actors are all way too old to still be doing what they're called on to do. Are there no fit fighting age men to step up? Cruise face looks like it's being held up by a girdle at this point in his career. Think back to the first three Bourne movies. Edge of your seat entertainment. Where have all the flowers gone? Long time passing, I would say. I know this so called movie made a ton of money, but I think that speaks more to the dearth of quality content than to the quality of this movie.

5.title: Hide all complexities behind Hacking, Face Masks & AI
5.content:
Nowadays, almost all thriller spy movies / series are so unrealistic, as if we are watching some video games. Makers always hide all complexities of spying world behind "hacking", "face mask", "plastic surgeries", "AI" (new entrant) & so on.

Train scene of movie is very similar to The Lost World: Jurassic Park & thus very predictive.

Most of these Hollywood movies / series are always around Alien attacks, Nuclear & Biological weapons. And then there are Superheroes, who saves the world. And, the villains are either from Russia / Korea / Middle East or some rogue from their own agency.

Looks like South East Asian movies are the only ones left, which still shows REAL actions in movies.

5.title: So much dialogue!
5.content:
The Mission Impossible series has quite impressively set a very high bar for action films and have basically delivered, and then some, with every single one (despite it being derided, MI:2 has some great action scenes).

It therefore feels inevitable that we were due an underwhelming film and for me this is very much that. My main gripe is that there is soooo much dialogue. If you're going to make an action film with such an enormous amount of dialogue then it needs to be interesting, fun, witty, engaging or at the very least it needs to advance the plot. For the most part the film largely fails on all of these points. There are some very clever and interesting lines regarding artificial intelligence and it's potential impact on the world but a few pithy lines do not make up for such sub-standard and largely boring writing.

The action is great but the series has set such an incredibly high bar for action sequences that I feel this film struggles to really meet.

I'll have to watch it again to see if it's better second time around but I hope Part Two is better.

5.title: Just ehhh
5.content:
I recently returned from watching the latest installment of the Mission Impossible franchise, and I must admit that my rating for it would be a C+. It saddens me to assign such a score, considering my genuine affection for both the Mission Impossible movies and Tom Cruise himself. I won't outright discourage you from watching it, but perhaps waiting to stream it would be a better choice. Here's to hoping that the next part redeems the series.

The film boasted its fair share of action sequences, alongside numerous storylines and characters that remained largely unexplained. Furthermore, to my surprise, there was even a classic love triangle thrown into the mix. In theory, these elements should have combined to create an engaging experience, but unfortunately, they fell short of expectations.

In terms of action, the movie delivered its trademark thrilling sequences that have become synonymous with the franchise. Tom Cruise's dedication to performing his own stunts added an extra layer of authenticity and excitement. However, the plotlines felt disjointed and lacked cohesion, leaving several loose ends and unexplored avenues. The character development also suffered as a result, leaving some individuals feeling underdeveloped and lacking depth.

Moreover, the introduction of a love triangle felt forced and out of place, diverting attention away from the core storyline. While such romantic entanglements can add complexity to a narrative, in this case, it seemed unnecessary and detracted from the overall experience.

Despite these shortcomings, Mission Impossible still possesses its trademark charm and the potential to entertain. The film may find a more suitable home when enjoyed through a streaming service, where one can appreciate the action sequences without feeling let down by the plot's shortcomings. With any luck, the next installment in the franchise will learn from these missteps and deliver a more cohesive and captivating adventure.

5.title: Another Tom Cruise Vanity Project
5.content:
I am not a die hard fan of Tom Cruise but I have seen all of his films. Edge of Tomorrow is by far my favourite.

I would have called this Tom Cruise vs ChatGPT.

An AI who grunts and can't speak? What?

Can Tom move his face any more? There was no emotion.

Ethan tired of Ilsa pretty quickly, replacing her with Grace in the blink of an eye.

The Italy car chase was too reminiscent of the ridiculous Fast X car chase. The train top fight scene reminded me of the latest Indiana Jones. And if you give me the choice between an aging Cruise versus a de-aged Ford, I will take Ford every time.

At almost 3 hours, it was monotonous. I was bored. I had already seen the "making of" the jump scene. The air conditioning was great though.

5.title: What a disappointing movie...
5.content:
I'm a big MI fan. I think it's the best spy franchise, better than James Bond. I've seen them all on a big screen since the first one. Rogue Nation is my favourite. This is not a bad movie but it's very disappointing compared to the last two movies.

1) A lot of inconsistencies in the scenes. Some scenes are dragging on and on (boring, yawning...) while others are cut short. I yawned several times during the following scenes and couldn't wait for them to end: the scene at the airport, the car chase in Rome, when the train was collapsing and Ethan and Grace were moving from carriage to another carriage, and to another one... And then you have major scenes like the one where they killed off a major character like Ilsa that lasted just 10 seconds.

2) Too many goofy, unfunny, and dumb moments. It feels like I'm watching a Disney Marvel movie at times, with jokes written by a 4 year old for illiterate teenagers with an IQ of 0.73.

3) Ilsa Faust is one of the best characters in the franchise, yet we barely see her in this episode. Besides they killed her off (why? What a mistake) and the send-off was lame. In the previous 2 MI movies, she was a kick-ass, first class fighter, capable of killing bigger, stronger armed opponents with her bare hands and feet. In this movie, she can hardly fight. She has a sword and the bad guy, Gabriel, has a tiny pocket knife, yet he got the best out of her. The fight scene lasts 10 seconds. It is very badly filmed, very badly shot, the choreography is lame, some small shots here and there... What a way to send off one of the best characters of the franchise... They might as well have just killed her off in a lame freak accident (make her trip on a stone while walking with high heels and fall on the floor cracking her skull). It was that pathetic.

4) The bad guy (Gabriel) is lame. Not scary at all, absolutely zero charisma.

5.title: Worst one yet
5.content: First of all, I wasn't happy that this is part one of two. It makes you not want to see the first part until the second part is out. Secondly, the story is weak and muddled. It's also too long. There are good action sequences of course which is the main attraction but at nearly 3 hours long they are overshadowed by boring scenes. I honestly feel that this franchise has had its day. There just wasn't enough interest in it for me to watch the second part so I think I'll just give it a miss, especially if it's nearly 3 hours long like this one. Maybe they could do a mission impossible in space like fast and furious.

5.title: Mediocre script and predictive action scenes
5.content:
I admit I have never been much of a fan of MI, but perhaps haven't missed a movie from the franchise. This one, however was a big disappointment.

The script was poor. I get it AI is fashionable, lets ride the wave, but the plot is just sad and mediocre. It felt like a story my little son was telling me. The actors were not impressive either. The one thing I liked more than the rest of the movies was the occasional fun scenes.

And yeah, I get it MI has always been about the action. That I appreciate, but still, the train, the motorbikes, the cars...nothing felt new to me. And yes, the script - it was poor. I am truly disappointed.

5.title: Mostly boring with some nice action scenes in between
5.content: Probably the worst one after MI2. The previous ones were just more fluid and fun. Action sequences were done better, storyline was a bit better. There was so much lull and dialogue in this one, and if felt like they were trying to do too much all at once. With the AI storyline, then a bomb, then random ppl having to die, the lack of emotional buildup and connection to Elsa's death, and the overall pacing was just not that great. Don't know if it was complications in production due to covid, but whatever it was, it ended with a subpar result. The fight scenes felt more like dances, car chases were alright, and the overall stakes just felt lower. Compare it to the visceral bathroom fight scene in Fallout, where the movements and speed were so good, it felt like an actual fight. Or the motorcyle (and car) chase in Rogue Nation, with the speed and way it was shot. The intro was mediocre as well. The scenes leading up to the iconic theme song are normally pretty suspenseful and really amp you up. But this one just went into it after the "your mission, should you choose to accept it" briefing. Overall, it just didn't really keep me on the edge of my seat, and i felt quite sleepy at a few parts. When the main actor and director have to preface the movie with a clip saying how much they worked on it and to enjoy it, you know it's not gonna be that good.

5.title: Stunts Shine in the too predictable 'Dead Reckoning
5.content:
Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning" finds itself in that well-trodden territory of action flicks that dazzle more with explosive set pieces than with a compelling plot. The film labours under the weight of dialogue that is as wooden as a boardroom table, with scenes that overstay their welcome, akin to a never-ending maths class on what should be a lazy Sunday. The storyline is straightforward to the point of suspicion, possibly the brainchild of artificial intelligence, stuffed with enough absurdity and plotholes to pad out its runtime.

Yet, Tom Cruise remains the spark that keeps the film watchable if barely, his synergy with Simon Pegg and Ving Rhames injecting some much-needed vigour. However, Hayley Atwell's character tests one's patience; her repetitive betrayals wear thin, her eventual predictable turnaround as surprising as a rain forecast in London.

In a twist of irony, the most authentic thrill comes from a motorcycle stunt - a jaw-dropping moment of madness that Cruise, ever the showman, performs himself. It's this dedication to the craft that pulls the film back from the brink of being a total write-off, reminding us of the unique magic that only cinema can conjure.

5.title: Mission Implausible
5.content:
Pretty much a disappointment. There is an awful amount of exposition and scenery chewing in between the fight/chases/stunts. A lot of characters do odd (or dumb) things for never explained reasons - it's really tough to figure out anyone's motivations.

There is too much humor, advertent or not, for the movie to be taken seriously but also too much violence and calculated pathos.

There is the usual amount of inexplicable coincidence (cf Indiana Jones), like Benji easily finding Ethan in all of Venice, not to mention Ethan's arrival on the train.

Lastly, the locomotive crash that we all saw in the trailer: it's shown from 3 different angles and doesn't even fill 10 seconds of screen time, and looks like good CGI even though we know it was done for real. Well, sort of for real because we know from YouTube that the bridge and the motorcycle take-off slope were entirely digital.

5.title: Very average
5.content: I was disappointed with this movie after all the hype. I enjoyed the opening sequence with the Submarine and the scene with Rebecca Ferguson's character in the desert. I felt the humour in the film was a little corny and didn't work. Disappointingly, Simon Pegg and Ving Rhames were under used compared to previous MI movies. At the end there was obviously no conclusion as this is part 1 of 2, but to be honest I didn't care and wasn't itching to find out what happens which is a tell tale sign I haven't really enjoyed the movie. I would say this movie is 2nd worst in the franchise. If we were comparing summer blockbusters, I though Indiana Jones and The Dial of Destiny was a lot more entertaining but that is just my opinion.

5.title: Could of been alot better
5.content: I enjoyed it at first, although it had alot of things going on, with alot of unanswered questions and moving parts. Halfway through it, I ended up spending more time trying to stay awake watching it. The action was good yet it seemed bland in a way it lacked build up and when the action and suspense hit it wasn't that good it seemed very boring making he want to fall asleep. All the tricks have been done before so alot of it was just on repeat. The bad guy was mediocre. Make sure you are wide awake when u watch it as it has alot of sneaky fall asleep elements in it surprisingly. Get lots of caffeine in ya to watch it!! I WILL still watch the next installment!

5.title: Mid-level movie
5.content:
The movie is the seventh installment in the Mission: Impossible franchise and the first of a two-part finale. It features Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt, who is tasked with retrieving an all-powerful, artificially intelligent algorithm dubbed "the Entity" before it falls into the wrong hands. The movie is both a timely rumination on the dangers of AI as well as a banger of an action sequel that never slows down

The film is directed by Christopher McQuarrie, who crafts a winding head trip that houses some of the most precise, rhythmically assembled, and tension-filled sequences in the series' history. The action sequences are thrilling and intense, and Cruise's performance is outstanding

The movie also features the return of the first movie's morally dubious intelligence head, Eugene Kittridge (Henry Czerny), which serves less as a wistful cameo and more as a throwback to the series' neo-noir roots - a welcome antidote to a summer overrun with empty nostalgia. The plot is well-crafted and keeps you on the edge of your seat throughout

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is an entertaining and enjoyable return for the Mission Impossible crew. It's a blast that highlights the dangerous world Ethan Hunt operates in. I would highly recommend it to anyone who loves action movies.

5.title: Huge fan, very disappointed
5.content:
Here's what's great: the stunts, the cinematography and mostly the sound.

Other than that, I was really disappointed in this one. The writing is incredibly weak and twee. It's action is beautifully choreographed, but it can't make up for the overwritten and sub-par dialogue. Feels like it was still at the first draft phase, which, having had friends work on the previous films, I imagine it was.

Personally, I love the franchise. I saw Fallout five times at the cinema. Even Henry Cavill's 'acting' couldn't ruin that film! But this is my least favourite in the series.

In Dead Reckoning, they go for laughs whenever they can and drain the story of any stakes.

Feels like a film made for a very young audience and sadly has lost the intensity and pace of Fallout.

Still go for the stunts, but honestly, you won't get much more of a thrill than what the trailer can offer, because you're never made to care.

5.title: Worse quality movie
5.content:
The movie itself was quite good however the quality of the picture was pathetic. Totally washed out bordering on something you may have seen on an original valve television. Started that way with the adds and trailers,however this did not improve with the actual movie. Personally I think Odeon stuffed up in a big way and should reimburse us .Previous movies that we have watched were amazing. Death on the Nile had fantastic scenery which even today I still talk about. Any other movie we watched at Odeon in Orange was always first class. The amazing scenery on a big screen is what helps make for an amazing movie. However after this pathetic showing today I would hesitate ever going again,in case this has been the result of cost cutting or just worn out projection equipment. Only reason I suffered through this pathetic showing was that my had been looking forward to watching this movie. Odeon,you are the pits for having the gall to put on something so inferior in quality.

Alex Uren.

5.title: Too Much of one and not enough of the other
5.content:
The 'other' being story.

I enjoyed the film, however, with a running time of 2 hours 38 minutes excluding the endless credits, this film could easily have been cut down to 90 minutes, 100 at a push.

There were too many car chases, actually, there were just too many chases, and they lasted too long.

Don't get me wrong, I love the franchise, it's great fun, tongue in check drama, but this episode is way off the mark when you compare it with its predecessors, there were no, ooh I wasn't expecting that as a mask comes off to reveal Ethan, or some tech is revealed that makes you wish it was real, the orange Fiat was fun. No none of the above, the title should have given it away, but we didn't actually get a true ending to make it all.worth while, no, we have to wait for part 2. I can only hope it is worth having to sit through the endless chases of this part.

I have given this 5 stars for showing up!

5.title: Bloated, unoriginal and verbose
5.content: This is what happens when you make one film into two. You end up with an overly long and frankly boring experience at the cinema. Overly long exposition, mediocre acting and lacking in set pieces. The cliff jump was in the trailers, the other set pieces we have seen a thousand times before in this series and other action films. Car chase - check (yawn), fight on a train - check (double yawn) and fist fights - check (choreographed by children!!). The last MI was infinitely more exciting. This bored more half to death. It was the one film I was looking forward to this summer. At least they had the decency to kill a main character!!

5.title: Disappointing
5.content: First, the action scenes were great. Haley Atewell was wonderful and her character was well served. But everything else... ohhh boy. The movie was too long. Bloated action moments were included seemingly because they seemed cool with a line thrown in to "explain it." There was no IMF team here. Benji and Luthor were sidelined for most of the movie or left to explain things and the way they resolved Ilsa... one word. Fridge. The villain was stock and boring. At this stage of the franchise they need someone to strongly challenge Ethan. Esai Morales could have been any generic bad guy and his beef with Ethan wasn't fleshed out enough to make me buy it or care. Not to mention that this is the first we have ever heard about any of it. This will end up being listed as one of the worst of the franchise.

5.title: Superficial nonsense
5.content:
Imagination in the story: 0/10 Characters: 1/10 (there were some hotties at least) Action: 4/10 (unrealistic, way too much) Cliche: 10/10

Nightclub scene: check Scene where protagonist has to choose which of two women lives: check Killer assassin girl that can overcome fully grown men: check

There was not enough story and far too much action instead. These bad guys chasing Cruise around for some reason was just so weak. It had absolutely no appeal to any of the few brain cells I possess.

When I think back to the tension and fear in the first film, where their mission has been sabotaged - that was a true secret agent film. Dead Reckoning should not be allowed to be called Mission Impossible.

I was very disappointed because the last MI was a good film. Will not be seeing the second.

5.title: A Bad Film
5.content:
Dead Reckoning starts with the promise of being the smartest of the franchise and ends up being a very poorly made film laden with bad dialogues and cringeworthy character development.

The tone of the film is inconsistent. The visual effects poor. The stunt pieces are well choreographed but doesn't feel authentic because of heavy CGI. And with heavy heart I must say Cruise looked decent in half of the stunts in the movie which is considered a failure in any day.

The film lacked emotions and although the stakes were supposed to be the highest but the film didn't convince it even for a second.

5.title: I Left Dazed and Confused
5.content:
"Mission Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One" fails to live up to its high-octane lineage, not just stalling, but derailing entirely. Tom Cruise reprises his role as Ethan Hunt, but from his very first scene, it's evident that the indomitable spirit of the agent we once knew is significantly dulled. Not only does Cruise look visibly aged and wearied, but the conviction in his performance is also notably absent.

SPOILER ALERT -One of the major plot holes is when Hunt is mysteriously in Moscow without any prior indication or reasonable explanation. It's as though scenes were cut without any thought to continuity. Another glaring oversight? The antagonist's motive seems to change three times throughout the film, leaving audiences scratching their heads in bewilderment.

The product placements are so overt, they're almost laughable. There's a chase sequence where Hunt, instead of focusing on his pursuer, conspicuously sips a branded coffee before dashing off. And, let's not forget the cringe-inducing moment when a high-stakes confrontation is interrupted by a character's ringtone - a jingle for a popular soft drink.

To add to the debacle, the supporting cast's performances are shockingly subpar. Key dialogue scenes felt like rehearsals, with lines delivered so flatly that they robbed the movie of any semblance of tension. The chemistry, or rather the lack of it, between the team was palpable, making their camaraderie feel forced and unnatural.

In conclusion, "Dead Reckoning Part One" is a muddled mess, riddled with plot holes, and overshadowed by its transparent attempts to cash in on product placements. The "Mission Impossible" franchise has seen highs, but this installment is undoubtedly a profound low. If there's any mission to accept here, it's hoping for a redemptive 'Part Two'.

5.title: Mission: Improbable
5.content:
Your mission should you choose to accept it, is to hold this key. The future of the world depends on it. So keep it safe. Oh yeah sure your jacket pocket will be fine. No, no need to check it. I'm sure it'll be fine. What's that? It's gone?!! Huh. Go figure.

Better idea. Let's build up a character with huge emotional potential using one of the most major actresses of our time. Do it over 2 films. She's deadly. Intelligent. Now let's kill her. But no not really. Let's have her go into hiding. Ha! No not really. Got you again! Now let's have her die again. Do it off camera so we can film Tom running. Lovely running that. He's too late. She's dead. Really dead this time. But er nobody cares, cos, you know, just replace her with a not very good pickpocket.

5.title: Action First, Questions Later
5.content:
Having watched the first film and Fallout, I was intrigued to learn more about this series and decided to check out the latest film. And I got to say, it is good time, but it was difficult to take seriously. Don't get me wrong, their are plenty of fun action scenes and I am interested in watching the next film in the future, but man...if you're looking for an interesting, well thought out plot, this is the wrong place to look.

The moment I learned that the main threat of this story was an alive artificial intelligent program, I almost left the theater. I was hoping for some master hacker or military spy to be the focus, after seeing the seemingly invincible Russian sub being taken out by its own missiles. But then I was greeted by a bunch government officials playing musical chairs with some boring exposition.

It goes on for way too long and nothing interesting happens during the discussion. It gets so boring that Ethan Hunt has to barge in and remind everyone what really matters. And then a miracle occurs. A fun action scene in the airport takes place with Die Hard Three riddle elements. Some fun car chases in Italy. And the films ends with a handful of tense fight scenes on a train to pay homage to the first film.

Again, the artificial intelligence threat is distracting, Its like putting a Digimon villain in a Die Hard film, with the past films focusing on realism, a terrorists as the main villains, this addition really doesn't work. But with how visually pleasing the action scenes are, I'm not complaining too much. It's an odd plot attached to a nice looking film.

5.title: Grace.
5.content: Good movie. Grace however is the most annoying character I've ever watched. She makes me cringe and makes the whole movie suck. She's simply annoying and idiotic. Ethan does everything perfectly, from treating her right, to giving her choices time and time again. Yet she ruins it and finds a way to give me the ick every time. 10/10 movie without grace. With her about a 5/10. I was very excited to watch this movie as well but I simply cannot find myself fully enjoying this movie with her in it. From the beginning when it seems that she is doing everything in her power to ruin things for Ethan to the part where she stays alive instead of Ilsa, it literally hurt to watch these parts. Other than that amazing stunts, crazy good action and great acting. Tom did amazing as usual, just sucks that grace had to ruin some parts.

5.title: Too much talking
5.content: This movie should've been an hour shorter by cutting unnecessary talking. There are some nice action sequences but nothing we've never seen before. The plot is so thin and weak that makes the movie lack substance. The added new back story feels forced. Overall entertaining but it makes you feel like something is missing at the end. I left the theatre feeling unsatisfied. I kept thinking what was missing but I can't put my finger on it but this could've improved by cutting out one whole hour from it. I think the filmmakers wanted to give all the characters enough screen time as this franchise is coming to an end soon.

5.title: A Series of Stunt Setpieces
5.content: Maskerading as a movie. And yes the rubber mask thing gets the meta treatment, hopefully put away for good. Car chases, motorcycle chases, parachutes, trains, knife fight, gun fight, sleight of hand, it's all there loosely connected to some kind of key mcguffin. And bringing back old characters, this Kitteridge guy is he a goodie or baddie? Hard to pay attention. Ving Rames is still the tired old computer hacker genius; pro tip Luther, just turn off the laptop wifi and you will be OK. Benji is just silly. Ferguson doesn't say or do much and gets a write-off. Cruise gives his all, two running scenes plus the physical stunts. Instead of biggest yet should have gone for best yet.

5.title: So-so
5.content:
Although this was an entertaining franchise to start it has become very ho-hum. Despite the mega-bucks it cost to make, despite the high octane action sequences and despite all the hype, all you really have is another Mission Impossible movie. Tom Cruz is ok and the others do their best to keep things moving along, but you keep getting the feeling that "I have seen this before". And, sadly, you have.

The plot here is quite complex (convoluted if you really try to follow it in detail) but that at least keeps things interesting.

To think that there is another half to this two part movie is not really a pleasant thought.

5.title: A mindless film filled with tropes and cliches
5.content:
I should rate this higher, but this movie doesn't meet it's own franchise standard. Sure it has a lot of fast paced action and Tom Cruise running, but that's not enough in my book. Esai Morales is a good bad guy, but the "guy from a past I never talked about" backstory is incredibly stupid. They managed to rotate female leads while ACTIVELY ACKNOWLEDGING the cliche, which I guess I'll count as a self aware thing and give that a plus, but it implies that your character is an idiot with no common sense. It's always nice to see Ving Rhames, and there was a pretty good chase scene with some original moments. Now for the negatives.

I'll start by taking the piss out of Tom Cruise's big stunt moments. We're witnessing a wealthy adrenaline junkie get off on having a good time at the expense of a major studio and the professional crew, it doesn't impress me anymore and at this point it just feels indulgent.

Next let's talk about the big bad AI. They knew that conceptually an AI would be a hard sell for a popcorn munching Mission Impossible audience, so they had it physically represented with a blue screensaver that made me laugh every time it appeared. They're at a party at one point and the lights and screens all turn blue and they look around like "oh no, we walked into a trap", as if the TV Screens are where an AI physically is or something. The whole AI badguy is just beneath Mission Impossible, at least the way it's being done as if an AI is a villain with an evil lair (not an exaggeration).

Can we do away with the 'stun gun instantly knocks out henchmen' trope? It's silly. There was also a gas bomb that instantly knocked people out (presumably without harm), then 3 seconds later the guy who threw it was standing in a cloud of the smoke completely unphased.

There was a laughably bad dramatic death scene where the person dying was looking wide eyed talking to someone and then just closed their eyes, how about a little effort?

Cary Elwes is always this dweeby Bureaucrat now, and that just feels like a waste.

Finally I think it's obvious that they're going to kill off Ethan Hunt with the next movie. It's going to be some big redemption making up for a past he forgot to mention or pursue for the last 9 movies but has apparently been burdening his mind the whole time. Then they'll try and continue the series with Hayley Atwell or something.

For the entertainment value and overall production this should get better than a 5/10, but for what it could have been or maybe even should have been that's as high as I'm willing to go.

But many of the scenes are unreal case in point if a nuclear sub gets destroyed in ends up at the bottom of the Antarctic Ocean no bodies are going to flow to the top in one piece or even make it out of the ship in one piece not to mention many other scenes better ridiculous.
