5.title: A Slick Stunt Show
5.content:
While Tom Cruise is important to this film, the stunts are the real star. The production values and the increasingly outrageous stunts are about as good as can be. The plot is preposterous and unwieldy, but not as dumb as a FAST AND FURIOUS film. For such a thin plot, the film's length seems unnecessary. The main villain is a malevolent computer, which could be an ominous threat, but it also deprives the film of a larger-than-life human adversary for Cruise's larger-than-life Ethan Hunt.

Ethan Hunt and the IMF team must track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens all of humanity if it falls into the wrong hands. With control of the future and the fate of the world at stake, a deadly race around the globe begins. Confronted by a mysterious, all-powerful enemy, Ethan is forced to consider that nothing can matter more than the mission -- not even the lives of those he cares about most.

5.title: Decent action movie, but poor script quality
5.content: I think an AI might have actually written the script. Some of the dialog was cringeworthy, but the action scenes as usual per a mission impossible film were great. It might be fun the watch for the action alone, but the story is a bit off. Some scenes with dialog are actually ridiculous, which was surprising given the high profile named actors in this film. That said if you are a mission impossible fan it is probably worth seeing. It continues off from the previous one. It is a part one, so you may want to wait for part two to come. Probably not worth paying to see in theaters, maybe rent, but not buy.

5.title: Old Wine in New Bottle
5.content:
Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1 continues the tried and tested formula of the franchise, presenting an edgy tech plot falling into the wrong hands, and Tom Cruise's iconic character attempting to save the day. While the movie delivers some thrilling action sequences, including a commendable jump from a cliff by Tom Cruise, it doesn't bring much new to the table.

The film follows the well-established Mission Impossible formula, with car chases, daring stunts, and high-octane action driving the narrative. While these elements remain entertaining, they don't offer any fresh perspective to the story, resulting in a sense of déjà vu for viewers familiar with the series.

Tom Cruise's dedication to performing his own stunts, particularly the cliff jump, deserves applause and adds an authentic touch to the movie. However, beyond these moments, Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1 feels like old wine in a new bottle, with a story that echoes previous installments in the franchise.

While the movie may not bring anything new to the series, it still manages to provide a satisfying and time-passing cinematic experience. Fans of the Mission Impossible franchise will likely enjoy the familiar action-packed adventure, even if it lacks innovation in its storyline, for others it will just be an average watch.

5.title: A 3 hours mess
5.content:
The beginning of the film tries to convey seriousness, to convince of the threat of AI, a threat that did almost nothing throughout the film. What did the AI actually do? It hid a person from cameras, ran a fake bomb through a metal detector, threw a party and hacked an agent's comunication. Now compare it to the AI from the movie Eagle Eye (2008), here we do have a threat. Also, the movie has many poorly developed characters that are not convincing, such as Hayley Atwell's character and the villain Gabriel. Hayley Atwell's character is a fearful, orphan and thief who doesn't know how to drive and has a poorly developed personality and backgorund. The villain is part of Ethan Hunt's past, a plot that was played in the film and also does not convince. There's also the point that now in the Mission Impossible universe, to be a great thief you just need to know how to do magic tricks lol. About the action scenes, some are too long like the car chase scene which for me got tiring after a while. I think the movie really didn't need to be 3 hours long. It's still a fun movie, but it's also pretty lost and confusing with a mess of character groups, objectives and stunts. I can't understand why so few people are criticizing these points.

This movie reminded me a little Indiana Jones 5, but unfortunately much less polished. In Indiana I found the action scenes much more fun, like car chase scenes and train confrontations and I didn't think that the group of enemies that trying to disturb the protagonist left the film confusion. Also I found the plot more congruent with a more convincing threat and the character of Phoebe Waller-Bridge much more interesting than MI7's Grace.

5.title: Decent action movie, but missed the mark.
5.content:
OMG, guys, I just saw the new Mission: Impossible movie, Dead Reckoning, and like, it was SO long! Like, seriously, I swear it felt like three movies in one. My butt was numb by the end, and I was checking my phone for the time way too much.

Don't get me wrong, I love Tom Cruise. He's, like, the ultimate action hero, right? But even he looked kinda tired in this one. I mean, the dude's gotta be pushing 60, and he's still hanging off buildings and jumping off of trains? I get that Ethan Hunt is supposed to be a badass, but maybe they should give him a desk job at this point.

And speaking of Ethan Hunt, the whole story just felt...off. I know Mission: Impossible movies are always crazy, but this one went way overboard. Like, there was sentient AI and stuff? I just wanted to see Ethan use his cool gadgets and do some sweet hand-to-hand combat against a worthy bad guy, not fight against some SkyNet wannabe.

I guess what I'm saying is, Dead Reckoning just wasn't the classic Mission: Impossible experience I was hoping for. It was too long, Tom Cruise looked like he needed a nap, and the story was all over the place. If you're looking for a fun, fast-paced action movie, it's okay, but I'd rather rewatch Fallout instead.

5.title: Thrills and Misses
5.content:
Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One: A Review of Thrills and Misses Strap in for a wild ride, but don't expect a masterpiece. Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One delivers on its promise of action, with adrenaline-pumping sequences that will leave you breathless. However, the film's complexity and pacing might leave you feeling lost and questioning the logic of some choices.

Keeping track of the players: The large cast and intricate plot require viewers to pay close attention. You'll need to remember who's who and their motivations, which can be challenging, especially during the film's fast-paced moments.

Car chases with diminishing returns: While the action sequences are impressive, particularly the motorcycle chase through Rome, some car chases feel unnecessarily long, dragging down the film's momentum.

Pushing the boundaries of believability: The Mission: Impossible franchise has always flirted with the impossible, but even for this series, some moments stretch credulity too far. Venice, usually teeming with tourists, appears eerily empty, pushing the suspension of disbelief to its limits.

Visually stunning, but not Oscar-worthy: The special effects are undeniably impressive, but the film relies heavily on them, sometimes at the expense of emotional depth and character development. While technically proficient, the film might not resonate with those seeking a more nuanced cinematic experience.

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One is a fun, action-packed ride, but it's not without its flaws. If you're looking for a mind-bending thriller, you might be disappointed. However, if you crave heart-stopping stunts and a globetrotting adventure, this film delivers.

4.title: One clever action sequence - after two and a half hours - does not make a good movie.
4.content:
Basically, this movie is big, loud, and stupid.

Definitely TOO loud, in fact. The music attempts to turn even the most minor scene into some sort of heart-pounding climax.

There are endless ridiculous fights in which Tom Cruise is predictably unstoppable, no matter how many opponents he's up against. Slim girls get to beat up multiple men. (Emily Blunt was right when, commenting on a fight in "Sicario" in which, refreshingly, she loses to a bigger guy, she noted that Hollywood fight scenes in which 110-pound women whip larger males are "so cheesy.")

The dull, tepid, way-too-pretty villain is, implausibly, a formidable fighter but sure doesn't look like one. An action movie is only as good as its villain is evil; this guy looks like a French fashion mogul.

He and Cruise fight on top of -- wait for it -- a moving train! Haven't we seen that ridiculous sort of thing a hundred times before?

The tediously overcomplicated plot makes it hard to keep track of who's on which side, nor do we care. Apparently, as is usual these days, we're supposed to root against the U. S. government.

In all scenes involving conversations, virtually EVERY line is merely plot exposition in which characters tell us, in stilted dialogue, what's going on, what's supposed to happen, and how we're supposed to feel.

The much-touted parachute jump is actually disappointing. It's over quite fast, and its main source of interest is that, if you've seen the promotional video, you know that Cruise himself actually made that jump.

The only truly enjoyable sequence -- the cleverly worked-out rescue attempts on the falling train -- comes at the end, after nearly two and a half hours of empty cartoonish nonsense...

Including, of course, an overlong cartoonish car chase, obligatory in dumb summer movies.

4.title: Grace's Mission.
4.content: The cold opening is tense, gripping in some ways and interesting in others. After the credits roll, Tom Cruise is still top-notch as Ethan Hunt and that signature run still excites. Something's off with his core team. They're barely on screen, especially Ving Rhames' Luther who disappears in the final act. The landscape is beautiful and the movie utilizes the elements in its action scenes, mainly in the desert scenes. The premise of a sentient digital world-controlling "entity" is intriguing. We're off to good start and then we meet Grace. I like Hayley Atwell. I don't like Hayley Atwell as Grace. Grace, the pretty pickpocket, is the key to everything. Ethan saves her, she betrays him, and leaves him for dead (or capture) and this cycle repeats throughout the movie, making the plot predictable and boring, and their chase scenes felt like a bad romantic and slapstick comedy. No matter how much Ethan saves her life or risks his for hers, she's never loyal to him. Nothing binds her to him. Yet, before Ethan does a death-defying stunt off a mountain to land on a train, he reflects on the great loves he lost or could lose and he sees IIsa's (Rebecca Ferguson) face and a love he lost early in his IMF career...and Grace. Grace? Why?! She's a great love of his life?? Again, why? Grace also caused IIsa's death, which is glossed over and passed off as IIsa sacrificing her life for Grace. I found that disingenuous as a fan. I love Rebecca Ferguson's IIsa character and she fit within the MI franchise. Grace is forced and forgettable. I think MI wanted Grace to be some mysterious, intriguing, unforgettable beauty like Halle Berry' Jinx or an Irene Adler and Hayley Atwell could not stick the landing. She did nail Tom Cruise. They were dating during filming. I guess it pays to date The Boss. Others things that failed Dead Reckoning for me was the villain Gabriel and his henchman Paris. Both were too generic to be memorable or any significant impact. The final never-ending train derailment almost made me exit the theater. MI 2 was my least favorite in the franchise until now. I'll catch MI: Dead Reckoning Part 2 at home on Paramount-plus when it streams at no cost.

4.title: What happened to good writing?
4.content:
This is just a 2 hour fight scene. Some of the action is good but there is SO much of it eventually it all just blends together into a booting mess. Without a story there is just nothing to be invested in. The story is seriously mediocre, and the dialog isn't much better than day time tv drama. It really hurts to listen to. Also there is wayyyy to much exposition. No clever cinematography to show us back story... just long explanationathons vommited at the viewer.

It's the sad state of modern cinema. Watch this movie back to back with MI1. Story needs to serve action not the other way around. It's bad.

4.title: oh no. there's a part 2
4.content: No one liked my indy review, so they're really gonna hate this. Its long. Long. Long. Even tom looked bored. It could have been the botox. But i doubt it. Something about a key to world domination. Did i mention the key. You'll be sick of it after almost three hours. Pegg and rhames are barely in this one. Maybe they'll have more action in part deux. I can't image another two plus hours of this, but hey. They don't pay me 20 million. You've literally seen all this before and if you haven't, they do all of it at least twice. I think the 20 minute car chase in the middle of rome was supposed to be funny. It wasn't. Did i mention the key. Oh brother.

4.title: Abort Mission!
4.content:
I'm amazed that some people were blown away by this, were we watching a different film?!

Made worse by the fact that I am a fan of the most recent MI films; everything that made them good seems to have been thrown out the window here and if anything, it was parodying itself. It was completely lacking in dramatic depth and the humour was forced in, over the top and lacked the easy chemistry between characters.

Hayley Atwell and Pom Klementieff are both super talented; they both put in ace performances and were wasted by the awful story, subject to cliches and ultimately ended up being saved by Tom Cruise. Add to that, Rebecca Ferguson's character suffering a death that didn't warrant any sort of attention seemed really off given all the build-up she had previously.

There are massive holes in logic- I do realise that MI films' missions are all generic and don't try to be too intellectual on purpose, but they at least manage to be believable enough to carry everything else. Everything here had me rolling my eyes; the writing really ruined this.

Yes, the stunts are brilliant as pieces of work, however nothing really blew my mind and we've seen all of it before.

It was all a bit tired and repetitive and didn't do anything new or exciting.

And can someone tell Tom Cruise to age a little more gracefully? His attempt to still look like he's 30 is starting to be more distracting and detrimental to his films than anything else that's gone sideways.

Lastly, why on earth was this 3 hours long?! There's absolutely no meat in the story at all, it could easily have been half that.

Unfortunately, I think Tom Cruise's time is up on this franchise.

4.title: Hugely disappointed but still good
4.content:
We expect something from a Mission Impossible movie. They are supposed to be the best of the best in everything. Even if their tech fails them or the situation changes, they can handle it. I don't know what the idea was exactly? Were they trying to make a comedy? That's what it felt like. The other movies had a comedic moment here and there. It was a quick laugh but back to the action. This one they tried the whole movie and it mostly missed. It's almost as bad as when they made James bond cry. When you try to change a proven formula you run the chance it will miss. It has worked for 6 movies so far. You don't have to reinvent the wheel for us to come back. I get that the gang is getting older and it's nice to have some more human moments. I like those. I'm almost as old as Mr Cruise. You don't have to make it funny.

The action was still on par with an MI movie. Those were amazing. I was on the edge of my seat for that.

I'll be back for the next one because it was still an entertaining experience.

4.title: Ruined by Haley Atwill's character
4.content:
I must admit I gave up on this film about 30 minutes in. Ilsa dead? Smug Haley Atwill character in and at the expense of the rest of the MI team? What were you on Tom? I thought Rebecca Ferguson was a fantastic match for Tom where as Haley Atwill just runs around stealing the key - did I mention acting smug, and has the personality of a fish wife as my mother used to say. I love the Mission Impossible series and love most of TC's work but even Tom can't fix this mess.

I'm hoping a fan edit will appear that deletes most of Atwill's scenes if that is even possible. I don't see her flagged as starring in Part II so maybe she got dumped. Fingers crossed.

4.title: Boring!!
4.content:
Way too long and ridiculously boring!!!

I can't believe I accepted the mission to watch this incredibly stupid movie. It repeats all of the scenes from the other movies: rubber masks, a firefight in the dessert, a 40 minute car chase in Europe, To Cruise jumping off of something, another 40 minute shoot out, blah blah blah, ... SNORE!!! 😴

There is also a lot of whispering for no apparent reason. Also, there is no reason why this two hour movie is a part 1. They should have wrapped it up in this film.

Also, whenever the villain is A. I. you can bet it's going to be a really boring movie. I won't watch part 2 when it comes out.

4.title: Corny, bad writing
4.content:
Lots of big effects and even bigger stunts but the writing is so lazy and corny, and the characters have no depth it's hard to care about them.

Two car chases in the same film? Really? Couldn't the writers have thought of something more original and suspenseful?

Cartoonish villains and dreadful dialogue make it impossible to suspend disbelief.

If the writers had done a better job, they would have told a decent story in a single sitting rather than pad out a third rate plot with more needless filler.

It's down there with Mission Impossible II.

This is billed as "Part One," but even the cliffhanger is so feeble, it left me with no interest in seeing the sequel.

4.title: What was Tom Cruise thinking
4.content:
First of all, I like Tom Cruise - as an actor. He normally not only does very good acting but also his own stunts. But that's not enough to save this snooze fest.

The plot is messy and uninteresting. Ethan's team hunts a key, criss-crossing the world, to something called the entity. The plot is as messy as the action scenes. Without depth and without feeling. Lots of interactions between people happen and you don't care about anyone. Conversations are quick and uncommitted. Cruise, who is often dynamic and electric in his roles interpretations, is so stiff here that he can only manage a single facial expression throughout the entire movie. A grumpy facial expression.

Tom Cruise should leave the MI swamp and return to movies that give room for story, suspense and character development instead of stunts. Because that's what this movie essentially seems to be aiming for. That Cruis should be allowed to do as many different types of stunts as possible. The story seems to be of little interest for the creators.

Overall, it's a snooze fest with a wooden Cruise and a lot of uninteresting characters that fails to engage.

4.title: The worst Mission Impossible movie
4.content:
I loved the previous Mission Impossible movies. This one was such a disappointment.

The plot of the story was just dumb. The adversary could have killed their opponents easily at any time, and didn't need a convoluted scheme.

The chase scenes were both formulaic and silly. In an early scene the new girl/buddy is trying to drive a car while being chased and she "can't control" the car to make the proper turn but she keeps going around a traffic circle?

There is far too much CGI in the movie and it is obvious.

There are even more plot holes than usual and they're hard to look past.

The movie is way too long.

There are too much dumb fight scenes where people suddenly lose their guns and have to punch each other.

The interactions between Ethan Hunt and his team have become silly and unprofessional.

4.title: About 40 minutes too long
4.content: The key the key the key....who has the key??? Mission Impossible films are supposed to be silly and far fetched, but at least make the dialogue make sense. The entity, was claimed to be understood by a few...a unbelievable love story, where Ethan is expected to choose between a long know associate and someone by her own admission "you don't even know me". The entity simultaneously knew everything and nothing to progress the threadbare plot whenever required. The 12a rating of this probably spoiled this a bit too, unbelievable fight scenes that never really made sense with knives being handed round like taffee at Halloween. Way too long after a promising start at Abu Dhabi airport. I probably won't bother with part two.

4.title: I'll be dead before reckoning why I saw this movie
4.content:
Sure, it's another Tom Cruise movie. Following Top Gun Maverick's well earned rating and public reception in addition to critics acclimation, I feel that Mission Impossible's newest installment-Dead Reckoning Part One-was littered with shortcomings.

The first matter of business I'd like to address is the poor story writing. I am the first to admit that a movie with poor story writing can be overcome by incredible choreography or exceptional dialogue, but Mission Impossible left us will nothing but a sorry excuse for the climax of the franchise. Not only was the plot poorly dragged on for over a 2 hour period, but me and my fellows in attendance found the plot so predictable that we could see major story events coming from a while away. A good flick keeps you in suspense-insomuch, a Mission Impossible movie keeps you on your toes and eager for the sporadic action and events that are to come-but this film's suspense and reception was diluted by its poor writing.

Second matter of business; poor dialogue. The best way to summarize the words of side characters and the antagonist within the film would be to compare the words and interactions to an N64 games' NPC's. Every piece of dialogue aside from a select few were very linear, one dimensional, and stretched to the limit. Because of this, crucial moments in the film were ruined by what I would coin as corny dialogue.

Finally, you can't discuss this movie without addressing action sequences. Yes, this was a phenomenal action movie, but some fight scenes seemed stretched to the point where the viewer may sit in unbelief. Who'd win in a fight: someone with a sword, or someone unarmed? Your guess was wrong.

In conclusion, was it a good movie? Sure. Will I rewatch it? Definitely not anytime soon. This may be Dead Reckoning Part 1, but I genuinely believe that the story could've been proof read and consolidated into a 90 minute flick from a 2 part cliffhanger.

4.title: Mission Impossible: Paid Reviews Part 1
4.content:
Not sure what movie everyone was watching; I saw very poor Mission Impossible with just 3 poor and messy action sequences, plus an extremely slow and boring "car chase".

IMF in this one, has turned into three very old and very tired men who don't even speak to each other anymore, and just spurt out exposition in rapid fashion.

The "big bad" is now ChatGPT and whole thing is about two selling two brass pieces with LEDs (a key) that goes into sunk Russian submarine. That gives access to ChatGPT (or something). It's not as bad as it sounds; it's worse. Everyone wants the parts of the key, although nobody knows where the key goes, so nothing really makes sense. Least of all, key itself, because locksmithing is... a thing... and key is simply a piece of filed copper.

Main antagonists are known weapons smuggler, played by insanely beautiful Vanessa Kirby, but who shouldn't even register as real threat for someone as badass as IMF, and... government of the US, which IMF is fighting against... WHY exactly?? Weren't they the last straw sort of unit of US? It starts to feel like actual ChatGPT would have written a better script than whatever this acid trip of an idiocy was. Maybe some earlier version did.

So there's nothing really to watch. Final train scene is somewhat more exciting than rest, but very messy and needlessly slapstick. I mean, try to describe what really happened, save from Tom Cruise doing a clown act through a fight scene... And there's no way human vision is so different that I saw something else; all those reviews praising this drivel to heavens can't be anything else than either blind or paid off people.

Mission: Impossible, the series is a beautiful lie. First two movies were halfway decent and third was cinematographic masterpiece. But from there on, it became very disposable and effortless. And by this installment, whole thing is almost as dead as Tom Cruise's face in most of the scenes. Maybe it's time to stop, since series thing never really worked out for them.

Trash.

4.title: Is this stupid on purpose?
4.content: First scene of the movie and I am asking myself a question: Is this the right movie?! It felt so 90s and not in a good way that I had to check. Okay it is the movie. Maybe it is some meta scene of Ethan watching a movie..? Nope. Ok, moving on. Then Ethan and his opening with just few lines but so dull idea and so little emotional weight. Ok, moving on. Then the exposition dump comes and boy is it the worst exposition scene ever?! It sure seems like they are trying. People just burp line after line as if they rehersed it for a high school play. Nevermind the subject of it that for change seems like it was written by a high school kid. And then just scene after scene of that garbage we have all seen and heard hundreds of times before without any attempt for innovative writing or movie making. Lines of cringe take turns with utter cliches. It all seems like an old script just getting dusty for 30 years and then in the pile of the scripts of Thor 7, Fast and furious 32 and Batman remake no. 482 where Batman is a dog, there lies this Mission Impossible 7 magic. No thank you. I will rather watch a car commercial.

4.title: A bit boring
4.content: First, it must be stated, I haven't seen all the other Mission Impossible Movies. I don't know if this was a continuation from those, but I found this very slow. It was odd, that 30 minutes in, the credits were still being shown on the screen Tom Cruise's character was boring. He seemed like an average guy, nothing like a James Bond, Bruce Wayne, etc. The story bored me, it was very slow moving. There was a lot of pointless dialogue, that was completely unnecessary to the plot. This would have been good as a two hour film, there was a lot that could have been edited out. Not nearly enough action.

4.title: This falls victim to high expectations
4.content: I remember the last "Mission Impossible" to be high octane and riveting. I expect as much for this installment, being that it's a Tom Cruise movie and I have always admired the actor for his intensity and commitment. However, in "Dead Reckoning" he almost tries to be an aloof man of not so many words like John Wick, but it doesn't quite work. Where are the snappy comments coming out of his handsome face? What we are left with is a high-budget tired old movie with an uninspiring plot. The special effects and production design are good, but that's about it. I give up around the two-thirds mark, which is a blasphemous thing to do to a Tom Cruise movie, which I have never done before until now.

4.title: Mission Impossible for Dummies
4.content:
This movie was aggressively bad.

Feels like they just wrote the big train jump scene, and then tried to reverse engineer a plot/script just to get to that point.

They should have spent less money on the stunt and more on a writer.

The plot is formulaic and unoriginal. The dialogue is terrible. I feel bad for the actors having to deliver the lines, particularly Luther and Benji from Ethan's crew. Luther's actor didn't put in a very good performance, but there isn't much to be done with that script.

The villains are comical. A mysterious man from Ethan's past that for some reason we have never heard before now, yet seems to be the most influential person in Ethan's life. A blonde Japanese French mime woman who can't drive, has some mental issues, and doesn't have any lines.

The pacing was bad, the directing was bad, the cinematography was bad, the fight choreography was bad, and to top it all off, it was only half of a story.

This movie should have been a 30 minute short film that just followed Ethan on his train stunt, then ended without any backstory or explanation. That would have been better and at least left me curious about the future of the story.

Rebecca Ferguson was completely wasted in this film. Haley Atwell, I don't even remember her characters name, it just seemed like they wanted to have an independent strong female character, but didn't know how to do it without also making her horny for Cruise, and it just didn't work. They try to make her seem smart and self sufficient, then she just resigns herself to becoming one of Cruise's side pieces.

4.title: I walked out.
4.content:
I give it almost 2 hours of my life. It's sad how so much "writing", effort, and the whole Hollywood shabang could be poured into a movie that fails to deliver.

The script feels forced and the dialogue was just too much all the time. Very little subtlety. The soundtrack was way to loud. What, we're y'all trying to do be like Christopher Nolan? It doesn't feel like a Mission Impossible film.

I hate when they introduce characters from "the past" that aren't in any of the other movies and try to make a plot line based on these characters which are irrelevant to the audience. It would have been much more interesting to bring back characters from the first few films, or at least have plot points that help tie it all together with Ethan's story.

I'm glad these are the final Mission Impossible movies, the last one I really liked was the third one so I've been waiting a while for the end.

4.title: Disappointment Surmounted
4.content: Plot was lackluster at absolute best. The stunts were overhyped and almost had no meaning on the plot. The 2 bjggest stunts were met with unneccessity. Theatre audience was dead quiet during the train fall and motorcycle jump. Pom Klementieff's talents were truly wasted on this film. This was the Tom Cruise-Hayley Atwell show. The missing stay power that are Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg, and Rebecca Ferguson really killed this movie. If you enjoy wasting a couple hours at the theatre for what turns out to be one of the overhyped movie, then this is the absolute movie for you. I started watching Mission because what I had seen was coming in this movie. This on par with MI2 and MI3. A far cry from Fallout.

4.title: Impressive Stunts Mask a Meaningless Plot
4.content:
Mission Impossible 7 is inadequate in some areas, which dulls the overall impression. The plot is action-packed, but sometimes too convoluted and confusing, so that the viewer has trouble fully understanding the action. In addition, character development takes a back seat, and some key characters come across as one-dimensional and poorly explored, preventing a deeper emotional connection to the film.

The movie disappoints with a lackluster and meaningless plot that fails to engage the viewer. While the action sequences are impressive, the film lacks a compelling and coherent plot that leaves the viewer disinterested and detached from the events on screen. Instead of telling a compelling story, the plot feels like a mere backdrop for the presentation of stunts and action sequences. This lack of substance makes the film less appealing, especially to those looking for an engaging and thought-provoking cinematic experience. Despite Tom Cruise's commitment to his role, 'Mission Impossible 7' falls short and earns only 4 out of 10 stars.

4.title: Meh.
4.content:
I had extremely high expectations for this, and it was very disappointing.

The plot was a bit flimsy, and the writing and dialogue were confusing at times.

Aside from the amazing motorcycle cliff stunt that TC actually performed, Olive thought the stunts and sequencing were run of the mill, in the scope of a movie of this magnitude. I'd seen most of this stuff before.

Of course Tom Cruise is a freak, and I admire his tenacity and abilities, but this movie, in my opinion, was far from as good as past efforts in the Mission Impossible franchise.

I hope the next one gets back to the relentless, breakneck bad assery that we expect from the series.

4.title: Tom is perfect, movie not so much
4.content:
Let's clear this up first. Tom Cruise was awesome, doing most if not all the stunts himself and the featured man "running event" !

The movie however is way too long, and the plot is full of holes and convenience fixings. There is just too many instances of pick pocketing to the point of being a plot service tool.

Tom parachutes (glides) into the train car at the exact moment and location to rescue his counterpart.

One item is where does the special key go? Sevastopol the sub but only one person knows. Gabriel doesn't know but Paris is working with him and she tells Tom as she is dying...how convenient!

I found it tedious to watch and frankly it got boring. I won't buy the BluRay disc as I have no desire to watch it again.

4.title: Overate and cliche storyline
4.content:
Honestly expect better plot from a Mission Immpossible movie. So predicatable that I couldn't wait for the movie to end. I don't think I will watch the second part in the movies which is a surprise as I usually watch all mission impossible movies in theatre. The main frustration is that some action scenes were copies from other movies. Especially, the train scene which was so dragged on.

Tom Cruise was awesome as usual but can't do much wi to a bad plot. The female lead 'Grace' was honestly irritating and it was just stupid how she would just slip away at the last second from trained agents. Just not believable.

4.title: Car chases and stunts.
4.content:
Nope. Just didn't do it this time. Really, a two part key that seemed to be everywhere all at once and yet no one seemed to know what to do with it. Car chase after motorcycle chase after train crash. For many people it's what they come for. If that's you, you'll love it but if you'd like some kind of a story, stay home. The rambling on about the entity, the missing key parts, etc became as tedious as the car chases. And I love Tom but the latest face lift makes him look strained. Or maybe he is strained after all these years of this franchise.

I can't recommend this. I left for 15 minutes to get a break and nothing happened while I was gone. You've been warned.

4.title: A Tedious Rehash
4.content: The movie is a rehash of the previous entries in the franchise, with nothing new to offer. It has some new characters and returning characters, but the plot twist and action sequences are all the same. The worst part is that the movie is nearly 3 hours long, and the pacing is glacial. Every scene is extended to a point where I get bored. So much could be cut from the movie without affecting the story. It feels like it was not tightly written at all. If you loved the previous entries in the franchise, you may enjoy this one, but for me, there is nothing new to see here. It is a shame that the filmmakers did not put in more effort to create something fresh and exciting.

4.title: Watch this movie, at home
4.content: The last movies in Tom Cruise's repertoire, being Top Gun and MI:6 we're grand and almost a masterclass at how to maintain the attention of the audience engaged through action and decent characters that wrap the narrative together. This movie however had a lackluster plot and superficial character writing and motivation. This first part doesn't feel so much like a movie, and more like a 3 hour brief on the next movie. Okay action, but the plot being as mediocre as it was made it sit backseat to exposition. The ask for suspension of disbelief is too high from the get go with the antagonist laying in the uncanny valley. I'd recommend watching at home to have the experience but not worth the ticket.

4.title: Boring Action
4.content:
2 hours and 40 minutes of the thinnest spy story you can think of, turned into a schematic series of chases neverending scenes.

The best MI movies were never just about chases with any transportation vehicle you can think of, but included good plot twists and engaging narratives, like the double masked scene in the hotel in Ghost Protol. Here we have just a long series of people chasing someone, often Cruise, or escaping someone, often Cruise. From time to time the action stops for some boring explanation of the McGuffin. I sincerely hope they will change direction in the next episode, and save money for good screenwriters.

4.title: Ludicrous spectacle sags under the weight of its earnestness
4.content:
If you're going to stretch out the thinnest and silliest of premises for almost three hours, unfurl an endless procession of over the top action sequences in which your protagonist escapes unscathed each time, then it wouldn't hurt to leaven the mood with a bit of knowing humour.

But nope, none of that in this dreary and drawn-out exercise in CGI and stunt-craft one-upmanship. Tom Cruise's earnestness about the whole enterprise does not help given the immense suspension of disbelief that is required of audiences. No amount of editing trickery or an incessant musical score can save this turgid mess of a film.

4.title: Characters stretched thinner than ever
4.content:
I have been enjoying the MIP series ever since I was first introduced to it. I have watched all the moves that came before. The dynamic of the main MIP team was the perfect mix of comedy and superficially badass, they were cool but didn't take themselves too seriously, and I loved that! However at this point we have gotten less of the original 3 and more of the new female character Grace. The movie starts off in a solid fashion, the airport scene was cool but from that point it all slowly falls off. If I were to name this movie it would be: "Mission Impossible - Ethan trusts a new conventionally attractive female character for no reason at all" For reasons I believe nobody can truly understand, despite Grace backstabbing him around 5 times, he somehow still trusts in her. At the bar / rave scene, he is offered to choose between killing a long time trusted special agent friend, and grace, a thief that has now backstabbed him for her own good several times now, and can't choose. He then runs off fights against some other conventionally attractive women, who has tried to murder him several times, and spares her, for no reason. When I was watching this with my family, we were at some point just screaming at the tv, for ethan to just shoot Grace, take the key, and finish saving the world. If Ethan had just a bit more pride than he does, and not allow himself to be betrayed, there wouldn't even be a need for a second movie let alone 90 minuttes of extra movie. It's so artificially streched out due to Ethan illogical trust in female characters and its honestly infuriating. His trust in Ilsa Faust was already a bit of a stretch, but all this all over again is just draining. I will probably not even bother with the second movie because it ended up so lack luster by the end, and lost about as much steam as the train did in the train sequence.

The stunts were great and effects are good, other than that, I would like a refund if I have to be completely honest.

4.title: Worst installment of the series BY FAR
4.content:
The mission impossible series has been consistent over the years, holding onto their realistically unrealistic action sequences and plots but this installment let's go of everything at the door. Sold as an 'ultra-modern' plot all they succeeded to do is stretch every single cliché and action trope into a nearly 3 hour long movie.

What we are left with is an 'ultra-predictable' and way, way too long film that overstays its welcome by an hour, at least. I can go on and on about how abysmal this film is but if you don't believe, please be my guest and waste 3 hours of your life.

I was a fan of the mission impossible series up till this point, and was excited for this installment but cliché after cliché kept pushing me towards utter disappointment and resentment to what the Mission Impossible series has come to.

4.title: Weak plot. Empty characters.
4.content:
I'm surprised how bad this movie is. Unbelievable the efforts put into the production of the film for such a weak plot and empty characters. There is total mischaracterization of what the Impossible Mission franchise is. It is hard to understand how the decision to make a film like this is made.

The length of the film wouldn't be a problem if it weren't so poor and shallow.

Grace, Paris, Gabriel, Entity? What a heck! Regrettable choices. Just don't fit.

Hints of comedy that have nothing to do with the real purpose of the film. I had high expectations for this movie but i'm very disappointed.

4.title: Really??
4.content:
What an absolute waste of time. Does this rubbish deserve such a long running time? The plot points are way too telegraphed and filled with nonsense buzz words.

I don't understand why we need to see the same stupid train scenes again and again. Haven't we seen all the suspenseful train fight scences we need by now? And more importantly, do trains even use coal anymore? And if you kill the guy loading the coal, won't the train stop?

This movie is one huge set up for another pointless sequel.

Fun fact, did you know Tom Cruise does his own stunts. Of course he's too modest to say anything.

Please treat your audience with respect. Read a book instead.

4.title: MI should not have been this much cheese!
4.content:
You are filming an epic entry with promising story which AI went rogue and also have it's own human underground organization So far so good, right? Thousands of possible epic sub stories... Yet, what you get is:

a key which can rule the world pickpocketed easily several times
self driving capability in an old fiat 500
completely pointless car chases
only way to enter a train is jumping from a mountain with a motorcycle and you are landing not even on the top of the train but diving through the window which is the perfect point to stop a bad guy
bad guy jumps from a train just on the timer and miraculously doesn't have any injuries
a stabbed girl some time ago, after her a lot of blood loss, not trying to escape the train but going the reverse side, and by luck(!) finding hanging 2 people in a vagon about to fall and pulling them by herself!


key can be delivered by tons of ways in tons of places but they choose an old train for delivery location
a woman shoots people with a sniper rifle in the sand storm without even covering the mouth or eyes
over the bridge all these spies somehow don't have a gun but a woman has a long sword (!)


and many more...

Such a waste of all that effort and perfect story possibilities...

Sorry Tom, you should have said "No" to this plot as an actor who also played in "Minority report".

4.title: Dead reckoning is dead on arrival.
4.content:
The movie begins with Russian submarine Sevastopol trying to protect itself from the rogue-sentient-military-AI called the "Entity". Well, the plot gets predictable right away at the beginning. The story of sentient machine going rogue and a group of ragtag, eccentric people racing against the time, is as old as Isaac Asimov himself.

We have seen James Cameron and Wachowski sisters carving entire franchises out of this plot. But I am afraid Christopher McQuarie is 4 decades too late. While Cameron and Wachowskis provided franchises that are visually spellbinding, philosophies that could question the very idea of human civilization and dialogues that could stir your emotions. McQuarie failed to ignite even a small spark inside me.

Nevertheless, it is a Tom Cruise movie through and through. It is his screen presence that kept this movie alive for it's almost three hours runtime. The action sequences were pretty basic and nothing extraordinary, I might add that I have seen better choreographed action sequences in Raiders of the lost ark (which came out in 1981). Every other actor apart from Tom Cruise seems to be pretty disinterested in taking part in the project and the deadpan, slapstick humour that the director has forcibly inserted in the movie falls flat for the most part.

Is it a bad movie? I have seen worse! Dead Reckoning might not have the same intensity of Brian De Palma or Brad Bird's's take on the MI franchise. But nevertheless it is a good action movie that you could enjoy with your friends on a Friday night, but if you are expecting a deep movie that could make you question the very reality surrounding you, you are in for a wrong movie. Dead Reckoning is dead on arrival.

4.title: Long, repetitive and meh
4.content:
Had very high hopes for this, having often rewatched it's predecessors multiple times on TV. Familiar blockbuster films you know you can trust to entertain.

The latest MI film is not that.

It's borrowed similar set pieces from prior MI films but reproduced poorer versions of them. The structure of the storyline shows real promise but they make an absolute hash of playing it out, it bounces all over the place with little sense.

There's also something extremely unlikeable about Hayley Atwells character, she doesn't seem to fit in at all and seems forced. Perhaps the alleged romantic involvement with TC explains her screen time.

Sad to say I've no interest in seeing the second part.

4.title: Let us Hope Ilsa is not Dead
4.content: I really enjoyed watching Rogue Nation (MI5) and Fallout (MI6), mainly because Ilsa Faust is character matching, as close as possible, Ethan Hunt's determination and stamina. The chemistry between them is also natural and respectful, and for us viewers, promising. For MI7 and MI8, I have been waiting anxiously for a formidable outcome for Ilsa and Ethan. Christopher McQuarrie and Tom Cruise raised so much my expectations! With their imagination, and lots of money I was ready to be amazed. Then comes Hayley Atwell as a pickpocket that does know anything about espionage, or even driving at high speeds. Her character's name is Grace. Bizarre, since the character Grace, in my view, has no grace at all. It is really concerning, really, because even this new villain, Gabriel, pales in comparison to Solomon Lane. Why would Chris and Tom let Ilsa die and keep someone as Grace in MI8? Are they afraid Ilsa would, then, be as popular as Ethan for the viewers, or is Ethan planning to keep babysitting Grace in MI8, and he did in MI7? All I can do between MI7 and MI8 is to hope that Chris and Tom have really good imaginative power to convincingly bring Ilsa back and give us an amazing closure to the MI franchise. If I hear Ilsa is not coming back in MI8, I certainly will not watch it in the theater, and will not buy MI7 and MI8 DVDs.

4.title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part On
4.content:
Quite simply, this is what it is.

If you enjoyed the other films in the franchise then there's no doubt at all that you'll enjoy this.

It's brimming with great visuals, it's good some brilliant action sequences, and Tom Cruise again delivers good old fashioned popcorn entertainment in the same way that he did with 'Top Gun: Maverick'.

It's not my sort of thing, all these films look the same to me, but it was engaging enough, and I would watch the second part of what is rumoured to be the last in the series with interest to see where all the many plot elements set up here lead.

Overall, fine.

4.title: Review for first-time M:I viewer
4.content: Yes, this is the first Mission:Impossible film I've seen. Mainly because I don't like Tom Cruise (too short to be an idol). But, I do like movies where things are blown up. And the movie does not disappoint in explosions, gun fire, car chases, and hand-to-hand combat. All pretty predictable for an action movie. The first thing I noticed was the close-ups of the faces. Having been aware of Tom's tirades while filming during the covid pandemic, I am sure these closeups are down to that. It's a long movie, so you get you're money's worth, but the sequences are too long. I think if they'd cut these down the movie would've been a reasonable length and just as exciting. It's going to be brutal watching this again to remember what happened when part two comes out. So, I'm still not a fan. Maybe I would be if I'd seen all the other ones. But definitely if Cruise wasn't in it. He's just too short to be an action hero. He should stick to dancing in his underwear. If I were you and you haven't seen it, wait for it to be on video and fast forward through the car chase, and the train fights. The whole idea of an AI taking over the world is prophetic concerning the movie was filmed years before the 2023 explosion of AI in all things. Maybe part two will tell us how to stage an uprising against the robots. Hopefully, part two won't be as long.

4.title: ETHAAAAAAAAAAAANNNNNNN
4.content:
2 points go to the comedy aspect which was surprisingly fun, 2 points go to knowing that Tom Cruise performed some amazing stunts. This allowed for some great single shot sequences, like the horse one (laying down, instantly standing up and getting on the house and riding away) and the motorbike one, among others.

Unfortunately there were way too many cringe cliche characters and moments, and the plot continued to feel more and more drawn out just to make this a two part movie.

With that said I'm just an average guy who has no idea what he's looking at, so my opinion is just based on what I took away from the movie.

4.title: A compilation of unoriginal action scenes and bland characters that resemble nothing of the MI spirit.
4.content:
Such an unexpected disappointment...I am a huge MI fan and admire Tom Cruise for the passion, dedication and incredible skill he brings to these movies. I don't know why so many things went wrong with this one.

The dialogue was bland, the action scenes unoriginal (****SPOILER ALERT** fighting on top of a moving train?!***) the humor was forced, the climactic moments deflated before they even begun die to the endless conversation scenes (***SPOILER ALERT** the meeting between the main chatacters and villain in the nightclub that hardly ever became a true fight***), the characters, especially the female ones, had weak story arcs - Ilsa is one of the strongest female characters we've seen but her presence in this story didn't do her justice.

Ethan Hunt could have been any generic agent on this mission - he brought none of his unique skills and wit to it.

Where did Hunt's obsession with Grace come from? Just because she's a skilled pick-pocketer he brought her on board and fought for her? This was a huge drive of the story but the character and story arc didn't justify it.

This movie lacked all the major elements that make Mission Impossible such a unique series: non-stop high stakes, strong team element, complex character dynamics, Ethan Hunt's wittiness and physical skill, innovative ways to pursue and complete an impossible mission while making all the unreal elements of it feel 100% realistic.

His "big stunt" wasn't nearly enough to save the rest of the compilation of unoriginal action scenes that this movie felt like. I'm not saying it's easy to create unique content in the 7th MI movie, but I feel like it didn't honor the previous installments.

I truly hope that Part II brings back MI's unique character and spirit.

4.title: Confusing rubbish
4.content: I don't get this film at all. Coming off the back of the other mission impossibles this film has very little story, no action, bad acting and it's just confusing. The previous films had solid stories, good action, Henry Cavill, Alec Baldwin, secret societies etc. This film takes nothing from the other films. There is no fun action, no decent dialogue. It's a stand alone bad action film totally unrelated from the others. It has no relevance to the other mission films and is by the far the worst of them all. Unfortunately this is part one and we are going to be to sit through part two aswell. Very disappointed with the whole thing. Bring back the real mission impossible.

4.title: Big fan disappointment
4.content:
How can we go from Ghost Protocol & Rouge Nation to this? Too much Tom Cruise running, at times I felt like watching a marathon in ESPN.

Lack of real, pure action, it was tame, Ethan turn into a first fight machine, but he fight choreography were lame, nothing innovating, no new moves, fight scenes we can see in 10 to 20yo movies

Car chases were also dumb due to the script, the female character that was awful at driving (script issue) made the driving stupid, not funny and annoying. Benji's car chase in the M3 same circumstances, top notch outcome

Awful new character, replacing Elsa (a cool character) for an annoying, naive, dumb, child like female character guarantee that I'll wait for Part 2 to come out in the RedBox

Simon, Rebecca, Vanessa & Ving (supporting actors) delivered an awesome performance.

Stunts, no main stunt, sad... I bet they were banking on the base jump; well it was uninteresting on the screen, I found myself yawning many times

Guns, I think no one fire a shot in this movie so if you love gun fight scenes, this movie will not deliver... I love John W. Movies but not all movies have to be like that... but this movie goes medieval, only sword & knives, completely a extreme.

This will movie will no go on my movie collection.

4.title: Worst MI movie, by far
4.content:
I loved the syndicate trilogy, Ghost Protocol, Rouge Nation and Fallout, and I was expecting something on the same quality level; I was deeply disappointed.

This movie often looks like a B-Movie, some close ups make you think that you are looking at a parody picture rather than a MI one, and the same can be said for the story, the Villans and the dialogues.

The only good action scene is the final one, on the train, but the others are nothing special, with lot of bad CGI that makes me thing that most of the movie budget was spent on the press and on SEO rather than on the movie itself. It's otherwise inexplicable how such a bad movie got very positive reviews and users reactions on each major Magazine and Web Site.

This is the only impressive feat of this MI: how they set a precedent on how to pay/manipulate reviews and feedbacks, something even Putin would be proud of.

4.title: This movie was pants!
4.content:
I loved most of the MI series. This one dropped the ball in the fact that an assassin woman with a sword loses against a geezzer with a switch-blade? WTF ??

Almost a 3 hour movie that never seems to get a focus. It's just a downward spiral th whole time

Easily an hour too long, mostly through the pointless exposition. Show, don't tell, seems to have been forgotten.

It's like watching a corporate presentation of what a mission impossible film should look like.

Paint by numbers, but with film making.

The action sequences are everything you expect from the franchise, well done, high octane and professional.

There isn't anything wrong with the acting either. It's what you expect.

But the material they are working with is poor, the direction and editing needed to be harder and slicker.

4.title: Frenetic nonsense!
4.content:
This was the first movie in many years that I've walked out on. Enjoyed previous MI flicks and had high expectations for this one, with an IMDB rating over 8, but it was not to be.

Almost left after an hour of non-stop pointless action, but hung on out of curiosity. Finally walked out after another hour, when the story failed to jell and Ving Rhames lectured everyone on computer science. The stunts and f/x were excellent, but the story was improbable and incomprehensible, with too many groups duking it out for a physical key that would somehow control an almost omniscient AI "Entity" that had sucked up all the knowledge in all the databases in the world and uses that knowledge to blow up submarines.

The female leads provided lovely eye-candy, but had mysterious histories with Ethan that seemed pointless and irrelevant. Ethan's sidekicks always seem to have suitcases containing unlimited computing power, but it reaches a new level of goofiness here. Also, there were a few too many rubber (plastic?) false faces that are apparently realistic enough to deceive anyone within two inches of the wearer.

I should have started with the IMDB synopsis and saved myself the time and $$$ of actually going to this movie. If this was Part 1, I'll skip Part 2.

4.title: What...A...Disappointment
4.content:
I love all the MI films, except nr.2, directed by John Woo. Woo strayed too far from the formula and that is probably why he never directed another MI film.

This MI film is an unmitigated disaster. McQuarrie has made the strangest choices in this film, and yes, he strayed completely from the formula. Did he develop a swollen ego? It must be. I cannot think of any other reason why this bloated 163-minute "Part 1" would be so tepid.

Even the now obligatory Cruise death-defying stunt comes late in the film, and just does not have any tension or awe in it. It also has no reason to exist in the storyline. At least in MI:2, the movie kicked off with a breathtaking stunt from Mr. Cruise; freeclimbing a sheer cliff - the only reason to watch THAT misfire.

The reason MI films have been so successful, boils down to the following (in my opinion):

1. Antagonists are always believable and brutal. There is always a clearcut motivation for the badness. And they NEVER stand and smirk instead of killing, outline their whole dastardly plan for the hero, or deploy deviously stupid strategies for achieving their goals. (The unhinged vengefulness of Philip Seymor Hoffman in MI:3, is probably the pinnacle of bad guys.)

2. There is always a singular scene that knocks you out in terms of its originality (infiltrating the Kremlin in MI:4), or simply a Cruise death-defying stunt leaving you breathless (climbing the Burj Khalifa in MI:4, hanging from the side of a plane in MI:5).

3. The films never take themselves too seriously, and there is usually some comedy interspersed with the action sequences.

4. And of course, the high-tech gadgetry deployed.

This film does not have any of the above. It is just one elongated chase sequence, interrupted by cringeworthy conversations filled with "importance" and "gravity", with a fair bit of voice over to tell the audience what the hell is going on in the convoluted plot. Any levity seems to be totally forced and misplaced (the long chase sequence in the yellow mini car).

I can write a book on all the misfires, but I will stick to three relatively small, but highly irritating elements:

1. A group of characters will each voice one important line, in succession, seamlessly tying in with the line said before. What on earth was McQuarry thinking? NO-ONE TALKS LIKE THAT! Are all the characters suddenly telepathic?

2. The whole film is backtracked with incessant, pounding orchestral music, quite similar to movies from the 30's. There is no space for quieter moments or natural sound for building tension. You have to be "told" by the music how to interpret the scene.

3. Bad guys always gleefully grinning and pausing right before the possible "deathblow", giving our heroes just enough time to escape it.

Anyway. That's it. My opinion will just be drowned in the sea of people who really want this film to be good. In truth, it is not. At all.

4.title: Way too much unecessary talking

When are we going to learn that you can have action and storytelling at the same time instead of keeping these blocks separated, resulting in scenes that are completely skippable considering the story is told again in the action scenes?

The action scenes are also not super impressive, as none of them are on a tight schedule, apart from the finale, and I genuinely don't understand how you can watch this twice.

4.title: This time it is just an impossible mission
4.content:
Certainly! The Chinese translation "Die Zhong Die" for "Mission: Impossible" holds a specific artistic meaning. It combines two parts:

1. (Dié): This refers to the discs (DVDs) that the protagonist receives at the beginning of each mission. It represents the missions and actions that unfold throughout the movie.

2. (Zhongng Dié): This term conveys the idea of "infiltrating spies" or "undercover agents." It suggests that during the mission, there is a constant interplay between light and shadow, where everything may seem clear, but there are hidden complexities and dangers.

Taken together, the translation "DZD" encapsulates the essence of the film's theme and plot. It highlights the missions and action-driven nature of the movie while also alluding to the suspenseful and secretive elements of espionage. The term "ZD" implies a world of intricate spy operations where appearances can be deceiving, and the truth is revealed only when the characters remove their disguises, unveiling the intricacies of the spy game.

4.title: Truly a movie for the tick-tock Generation
4.content:
If I was a professor at an university teaching film-making this would be an example of "how not to write a movie script". Well let me try to explain this statement. Imagine an action movie which spans over an unnecessarily long 2hrs and 36min and is paced for the average attention span of a 15yr old tick-tock user. Every dialogue scene is rushed to such extent that it makes the movie feel like its playing on 1.5x speed. Not saying that any mission impossible movie is being watched for its dialogue, but at least the other titles created enough time for you to get introduced to the characters and at least fear the possible consequences of the villains actions.

Next up is "how to waste money on a talented cast". Due to the unnatural speed of this movie and constant changing of locations, the actors are not granted any room to show of their potential. I mean even Tom Cruise the main character of this movie series feels misplaced throughout the entire length of the movie. Additionally all other actors seem fed up and bored with the script and havent changed their position on camera since Mission Impossible 4. Combined with the strangely extensive cast we are constantly jumping from one sub-storyline to the other, trying to somehow balance this fragile script and hoping to cover up the fact that McQuarrie let chatGPT write this entire thing. The death of Ilsa Faust, a character who was groomed into Hunts new lover over the last couple of movies is killed 2 times in the most dull way possible. On top of that it took Cruise literally 2min to get over her and start saving the new helpless hottie with the combined IQ, competence and intrigue of a rotting banana peel.

"Silence is key" something which no director has ever said in Hollywood. However McQuarrie accidentally deleted all soundtracks in the editing process but was already too coced up to even consider going back and hire people to write some solid basic musical themes. It was seriously astonishing to me how quiet and empty most of the action sequences felt.

Lastly, ending this movie as the "first part" of this unbearable story line is the final middle finger which led me to write this review. The only reason this movie even deserves 4 stars is because the camera operator and the stunt team gave it their absolute best shot. If you want to spend your 17 euros on an alternative sleeping pill go ahead but dont come back asking for a refund.

Speaking of contrived.. Hayley Atwell as Grace. I didn't buy for a second the forced dynamic between her and Hunt. I can only assume Rebecca Ferguson signed a three film contract and refused to come back for a fourth. Why else would they kill her character, only to replace her with virtually the same character? I swear people are just pretending to like this movie because they enjoyed the last few.
