1.title: A waste of money! Retire this awful franchise.
1.content:
$291 million dollars was wasted producing this piece of garbage. I rarely watch new movies because too much money is wasted on a result which insults viewers. Mission Impossible has failed with Dead Reckoning part one. This train wreck wasted almost three hours of my time. By the end of the movie I groaned in despair when the subtitle indicated this would continue with part two, the next movie. I forgot that they told us this was part one at the beginning of the movie. I pray that part two never makes it to the screen. A lot of money could be saved and hopefully some of it would be donated to charity.

I watched this turkey on Amazon prime grateful, that I did not waste a lot of money seeing this in a movie theater. A movie made at this level should have unquestionably great writing and a plot that makes sense. This budget seems to have gone entirely to special effects. However, this cannot carry a movie alone.

The keys annoyed me more than anything. Over and over we heard about the keys. The villain is some AI beast called the entity. The whole thing is over thought and over complicated.

As a child I loved the Mission Impossible television show. Each week a professional group ventured out to thwart evil plans and succeeded. There was team work and watching the bad guys lose was fun. The theme was iconic. One wonders if Bruce Geller who died prematurely in 1978 has been rolling over in his grave with the movie version.

Back in 1996 I realized that the movie version of Mission Impossible (MI) was set up as an action movie vehicle for Tom Cruise. They ripped off the name, iconic theme song, and recorded mission instructions which would self destruct. Other than that there is nothing else that made the MI tv show great. I have not watched this movie series. I am looking at this movie without that baggage.

I watched this movie because I learned that Cruise actually leaped off the cliff on the motorcyle and really parachuted down to the ground. I respect 61 year old Cruise for having mastered this stunt. He did it several times and without a missing a beat told the director that he could do it again. The whole stunt is only a few seconds of the movie.

Cruise and his little used team consisting of Ving Rhames and Simon Pegg are older guys. The cast of women lead by Hayley Atwell's Grace are at least 20 years younger than the guys.

Recently, there was controversy at the Olympics in that a genetic male posing as a female beat the tar out of a women in the women's boxing event. MI appalled me presenting the women as physically equal to the men. Ilsa Faust's Rebecca Ferguson is fighting with Esai Morales' Gabriel who is some thirty years older than her. Cruise's Ethan Hunt gets into a knock down fight with Pom Klmentieff's Paris. What happened to common sense? Men and women are built differently. That is a fact and you will not have a fair fight between men and women. I long for the days of Sean Connery's James Bond fighting off Robert Shaw's Grant in an epic fight scene.

Paris kills this movie on her own. No one will convince me that Pom Klmentieff would make a scary killer. She is scrawny and could not physically beat up men twice her size. The script provides no incentive for Paris to switch sides and help Ethan out.

Grace is annoying because she constantly betrays Ethan. The chemistry between them is lacking. That's probably because the 61 year-old Cruise is more like an uncle to Hayley Atwell. Wait a minute, Atwell is on record stating that Cruise is like an uncle to her. She was responding to rumors that the two dated during filming. I watched Atwell some ten years back when she was involved in the Marvel series. She is overrated.

Henry Czerny as Kittridge is effective. He has a strong presence on screen. If there were a MI loyal to the successful tv series Czerny would excel as a member of the MI team

Tom Cruise is 63 years old now so he will be close to his mid sixties when part two of this turkey movie comes out next year. Grandpa Ethan Hunt will be back. It will be even worse than part one and a colossal waste of money. I started watching the movie with my wife and son who is 19 years old. Both quickly tuned out. I allowed myself to be tortured for the next three hours in order to catch the few seconds of Tom Cruise's amazing motorcycle, parachute cliff dive.

This MI movie committed cardinal sins against good movie making and common sense. I will never subject myself to another MI movie again.

1.title: One mission incompetent : the most infuriating films you'll ever see

Ethan goes head first on a horse into trained assassins, firstly how stupid is he and secondly how can none of them hit him and manages to kill most of them. Then he saves the girl and decides to get the key and destroy the entity in order to save the world - perfectly fine idea. This idea goes out the window when he sees a pretty girl steal a key from someone else. After she takes the key he decided to immediately trust this known thief with the safety off the world and ignore his self set mission. He endlessly saves a woman he fancies, who continuously betrays him and leaves him for dead. This woman is being hunted by people she clearly understand are more capable killers than she is yet whenever she gets help from Ethan she betrays him in a way that never really helps her out just puts him in a worse situation. AI is tracking Ethan's thought patterns to predict the best moves to make so it's suggested he stop thinking like he normally does and acts more methodical to which he simply says "no". Then Ethan has a choice between the woman who's betrayed him and the woman who clearly loves him and has his best interests at heart and he can't seem to make the obvious call. They try to fight off the whole security team when they are sitting next to their boss with a knife on the table. She just let the villain walk out because he threatens her life but at no point do they think to do the same to her, grace even picks up the knife and has to get passed her to flee. Then the woman Ethan saves who clearly loves him decides to save the same woman who continuously betrays the team and decides that instead of using her sword to keep distance between her and the man with a knife she should jump on to his shoulders. The guy is literally holding a knife and inch from her kidneys and she has a sword that now can't reach him, but fear not he doesn't capitalize on that for some strange reason. The whole things a joke, Ethan has no issue killing all the people at the beginning of the film to save a woman he cares about but then doest kill any of the people he should along the way through the film. The film could be 30mins if he was actually a spy because he would kill the people who were a threat to global security. I get it's a film so they flesh it out, but that usually requires you to add more to the story but instead they repeat the same story of "hello miss, I just saved your life - oh no she trapped me in a dangerous situation and ran off with the key". This man is the guy the secret service call when they can't get a job done and we find out he has become an old pervert so attracted to a much younger criminal he will risk the world to try and win her over. Don't get me wrong I'm sure on paper they thought it would be a good film but then someone decided it needed to be 3 hours and they didn't bother writing anything extra to make it warrant being 3 hours. I had to take a break half way through the film because i couldn't handle the stupidity. I love fantasy and scifi so don't care if things are realistic but I need to believe the character could exist. I just can't believe this version of Ethan hunt could be a real person, he is incompetent. I ended up cheering for the AI because it made rational decisions unlike anyone else in the film. The only thing I can compare this film to is telling someone with a PhD in neuroscience not to touch fire because it's hot then watching them continuously touch the fire until the fire gives up burnint them.

The masks...I'm so confused. Do they exist or don't they? The franchise can't decide. One second, people are checking to see if their target is wearing a mask, and then the very next second they're not. People are randomly surprised or not surprised by their existence.

I'm fine with whatever you want, movie! Everybody knows. Nobody knows. Only we know. I don't care. Just pick one! For God's sake! I can't turn off my entire brain. I need some of it to watch the movie.

You can't just do stuff and then explain it after over and over again like I'm waking up from a coma. You get one coma per movie. Not dozens.

The movie spoon feeds spells out in incredible meticulous mind-numbing detail with copious random buzzwords thrown in that THE ENEMY IS DIGITAL. DIGITAL. DIGITAL.

Then it spoon feeds us about this super secure nondigital analog room. Awesome. It's playing by its own rules. Then

And then... the team is surprised, confused, and unprepared when THE ENEMY IS DIGITAL. What?? What am I supposed to feel??? You can't re-reveal something you already re-re-revealed! Stop revealing it! I'm so confused!

You've dumber this down so much that you're using words that most people actually understand now as if we have no idea what they mean. Cloud AI machine learning blah blah blah. It's fine. My brain is off. I'm on board.

But then you don't even follow the dumbest version of your own rules? The enemy is digital. Oh whoops, the good guys forgot that part.

I really don't get it. I have no idea how to watch this. I have no idea what to do expect or how to interpret or how to react to what's happening.

I feel like I'm being condescended to. The characters are explaining things to each other that have already been in explained to me, and then they're forgetting about them.

I want to enjoy this movie. There's so much to enjoy. All these funny physical comedy moments, call-back's, charisma....

But I just... Is it a B-movie? It feels like it's trying to be a B-movie that I'm supposed to enjoy ironically. I've never been good at that.

I feel like the movie thinks I'm extremely extremely stupid. I need everything explained slowly with simple words which I am not expected to understand, and then I am also supposed to forget everything I've been told every five minutes.

How do you make it this hard to enjoy an action movie. You boiled it down to the stupidest possible idea. Enemy bad. Enemy digital. Enemy everywhere. Good guys good. Good guys no kill. Good guys analog.

I'm with you! Just let me follow you! Stop trying to lose me like you're being tailed! This is not a car chase! This is not a foot race! You are crawling away from me while kicking me in the face for trying to follow you.

Not this grainy, over saturated, over-contrasted and glaring paint by numbers cinematography. Can you imagine actually looking out of your window and just seeing a dystopian white glare. The special effects and stunts are like cartoons except not funny. In one scene our heroine in a car mows down 20 motorcycles that were all parked closely together. It is hilarious the way they crumple and fall down like Tonka toys.

1.title: Not a good sequel
1.content:
Suspend your disbelief as you delve into yet another mission impossible movie, only this this with less coherent story line, long uninteresting action scenes, and too many last second saves. This was felt more like a playstation game with Quick Time Events, only you are not in control.

Let me break it down to the 3 main issues.

Action: Some of the action scenes in the movie are extremely long, and too often, making it a tiring watch. No doubt it has some of the greatest action scenes ever recorded, but that doesn't make it an interesting watch.

Dialogues: Generic dialogues bring down the sincerity and reduces it to a school theatre play. The philosophy of show, not tell, is reversed here and we are subjected to long description of each event that has happened or is about to occur. This makes this action movie even more boring to watch.

Storyline: If I compare it to previous MI installment, this movie has the weakest storyline of it all. The main antagonist is extremely generic, and the main henchman is uncharismatic to say the least. They have wasted good story buildups of previous movies, specifically wasting the talent of Rebecca Ferguson.

I would recommend to watch this once and get it over with, and not be too optimistic about the next MI movie as they have demolished an action movie franchise for a quick cash grab.

2.title: Unfortunately everything's wrong
2.content:
I couldn't be more excited to go see it. My family and I are big fans of Tom Cruise's action films and mainly MI 4, 5 (and 6). I was so certain I'm going to watch this, that I had avoided any trailers and spoilers. The movie was a complete disappointment, I can't believe I'm writing this, and I'm saddened, because I'm afraid the franchise has run its course.

Throughout the whole duration, beginning with that cheap opening scene (btw why were they speaking in English?!), I was unconsciously trying to convince myself, that the "good part" is coming up, but it never did. The end credits started rolling almost 3 hours in and not a single scene had stood out in my mind. Everything was bland, forced and unoriginal. There was no story, rather a compilation of scenes [******Spoiler Alert: Key lost, key found, saved Grace, Grace stole key and escaped, repeat******]. It also felt like there were never any stakes, no one was ever in peril, and no one including me was having any fun. Additionally:

-Where was the great team element & dynamic we've seen in previous installments? Past characters were present here, yet never really utilized. Am I wrong, Ilsa? Was that a decent story arc for Ilsa, an awesome female character equivalent to Hunt we met in MI 5?

-What did Ethan Hunt bring to this mission? Anything? He could have been replaced by a generic agent.

-Why was Hunt so obsessed with Grace the whole time? 'cause she can pick-pocket greatly?! Her involvement felt out of place.

-Where was the actual "impossible" mission, where the stakes feel real and intelligence, teamwork and innovation is required?

-Was there anything you haven't seen before? Sure, it's pretty hard to create original content in a 7th MI, yet again, honor the previous installments and put in the work.

-Shockingly, all action scenes were lifeless and of low quality. Topping previous MI stunts must be almost "impossible" and sadly, they definitely made that clear here. Also, such a pity, that bad CGI and filming made it look as if Cruise didn't do his biggest stunts.

-MI films are also known for their wittiness and funny interactions during high stakes. Were there any jokes here that didn't feel forced?

Tragically, the awesome Top Gun 2 feels more like the sequel to MI 6 than this. MI 7 was lifeless, ultimately joyless and forced. It's such a bummer. I could also feel that the movie was filmed during the pandemic, many scenes where characters were discussing with each other didn't look good, because we were only seeing close-ups of each character. Did it really had to be filmed during the pandemic? Can Part 2 capture the previous awesome MI spirit? Too late for diferent director and screenwriters.

2.title: Lazy and mindless

2.title: A Deeply Disappointed Mission Impossible Fanatic
2.content:
Take this review with caution as it comes from someone who is heavily devoted to the franchise.

The Mission Impossible movies are my favorite action movies. They have a core that is based on emotions to connect to our world rather than simply wanting to be "entertaining" and simple distractions from our lives. That is why I am very upset that movies such as Rogue Nation (my personal favorite) and Fallout are followed up by a movie that completely misses almost everything great about the previous ones.

The plot was promising from the beginning despite the odd intro. However, it moved between these large concepts without allowing us to absorb them. IA as the villain is very cool and relevant. The hard part is making it feel grounded and more of a concrete obstacle. While they had a segment explaining the IA's capability, it should have gone into a bit more of how it worked. Not for the sake of the viewer to understand it but rather to give the illusion of understanding it and showcase its actual deprecations'. I definitely don't mean they should explain it in detail, but the explanation that they give (something virtual can get into any system) doesn't make the character of the IA seem meaty.

They also jumped between a lot. It moved between different places which I generally like. However, the places were not as big of a character of themselves as in some of the previous movies. The scenery usually perfectly emulates the mood. They usually combine it so well but this time it felt like they were puzzling together everything. I liked the dark scene in Venice though. Furthermore, the introduction of too many villains that were not explored was unnecessary. Nor did they explain whose side they were on which made it confusing and jumpy. The dilemma that some of them faced about whether to harm Hunt was interesting but felt contrived as they were such a small part of a very long movie. They should have scaled it down. A bigger plot is not always better. Focus on bigger stunts as they have previously done rather than making it into a big jumble. The newcomer Hayley Atwell's character) lacked depth and heart. I do not understand why Ethan gets all heart eyes around her. She clearly does not care that deeply. I do not like her character. Not because Hayley Atwell did not perform well (because she was good in the part) but rather that she was trying to fill a role that Ilsa already had while adding some distance on the situation (she is not part of the undercover daily life) and superficial humour that did not fly. She could have been included as the new team member who had platonic relationships with all the other characters not competing with Rebecca Ferguson's character. Ethan does not have to choose between the two. Come on! There can be more than one interesting good female character.

Now I should add a scene I liked to counter a bit of what I am going to write. I loved the scene with the dismantling of the bomb. Some Luther-Benji time was really good and it showed that the characters were not solely in relation to Ethan. It felt like a typical Mission style where it came to the last second.

Now the thing I absolutely despise. I almost walked out of the theatre when this happened and I am not one to do that. So real spoilers ahead: WHY kill Ilsa off! Now I enjoyed her fake death but killing her off for real when she has barely been in the movie, come on! She is the most interesting character only competing with the lead role. The scenes that she is in are magnetic. Her relationship with Ethan is so fascinating and effortless. Her silent presence is so commanding and delicate at the same time, especially when around Ethan. She also has an interesting and separately unique relationship with both Luther and Benji. So why kill that off? Before this movie, I remember googling "top mission impossible characters" and she was number one. That is not the case anymore (same site btw). They dishonored that character. She was interesting because she was a stand-alone character having her own issues (often finding herself on opposing sides to Ethan). By making her be affectionate just before she dies made it almost seem as if she was simply arm candy. Just as expendable as all the previous girlfriends (but she wasn't just his girlfriend!). By killing her off it shows a pattern of replacing female brunette actors. It saddens me. Powerful female characters are at the heart of this movie franchise starting with Vanessa Redgrave as the villain. A more natural death would have been Luther. I do not want his character to die because I think he is amazing and I am heavily emotionally attached to him but it would have made more sense. I also would have loved for Pom's character to have been given more movie time. Despite her lack of screen time, she established herself as an interesting very withholding character. I definitely could have seen her as the main villain (representing the side of the IA). Maybe even better would have been to introduce her into the gang instead of Hayley's character. It might seem controversial but sometimes the better build-up is creating a slightly bigger crew rather than picking them off. She did not have to die. Her death was surprisingly heroic but it could have been better if she had been given more time.

I am simply disappointed. With more Ilsa the movie could have resembled the latest two movies a bit more and kept more of the beauty of Mission. I wish they could reverse it somehow. At the emotional state of disappointment that I am currently in I would not recommend for any big fan of the Mission Impossible franchise, to see it. It is probably the worst Mission Impossible movie so far.

2.title: You saw it all in the previewor on ET
2.content: I'm usually pretty easy going when it comes to watching movies but this movie is almost as bad as 65 but worse in a way because it wastes almost 3 hours of your time. Other than some very basic plot twists this movie lacks everything that I was hoping it would be. They do not use Ving Rhames or Simon Pegg nearly enough. If I only could have gotten my money back I'd give it 3 stars. Please, please don't waste your time and rent it or watch it for free when it's available in 2 weeks because that's about how long it's going to take to be on a free or rentable streaming service. I usually don't take the time to write a skating review but this movie deserves it.

2.title: Number one fan of MI here and what was this!?
2.content: Ok, something very, very, very, very weird happened here. We are talking about Mission Impossible - and it should never EVER be a movie to take lightly. Why? Because this was and is a so good movie to enjoy with family and Tom Cruise was only getting better BUT: what happened to the script? All actors are good and major in what they do, so why do we watch it as we are watching a joke in SNL? This was not well written and well directed at all. The only scene that was good to watch was when Tom jumped with his motorcycle. The end. There is this HUGE budget, so I think that the least they could've have done was hiring a great screenwriter. Part two should hire a better team to make a better story. Is the only movie of the franchise that has poor writing.

2.title: The cardinal sin: it's boring
2.content:
This was such a huge disappointment! Big spoilers ahead. How dare they fridge Rebecca Ferguson, who was the single best female member of the team that could hold her own and was all-around bad ass!? But they killed her off to motivate Tom Cruise, and replace her with basically a damsel in distress that he has to rescue. Absolute cliché garbage. The best thing about this franchise is that I kept feeling surprised by the new things they dared to do. Killing off the female love interest to motivate the dude is the oldest, most predictable thing in the world. (This is no shade to Haley Atwell who is an absolute gem 24-7. I don't blame her for this at all.)

On top of all that, it was slow and boring! The action scenes were ho-hum, and really started to feel forced and just lame. The bad guy is a computer?? Oh my god that's so 90s. I think they finally jumped the shark. I have loved this franchise since the beginning (except 2, of course) and this might be the death knell for me.

2.title: Impossible
2.content: I get that mission impossible is supposed to be impossible, but this one stretched it a little too far. The whole "AI taking over the world" thing was not well executed in addition to becoming cliche. Much of the disruptions to technology was unrealistic l; either the technology wasn't disrupted when it should've been (I. E. switching to older comms wouldn't have solved anything since both satellites and the older comms rely on radio waves), or technology shouldn't have been disrupted when it was (IE the mask machine likely wouldn't be created in a way in which the AI could have easily affected it). It was also very predictable (especially everything to do with the train) and Tom Cruise moved on from that one woman wayy to fast in addition to getting attached to the other woman wayyy to fast (considering he shouldn't be getting attached to anyone with the nature of his job). All in all it was just too much for me. The only scenes I enjoyed as the opening scene and the handcuffed car chase scene.

2.title: WHY!?!?!?
2.content:
Many fans, myself included, are questioning why Ilsa Faust had to die in the latest Mission: Impossible film. Her character, portrayed by Rebecca Ferguson, was one of the most beloved and intriguing additions to the franchise. Ilsa was not only a strong ally to Ethan Hunt but also a complex, independent woman with her own story and moral struggles.

Her death felt unnecessary and even illogical within the context of the film. It seemed like a cheap way to create emotional impact rather than a natural progression of the story. The tired trope of "killing off a woman to motivate the male hero" was disappointingly used again, especially in a franchise that had built a reputation for strong female characters.

What makes it even more frustrating is how her death is barely acknowledged for the rest of the film. It didn't feel like a tribute to a significant character but more like an afterthought in an already overcrowded plot. Ilsa deserved a better ending-or better yet, no ending at all.

Fans loved Ilsa because she wasn't just a love interest or sidekick. She was an equal partner to Ethan, with her own skills and agenda. Her death strips away a significant part of the heart and soul of the franchise, and that's a shame.

Hopefully, the creators will take this criticism to heart for future films, because the loss of Ilsa leaves a bitter taste behind.

2.title: AI kills cinema and the MI series
2.content:
I've defended Cruise for a while but no more. This thing hurt me.

The movie begins like a mix of Red October and Spy Who Loved Me, which will be a recurring motif throughout the film. Try and list how many movies you've seen just like this. Playing this game helped me stay invested because I sure wasn't getting that from the dialogue. For some reason, everybody in this movie talks like a robot or like their dialogue wasn't written by a human. There's a scene early on when all the top defense people are talking in a room and for whatever reason, they speak in runoff sentences so the next person can pick up where they left off. Like a hive mind. Really strange and even when Cruise shows up, there's so little energy, you'd forget he's even there. It literally felt like they uploaded all the MI films to an AI program and then the machine spat out the script for a two-part finale. Was this intentional?

The plot at it's most simplest, is that there's a key that can control "the entity" which is like an AI program that can change and manipulate various things in our technology driven world. Not much is explained on how the key controls it but it serves as a mcguffin to give our characters something to do for 2+ hours. They run about and chase it but if you've ever watched any of these movies, you know exactly what's going to happen. Tom's gonna have it, then he'll lose it, then it'll fall into the wrong hands. We've seen this type of thing countless times before and it's no more exciting here, just incredibly predictable.

This is a problem the whole film suffers from. A lack of originality. Writing this review, it's hard enough just thinking of what sequences to even bring up. There's a chase in Rome that's... alright. Felt a bit too similar to previous films chase scenes and looked twice as fake. Tom does his signature run through the streets, we get some knife fights, an alley fight, Tom riding a motorcycle, etc. Same old, same old. I know the spy genre has lasted 60 years but some originality goes a long way. They even rip off non-spy movies like Indiana Jones and Jurassic Park. It's embarrassing.

Which brings us to the elephant in the room. I was under the impression that these films were about doing real stunts in front of a camera but this wasn't even true in the first movie, so what they actually do is lie about no-CGI being used. Well it's kind of hard to hide that fact when every shot, looks like it was shot and edited by an AI program. Actors aren't acting in this film, they just say their lines into the camera and then through the power of editing, it appears like a conversation. There's so much blatant green screen used that I doubt the actors ever had to interact with each other. Notice how whenever somebody walks past or interacts with somebody, their arms or legs are usually out of frame. It's so lazy.

This is made even worse with the action scenes, which look as believable as the inflatable boat sequence in Temple of Doom. I feel so disconnected from everything that happened in the movie because I could just tell the actors are nice and same in the green room. When Tom does his motorcycle dive, it looks no different from a similar superimposed shot in Goldeneye (1995). When Tom is clinging to the top of the train, it looked identical, CGI-wise to the train sequence in the first Mission Impossible. I keep hearing this was an expensive film to make, so where did the money go? Clearly it wasn't on that train set because half of it wasn't even there. Even when they were sitting on chairs, it looked fake. Felt like I was watching a Peter Jackson film at times and like his films, it was making me sick.

The MI series is known for it's ridiculous, almost cartoony logic at times but it was taken to a whole new degree by the end of this movie. Tom and lady are running through this train as it's falling off the tracks and it might as well be a fully animated movie at this point. My suspension of disbelief left the room after they somehow navigated the trains kitchen without getting burned by hot oils. They don't even receive a scratch. Absolute nonsense and this is where the film chooses to end. I'm sorry but if Tom and lady can survive that, do I even need to see the next one?

I used to say that regardless of who Tom Cruise is, at least he can still make a fun action flick but sadly that's no more. Remember when people used to say MI2 was the worst one? I honestly don't see how that's possible anymore. That film was a piece of art by comparison. Even the JJ one had some interesting moments. This one? None. An interesting concept, maybe but every sequence is so played out and unnatural, it ruins the whole experience. Don't waste your time, this is not the Cruise you're looking for.

2.title: Was this written during the writer strike?
2.content:
I don't know what everybody's talking about giving this positive reviews this is one of the dumbest worst written worst acted worst dialogue movies I've ever seen in my life it's giving Transformers 4 a run for its money.

The actors literally take turns line by line explaining every moment and storyline of the plot. Each taking their turn to add something to the dialogue instead of just talking in a full sentence or having a normal conversation, it's infuriating.

Every single moment of the plot is described in dialogue right before it happens or sometimes write while it's happening it's unbelievable.

I liked every single Mission Impossible movie up until this one I don't know what they changed I don't know if it's the same director but this is utter nonsense

And as bad as the plot being spoon-fed to you is it's nothing compared to the actual plot itself. Unbelievably stupid an entity is the bad guy

I seriously think this was written by a scab during the writer strike even though I know it was out before then.

I gave it two stars instead of one because I like the girl from Guardians of the Galaxy.

2.title: SMHV (Shaking My Head Violently)
2.content:
***Spoiler Alert****

I've come to love the MI franchise over the years from the beginning. Just returned from the movie theater, after quickly departing when the movie ended. The whole way home I was whinging to my husband as to my disappointment. The movie seemed to drag on forever - too much talking - too little action - and it was mudded by the lady in distress always hollering "Ethan". The one woman who could handle herself - and who I've come to really like from the beginning of her entrance into the franchise was killed off early in the movie, under ridiculous circumstances. I've seen Ilsa put up a good fight and come off victorious, so having a hard time seeing how she lost this one. And to have her character sacrificed over a woman who ever chance double crossed and ran - again smh! This movie tried to do much and veered away from their previous simple, but good formula. AI as a threat - my goodness this has been done to death, but I feel as though the storyline for this AI doesn't make sense, poorly written and executed. It also feels as though they are setting up and introducing the new IMF additions and possibly individuals who will pick up the franchise. The woman thief, the agent Degas. Coupled with spatterings of flashbacks that don't appear in any movie makes me say it again - too much going on and why didn't they just stick to the formula. I will admit it was good to see Henry, but with that said feel as though his character has manifest himself out of the blue. Director of the IMF - where have you been?!? Needless to say, I feel as though if I had to do it again I would have waited for this to be released on video, but this I know for sure, won't make that mistake with the 2nd release in 2024.

2.title: Film Making for the Goldfish Generation
2.content:
All sizzle, no steak. There is no meaningful story, or arc for anyone here. Its just 'bang, bang', 'run, run', 'hit, hit'.

Always been a Tom fan and Hayley is beautiful, but this film is just cartoonish nonsense. The supposed storyline is all about a MacGuffin; a key that everyone wants, but seemingly no one knows what it is for. There is something scary called the 'Entity' which knows everything about everyone and what they are going to do, but then that notion gets dropped and we get another actions sequence that accomplishes nothing.

Confused by the way they have the Ethan character seemingly confused at times and then scared, even cowardly at others. If this is an attempt to add depth, it fails badly. The whole thing is just a cliched popcorn muncher for those who don't need characters, story or meaning. Sorry, that's not me.

2.title: Grace's Casting: A Misstep in the Franchise
2.content:
The introduction of Grace, played by Hayley Atwell, was supposed to bring a fresh dynamic to the Mission: Impossible franchise. However, her casting and character execution felt out of place and, frankly, underwhelming.

Grace is portrayed as a skilled pickpocket and con artist, but her character lacks the depth and charisma needed to fit seamlessly into the established Mission: Impossible universe. She comes across as more of a liability than an asset, constantly making reckless decisions that put others at risk. Instead of feeling like a valuable addition to the team, she often feels like a frustrating distraction.

One of the biggest issues lies in how Grace is written to replace Ilsa Faust's role in the narrative. Where Ilsa was confident, capable, and emotionally complex, Grace feels like an inexperienced rookie with little to offer beyond being a plot device. The chemistry between Ethan and Grace also feels forced and awkward, especially when compared to the genuine connection Ethan had with Ilsa.

It doesn't help that Hayley Atwell's portrayal doesn't elevate the material. While she's undoubtedly talented, her performance here feels one-dimensional and uninspired, failing to make Grace a character the audience can truly root for.

In a franchise known for its strong, memorable characters, Grace is a glaring misstep. Instead of enhancing the story, she detracts from it, making viewers long for the days when the team dynamic felt cohesive and every character brought something meaningful to the table.

The franchise thrives on high stakes and character-driven drama, but Grace's introduction feels like a step backward rather than forward. Hopefully, the writers will rethink her role-or improve her characterization-if she's to return in future installments.

2.title: A Film That's Impossible to Take Seriously
2.content:
This so called Movie is so migraine-inducingly atrocious it makes me yearn for the nuanced character development of a Michael Bay film. The plot is basically the cinematic equivalent of a toddler banging pots and pans together - loud, nonsensical, and liable to make your ears bleed.

The characters spend most of their time posing while wind machines blast their lustrous locks. Actual acting seems restricted to bugging out their eyes and screaming "NOOOOOO!" whenever something explodes near them (which is always). The villains' motivations are about as clear as a kindergartener's finger painting titled "I Like Trucks."

The locations are very similar to Fast and Furious 9, and the movie feels like a cross between F9 and John Wick in slow motion.

The action sequences drag on longer than a Lord of the Rings extended edition marathon. After the 300th slow motion shot of something blowing up, I found myself praying for a long, dialogue-heavy scene - but no suck luck. The locations are generically apocalyptic, like every major city got turned into a slightly dusty parking lot.

Watching this movie felt like being stuck on a crowded subway car while obnoxious teenagers blast dubstep remixes directly into your ears. I'd rather get a root canal than sit through it again. My only consolation is the fond memories of the 3 hours of my life I'll never get back.

2.title: Not good old MI nonsense, bad MI nonsense
2.content:
I don't expect MI films to be realistic. They are an entertaining joyride.

But the earlier ones had the tension of high stakes, World-threatening ride-alongs. They had great set pieces.

This, however, is incredibly badly written and badly acted, The actors so carefully take turns saying lines in meetings that it looks like a school nativity where everyone gets a go. Pegg is awful. Gabriel is awful. The blonde haired assassin makes no sense. And Toms face looks like any middle aged man's now, loose cheek skin flapping in the wind. He would do better to become the grumpy old man actor like Nickelson did.

But the worst thing is the plot. The plot is woeful. Why is there a key? How does everyone always know roughly where it is? Why is not one soul awake at night time in Venice?

A good example - Tom misses getting on the train as he arrives to late (as Gabriel put it into full speed). But it wouldn't have been that much earlier than normal. Given they dropped Grace off to get onto the train, Tom should have been set up at least half-an-hour before the train arrived to jump on it. Then he's all 'I can't do this' to Simon pegg, a role reversal of characters. It's nonsense. But not the good old MI nonsense, terrible new mi nonsense.

Given 2 stars instead of 1 just for the yellow car going round and round scene that made me laugh.

Please don't make part 2.

2.title: I'm 20 minutes in and already don't want a Part 2.
2.content:
The script in this movie reads like it was written by A.i... which is odd given it was written by the "9th most successful acreenwriter" in Hollywood. Truly painful first 30 minutes makes me unsure if its worth staying on for the ride.

All this movie accomplishes is making me miss the days when action movies also had great characters, witty scripts and something else than trying to 1 up how big a stunt is.

I really don't have more than that to add other than 135 characters so that I can submit this review, so just move on at this point if you haven't already. If you have the choice between this and Oppenheimer, do yourself a favor and avoid this.

2.title: This movie is a tiresome claptrap!!
2.content:
I'm not a fan of Mission: Impossible, but I have to say this that "It was very disappointing y'all'.

It made $522 million to date, but still considered a flop as well as "The Super Mario Bros. Movie" it flopped too since its debut 4 months ago declining at 41% of the ticket sales.

Only a few months ago after the debut, Paul Schrader has weighed in on 'Mission: Impossible 7' that he absolutely hated it. The views stated via Facebook, that Schrader has purposefully reflected upon the script of the film. The movie is a "tiresome claptrap" and critiqued the film's writing. There's no reason that AI, given the correct prompts, that couldn't have written this script", he said. As I expected, Dead Reckoning is the worst Mission Impossible, and it's worse than you remember.

I wish Mission: Impossible franchise will never be resumed, but Sonic will do better for Paramount, except Scream.

2.title: Utter Tosh
2.content:
2 1/2 hours and nothing happens. At all.

What a load of nonsense.

Avoid this movie and eat some Pringles alone in the dark instead, or stick pins into your eyes.

Both are more enjoyable.

A cinematic experience that leaves audiences exhausted for all the wrong reasons. Clocking in at a mind-numbing 2 hours and 43 minutes, this action film takes the phrase "too much of a good thing" to a whole new level.

The plot, if you can call it that, is a convoluted mess of clichés and recycled ideas.

The excessive runtime only serves to exacerbate the film's problems. Scenes drag on, and subplots meander aimlessly, leaving audiences checking their watches and wondering when the credits will roll. By the time the climax finally arrives, it's hard to muster any excitement or interest.

2.title: Truly awful
2.content:
Boring predictable completely unbelievable script The big motorbike jump stunt was completely wasted on bad camera work

It just drones on & on I really liked the MI series but giving up on it now Tom cruise has good screen presence but let down such a poor film.

Maybe it's made for 6 to 13 years old ?

Shame 1st James Bond went down hill then this.

I found myself just switching off half way through ( me not the film I was at cinema big mistake )

I think quality of films are reducing , I've decided to wait until they come onto the stream services then I really can just switch off if no good.

2.title: Meh.
2.content: Way too long, ridiculous video-like fight sequences that went on and on and on, and a ludicrous plot even for Mission Impossible. Lots of close-ups of Tom Cruise and costars whispering profound things to each other. It just misses the mark - kind of like it was trying to hard. Oh wait! That was probably the Entity. Let me think about this again myself without AI. Nah - still blah. That's not to take away from the stunts Cruise performed, and there certainly is a lot of "action". But it just was not cohesive - But maybe that was due to the confusing dark influence of The Entity - nothing appears as it seems. Lots of plastic masks being used. Still. Bleh.

2.title: Sadly, the worst MI in the series. It's time for Tom to stop running.
2.content:
I've loved the MI films - well apart from the 2nd one which was mince. Sadly this one is the worst one yet. Tom looks old, as does Simon pegg (but I guess they are. The stunts look okay-ish but so much is digital that it just doesn't feel real and is more like a playstation game (mad max fury road just did this stuff so much better).

Plot is nonsensical. The entity idea is beyond abysmal. I mean absolutely awful. And the whole key thing is ludicrous (bad ludicrous, not good ludicrous).

The actress playing Grace and the bad guys are completely forgettable.

With a 12 rating the fight scenes are tame and there is absolutely no sense of jeopardy.

So far fetched, that it's more like a comedy although who doesn't love watching two old guys fighting on top of a pretend runaway train.

Here's an idea - stop all the terrible digital effects, pay actual writers to write a decent script and hire some charismatic actors (or even just some good ones).

And they nicked the end bit from the uncharted two game.🤦

And it is so, so long...and this was just part 1. A complete let down.

Basically the same two word review spinal tap got for their album "shark sandwich"

2.title: You reckon it's dead... impossible.
2.content: Spoiler alert, these movies are Rocky revisited. To be honest, i fell asleep about a third of the way through. I feel like these movies are made for Dory, exact same formula with a few alterations to the same suit to make it fit the fattened audience. Same hero defying all the corrupt world leaders, yet still managing to stay loyal. Same chase seen where hero is getting shot at by dozens of bad guys who you wonder how they got to be bad guys if they can never hit their target? Same endless cut and paste car chase with car doors removed, driving downstairs and against traffic. Same 'romance'. Same scene where Ethan runs fast with karate chop hands. These movies engage the senses with lots of explosions because they cannot engage the brain with character development.

2.title: Very disappointing.
2.content: I had high hopes for this movie. I have enjoyed most of the franchise immensely. This movie though, is very poor. The broad picture is one of a super computer, with the power to destroy humanity. Think Skynet. Most unoriginal. It's ability to predict the future has been done in movies many times. It's achilles heel is the same. It has the ability to be everywhere, all the time. Yet somehow, it's fate is tied to one piece of hardware. I would have expected far more originality for such a big production. On the small scale, the plot is littered with a way too many moments where suspending disbelief is the only way to get through. Everyone is an expert pickpocket. Accept all law enforcement personnel, who are totally incompetent. On the whole, a very predictable, unimaginative movie. The silliness of it all could have been softened with a bit of humour, but it takes itself way too seriously. I for one, won't be looking forward to the second installment.

2.title: Not just this one, the entire MI series is overrated.
2.content:
MI series is literally overrated. You don't believe me? Okay then take This movie as an example and ask yourself these questions : 1. How were eathan & his team talking with each other while there was no radio or not even a earpiece in his ear. Literally in every movie, this thing irritates me & I just can't understand, why? A simple earpiece, that's it. Even they could've used their fancy tech & show any scene where there is a nano microphone lol.

2. Exaggeration of technology. What is the point of using such things that doesn't even exist while you're trying to make the movie realistic? Lots of computers, lots of codes, lots of unreal techs. And the funniest part is even if there is a single piece of picture appears in their monitor, there is code running all around the monitor. Why man, why! Nowadays, everyone knows about tech, you can't show anything you want.

3. Mask printing & becoming anyone you want in a minute. Wow! What a great idea. But actually, that doesn't exists and will never exist. They just print a face & just like some Indian TV serials they stick it to one's face. Can't even properly fake that scene so every time while doing that, they turn the camera back & shows the backside. And tell me one more thing, if the face changes anyhow, how can the voice also changes?

4. In this movie, Luther is hacking a Russian satellite by his laptop, within 1 or half minute. Wow, what a genius, isn't it? No, that's just stupid & funny.

5. They can track anyone, anywhere, even if they don't even have any traceable device with them. Again wow, isn't it? Nope. The filmmakers thinks the audiences are fool, but in reality they are fool.

If I point out such points, there will be countless points, believe me. This movie and overall the series is just so overrated & irritating to watch. But I appreciate Tom Cruise's efforts and acting skills.

2.title: The worst MI installment
2.content: This is the worst of all Mission Impossible movies. Lacks story and script. Sure, the action is great; All stunts are very well done, but at the expense of the script. Someone said let's add "AI" and "crypto" to this movie, but it was badly written. And Tom Cruise's acting in this movie is also the worst among all his movies which I think is due to the poor script. And the idea of computers can track everything is also very far fetching. Tracking identify using face recognition is done in China only. Nowhere else in world will allow face recognition like shown in the movie. And the way "Entity" is added to the script is also cryptic; It seems like Entity is AI and presumably it will be revealed in part 2, but there's no suspense in the way Entity is woven into the script. Overall, this is the worst MI movie ever.

2.title: Hollywood at its clichést!
2.content:
Is this reviewer getting pickier and wiser or it the M:I franchise more and more cliché, non-sensical and over-the-top?

Just a few examples as an amuse-bouche: the amount of sweat on the submarine's captain's face, the dialogue between Ethan and the new recruit "Not yet, you need to ask me the security question first", the eye-pad, the black-and-white flash-backs, the twenty year age gap between the old improbable hero and the beautiful 100% Caucasian female love-interests, the very exotic but imprecise "Arabian Desert", the intense look on Ethan's face when he discovers Isla shot dead - but not without first having dramatically removed his scarf and goggles, the ridiculous and endless pitch to the facing-the-window boss in the war room, defining a word ("sentient") by having a character ask a rhetorical question ("You're telling me that this thing has a mind of its own?"), the world dominion scheme, the not-so-subtle eye-rolling and head-nods one protagonist sends to another to signal the next moves, the kitchen staff minding their own business in the runaway train, etc.

Feel free to watch this 1990's tough-guy-bringing-his-girlfriend-to-the-movies-"Ryan said it's actually a romantic" film, or choose to spend your valuable learning of Oppenheimer's story or enjoying Barbie's satire of machismo.

2.title: Sad and trite.
2.content:
Tom is getting old. He tries but he looks strained even in the huge set pieces. The impossible stints and situations seem pathetic and silly. The dialogue is hokier then. Saturday morning cartoon. The briefing at CIA headquarters was dialogue out of a bad Edward Albee play. It's hard to believe the writers were allowed to write this and editor didn't cut it all out.

I know this is a new Mission Impossible. The first couple films were silly fun but not offensively trite and stylish over all substance. This is all with a good shooortong cast that does their best to make Tom look good. After his decent reprisal in Too Gun:Maverick I expected better and certainly can't imagine a part two.

2.title: Every cliche under the sun
2.content:
Just...where do you start with this tired hackneyed kind of film? One where you've seen every scene before, multiple times (and not just in this franchise) and yet they keep making it. And we keep watching it!

Ok so there's a mysterious online entity, baddies who drive black cars and are just everywhere...all the time, intelligence agents all talking in turn to explain the plot, a mysterious (bad) blonde oriental type woman oh, and a British female lead, (and she's an orphan), a party in Venice of course, and a destructive car chase through a major city, just again and again...the same film made so many times. This could be yet another Fast & Furious movie, a Daniel Craig Bond film or a Bourne snore fest and we wouldn't blink.

This one is different in that it's longer than most others, at two and a half hours or more. It's time to retire this franchise. And Tom Cruise just looks like he's had enough...even he can't carry it anymore.

2.title: When will such childish productions stop?
2.content: Yes, I've seen it and what a disappointment! As expected, the movie begins with desert villains (Arabs to be sure) and riding horses or camels (take your pick), then the stereotypes of evil vs. Evil-but-hey-it's-the-Westerner-kind-of-evil rolls out like a good old Big Mac and the tradition of the hollow hollywood American tradition. Nothing new, no sophistication, all formulaic to the letter; a shallow unbelievable script that only alcoholic teens can get absorbed in; a rebel hero with Superhuman powers; impossible gun fights with dozens of no-name villains slain, topped by the usual barrage of nonsensical screen noise you'd expect from Hollywood's mind-numbed directors and producers who copy/paste everything from the special-effects basement. 2.title: Not totally stupid

2.title: Almost a parody. Terrible. Don't waste your time.
2.content:
I'm really sorry to say it, as I enjoyed all of the prior Mission Impossible movies, but Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One is just plain terrible. The premise, that is, the "villain," is an absurdity. The writing is absolutely horrid. It's kitschy and silly and almost a parody of most thriller/spy movies. And, the much of the action is ridiculous.

Yes, once again, the Mission Impossible team has delivered with enormous vistas, incredible sets and amazing action sequences. Unfortunately, many of the action sequences are just utterly ridiculous. One example is a scene in which Cruise and Atwell are racing away from the bad guys in a mini-Fiat, that sounds like it's an EV and is surprisingly fast and powerful. Cruise is driving, but, after the car tumbles down a set of stairs, they have reversed their positions in the car and she is now driving - and, of course, she is a laughably bad driver.

Like I said, a terrible movie. Don't waste your time.

2.title: Too many goofs
2.content: Behind the glamor of effects and chases, the movie suffered from numerous goofs. So, the result was a disappointment. Here are 3 out of numerous examples of goofs and erros. 1) At some point the small VW Beetle car tumbled and when the car landed, Ethan and Grace inadvertently switched seats. That is physically impossible, considering the small size of the car and the impossibility for them to float up, while the car was trumbling, then land in each other's seats, come on! 2) The high-speed steam train cannot continue traveling for long, after Gabriel killed the controller who was supposed to continuously provide the steamer with coal or diesel and that is how steam trains operate. 3) When Ethan and Gabriel were fighting on the top of the train, with Gabriel facing the direction of train movement, Gabriel laid down to avoid being struck by the fast-approaching bridge edge. Then Ethan turned his head to realize the same thing and then also laid down. There should not be enough time for Ethan to look behind and then lay down, he would have already been struck by the bridge edge. Ethan should have followed Gabriel and laid down immediately without wasting time to look behind and then lay down.
